title: first fire and subsequent first fire sequence
question:
Hi,
when resolving Defensive First Fire against a moving unit (unit A) that spends 2 MF to enter a hex in LOS of 2 enemy units (B and C), what is the correct resolution?
- Unit B uses First Fire, then Unit C uses First Fire, then both Unit can use Subsequent First Fire to fire on the 2nd MF spent
- Unit B uses First Fire and then its Subsequent First Fire, then Unit C uses First Fire and then its Subsequent First Fire
- a mix of the 2

Thanks!
author: Mozumbooo
consensus_answer:
when resolving Defensive First Fire against a moving unit (unit A) that spends 2 MF to enter a hex in LOS of 2 enemy units (B and C), what is the correct resolution?
- Unit B uses First Fire, then Unit C uses First Fire, then both Unit can use Subsequent First Fire to fire on the 2nd MF spent
- Unit B uses First Fire and then its Subsequent First Fire, then Unit C uses First Fire and then its Subsequent First Fire
- a mix of the 2

As above, there is no ordering of DFF from different units/fire groups within a single expenditure. The units may make their allowed two attacks in any order desired.

title: Pinning a wounded leader that is being portaged
question:
A17.2... A Good Order wounded man who is not portaging a SW may be carried by any Good Order MMC at a cost of five PP. A wounded leaders two MF bonus for accompaniment throughout the MPh still applies.

A SS squad picks up their wounded leader and carries him, as if he were a 5PP SW.
Defensive fire gives a 1MC, which the leader just passes, and the squad passes.

Does the pinned leader stop in the hex, or is he carried onwards?

On one hand, Pin result stop the leader moving
On the other hand, he is being carried anyway, and if he was a 5PP SW, then the squad could continue moving.
author: Minedog3
consensus_answer:
First cut: this condition is not on the list of "Pin NA" situations in the Index. This is not an exhaustive search, but should be good enough: 
Pin NA: A7.8 [Berserk: A15.42] [Cavalry: A13.52] [Climbing: B11.4] [Fording: B21.41] [Hero: A15.2] [Human Wave: A25.231] [Japanese SMC: G1.4] [LC Passengers: G12.13] [Motorcyclist: D15.54]

So the leader has to stop and they drop him if they want to move on. Which maybe is what this situation represents, leader writhing in pain from wounds, they lose control of him in portage (carry). He's personnel, not a support weapon, yeah? Note that they carry him, not portage him, if that distinction matters.

A4.4 PORTAGE: A SW may not move by itself; it must be carried or placed on a vehicle by Infantry/Cavalry at some cost to the latters MF allotment.

On one hand, Pin result stop the leader moving
On the other hand, he is being carried anyway, and if he was a 5PP SW, then the squad could continue moving.

I tend to favor that the squad can continue moving because the SMC is not moving (itself); it is being Portaged. But...

That leads to awkward questions, like if the SMC is not "moving" are attacks against it subject to FFMO/FFNAM? Can a Wounded SMC that was Pinned before it began its MPh (e.g. by SAN during the PFPh) be picked up and moved anyway? Does a Pinned, Wounded Leader still give its Leadership movement bonus?

I suppose SW are also "subject" to FFMO/FFNAM in that Random SW Destruction [A9.74] will be based on the Final IFT DR, not the Original. Being able to pick up and move an already-pinned SMC sounds odd. Applying Leadership movement bonus from a Pinned Leader also sounds odd.

One can easily make reality arguments either way, so no help there. I don't see (yet) any rules that give more clarity to the question.

I would play that the MMC and the leader are nevertheless moving as a stack.
If the leader pins, the MMC can then move independently but, as it was carrying 5PP, its MF has been reduced; and it cannot count on the leader bonus.

Leaders, wounded, carried, or not, take morale checks and pin checks, whereas support weapons do not. The leader has his own separate morale condition unrelated to the unit carrying it. Nothing changes that. There is no logical means to compare an unpinnable SW to a pinnable leaders, carried or not. Mainly because SW are not personnel. 

Further, there is no reason given in the rules that wounded, carried leaders would not suffer pin results to full effect. It would be hard, perhaps impossibly stubborn, to argue against the clear criteria given in the index regarding "Pin NA," especially based only on the opinions or conjectures I've seen so far. 

In the absence of some Q/A tangential to this discussion ((I don't see any direct Q/A about this), I know how I'd play it without asking further. But find something in the rules / Q/A that contradicts or supplements the Index, or if someone gets a ruling, that may change things, of course! cheers and enjoy the debate

Prisoners are another case where entities are "moving but not exactly moving themselves." Prisoners are not subject to Pinned results directly [A20.54] but inherit their Pinned status from their guard. I would kind-of expect similar behavior for a portaged, wounded SMC. But again there is no rule backing this up.

Prisoners are another case where entities are "moving but not exactly moving themselves." Prisoners are not subject to Pinned results directly [A20.54] but inherit their Pinned status from their guard. I would kind-of expect similar behavior for a portaged, wounded SMC. But again there is no rule backing this up.
I initially thought this made sense, and it does from a "congruency" point of view. 

But not at all from a "realism" point of view.  A wounded leader is not the same "entity" as a prisoner. Prisoners are captives, likely to be be bound, and not at all in charge of what is going on in the hex. A wounded leader in the hex (presuming no other higher ranked leaders)  IS IN CHARGE of what is going on in the hex. He is ORDERING his men to carry him. If he panics and breaks, they can't carry him any more, he's gonna run away. If he freezes or experiences a rush of pain (pins) he tells them to stop carrying him and they either carry on or not. 

Therefore, I reject this notion there is some kind of parallel with wounded leaders and prisoners because they have some commonalities as "entities". 

This is not a game about entities. This is a game about soldiers and soldiering. 

There are some players who view this game only through the scope of the rules, and not from the scope of the game being a simulation. 

This leads to unintelligence design decisions that crept in from the very beginning, such as

a) Twinkle-Toes Elefants
Elefants with an MP of 8 being able to do a free CA change with an unfired MA, but Halftracks with an MP of 16 cannot because the MA is an AAMG.
This means the former can get out of trouble faster than the latter. Make sense to you? Then you are among the ranks of rule-based players.
Simulation-based fix -- allow Halftracks that haven't fired their MA a free CA change

b) Schrodinger's Residual Firepower 
Road junctions on the short geo-map edges have quantum-mechanical effects. If you see a residual FP in hex GG5, no matter! Use the road rate on GG6.
If you think this is okay, that to stop vehicles entering the map on the edge by the road should have to fill RFP in two hexes, contradulations, you are a rules-based player. 
Simulations based fix -- at the start of any scenario, define that road edges only work on the 5 coordinates. 

c) VBM freeze tactics
If you think this is how tanks and infantry actually fought on a regular basis and is a great idea, then you are a rules-based player. At least the designers of Dinant got this right. Simulation-based play. They don't allow it:
DN11 VEHICLES & ENEMY UNITS: A vehicle may voluntarily end its MPh (or attempt ESB; D2.5) in the same hex as an unbroken enemy Infantry unit only if any of the following apply:  	
It is under Recall (D5.341); or
It started the MPh already in the hex (and it does not leave the hex); or
All enemy units in the hex were hidden at the moment of entry.5

d) Frozen at Bail Out
Swing those turrets to force involuntary bail-outs! The men would never bail out without being swept off their feet into the dirt!
If you think this actually happened all the time deliberately, you are a rules-based player. Especially if you won't simply just allow voluntary bail-out by any riders of AFVs, thereby allowing riders of turretless tanks to do the same trick. 

etc. 😍

Of course, the game must be played by the rules. But let's not add to the bag of tricks that veer the game away from its design intention.

FWIW, I put down the pinned leader in the hex, and stopped the squad in the hex because he now only had 2mf

If I was re-designing ASL I would
1. Make leaders command units, not be fire direction leaders
2. Get rid of bypass movement entirely.
3. no crew survival for tank crews, just the passengers.

there would be more..

title: Booby Traps in Scenario 131, Penetration of Rostov
question: This scenario has an SSR that states, "Russians have Level B Booby Trap capability, which can only be activated by German TC". Does the second part of this sentence mean that Mopping Up (which would normally cause a Casualty dr if the DEFENEDER has Booby Trap capability, if I understand the rule correctly) will not cause such a dr here, only explicit German TCs will? Is Mopping Up the only thing other than a TC that can trigger a Casualty dr because of Booby Traps? I don't think I've ever played a scenario with Booby Traps before so just want to make sure I'm interpreting this correctly.
author: bnscott
consensus_answer:
Too bad you picked this as your first booby trap scenario! The SSR means exactly what it says...?  Is there a reason to think otherwise? Yes, unfortunately. 

The reason to think otherwise is that there is no definition of "booby trap activation" anywhere in the rule book. The author of the SSR is making up a concept, perhaps trying to conserve space on the scenario card (?) to add a nearly pointless SSR. Searching the ASLRB, there are (B28.9) "booby trap resolution", "booby trap attacks", and "booby trap capability", also "booby trap trigger (D15.54)" but no such thing as "booby trap activation".  The SSR lazily cites no rules to help clear things up, even though there is plenty of space on the scenario card.

This forces us to conjecture what the hell the designer wanted when he wrote this. I would personally lean towards MR's view on this, but JR V has an equally valid argument, because no-one knows what the designer really meant here, so we are forced to offer opinions. 

Since it's a matter of opinion due to poor SSR wording, I'd roll it off with the opponent if they disagree. But here is the silly thing... such a minor nuance is a bit over the top! Why are these booby traps in this scenario not effective under all circumstances possible? Is the scenario that finely tuned that the balance is in question without this scenario special rule? Which is, in any event, unclear? I can't possibly this scenario outcome hangs on a dime such as this! I can only imagine some weird playtest outcome caused one side to win when they otherwise "didn't deserve to" according to the views of the designer. Who knows? 

Maybe use this: poorly worded and nearly useless SSR are to be ignored. Play on.

title: VCA, TCA or both?
question:
Hi all.

In the enemy MPh, I have a Sherman tank facing forward with no AAMG. Its bow-mounted MG and MA have already fired in this phase. 
Now, a German tank approaches from the flank. Can I change the VCA to fire at it with the CMG (taking the corresponding penalty but exposing my frontal armor)? Or, since it is a coaxial machine gun, am I only allowed to change the TCA?

I understand that I can choose either option, but I would appreciate confirmation.

Thanks.

title: Set DC versus AFV.
question:
Hi all.

We know that for a Placed/Thrown DC to attack an armored vehicle, that must be pre-designated as its target. But what about a Set DC (other than a Japanese A-T set DC)? Can it destroy the AFV, or will it only affect vulnerable PRC?

Thanks in advance.
author: Pavlo
consensus_answer:
A23.5 "In order for a DC attack (as with any ordnance Direct Fire vs a Location containing an AFV in combination with unarmored targets) to affect an AFV, it must be predesignated as being made against the AFV."

A23.71 " A detonated Set DC is resolved on the 36+ FP column of the IFT (or with 18 FP [the 16 FP column] vs concealed units) with a -3 DRM and no TEM including vs the vulnerable PRC of an AFV (with +2 CE DRM)." 

A DC can't be declared as set against a vehicle (and it is unlikely that there would be an enemy vehicle in the Location when it is set anyway). The only effect will be general collateral vs. PRC and/or possible indirect effects vs. terrain.

An A-T Set DC can affect a vehicle [G1.6121].

title: Landing Craft vehicle unloading costs
question: A LCM(3) (4 MP movement allotment) beached across a not-exposed reef hexside last friendly MPh. At the start of this friendly MPh it unloads its Passenger Sherman. The cost for the Sherman is 1 MP to Start, 4 MP to unload to unload (25% of its MP allotment (FRU) = 13 * 0.25 = 3.25 MP, FRU to 4 MP) and 3 MP to wade in the reef hex (2 MP + 1 MP COT for waterproofed, fully-tracked)  for a total of 8 MP. What is the cost for the LC? Is it 1 MP (25%) to unload, 2 MP (1 MP spent while the Sherman started plus 25% to unload) or 3 MP (the Sherman spent 61.5% of its MP allotment in unloading, and the LC must expend a corresponding percentage of its MP allotment)?
author: jrvjrv
consensus_answer:
The LCM(3) is a landing craft. I'd say LC rules apply, particularly this one quoted below. This rule does address the aforementioned uncertainty about the 25% MP expenditure. What I don't know is why an LTV4 is being cited here in reference to the question, instead of the data for LCM(3) and landing craft? I guess the unloading procedure could be similar for the lighter vehicles that the LTV4 can carry per chapter G, but it can't carry the Shermans. 

As for the cost, I agree that more than 50% of the total cost of the vehicle to leave the LC is used, but less than 75%, so that would mean 3/4 of the points are spent. I don't think this is staggered incrementally but is totalled up. 

[ EDIT -- USA Vehicle note 51 speaks of MP allotment and movement allotment in the same paragraph. Note that while MF and MP are defined in the index as "measures of movement capability" (no mention of "allotment"), MF allotment is adequately described in A4.11 and MP allotment is not so adequately described in D1.1. There is NO general definition of movement allotment, though it is used in A4.1, D12.5, USA Vehicle Note 51, Korean Vehicle Note 25. We can deduce that movement allotment really means MF allotment or MP allotment, depending on the unit type. IMO "movement allotment" should be added to the Index and defined. ]

12.4 (UN)LOADING: Except as stated otherwise, normal Vehicle—not Boat—(un)loading rules (D6.4-.5; D8.5) apply to LC and their Passengers. A LC Passenger may unload into an enemy-occupied hex. If a LC is Aground (or is Beached across a hexside that is not within its VCA), units may unload from it only into its hex, and do so by expending 25% (FRU) of their MF/MP allotment (plus COT MP if it is a vehicle). There is no D2.14 penalty cost for the presence of the LC in the Location, but Overstacking will apply when a vehicle [EXC: motorcycle] is in the same Location as a LC but is not a Passenger on one. A unit wishing to load onto an Aground LC must be in (or enter, expending that Location's COT to do so—plus, if it is a vehicle, one extra MP for the presence of the LC; D2.14) that LC's Location, then expend 25% (FRU) of its MF/MP allotment (plus, if it is a vehicle, one MP as the LC's COT and one MP to Stop).

replies.body: my guess is 3, based on the description in Chapter H for the LVT4

Vehicle Note 51 (LVT4):
Unloading a Passenger vehicle consists of driving it off the LVT4 into the LVT's Location at a cost of one MP for starting, plus one-fourth of the Passenger vehicle's MP allotment, plus COT. There is no MP cost for entering the LVT's Location (D2.14), but Overstacking will apply. Loading is the reverse of this procedure; i.e., the vehicle first enters the LVT's Location if necessary (paying one extra MP; D2.14), and then expends one-fourth of its MP allotment plus one MP for COT to load onto it, plus one MP to stop. Otherwise, the normal principles of D6.4-.5 for (un)loading Passengers apply, including the "simultaneous expenditure" of each 25%-segment of movement allotment by both the Passenger vehicle and the LVT4 during the turn of (un)loading.
It's the "the "simultaneous expenditure" of each 25%-segment of movement allotment by both the Passenger vehicle and the LVT4" part that is unclear to me. The "25%-segment" might be referencing just the unloading cost, which is the only cost that is 25%. It might be referencing costs spent by Passengers while loaded, or it might be, as you suggest, the cost for the entire unloading. In short, I can read the vehicle note as suggesting any of the three ways, although perhaps the second (two MP) is weaker than the other two.

D6.5, "Disembarking Personnel must expend one MF to be placed beneath the vehicle and are additionally considered to have already expended one MF for every one-fourth of the MP allotment (FRU) used by the vehicle during that turn prior to unloading." This is phrased for Infantry, so I am assuming a Passenger vehicle spend the ¼  of its MP allotment for every ¼ MP allotment spent by the transporting vehicle. I can't find a corresponding rule that says that MP (or MF?) spent by the Passenger cause the transporting vehicle to spend MP.

title: MMG vs HMG
question: Generally, HMGs have a better ROF, range, and damage than MMGs. But rules-wise, are there any differences? Is there any rule that applies to an HMG but not an MMG?
author: chris99
consensus_answer:
Just realized some other differences between LMG and MMG/HMG. A LMG does not have restricted Field of Fire [A9.21] when firing from woods/building/rubble. A LMG can't be dismantled [A9.8]. For some nationalities (e.g. Japanese, Ethiopian) MMG/HMG is a crewed weapon. A LMG can be fired from crest [B20.95] or marsh [B16.32] and can fire outside the protected hexsides (as Area Fire) from a wadi [F5.41]. A LMG can be fired by a Passenger [D6.1]. A LMG can't be bore sighted [C6.41].

I'm going to stop now, because that wasn't the original question. The differences between MMGs & HMGs are certainly fewer and may only be the Light AA difference.

replies.body:
No rules differences between (EDIT) LMG/MMG/HMG.
Now, some MMG (US, Japanese, German) are only 3PP, so a broken unit will be able to rout with them.
German MMG/HMG, when dismantled, fire like an LMG.

There is a rules difference between LMGs and MMGs/HMGs. LMGs can fire in the AFPh after having moved, but MMGs/HMGs may not [A4,41]. I can't think of any difference between MMGs & HMGs beyond those given by factors such as PP cost, range, FP and ROF, etc. There may be such, but I can't think of any.

title: Does the "No Quarter" declaration allow use Low Crawl to units adjacent to the enemy?
question:
Hi all.

As stated in the question, I have a doubt regarding rules A20.21 and A20.3. If one side has declared No Quarter, can an enemy unit use Low Crawl if it is adjacent to that side at the start of its Rout Phase? Or does the prohibition under rule A20.21 still take precedence?

Thanks in advance.
author: Pavlo
consensus_answer:
Why are you equating Low Crawl with being ADJACENT????

10.52 LOW CRAWL: Low Crawl is a rout of one Location which requires 
the entire MF allotment of the routing unit (but is still considered a form of 
Assault Movement should the routing unit enter a FFE Blast Area). A rout-
ing unit using Low Crawl cannot be Interdicted. Low Crawl cannot be used 
to enter Marsh or a Water Obstacle, or in any stream unless dry. Low Crawl 
cannot be used to exit an enemy-occupied Location [EXC: Night (E1.54)]. 
All other Rout provisions apply unchanged to Low Crawl, e.g., rout must still 
be towards the nearest woods/building Location within 6 MF.

Nothing in 10.52 requires a unit that wants to Low Crawl be ADJACENT to an enemy unit (Known or otherwise).

A Routing Unit has these options:
* If not subject to possible surrender, it designates its Rout target (nearest woods/building within 6 MF) and:
1) Routs using its 6 MF (3 for Wounded Leader, etc). towards that target; if moving into Open Ground it may be subject to Interdiction (A10.53; A10.531).
2) Declares Low Crawl and only Routs a single hex, AGAIN TOWARDS THE ROUT TARGET.

*If No Quarter has NOT been declared and it begins the Rout phase adjacent to a KEU and cannot Rout in any way to avoid Interdiction, it Surrenders to that adjacent KEU.

*If No Quarter HAS been declared and it begins the Rout phase adjacent to a KEU and cannot Rout in any way to avoid Interdiction, it does NOT Surrender and may either Rout using its 6 MF (taking the Interdiction MC(s)) or Low Crawl one hex and avoiding all Interdiction rolls.

Note that if the broken unit begins the Rout phase adjacent to a KEU, but has a VALID Rout path that does _not_ subject it to Interdiction, it does ** NOT ** Surrender and can Rout via the first bullet above (either using full 6 MF or Low Crawling one hex ... but both still must be towards it's designated Rout target).

units faced with No Quarter (20.3) never surrender via the RtPh method; they always use Low Crawl or risk Interdiction to avoid surrender.

It is because of the factor incorporated into this discussion (but not discussed as much as it should be) of Disrupted units.

Disrupted units are not allowed to Rout normally.  They either are locked in current position, or they surrender when an enemy unit is adjacent when No Quarter rules are not in effect.

When No Quarter rules are in effect, it primarily effects the treatment of Disrupted units.

With No Quarter in effect, a Disrupted unit will NOT surrender to the adjacent enemy unit ... but will rather either Low Crawl or Rout normally (risking Interdiction as needed) rather than surrender.

So the ADJACENT factor under No Quarter is technically only applicable to Disrupted unit behaviour (not your run of the mill "normal" broken unit).

Visualizing what is going on here in reality and what the rules are trying to simulate -

Once it is known by one side or the other or both that the enemy kills all surrendering prisoners post haste ... then there is no point in surrendering to a certain death at the hands of the enemy.

So again, the No Quarter rules are there to modify the Surrender Rules/Conditions (NOT the underlying base Rout rules).

title: Crew Final fire with Ordanace
question: If a crew manning an AT gun first fired with its inherint FP,can it  then final fire with the AT gun in the MPh or Dfph?
author: Mongoose56
consensus_answer:
It would be considered Intensive Fire if the Gun wasn't fired yet? And if so could the Gun fire on any target or just an adjacent one?
C5.6 does not mandate that the gun itself needs to be fired before Intensive Firing. 

Read below you will see nothing about previous firing as a gun being necessary for it to engage in Intensive Fire: 

CASE F; INTENSIVE FIRE: Intensive Fire is available only to Guns (not SW), and can be used only if the crew of the Gun is not pinned, shocked, stunned, or marked with a Final/Intensive Fire counter. 

As to your second question, here is the index entry to read and study:

Intensive Fire (IF): C5.6 [AFPh Restriction: A4.41, A7.25] [Area Target Type: C3.33] [B#/X#: A.11] [Conditional ROF: C2.5] [Depletion Number: C8.92] [ENEMY will only use against an ADJACENT Target: S8.21] [Final Fire Restriction: A8.41, C2.241] [OVR Prevention: C5.64] [Pinned: A7.81] [Subsequent First Fire: A8.3]

As you can see, there are AFPh restrictions, and most importantly for your situation, final fire restrictions, A8.41, read those.

title: Gullies
question: If a squad advances into crest status from IN a gully does it lose concealment? And what is the TEM be for units in crest status?
author: Mongoose56
consensus_answer:
It depends...

If a unit can see it through a non-Crest hexside or that have LOS into the gully (per B20.92), then I would say 'yes', as it is in Open Ground per A10.531.  But if the only units that can see it must cross a Crest hexside, then it gets the Crest TEM (B27.3 via B20.92) of +4 versus OVR or OBA and +2 versus non-CC, FT attacks.

Depends 🙂

IF the unit with LOS can see INTO the Gully (i.e. has sufficient height advantage), then concealment is lost because the unit does not qualify for the +2 TEM.

If the unit with LOS cannot see INTO the Gully, then it maintains concealment because it qualifies for the +2 TEM so is not in 'Open Ground' during the Advance.

The squad in question was advancing in the APH phase.So if the only LOS is through the crest hexsides, concealment is maintained. Correct?
As per previous answer, if the unit's change of position would have been subject to the FFMO DRM during the MPh, the unit loses concealment. If the unit benefited from the +2 TEM for crest status, then concealment would be maintained. If the unit benefited from some other TEM (e.g. gully-woods) or the terrain was not otherwise Open Ground (e.g. gully-brush, Fog) then the unit would maintain concealment. If the +2 TEM for crest did not apply [e.g. the viewer had LOS INTO the depression hex, B20.92] and there was no other terrain in the hex and there was no other external factor, then the unit would would lose concealment.

All is covered in the rules TBH.

There are other subtleties to Gullies/crest you need to be aware of...they are a unique position to be in.
It bends a LOT of rules

title: Unknown enemy units

author: Mongoose56
consensus_answer: There is another way of "attacking" when the only target in the hex is out-of-LOS: WP. The WP counter will generally "fall" to the ground level Location [C8.52]. When a WP counter is placed in a Location, all units in that Location must take a WP NMC regardless of whether they were hit or not (and if not in LOS with no other units that are in LOS the units not in LOS could not be hit) [A24.31].

Sneaky!

a MG can place a Fire Lane without firing at any moving target if it can place a Fire Lane Residual FP counter in a Location that is Bore Sighted by that MG; however, if it does so it must thereafter place (if otherwise able to do so) a Fire Lane to that Location in every enemy MPh (and must do so before the ATTACKER begins moving his first unit in that MPh) until the start of an enemy MPh in which it can see a Known enemy unit.

A fire lane can be placed beyond LOS during the day as well, and could potentially attack a moving unit that is out-of-LOS. The major difference is that for day the original attack has to be at an in-LOS enemy unit to place the firelane, while the special bore site fire lane can be placed without ever having seen an enemy unit. At night ordinary fire lanes may also be placed out of LOS too, where the LOS might be blocked by NVR or hindrances as with day.

title: RB 1 SSR 3 question
question: RB 1 SSR 3 states that Russian MMC must take a NMC after German reinforcements are setup. It states that a unit loses its concealment "only" if it loses its good order status. Does this mean that failure of the NMC only strips concealment or is the unit subject to breaking, ELR, casualty reduction also?
author: Jgolch
consensus_answer:
RB 1 SSR 3 states that Russian MMC must take a NMC after German reinforcements are setup. It states that a unit loses its concealment "only" if it loses its good order status. Does this mean that failure of the NMC only strips concealment or is the unit subject to breaking, ELR, casualty reduction also? 

RB1 SSR3 "Each such unit loses its concealment (if any) only if the NMC causes it to lose Good Order status, regardless of enemy LOS."
Could be read as: ""Each such unit loses its concealment (if any) as the sole consequence if the NMC causes it to lose Good Order status, regardless of enemy LOS.",
or could be read as: ""Each such unit loses its concealment (if any) just in the case when the NMC causes it to lose Good Order status, regardless of enemy LOS."

I can see reading this two ways, as you suggest. In one way the "only" is attached to the loss of concealment clause, i.e. the sole consequence of losing its Good Order is to lose concealment. But that means that the sole consequence of failing the NMC is to lose concealment, i.e. not only does failing the NMC not HoB, ELR or casualty reduce, it also does not break. If that is the case then the unit never breaks (or goes berserk) and so always remains Good Order after the NMC and so never becomes unconcealed. That seems unlikely. So I have to conclude the intention was the second interpretation, i.e. the NMC causes all normal effects including breaking, HoB, ELR and Casualty MC. If after that MC it is no longer Good Order, then it loses concealment. So for instance if the result of the NMC is HoB with hero creation and battle hardening then the unit does not lose concealment, but if the result is HoB, berserk then it does lose concealment.

consensus_answer:
If I read you correctly:

While in G11, I9 was ignore-able (owing to the no-farther-from-I11 allowable EXC).

I9 is too far away to be considered in G11. It is four MF, vs. three MF for G9 & F9. F9 is ignorable but G9 is not. Klas's trick is to choose F9 anyway, knowing that the rout to F9 will be prevented once the unit reaches G10 by D3. 

While in G10, you seemingly imply I9 is no longer ignore-able (owing to I11 LOS having been lost?).

The way A10.51 is written, a unit allowing ignoring of a hex has to be Known, but unlike routing toward KEUs where the condition is either currently Known or Known at some point during this rout, ignoring due to Known unit does not mention units seen during the rout but no longer in LOS. The two are different; one uses memory, the other does not.

I could imagine this being overturned in a q&a, i.e. that what is ignorable is based both on current LOS and on memory, but I could also imagine it being sustained as it seems to be written. I would give it 60-40 likely sustained, but that is merely my guess.

While in H9 (w/I11 back in LOS and thus Known -- again) I9 (initially ignore-able, owing to I11) is no longer ignore-able (even though it was at the beginning)?

While in H9 the broken unit has no reason to re-figure its rout. If it had a reason to re-figure its rout then I9 would be ignorable, but it can't start the re-figuring process. Re-figuring is not something that can be done whenever you want. You have to be prevented from reaching your previously designated rout target to re-figure. The q&a you give below says that.

title: Pin task check

PTCs do not have any "special values." There is no odd thing that happens if you roll two, twelve or equal to the morale level [EXC: Booby Traps B28.9].

title: Desperation Morale
question: What does "taking the possibility of cowering into account" mean in rule 10.62 ?
author: Mongoose56
consensus_answer:
What does "taking the possibility of cowering into account" mean in rule 10.62 ? 
Take all thirty-six possible DRs, from 1,1 to 6,6. Look up the result on the IFT for that FP (applying the DRM for the attack) for all the thirty-six DRs. If a particular DR is a doubles, and the attack might cower, use the result from the IFT column for the cower, not the original IFT column. At the end of the exercise you will have thirty-six possible results. If any of them is a NMC or better, the broken unit is marked with a DM.

As a practical matter it is sufficient to look at the result on a DR of three if the attack can cower or on a DR of two if the attack can't cower. If the result is a NMC or better, broken units will be marked DM by the attack.

In both cases this is regardless of the actual IFT DR.

Yes, consider all DRMs, etc.  Like the one example up-thread ... a 4 FP attack at +3 DRM (regardless of where that DRM comes from ... TEM, the firer being CX, Hindrance DRMs, etc) would result in DM because a dr of 3 on the 4 FP column would be 3+3 = 6 and a 6 is a NMC.

A 4 FP attack with a +4 DRM (say into a wooden building for +2 TEM, but through a +2 smoke hindrance) would /not/ generate DM unless the unit was immune to cowering, since a dr of 2 would cower, resulting in a 2 FP attack and a 6 on the '2 column' is a PTC. As a practical matter it is sufficient to look at the result on a DR of three if the attack can cower or on a DR of two if the attack can't cower. If the result is a NMC or better, broken units will be marked DM by the attack. 

THIS.  Just always look at what a '3' dr result would be (if the unit /may/ cower) or a '2' dr result would be (if the unit CANNOT possibly cower).  In all cases, if the result would be at least a NMC (** NOT ** just a PTC), then the fired upon unit(s) will be marked DM regardless of what you actually roll(ed).

THIS.  Just always look at what a '3' dr result would be (if the unit /may/ cower) or a '2' dr result would be (if the unit CANNOT possibly cower).  In all cases, if the result would be at least a NMC (** NOT ** just a PTC), then the fired upon unit(s) will be marked DM regardless of what you actually roll(ed).

This is not necessary. A DR of three never cowers. Even if the snakeeyes double-column cowers instead of single-column cowers, the result for three will always be on column. Because of the way the IFT is constructed if a single-cower on a two would still be a NMC (or better), a three will also be a NMC (or better).

It means that a no-result attack upon a Broken unit will never-the-less induce Desperation Morale if and only if it =might= have produced a NMC result on a better DR -- even if the shooter had Cowered on that better DR.

If the shooter is capable of Cowering, and if the only possible NMC DR result would have been a Cower roll for that shooter, then Desperation morale would =not= be induced by the no-result attack.
And if Chuck Norris was involved, the unit suffers DM no matter what.  Don't even roll.

yes it can. the woods rises to level 1. the units are at level 1. It's the same as open ground at level 0, which rises to level 0, and the firing targets units at level 0 can see each other. The situations are geometrically congruent.

Which is to say, if the ground is level 0, the woods will be an obstacle up to level 1.

This takes some mental reorientation to understand, but once you get it, it'll be automatic. Level 1 obstacle = you must be this tall (level 1) to see over this rid...er, obstacle.

It doesn't refer to the height of the obstacle as much as it refers to the level you have to be on to see over it (blind hexes notwithstanding).

Remember, that ASL exists in a 'pancake' world.  So a level one obstacle is a perfectly flat pancake that goes from 0 up to 1.0, but not 1.01 or higher.  Two units both at level 1.0 would see each other, just the same as two units as level 0.0 would see each other with only 0.0 level terrain in between.

The trickier part is that a unit at level 1 can NEVER see over a level 1 obstacle at a unit at level 0, again, because the ASL world is seen as 'pancakes'.  Level 1.0 /can/ see over level 0.5 (hedges, walls) to fire at units at level 0 ... but otherwise, level 1 units do not gain a tremendous amount of LOS from being at level 1.  Level 2 is the magic level where you start to /really/ can visibility, as you can now see over level 1.0 obstacles (though blind hexes, etc. need to be worried about).

title: Assault movement
question: If a squad with a leader declare assault movement and the squad attempts to place smoke before moving and the die roll comes up six,does the leader have to end it's move too?
author: JTV656
consensus_answer:
If a squad with a leader declare assault movement and the squad attempts to place smoke before moving and the die roll comes up six,does the leader have to end it's move too?
No, the dr of 6 only affects the unit that rolled it [A24.1]. There could be many squads moving as a stack, all trying to place smoke grenades at the same time; only those that roll "6" will end their MPh.

The MF expense to place the smoke would be shared by the stack, though, I believe. 
Correct; all MF expenses spent by some member of a stack are expended by all members of the the stack. You can't have a stack where individual units have spent different amounts of MF (or MP in, for example, a multi-hex stack using Platoon Movement, although the MF and MP spent for a stack that includes vehicles and infantry might be different). As more examples, if one member of a stack places a DC or recovers a SW, etc., all members of the stack spend the required MF.

Different things can be done by different stack units on some same stack MF expenditure.

E.g, for 1 MF, a stack of 2x squads A & B, say, could concurrently attempt a Smoke grenade in hex (by A) and, say, attempt recovery of an unpossessed weapon (by B), all on that 1 MF stack expenditure.

The stack could divide, thereafter if, say, squad A 6-ed its Smoke dr.

title: Heroes
question: If a hero is created by a squad that's expended MFs,how many MFs does the newly created hero have? Does the hero have 6MF still to use or is it considered to have used the same as the squad?
author: JTV656
consensus_answer:
If a hero is created by a squad that's expended MFs,how many MFs does the newly created hero have? Does the hero have 6MF still to use or is it considered to have used the same as the squad?
A15.21 "The hero shares the MMC's fire/movement status at the time of creation; i.e., if the MMC was marked with a Prep Fire or TI counter, so is the hero."

Presumably the "i.e." should have been, "e.g." Here is a q&a that gives some idea how the rule should be interpretted:
A4.5, A15.21 - A squad declares Double Time at the start of its MPh and thus has 6 MF. On the expenditure of its 3rd MF it is attacked by the enemy, triggering the creation of a Hero by Heat of Battle.

Is this hero CX?
A.Yes the Hero would also be CX.

Are the squad and the Hero considered to be moving as a stack despite the Hero being created after the start of the MPh of its parent unit?
A. Yes, they are considered to be moving as a stack.

Does the hero have left 4 MF (8 - 50% MF moved previously by the parent unit = 4 MF) or 5 MF (8 - 3 MF moved previously by the parent unit)?
A. 5 MF

title: Pinned for PAATC?
question:
Hello there!
During Advance Phase, an MMC advances against an AFV and, to do so must perform a PAATC. If the result of that PAATC is exactly the morale value. Is the PIN result applied to the MMC?
Thank you!
author: MikeMacCrego
consensus_answer:
During Advance Phase, an MMC advances against an AFV and, to do so must perform a PAATC. If the result of that PAATC is exactly the morale value. Is the PIN result applied to the MMC?
Pinning for rolling exactly the Morale Level is an effect of a Morale Check [A7.8], not a Task Check. For a TC the unit fails only if it rolls > the Morale Level [A10.1].

title: 22.612 vs ARMORED TARGETS - Residual FP
question:
We have just played the scenario Esprit Combatif and had a blast because the French threw endless molotovs at the German invaders. Two questions that came up repeatedly: When a French squad throws a MOL at an adjacent German CT tank with no vulnerable PRC and no accompanying infantry, can the firing unit choose to fire its inherent FP at the hex in order to leave residual FP? And if allowed, would the residual FP be halved because there is no vulnerable target?
As far as I understand the rules, the firing squad must use its FP because of Mandatory FG (mentioned explicitly in 22.611, last sentence).
author: Lebenslicht
consensus_answer:
But keep A9.52 in mind when spraying: the second hex will only get half as much residual FP, correct?
Correct. Which is why I mentioned having "enough FP." If you used spray fire from a LMG (four FP after doubling for PBF) against an adjacent vehicle the main attack will be at two FP (halved for spray fire), leaving one FP residual, and the second hex attack would be at one FP due to halving for no Known target, leaving no residual FP. A MMG (four FP) would leave two residual FP in the adjacent vehicle's hex and residual FP in the other hex.

title: 10.51 Rout Direction
question:
I have probably played this wrong for more than 30 years: The rules say: "...a routing unit must move to the nearest (in MF calculated at
the start of its RtPh) building or woods hex...". Can this be a hex to which the unit has no LOS? I cannot understand the design idea behind that.
author: Lebenslicht
consensus_answer:
I have probably played this wrong for more than 30 years: The rules say: "...a routing unit must move to the nearest (in MF calculated at
the start of its RtPh) building or woods hex...". Can this be a hex to which the unit has no LOS? I cannot understand the design idea behind that.
The rout target does not need to be in LOS.

My explanation is that the unit is somewhat aware of its position and surroundings on the battlefield. It has probably scouted the area the vicinity enough to know that there are a few buildings in that direction and a woods line in the other. In the game the unit may have moved in LOS of the hex that later becomes its target. So if you really, really want to be sure the rout is to a place the unit "knows about" (even disregarding hypothetical, extra-scenario scouting or movement) you would have to track every hex seen by every unit. That's a nightmare. And although you may envision the rout as a pell-mell, headlong flight, it could instead sometimes represent a more cautious and calculated movement, trying to find a place to regroup. Limiting the unit's knowledge, either past or future, to just what it has in LOS right this second is probably as bad a simulation, and possibly worse, as how the rules work.

As for what was in the mind of the designer,  we only can speculate.

author: MikeMacCrego
consensus_answer:
So if he abstains from rolling at all, it isn't a voluntary loss of Contact?
C1.22 (above) can be confusing owing to negatives therein.  [The OBA flowchart (excerpt below -- see right-hand tree) de-tangles this only a little]

If, disregarding SMOKE, he can =see= the SR but opts =not= to roll for Contact, then it =is= voluntary loss of Contact -- access is lost and "counters" (SR & Battery Access & Radio Contact) are removed -- end of Fire Mission, effectively.

If he =cannot= see it, then it =isn't= voluntary loss of Contact --  SR & Battery access counters remain -- though Radio Contact counter will be removed (implicit in C1.22 full text).

However, failing to roll for Contact/Maintenance is considered voluntary loss of Contact only if the Observer has no LOS to the SR's/FFE's Blast Height; 1.32).

If the Observer has LOS, then failing to roll is not "voluntary." If the Observer does not have LOS, then failing to roll *is* "voluntary." If the Observer is unable to roll (e.g. broken, radio malfunctioned), then that is also not voluntary loss of Contact.

title: Unit using Assault movement goes Berserk.. does it use the remaining MP to charge further than 1 location?
question:
Unit using Assault movement goes Berserk.. does it use the remaining MP to charge further than 1 location?

my immediate thought was it does, but I can't actually find it clearly stated in the rules.  A15.431 is clear on a moving unit using it's remaining MF (8MF - expended)
A unit which becomes berserk while still moving (i.e., not pinned or wounded) must use the remainder of its MPh to charge. The units MF allotment for the rest of that MPh is eight minus whatever MF it has already expended during that MPh.

A4.61 is the part that troubles me, since whilst it is clear that the FFNAM modifier is no longer applicable, it doesn't clearly state that move can be greater than 1 location.
author: Minedog3
consensus_answer:
As you have stated:
According to A15.431, a unit which becomes berserk while moving must use the remainder of it's MF to charge. So if you used 2 MF to Assault Move into the woods, then you must use the remaining 6 MF to charge etc etc.

Regarding the rule A4.61 for Assault Movement, once the unit has finished its one hex move, it has been attacked and gone berserk etc. is no longer limited by the rule for Assault Movement.

The point is that you have completed the one hex Assault Move for <4 MF, then gone Berserk and now you are off and running.

The point is that you have completed the one hex Assault Move for <4 MF, then gone Berserk and now you are off and running.

This got me thinking. What if you haven’t spent any MF yet? Do you have the full 8 MF for the charge? If, for example, a unit attempts to move into a hex and gets shot with a snapshot, have they expended any MF?

From A8.15:
"If affected by a Snap Shot, the moving unit is considered in the Location entered thereafter."
So given that the MF are considered expended when the move is declared, you would end up in the destination hex, berserk and charging with any remaining MF.

The only case I think of when a unit goes Berserk during their MPh without having spent a MF, would be if it is attacked by aircraft before it moved.
Otherwise, DFF always occurs on an MF being spent.
Can also happen if units are in a hex where a Sniper attack eliminated a leader and the they go Berserk when taking the LLMC.

title: Spotters and acquisition
question: If a squad whos a spotter for a mortar becomes broken, does the mortar lose acquisition if that  squad rallies?
author: JTV656
consensus_answer:
Yes.

In most cases, MTR Acquisition is lost when its Spotter is broken.

Easiest:  apply to the MTR Spotter all the Chap C divider Table C6.5 ACQUISITION LOSS triggers as though the Spotter were manning the MTR.  So, if the Spotter breaks, the MTR loses any acquisition dependent on that Spotter.

C9.31 example (last 3 lines): does this mean a spotter loses a mortar acquisition under all the loss conditions expressed in C6.5 (as
if it were firing the mortar itself), such as: interdicting, leaving present Location, etc.?
A. Yes.

Per table above, acquisition is lost if Gun manning Infantry is broken.  Per the Q&A, treat the Spotter as the manning Infantry in this regard.  Upshot:  if Spotter breaks, Acquisition is lost.

title: Three OBA questions.
question:
HI guys. I've reviewed several threads on these issues but I want to make sure I've understood them correctly. Could I get some confirmation on the following?

If accuracy isn't achieved, the AR can deviate by up to 6 hexes if that result is rolled on the white die. But if you later  try to Correct it, the maximum deviation is one hex for every three you modify it.

OBA FP isn't halved against HIP units. And somehow your opponent must inform you of the effects on it (e.g., if the unit is eliminated or must take an MC). Provided it's affected, of course.

If OBA scores a CH on a unit in Woods, does it receive both the -1 Airburst and the -1 TEM (for a total of -2)? And if the unit were in a Foxhole, would the total be -5? Or does only the -1 Airburst apply?"

What if the CH was from a mortar on the board? Would it be -1 (airburst only), -2 (airburst+TEM), or -3 (airburst+Foxhole)?

Thanks in advance.
author: Pavlo
consensus_answer:
If accuracy isn't achieved, the AR can deviate by up to 6 hexes if that result is rolled on the white die. But if you later  try to Correct it, the maximum deviation is one hex for every three you modify it.
Technically the AR is placed first, accuracy is rolled and and if not accurate, based on the Extent-of-Error DR the resulting SR or FFE is placed relative to the AR, i.e. the AR is not moved. Purely a technical point; you can move the AR then place the SR/FFE on it if you like with little harm.
OBA FP isn't halved against HIP units. And somehow your opponent must inform you of the effects on it (e.g., if the unit is eliminated or must take an MC). Provided it's affected, of course.
Correct, but this is not special for OBA. You can fire against HIP units too with IFT fire or ordnance fire, and your opponent has to evaluate the effects.
If OBA scores a CH on a unit in Woods, does it receive both the -1 Airburst and the -1 TEM (for a total of -2)? And if the unit were in a Foxhole, would the total be -5? Or does only the -1 Airburst apply?"
Only positive TEM are reversed [C3.71] (with certain exceptions, e.g. pillbox); negative TEM still apply normally. So an air burst is just -1. A CH against a foxhole would have a -5 DRM. 
What if the CH was from a mortar on the board? Would it be -1 (airburst only), -2 (airburst+TEM), or -3 (airburst+Foxhole)?
Using the same principles, the DRM is -3.

title: HIP to Concealed.

title: Off-board setup and right of inspection
question:
Assume player A sets up all units on the board, and player B sets up all units off-board to enter on turn 1.

I have always played this so that both players set up everything concealed, meaning neither player sees anything except stacks with "?" at any point.

My opponent argues that, based on the way the rules are written, the player setting up off-board must place their units first without concealment. Then, after player A has seen their setup (basically, the counters on top of each stack), they may place "?" markers on top of everything.
author: norev
consensus_answer: My "as written" read would be that standard setup is performed for reinforcements, just like pre-game setup. The first player sets up his reinforcements on "any randomly chosen unused board(s)" [A2.51]. The opposing player now places his scheduled reinforcements on similar unused boards, perhaps the same ones depending on scenario instructions. The free concealment counters are now placed. If only one side sets up on those unused boards, free "?" counters are placed by that side without the second side being able to see the stacks unconcealed [A12.12].

title: Advance phase and foxholes
question: Can a squad advance into an adjacent hex and into a foxhole in the same move?
author: JTV656
consensus_answer:
Can a squad advance into an adjacent hex and into a foxhole in the same move?
As previous, yes. Outside and inside the foxhole are the same Location for movement purposes [B27.13], so you aren't moving more than one Location. You can even move from IN a foxhole out, into the next hex then IN a foxhole in that hex. A downside is that if the cost to move between hexes is two or greater (e.g. brush, woods) or if the unit possesses more than its IPC it may be an Advance vs. Difficult Terrain [A4.72].

title: Disclosure of artillery set-up in buildings
question: For small target AT gun (C2.271) (B23.423):  Is its occupation of a ground floor building hex made known at the moment an enemy unit can see that hex? ….. or can the disclosure be delayed until the gun opens fire at a target
author: Pushofpike
consensus_answer:
For small target AT gun (C2.271) (B23.423):  Is its occupation of a ground floor building hex made known at the moment an enemy unit can see that hex? ….. or can the disclosure be delayed until the gun opens fire at a target
A HIP Gun in concealment terrain (which includes buildings) is not revealed on LOS to that Location [A12.34]. It is placed on board if it fires, but also if its crew performs an action (e.g. place a Starshell). Changing CA is concealment loss in LOS, and would require the Gun to be put on board even if not in LOS.

Note that HIP *is* lost (replaced with concealment) on LOS if the Gun is set up in non-concealment terrain.

author: Pavlo
consensus_answer:
BTW how can there be more than one vehicle in one location?

Section A5 gives Stacking limit explanations. A5.2 states the restriction on the number of vehicles that can occupy a Location as one without any penalties. D2.14 allows the player to move vehicles into other vehicle/wreck occupied locations but with additional MP costs and A5.132 how firing into a multiple vehicle location is handled.

title: Half squads
question: If a half squad has two MG's in its possession and first fires with one of the MG's and it malfunctions,can it then SFF with the other MG?
author: JTV656
consensus_answer:
A7.35 "Usage limitations for each type of SW are listed on the SW Chart." Per note B, which applies to halfsquads and crews, "B. May fire one SW but at cost of inherent FP." This unfortunately is murky as to its exact meaning because of SFF & FPF. However it is generally understood that once a halfsquad uses a SW during a player turn, it may use no other, although, depending on the type of SW it used, it can switch to its inherent instead for SFF & possibly for FPF. 

EX: a halfsquad fires a BAZ as first fire. It also possesses a LMG. It can now fire its inherent as SFF & FPF. It can't use the LMG for SFF/FPF.
EX: a halfsquad fires a MMG as first fire. It also possesses a LMG. It can now fire its inherent as SFF (or it could use the MMG), but it *must* use the MMG for FPF. It can't use the LMG for SFF/FPF, even if the MMG malfunctions. If the MMG malfunctions the halfsquad can use its inherent for FPF.

A7.352 & A8.4 1) A HS fires its PSK in the MPh and is marked with a First Fire counter. In the DFPh, may that HS attempt a PF shot vs. an ADJACENT vehicle? A. No, per the SW Chart, a HS can only fire one SW.
2) Is the answer any different if the HS had fired its Inherent FP in the MPh, instead of the PSK? A. No. 
See the q&a compilation for more similar fragments of the principles. 

This is a subject that could use some cleanup. It is possible this has not addressed because of fear of breaking it. It may also be that everyone who should be considering rewriting the rules here has so internalized the principles that they don't realize the need.

title: Stuka point attack and ?
question: Does a Stuka making a point attack that automatically Pins its target also result in automatic Loss of Concealment (if in los of enemy) for that target?"
author: adolfinger
consensus_answer:
Does a Stuka making a point attack that automatically Pins its target also result in automatic Loss of Concealment (if in los of enemy) for that target?"
No. A unit has to be affected by a PTC result to lose concealment. A Pin caused by a Stuka is not a PTC. 

q&a:
E7.403 The Stuka conducted its first MG attack vs two concealed units (only one which is moving), and the DR was a 9 (5,4). Rule E7.403 states my units which were attack by the Stuka in the hex become pinned. Does the MG attack both of my units or just the one who moved? Does a Concealed unit which becomes pinned due to the first MG attack during a Point Attack from a Stuka lose its Concealment automatically or only if an enemy ground unit has a LOS to the just attacked unit? If the answer to Q2 is the unit retains its Concealment because no enemy ground unit has a LOS to it, is the unit considered Concealed or unconcealed for the second MG Point Attack (and any Bomb attack)?
A. Both. The automatic Stuka pinning does not cause Concealment loss. A PTC result or better on the attack would cause Concealment loss if in LOS of enemy ground unit. The status does not change from the first attack to the second. (If in open ground, the target might be treated as unconcealed.)

title: Bocage and setup
question:
I have 2 questions regarding: Bocage and setup:

Just to be sure I understand B9.55 correct

1) If opposing side enters entirely from offboard, can I set up Dummies in non-conclement terrain if they have WA over a Bocage hexside?

2) Can units set up HIP in open terrain if they have WA over a Bocage hexside?
author: Nslcole
consensus_answer:
1) If opposing side enters entirely from offboard, can I set up Dummies in non-conclement terrain if they have WA over a Bocage hexside?

2) Can units set up HIP in open terrain if they have WA over a Bocage hexside?
Correct on both in concept. Note that in the first case the unit does not actually have to have WA, only that it's possible it could. For example Dummies could set up in graveyard (non-concealment terrain but with +1 TEM) HIP as if in concealment terrain if one or more of the hexsides are bocage. The first should perhaps be stated as, "Dummies may set up as if in Concealment Terrain if it could claim WA over bocage," but that is a quibble with your phrasing.

Also note that the HIP in the second case is a weaker form of HIP in that if at any time during the game a GO enemy unit has LOS through a non-bocage hexside, the HIP unit is put on board concealed.

title: Fire Group and vehicle
question: If an infantry unit is in the same location as an armed vehicle that is not a halftrack or a carrier, they cannot form a Mandatory Fire Group. Therefore, each unit fires separately on the same enemy unit's movement. Correct?
author: runrun
consensus_answer:
If an infantry unit is in the same location as an armed vehicle that is not a halftrack or a carrier, they cannot form a Mandatory Fire Group. Therefore, each unit fires separately on the same enemy unit's movement. Correct?
Correct. A7.55:
 If units/weapons capable of forming a FG with each other in the same Location are going to fire at the same target (i.e., at both the same Location and the same unit and the same "simultaneous" [8.1] MF/MP expenditure; see D3.5) during the same phase they must form a FG.
If the units/weapons are not capable of forming a fire group then mandatory FG does not apply and they may fire separately. Note that the phrase regarding capability to form a fire group was inserted as an erratum from Journal 13.

title: MPs spent for non-stopped TCA changes
question:
D2.17 DELAY: The expenditure of MP without moving is termed Delay and can be used only while the vehicle is stopped or using platoon movement (14.21). ...

D3.12: ... The TCA may change as a result of firing ... or at the end of any friendly fire phase ... The TCA may also change freely with each MP expended during the MPh. The TCA change must be announced as the MP are expended but can coincide with MP expended for movement, stop, start, or Delay purposes; i.e., the MP cost for a TCA change is not in addition to other MP expenditures.

A non-stopped AFV expends some MPs to move into a new hex/hexside. The AFV, now wishing to burn a few MPs, announces some pointless TCA changes for 1 MP each but without changing its VCA or entering a new hex/hexside. Is this permitted? E.g., the AFV is still non-stopped but the chassis wouldn't be changing VCA or traveling forward as these postulated TCA-change MPs are expended.

(I know a vehicle can announce it is expending more MPs than required to enter a new hex, D2.18, but that doesn't seem applicable to this situation.)
author: BillNC
consensus_answer:
As per previous the TCA change is done in conjunction with some other expenditure. It is not an expenditure in itself. However changing VCA *is* an expenditure in itself, and the "traditional" way to burn MP (besides expending more MP than necessary or stopping and delaying, etc.) is to change VCA over and over. There is a risk that you change your VCA from front to side to a threat, so watch out. You also can't do this in bypass.

This is by official rule.  Or you can play with laid back people who just say "Sure, you can retro your initial movement into the hex to expend the extra MPs and do you TCA upon entry of the hex."  It all depends on how competitive you want to be (though if you ever go to tournaments, it would be strongly recommended to stick closely to the exact written rules ...).

My group is full of 50+ Grognards who don't have infinite free time and are in it for a combination of competitiveness, comradery, and catching up with each other ... so we couldn't care less if you asked to 'correct' your MP expenditure, even if we had declared fire on the vehicle, etc.  It's a game, after all ... it's about enjoying the time playing and feeling like you beat your opponent through your skill (read: VASL dice gods), not through a minor-speed-of-play issue (read: we do this to also prevent people from spending 15 minutes trying to think out their entire movement as these minor oopsies are easy to 'fix' ...  but we don't generally allow things like completely re-doing a movement from multiple hexes back, etc.).

Ok... we're rusty and trying to work our way back into knowing the rules after a long hiatus from play.

Playing T3 Ranger Stronghold and have the following situation (US Prep Fire):

The US 747 in K1 fires at the German tank that is immobilized in K4.  The tank's VCA is facing J3/J4 and the TCA is facing J4/K5.

A turret hit is rolled and the TK roll was a '9'.

First, the CA of the tank is the side/rear, so we look at the 3 armor, but a turret hit means that (due to superior turret) it becomes a '4'.
But because its actually the REAR target facing of the TURRET, the TK# goes from 13 to 14 (+1 TK# due to Rear Target Facing).

So when we compare the '9' (die roll) + '4' (superior turret armor) versus the TK3 ('13' base +1 for rear), we end up with a roll of '13' versus a total TK# of '14', meaning the tank is eliminated.

Did we do this correctly or did we mess up with the different VCAs, etc.?

author: kbernatz
consensus_answer:
Yes.  Rear from 4 to 3 Armor.  Hit with a TK roll of 9, 13-3= 10 TK.  No height restrictions as its not a mighty PIAT!

C3.9  LOCATION OF VEHICULAR HITS: It is often necessary to know the location of a hit vs a vehicular target in order to determine the correct AF (or in the case of a HD target, whether a hit has been scored at all). An ordnance hit vs a vehicle strikes its turret/upper-superstructure Aspect (as opposed to its hull Aspect) if the colored dr of the Original TH DR is < the white dr [EXC: A CH vs a HD target is always considered to occur vs the turret/upper-superstructure, and can occur on an Original 2 TH DR; 3.7]. title: Follow-Up Attacks, MF spent, and Defensive Fire
question:
Trying to learn the full game (coming from SK) - In the spirit of trying to read what the rules say and not interpret them, I understand the following in A8.14:  if a broken or pinned unit spent at least 2 MF, it can be attacked again (follow-up attack).  A8.3 says that a unit cannot be fired upon more times than the MF spent.

Here are my questions:  

A8.14 discusses broken or spent units but based upon A8.3, units that spend 2 or more MF (it doesn't say good order or broken) could still be fired upon.  Is a "follow-up attack" different than Subsequent First Fire?  I'm not sure I'm understanding if there's a difference between the two rules given that A8.14 mentions broken/spent units specifically.

Also, I'm assuming (I hope safely) that a unit that moves through grain (at 1.5 MF) isn't subject to SFF because they haven't spent 2 or more MF (since FRD should apply).  So, if a unit moved only hex and it was a grain hex (in season, of course), only one defensive fire attempt could be made against it.

Hope all that was clear.  Thanks.
author: Baetis
consensus_answer:
A8.14 discusses broken or spent units but based upon A8.3, units that spend 2 or more MF (it doesn't say good order or broken) could still be fired upon.  Is a "follow-up attack" different than Subsequent First Fire?  I'm not sure I'm understanding if there's a difference between the two rules given that A8.14 mentions broken/spent units specifically.

SFF is an mode of attack based on the attacker's state. A unit or MG/IFE that is marked with a First Fire counter can use SFF (subject to all the limitations for SFF of course) [A8.3]. Depending on previous history in the turn (e.g. the DEFENDER had fired on other targets prior to this one or had fired on this target on a different expenditure) the first attack against a particular target on this expenditure might be SFF.

The possibility of follow-up attacks are based on the MF spent by the moving unit and are independent of whether SFF is used. If a moving infantry unit moved into brush up a hill (four MF) and the DEFENDER fired a MG, if the DEFENDER was lucky with ROF none of the attacks would be SFF. If the MG was unlucky with ROF the first attack might be First Fire, the second might be SFF and (if the DEFENDER were ADJACENT) the remaining two attacks would be FPF. 

The two are only indirectly related, and then only by normal play, not by rules. A SFF attack might or might not be a follow-up attack. A follow-up attack might or might not be SFF. Often a follow-up attack will be SFF, but that is only because inherent FP doesn't get ROF and ROF from MGs is more likely to fail than not.

Also, I'm assuming (I hope safely) that a unit that moves through grain (at 1.5 MF) isn't subject to SFF because they haven't spent 2 or more MF (since FRD should apply).  So, if a unit moved only hex and it was a grain hex (in season, of course), only one defensive fire attempt could be made against it.

Correct, unless there was some other reason the MF were increased, e.g. gaining elevation, entering concealment terrain at night, etc.

Not sure what you are saying here. The paragraph addresses various forms of multiple attacks against a single unit. These might be repeated attacks by a single fire group or they might be different attacks by different fire groups. These combinations are both lumped together in this paragraph.

The bit that threw me was that the rule specifically identified a target type - broken or pinned units. It makes it sound like follow up attacks aren't allowed on units that weren't affected by an initial attack. 

A8.14 A unit broken or pinned by Defensive First Fire can be fired on again in its current Location by other same-phase Defensive First Fire attacks, but is attacked in its broken or pinned state. A unit that survives a Defensive First Fire attack with no effect can be fired on again in that same Location during its MPh before expending additional MF/MP, but only by different attackers or if it expended at least two MF/MP in that Location (see 9.2). 
If you read this carefully you will see that two different things are being discussed in the two sentences. The first sentence is about the state of the target for attacks that occur after the target has been been broken/pinned. The moving unit is attacked by the DEFENDER on its first MF (and in this sentence it may be the only MF spent), and is broken or pinned. Another unit can fire on that first MF spent but the unit now considered broken or pinned (which, for instance cancels assault move for broken and FFMO/FFNAM for pinned). It might also be fired on by the same DEFENDER for the second of two MF spent, and again is now in its new state. The first sentence says that the target's state is its current state, regardless of how many MF were spent and regardless of how many DEFENDERs fire on it. This sentence can apply even when the moving unit spent only one MF because there could be multiple DEFENDERs attacking on that expenditure. The second sentence is discussing more attacks by a unit that already attacked on this expenditure. Such a unit can make more attacks against the same expenditure only if ≥ two MF have been spent in the expenditure.
For example, two British units fire on a moving German unit (who spends 2 MF) and the first attack has no effect. The German is still Good Order. Since he spent 2 MF (and assuming no other closer unit) SFF would be allowed. But the follow-up attack rule (A8.14) seems to suggest that the additional attacks aren't allowed because the unit wasn't broken or pinned by the initial attack. 
The is applying the first sentence in a wrong way. The squads fire on the first MF of two. The moving unit can be attacked again, either by the same unit(s) (by the second sentence on its second MF) or by other DEFENDERs on its first MF of the expenditure. By the first sentence the unit would be in its new state if that state changed, regardless of whether the follow-up attack were from the same DEFENDER on the second MF or from different DEFENDERs on the first MF.

Note that the order of follow-up attacks on any given expenditure need not be in any particular sequence. If a moving unit spends two MF in a single expenditure DEFENDER fire groups A & B could attack A-B-A-B, A-B-B-A or even A-A-B-B. In the last case (A-A-B-B) if the moving unit is broken by the second "A" attack it is attacked as broken by the first "B" attack. The sequence is as performed by the player, and there is no trying to reconcile the different "MF spent" into their "actual sequence."

title: When KW steep hills are in play, wounded SMC are always subject to the MF costs?
question: Per W1.34 any Infantry portaging ≥ its IPC is subject to extra costs for crossing a steep hill crest line. Wounded SMC have 0PP IPC [A17.2], so a wounded SMC would seem always to be portaging ≥ its IPC (unless one of the exceptions in W1.34 apply). Does that sound correct?
author: jrvjrv
consensus_answer: While composing my q&a I looked at W1.34 more carefully. It says, "The following apply to an Infantry unit/stack entering a Steep Hills hex if any unit is carrying ≥ its IPC (A4.42)." I still plan to q&a this, but I now lean toward saying as written a wounded or CX SMC will pay the extra MF costs for KW Steep Hills.

title: Red barricades factory AFV entrance
question:
If I've got this right, a fully-tracked AFV entering a Gutted Factory hex in RB via a vehicular-sized entrance pays 1/4 MP ( for the Debris). It takes a Bog Check with a +1 DRM for Debris (and potentially another +1 for Ground Pressure). Correct?
​Conversely, if the factory were non-gutted, would the entrance hex be considered Open Ground for the initial entry, with Bog Checks only applying if the vehicle continues deeper into the building?
author: adolfinger
consensus_answer:
I believe an AFV entering a gutted factory via a vehicular-sized entrance is subject to a +1 Bog DRM for debris plus another +1 Bog DRM for factory hex ( probably also ground pressure ) because the benefit of treating the entrance as Open Ground is negated if the entrance is roofless, as per my understanding of B23.742.
There is a somewhat-related q&a:

B23.1, O1.2, O5.42 - In Red Barricades what is the MP cost for a fully tracked vehicle to enter a roofless factory hex from outside of the factory? Note this is not a VSE. Is it ½ of its MP for entering a building, ¼ of its MP for entering debris, or ¾ of its MP for entering a building and entering debris?
A. One-half of its MP.

The person who asked apparently thinks that a vehicle-sized entrance makes a difference because such a hex was excluded from the question. If being a vehicle-sized entrance is different then the cost to enter a vehicle-sized entrance hex would be ¼ MP allotment because for movement purposes the hex still uses Open Ground MP costs as its base. I don't see any rule that says that a vehicle-sized entrance becomes an ordinary factory hex if it is filled with debris due to being roofless, so I would be inclined to say that it does not become an ordinary factory hex. Unfortunately the answer to the q&a does not cover what happens to a vehicle-sized entrance in a roofless factory, so it sounds necessary to request another q&a for that case.

title: quick summary of Journal 16 rules changes: VBM related
question:
This is a quick summary and comments on the rules changes in ASL Journal 16 related to VBM.

1) The most important is that a vehicle (in bypass) has to be in the same Location to invoke A7.212. Being at ground level but subject to TPBF from an upper level no longer does. This of course usually prevents/ends firelanes from the ground-level Location but at least allows DFF from the upper levels until ROF runs out. 
2) Ending the MPh in bypass no longer automatically strips concealment of DEFENDERs in the ground-level obstacle Location. Instead passing a PAATC will allow units in the bypassed obstacle to keep concealment [A12.42]. 
3) Regular ambush CC DRM is now in addition to street fighting ambush DRM rather than in lieu of it [A11.8].

The first still leaves the bypass vehicle as the closest enemy unit and so prevents SFF/FPF out of the hex even from upper levels. In addition if the hex is a single-hex, multi-level building the upper levels will be subject to upper-level encirclement by the appearance of a vehicle in bypass at ground level. The second fixes a strange rule that always left me scratching my head. It was never clear (to me at least) why a vehicle in bypass automatically stripped concealment when one in-hex did not. Although the third sounds impressive, unless infantry advance in there won't be ambush rolls (unless a HIP unit turns up) [A11.4].
author: jrvjrv
consensus_answer:
Thoughts on changes to tactics:

If the DEFENDER is at ground level, VBM freeze works as it always did during that first MPh, with the exception of additional risk to to vehicle due to the street fighting DRM counting for CC-RF for SFF & FPF. I suspect I played this point wrong (but in line with the Journal 16 changes) so for me it does not change my calculus. If you played this correctly it does increase the importance of minimizing your exposure by making sure you spend the fewest MP possible in the DEFENDER's hex by bleeding off MP prior to entry of VBM. But that was probably true before the Journal 16 because if you didn't then by the D2.4 requirement to spend all MP if possible the bypassing vehicle might have to stop in-hex in order to Delay [D2.17] (making it Stopped and thus even more vulnerable to CC-RF), continue bypass or overshoot the bypass hex and be required to exit.

If the DEFENDER is on an upper level, VBM freeze is no longer possible. DFF from upper levels is now allowed even though there is a TPBF opportunity to ground level. The best a bypassing vehicle can do in such a situation is restrict SFF & FPF by being the closest (zero-hex range) enemy target. This is not a bad thing to do but it does allow an upper-level DEFENDER to use all its non-SFF/FPF fire, including ROF, outside its own hex even if there is an enemy vehicle in bypass at ground level.

This in turn suggests some changes to play. First against an upper-level DEFENDER the ATTACKER might consider delaying moving into the hex in bypass until after the the DEFENDER has become marked with a First-Fire counter. The DEFENDER is going to be able to fire outside the hex anyway, and those attacks may have a result that eliminates the need to freeze (now with "SFF freeze") the DEFENDER. The DEFENDER may cower, or it may malfunction its MG, etc. That would leave the ATTACKER free to use the vehicle that was held back for "SFF freeze" for other purposes. Plus because the DEFENDER would now be marked with a First-Fire counter, its FP would now be halved and the risk from fire from above would be reduced. CT AFVs can perform "SFF freeze" while BU, which reduces the risk to them from small arms/MGs to zero if they wait until the DEFENDER is marked with a First-Fire counter. If the situation allows it, the ATTACKER might consider moving to range one rather than in bypass at range zero. This will still "SFF freeze" an upper-level DEFENDER for ranges > one, plus for OT AFVs may avoid the risk of being treated as an unarmored vehicle [D5.311] even to the point of allowing them to BU (but note that an OT AFV is still vulnerable as a soft vehicle at range one against a DEFENDER at level two).

Alternately the ATTACKER might enter bypass of the hex before the upper-level DEFENDER is marked with a First-Fire counter and try for a vehicular Smoke dispenser. Vehicles with high Smoke Dispenser usage numbers in most cases should be able to nullify an upper-level DEFENDER nearly as effectively as VBM freeze. When shrouded in Smoke the DEFENDER no longer qualifies for FFMO and gets the extra hindrance for firing out of Smoke at level one (or level zero). At level two the DEFENDER won't be firing out of Smoke but will still be firing through Smoke to lower levels. Even if the vehicle doesn't have a high (or even any) Smoke Dispenser usage number it can try to Vehicular Smoke Grenades [D13.35] for the same effect. If Smoke is successfully placed the vehicle might then move on to do other things, including BFF at other enemy units. If not the ATTACKER has the option of either remaining in-hex (subject to figuring out how to spend the remainder of its MPs per D2.4) or try again with another vehicle if available.

q&a:
A9.21 A SW MMG/HMG on the upper level of a building fires at a unit in bypass of that building. A9.21, “If it fired up or down a stairwell within its same hex, its CA is defined vertically and subsequent shots during that phase (other than vs its own Location) are limited to the same direction up or down the staircase.” Is firing at a unit in bypass considered firing down a staircase? Is its field of fire restricted to down in the same hex? Assuming not, could the MG choose to have its field of fire point down the staircase in its hex?
A. No to those three questions.
Must the MG’s field of fire that includes the hexside being bypassed? If a MG has its field of fire already restricted to a non-vertical direction, may it fire down at a unit in bypass of that hex if the hexside bypassed is in the field of fire?
A. Yes to these two questions.

If you do have a situation with an upper-level DEFENDER where you want to "SFF freeze" it, and the DEFENDER has a weapon (e.g. MMG, HMG) that is Field-of-Fire-restricted [A9.21], you should probably consider where possible using VBM on a hexside that will prevent the weapon from using DFF in the direction you want to mask. If the upper-level DEFENDER fires at the bypass vehicle it is now Field-of-Fire frozen. If it does not fire your situation is no worse than it was before.

VBM freeze against upper-level DEFENDERs was omni-directional (unless the DEFENDER eliminated the bypass vehicle), but now there is a directional consideration.

title: bump scouting from foxholes
question:
I just noticed something about the recent rules changes that I think will be a neat new tactic. Per a recent q&a a unit in a foxhole that assault moves out to an ADJACENT Location using a combined expenditure into an enemy unit is A12.15 pushed back INTO the foxhole with no opportunity for the enemy to fire while out of the foxhole. Assume a CPVA unit has gotten adjacent concealed, and because of previous fire your unit in the foxhole is not concealed. You are rightly concerned about the ambush next turn. You can fire (here at six FP, add one if night), but that does not guarantee a result. Or you could instead bump-scout using a combined expenditure. That's guaranteed to strip concealment. The enemy can fire first of course (as DFF or DFPh) but you get the +2 TEM from the foxhole (+3 including night LV) and no FFMO or FFNAM. If the moving unit survives it can fire in the AFPh (using assault fire here) at the now-unconcealed unit. And you can use Opportunity Fire for units not actually performing the bump-scout.

This applies for a variety of nationalities, not just the CPVA and Americans I show here. I use them as example because I am in the middle of 210 "This Is Where We Stand", with the CPVA pushing up the hill against my Americans. The Good Order CPVA are all stealthy [W7.9], so avoiding ambush is a really good idea. Of course if the concealed target has more than one unit you might not strip concealment from all units, and if the target is a dummy, you might be in an awkward position after the move.
