title: isolated areas and Front Line hexes in a CG
question:
Does an isolated hex or group of hexes have Front Line hexes?

I think "yes", but I would like more opinions.
author: mtrodgers99
consensus_answer:
For KGP a Front-Line hex is "A Setup-Area hex that shares one hexside with one hex of an enemy-Setup-Area/No-Man's-land/Uncontrolled-Territory hex" [KGP8.2]. This is independent of whether the hex is isolated or not in KGP, as is "Setup Area" [KGP8.2]. At least in KGP all setup areas would have one or more front-line hexes unless the setup area was the whole map. But your test rules set may be similar but not be exactly the same as KGP, and I can't say what is true in rules I don't have.

In contrast to KGP, in RF map-edge hexes are also front line locations. This, for instance, prevents mines from being placed on map edges.

title: Deep Stream - exit MF cost
question: An infantry unit enters a Deep stream at 4MF. Assuming it exits during the same movement phase into an open ground hex, is the total movement factor cost 6MF?
author: Bombadil929
consensus_answer:
An infantry unit enters a Deep stream at 4MF. Assuming it exits during the same movement phase into an open ground hex, is the total movement factor cost 6MF?
There is no additional cost to exit a deep stream, so whatever the normal cost to enter the adjacent hex is. That would typically be two MF to move to open ground up one level.

An infantry unit enters a Deep stream at 4MF. Assuming it exits during the same movement phase into an open ground hex, is the total movement factor cost 6MF?

Also, you don't combine the entry and exit MF in one blob.
They are separate expenses.

title: Close Combat and Concealed units
question:
Hello,
Can 2 enemy units concealed in the same hex and in the same location refuse to fight during de CC phase when no ambush occurs ? The defender may decline the combat but is the CC mandatory for the ATTACKER ?
Thank you for yourclarification.
author: runrun
consensus_answer:
At the end of a Zerker's charge and AFPh, attack " Survivors are not yet held in Melee, and the stack is marked with a CC counter to indicate this." (A15.432), which has a bearing on the APh, where units marked with a CC marker from advancing (A4.7 "...Infantry units which are neither broken, pinned, TI, nor marked with a CC counter may use the APh to move one hex...").
After the CCPh, A3.8 states : "Remove all TI/Pin counters. Flip CC counters over to Melee side or remove them." (ASOP confirms it : "8.31B ... Flip/remove CC, or retain/remove Melee, counter as appropriate.")
So, in the present case, you will remove the CC counter, as no Melee occurred.

There is no rule saying anyone has to attack, attacker or defender, concealed or unconcealed.

One can imagine a variety of situations where neither side would attack or where neither side could attack. Case 1: an unconcealed halfsquad advances on an unconcealed Panther G with a non-functioning CMG, primarily so the Panther can't fire out of the hex [A7.212]. Since there is no Melee (yet) the broken enemy unit may not Withdraw, nor may any unit attack. After their quiet CCPh a Melee forms.
Even a berserk unit is not *required* to attack by rule.

title: RR embankment
question: If a target is on a RR Embankment and your firing at it from two hexes away, does a wreck between the attacker and the target cause a +1 Hindrance?
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
We will need to make some assumptions to answer your question. Assumption 1: the unit firing is at level zero relative to a level ½ RR Embankment. Assumption 2: the wreck is either at level zero or level ½. If so then as above, F6.52, "A "half-level" Hindrance (as defined in 4.51), whether on a hillock or not, can affect LOS/LOF to/from/across a hillock hex only if both the firer's and target's elevations are within a half-level of, and the elevation of at least one of those units is ≤ that of, the Hindrance's Base Level." F4.51 says a wreck is a "half-level" Hindrance. With the two assumptions the wreck is within a half-level of that hindrance and also at least one of target or firer is ≤ the level of the hindrance.

If the assumptions are broken then the wreck may not be a hindrance. In particular if the firer is at level ½ (presumably also on the embankment RR, the wreck is at level zero and of course the target is still at level ½, the wreck is not a hindrance.

title: off board actions & fire lanes
question: sorry, been a long time. 1. can a squad try and place smoke grenades in hex it is about to enter on? 2. fire lanes have to leave the firing hex along middle of a hex side or along a hex spine, and have reach initial target hex on centre dot ? any help much appreciated
author: pedrosantos
consensus_answer:
sorry, been a long time. 1. can a squad try and place smoke grenades in hex it is about to enter on? 2. fire lanes have to leave the firing hex along middle of a hex side or along a hex spine, and have reach initial target hex on centre dot ? any help much appreciated
1. No. The only actions allowed by an off-board unit are deployment and movement [A2.52]. Furthermore there has to be LOS to place smoke grenades [A24.1, definition of ADJACENT] and that does not exist from offboard to on-board [A2.51].
2. Not clear what you are asking. I'll guess this as the answer: a firelane has to include the initial target hex, but the LOS to the initial target need not be directly on a hexspine nor out the center of a hexside, although such initial attack LOSes often will be. For instance in the A9.222EX the HMG fires on a unit entering BB5 and puts down the alternate grain firelane even though the initial LOS from Y6 to BB5 is neither down a hexspine nor directly through the center of a hexside. A firelane down a non-alternate hexgrain is more likely to have the initial attack trace its LOS through the hexside center, but again in the A9.222EX if the MMG is making its initial attack at a target using bypass of BB5 on the AA5 side, the MMG might trace its LOS to either of the vertices of the hexside instead of to the center.

title: Can a Pillbox setup HIP?

author: tobiwonknobi
consensus_answer: Additional: if a pillbox sets up HIP so do all its contents [B30.7]. That applies even in non-concealment terrain. A.5 ATTACK DRM: Whenever an attack is made against multiple defending units, if a modifier applies to some but not all of the defending units, that attack is made with only one DR by applying the appropriate DRM only to those units—thus getting two or more Final DR from the same Original DR. Conversely, whenever an attack is made by multiple attacking units/weapons, if a modifier applies to some, but not all, of the attacking units, it applies to the attack only if detrimental to the attacker. title: Mortar Fire - enemy is not in LOS
question:
A mortar fires at a multi story building hex. The only enemy infantry units in the hex are on level 1, which is not in the firer’s LOS. The spotter can see level 2 of the building but there are no enemy units on level 2.

Is it possible for the mortar to affect the units in level 1, besides a potential rubble result?
author: Bombadil929
consensus_answer:
I’m going with yes! For area fire units are not targets, the hex is, so C3.4 is moot and C3.33 applies. 
No. As Klas says. The firer has to hit something it *can* see (i.e. in LOS and not HIP but concealed ok) before it can hit something it can't see. And in fact it has to hit the hardest thing to hit it can see before it can hit something out-of-LOS.

There is one sort-of exception in that WP can *affect* a unit at ground-level even if it does not hit the hardest-to-hit-in-LOS target because the WP counter falls to the ground level [C8.52], and the WP NMC affects both units that are hit and also units where the WP counter is placed, hit or not [A24.31].

In the case described (LOS only to second level, only enemy unit on first level) firing WP ammo with ordnance would not affect anyone because there would be no out-of-LOS hits per C3.33 and because there was nobody at ground level., If there were also a unit at ground level then it would be affected by the placement of the WP counter per A24.31. If there were also a non-HIP unit or units at level two then there might be out-of-LOS hits per C3.33.

title: When does the Foxhole TEM come into play?
question:
Here's the situation:
German Squad Assault Moves into Open Ground in front of a Pinned American Squad in a Foxhole.  Pinned American Squad First Fires, inflicting a 1MC, which Assault Moving German Squad rolls Snakes, so HOB.  The rolls 11 on HOB roll, going Berserk.  Other Allied units firing have no further effect.  Berserk squad must now continue to move, no longer under the Assault move window, and has to enter the hex with the American Pinned Squad in a Foxhole, which it does for its 2nd MF.  Pinned American Squad Final Fires with TPB Fire with a -2DRM.  No effect.  Since the Berserk German Squad is already in the Hex, does he still have to spend another MF to get into the Foxhole?  If not, when he TPB Fires in the AFPh, would the Pinned American Squad get the +2 TEM of the Foxhole?
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
German Squad Assault Moves into Open Ground in front of a Pinned American Squad in a Foxhole.  Pinned American Squad First Fires, inflicting a 1MC, which Assault Moving German Squad rolls Snakes, so HOB.  The rolls 11 on HOB roll, going Berserk.  Other Allied units firing have no further effect.  Berserk squad must now continue to move, no longer under the Assault move window, and has to enter the hex with the American Pinned Squad in a Foxhole, which it does for its 2nd MF.  Pinned American Squad Final Fires with TPB Fire with a -2DRM.  No effect.  Since the Berserk German Squad is already in the Hex, does he still have to spend another MF to get into the Foxhole?

There are two questions there. Question 1: is the Berserk German squad *required* to spend another MF to enter the foxhole, or can it just end its MPh after entering the hex? The latter. The German unit has entered the Location with its target per A15.43 and so need not move farther. The foxhole is not a separate Location [B27.13]. Second question, in order to be entitled to the +2 TEM for the foxhole would the German unit have to explicitly expend an extra MF, or would it "fall into" the foxhole in the same way that units "fall into" shellholes? The former. Unlike shellholes units are not put under foxholes without expending an extra MF in the MPh, RtPh or APh [B27.4]. Since a berserk unit can't rout and can't rout or advance, it would have to move under the foxhole in the MPh. Side note: it would be subject to any residual FP from the TPBF attack it received.

Bonus question: can a berserk unit expend one MF to enter an entrenchment once it reaches its target Location? I believe so. There are q&a saying that it may not place smoke grenades but nothing saying that entering an entrenchment is not allowed.

 If not, when he TPB Fires in the AFPh, would the Pinned American Squad get the +2 TEM of the Foxhole?
The American squad would be entitled to the +2 TEM of the foxhole regardless of whether the German unit entered the foxhole with it or not.

OK.  So this also would mean, after the Berserk Squad first took a Residual FP for spending another MF getting into the Foxhole (presuming is would also now benefit from the Foxholes +2DRM), the allied Squad would be required to Final Protective Fire, correct?

But, the Berserk SQuad is not "required" to do this, correct?

OK.  So this also would mean, after the Berserk Squad first took a Residual FP for spending another MF getting into the Foxhole (presuming is would also now benefit from the Foxholes +2DRM), the allied Squad would be required to Final Protective Fire, correct?

No. Requirement to TPBF is only on a MMC *entering* the Location [A8.312]. Once the enemy unit is already in the Location there is no requirement to fire more because the enemy unit expends more MF. The DEFENDER could (at its option) DFF, including with FPF, but is not required to do so.

But, the Berserk SQuad is not "required" to do this, correct?
Correct. If the target had been in a different Location (e.g. an upper level of a building) that could be entered (e.g. not a pillbox) the berserk unit would have to move within the hex to enter the target Location, but once the berserk unit enters the Location with the target it is not required to move more.

title: Boxcars on a MC
question: Can't believe this has never happened in one of your games before, but my opponent believes differently.  According to A10.31, a unit that roles an Original 12 on a Morale Check, irregardless of a Leader Bonus and/or TEM, suffers a CR and possibly ELR, yes?
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
Can't believe this has never happened in one of your games before, but my opponent believes differently.  According to A10.31, a unit that roles an Original 12 on a Morale Check, irregardless of a Leader Bonus and/or TEM, suffers a CR and possibly ELR, yes?

Just to verify, we are talking MC and not Rally DR.

A10.31 "CASUALTY MC: If an unbroken Personnel unit rolls an Original 12 during a MC, it suffers Casualty Reduction and is broken (or eliminated if not subject to breaking) [EXC: A hero/berserk-leader is wounded and must add +1 to his Wound Severity dr as if already wounded (17.11); see G1.14 for Japanese squads]—after any unit Replacement which may also be required by ELR Failure (19.13). If a broken unit rolls an Original 12 during a MC, it is eliminated."

An unbroken Fanatic, eight ML MMC with a Good Order 10-3 leader that rolled an Original 12 on a NMC would become a broken halfsquad despite its final MC DR being ≤ its morale. In this particular case it would not ELR. A broken, Fanatic, nine ML on its broken side MMC with a Good Order 10-3 leader would be eliminated, again despite its final MC DR being ≤ its morale.

replies.body: Correct (though ELR only applies if the unit was not already broken).  If broken, this means an entire squad is usually eliminated (12 causes casualty reduction due to the '12' and then a failed MC while broken causes a second casualty reduction in most cases).

title: Concealment and CC
question:
Wow, my opponent and I are getting into some serious crazy stuff all of a sudden with this  Campaign game.  No sooner did I find out that Bombardments can level buildings (and kill everyone inside instantly), which just happened to my 8-0/Squad/MMG;-(.  Got the info about being in an adjacent Foxhole a day too late.  Luckily my guys in the Train Station survived in good order.

We started our 2nd day today live over VASL/Skype.  First turn done and Germans lost 2 Squads and an 8-0.  The Americans have lost 2 Squads, 2 half Squads, an MMG, a Mortar and an 8-0.  

My question comes from a CC in my first turn.  I advanced into a hex with a German Concealed half squad.  He chose not to attack back and stayed Concealed.  I therefore attacked at half FP, which ended up being 1:1, my squad being a 6-6-6.  I failed to cause any harm.  So if we are deciphering the rules correctly, we are not in Melee since he maintained Concealment and his half-squad can therefore either TPB Fire in his upcoming Prep Fire Phase, or leave the hex in his Movement Phase, correct?
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
I would have been only Pinned if the Wreck also added a +1;-)
Even if the wreck were available, i.e. the attacker were outside the Location, both wreck and shellholes are TEM, and TEM are not cumulative unless the hex is cumulative terrain per A2.4. One *could* imagine that Wrecks are cumulative but D9.3 says they are not, "This TEM is applicable only if the unit can claim no other positive TEM." So the the only difference between an in-Location attack like you had and an out-of-Location attack is that if elevation effects reduced the shellholes to zero TEM [B9.33; this is a rule that is not cross-referenced in shellholes, entrenchments and bridges but you should be aware of it], the out-of-Location attack would still be eligible for the +1 TEM for the wreck.

Is this correct?  That when the concealed unit drops concealment and fires, it isn't marked with a Melee marker after its fire?  Would this change if the target was not broken?

Is this correct?  That when the concealed unit drops concealment and fires, it isn't marked with a Melee marker after its fire?  Would this change if the target was not broken?
If there is an existing Melee involving other units, when the concealed unit drops its concealment it is in the Melee after whatever caused the concealment loss.  A11.15, "Upon losing its "?" such a unit in a Melee Location is immediately held in Melee." The cause for loss of concealment need not be making an attack (e.g. it could lose concealment due to an outside attack on the Location), but making an attack could do it.

If there is no existing Melee loss of concealment does not create one immediately. This is not one of the situations when a CC counter is placed, so the unit losing concealment by making an attack is free to advance out of the Location.

so many little periphery cases as a result of 'equational thinking'.  Not sure if that's a phrase, but I'm always amazed at the cases that result from putting 2-3-4 rules together in a specific situation and seeing the result explained by someone (like JRV) who knows the rules.  It's what makes ASL "the game"

One odd case for the existing Melee situation is when the only enemy units with LOS are the ones in the Melee. In that case making an attack does not cause loss of concealment (because the enemy unit causing loss of concealment has to be Good Order, i.e. not in Melee). The friendly concealed unit can fire into the Melee with TPBF but it won't lose concealment and so won't become embroiled in Melee. Of course this doesn't happen any more than once in every three or four games played.

title: LOS through smoke to higher levels
question: does the observer under smoke in oF5 have los to blast height ? mu guess is yes for the blast height rises to level 2 while the smoke rises ( from the hillock base ) to level 1,5.... if I correctly understand A24.4 and C1.32....
author: adolfinger
consensus_answer:
But doesn't hindrance affect only same level Los ? 
A24.2, "All Direct Fire and on-board mortar fire traced into, through, within, or out of (see 24.8) a SMOKE Location is affected by a Hindrance DRM." Note this is different from and overrides A6.7, "All same-level Direct Fire and spotting attempts traced through (not just into or out of) an effective LOS Hindrance hex are modified by a +1 DRM." Also in A24.4, "Conventional smoke is treated as a two level Hindrance to LOS and does not Hinder LOS occurring above that elevation." A two-level hindrance (from level zero) does not hinder that occurs entirely at level two, so squad A & squad C see each other the A24.4EX. In my mind I imagine SMOKE as rising to the ankles of units on level two, which lets me remember that fire at the same level would not be hindered but fire down from level two would be hindered.

One thing that is not well-explained is whether a between-levels LOS goes through a multi-level SMOKE Hindrance Location or not. I don't believe there is anything that spells this out but my understanding is that if turning the SMOKE into an obstacle would block LOS then the SMOKE is a hindrance. That covers most situations. It does leave the case where there is SMOKE starting from a level higher than the ground level, e.g. Drifting SMOKE or blaze/grenades in the upper level of a building but *not* SMOKE ammunition, grenades or blaze in a hex with a crest line. For same-level LOS or LOS from the base level of the SMOKE to a lower level it should be obvious whether the LOS is "beneath" the SMOKE but for LOS which starts higher than the base level of the SMOKE and ends lower I don't know of a rule that covers the situation in general. But it is rare to have SMOKE at an upper level in a hex but not at a lower level. There is this q&a:

A24.61 When applying the phrase in A24.61 that drifting smoke is “...never a Hindrance at levels below the Location of the original SMOKE source.” is it necessary that both the firer and target are below the location of the original SMOKE source? For example, assuming original SMOKE in 2L7 has dispersed and drifted to level 2 of 2M8 and 2N8, would fire from 2O8 to 2M10 be hindered by the smoke?
A. No. No. See the A24.61 Example and turn it upside down.

This covers one of the "easy" cases (LOS from the base level to a lower level), and although reassuring that nothing too crazy is going on it does not answer a more complicated question like 2P8 level three (SSR a building in the hex) to 2M9.

When a SMOKE source (ground-level blaze, primary SMOKE ammunition or grenade, but not Drifting SMOKE) is in a hex with a crest line B10.1 applies. The SMOKE rises from the lower elevation in the lower part of the hex and from the upper elevation in the higher part of the hex.

Also per C8.52 SMOKE ammunition which hits the upper level of a building but not the ground level (which presumably is masked or has hindrances that apply ), the SMOKE counter falls to ground level anyway unless the building hex is interior.

title: Can I gain/retain Acquisition and leave Residual if a unit moves on?
question:
I can see that Acquisition is lost for a number of reasons (mainly firing on another target). But if a unit moves out of the target hex can my Acquisition move with it, and can I also place a Residual fire in the target hex (if I don't fire on the unit again)? I cannot see anything that would prevent it - but intuitively it doesn't make sense that the gun can rain fire down on the original hex whilst tracking a unit through multiple other hexes.

Cheers,
Neil
author: doktor avalanche
consensus_answer:
I can see that Acquisition is lost for a number of reasons (mainly firing on another target). But if a unit moves out of the target hex can my Acquisition move with it, and can I also place a Residual fire in the target hex (if I don't fire on the unit again)? I cannot see anything that would prevent it - but intuitively it doesn't make sense that the gun can rain fire down on the original hex whilst tracking a unit through multiple other hexes.

This depends on the type of acquisition. A ⅝ inch acquisition acquires a hex and does not move out of that hex without the weapon firing elsewhere [C6.521]. A ½ inch acquisition must track at least one of the acquired targets leaving the target Location when possible [C6.51].

To my mind residual FP does not represent continued fire on the target. Otherwise residual FP would be removed when an attacker makes a SFF/FPF attack. Residual represents the noise and mayhem from the original attack. An ASL MPh takes actions that are in reality simultaneous or nearly so and spreads them out in a sequence. When one unit moves then a second one moves through the same Location, these units are in that same Location at roughly the same time. The second unit is not in exactly in the same place at the same time but it is close enough to be affected by the original attack, possibly only psychologically, e.g. they see bodies lying everywhere and get scared.

title: Night Scenario- lose cloaking/?
question: A cloaked unit is using non-assault movement in an enemy’s NVR but not in an illuminate area and is attacked by DFF with the result of a Pin. Does the unit lose both cloaked and concealment status?
author: Bombadil929
consensus_answer:
A cloaked unit is using non-assault movement in an enemy’s NVR but not in an illuminate area and is attacked by DFF with the result of a Pin. Does the unit lose both cloaked and concealment status?
E1.4, "All rules pertaining to "?" apply to Cloaking counters except as specified otherwise herein."

Movement at night in an unilluminated Location does not cause concealment loss per E1.31.

Per A12.14 a unit loses concealment when it "is attacked resulting in at least a PTC." This is not changed by the night rules.

So the unit does not lose concealment for moving but does for the DFF attack which resulted in a PTC.

title: Residual FP with guns

author: poifpoif

Often but not always. Residual is left after any attack per A8.2 but, for example, some ammunition types don't leave residual. AP does not leave residual, for example [A8.2]. title: Passengers and bounding fire
question:
From the rulebook:

6.1 PASSENGERS: 
Passengers ride inside their transporting vehicle and have their FP halved for Mounted Fire [EXC: armored halftracks; 6.63] (in addition to any penalties for Bounding (First) Fire/Motion).

Isn't Bounding Fire specific to vehicles? Could passengers fire during the (carrying) vehicle MPh? 
If not, why the in addition to any penalties for Bounding (First) Fire comment?

What does the *MA:12.7” info means on the back of the M3A1 Scout Car counter?
author: poifpoif
consensus_answer:
From the rulebook:

6.1 PASSENGERS: 
Passengers ride inside their transporting vehicle and have their FP halved for Mounted Fire [EXC: armored halftracks; 6.63] (in addition to any penalties for Bounding (First) Fire/Motion).

Isn't Bounding Fire specific to vehicles? Could passengers fire during the (carrying) vehicle MPh? 

D3.3 "Vehicles are not eligible for Opportunity Fire (A7.25), but unlike Infantry, a vehicle/its Passengers/Riders may move and also fire."

If not, why the in addition to any penalties for Bounding (First) Fire comment?

N/A. 

During their vehicle's MPh, Passengers are halved once for mounted fire, halved again for BFF and possibly halved again if not stopped. Passengers on Halftracks and Carriers are not halved for mounted fire.

What does the *MA:12.7” info means on the back of the M3A1 Scout Car counter? 

The MA (the four FP MG) is a 12.7mm (.50 caliber or thereabouts) weapon. These weapons have larger caliber ammunition than standard MGs and so have a better TK#.

title: Leader Bonus when MMG keeps ROF
question: So I just got attacked with an Squad/MMG and 8-1 Leader.  The MMG kept ROF.  In the Defensive Fire Phase, can the the Leader still Direct the MMG, even though he and the Squad are marked with First Fire?  And would he be able to Direct Fire a third time if the MMG keeps rate again?
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer: As above per A7.53, "a leader can direct the fire of a MG as many times as the MG can fire, even if he also directed other units as part of a FG in the MG's previous attack." title: AFV firing their MG during DFPh
question:

Let’s say enemy attacking Infantry units are approaching the rear of an AFV unit in order to CC during the upcoming APh. 

The AFV could try to defend itself targeting those incoming enemies firing its MA, provided its MA offers some HE option against infantry units (or AP/HEAT provided the proper terrains are being targeted). The To Hit DRMs here are obvious.

But what about the mounted MGs? What can the defending AFV do with its mounted MG during the Defensive Fire Phase against those units outside its VCA? 

Can the BU AFV rotates to fire all its available MG (bow and coaxial)? What’s the drawback (DRM) then? Can the AFV rotates its TCA only and fire its coaxial MG, forfeiting its BMG? What’s the drawback then?
author: poifpoif
consensus_answer:
JRV, could you please point me to the rule that spells out what you wrote in the post previous to this? I thought that the MA shot on the Pz4 would have a +3; i.e., the full CA change penalty.
D3.51, "If, after firing, another turret-mounted weapon (or the MA which has retained a Multiple ROF) wishes to fire at another target outside the current TCA, the Case A TH DRM would be applicable based only on the move from the current TCA to the new TCA (C5.12) but only if the preceding shot(s) were taken at a Known enemy unit; otherwise no further change in TCA is allowed during that phase."

This prevents TCA changes or VCA changes from accumulating. D3.51, with its "based only on the move from the current TCA to the new TCA," explains how multiple weapons interact.

Also note that a TCA change can't wipe out or reduce a VCA change and vice-versa. If in my example during the first shot the VCA changed as well as the TCA (perhaps to get the hull frontal armor pointing in a better direction), the first attack would have a +5 TH DRM, +2 TCA, +3 VCA, and the second attack would have a +4 TH DRM, +1 TCA for the most recent TCA change but also +3 for the most recent VCA change even though the VCA did not change as part of the second shot. 

C5.12, although part of the process, to my mind it does not explain what happens when different weapons cause different CA changes. C5.12 seems more geared toward Guns, where there is only one weapon causing CA changes.

Again I think the designers knew this was something of a potential sleaze where the CMG would be used to "bleed off" some of the CA change TH DRM, so they required that the attack be made against a Known target to partially mitigate that sleaze.

replies.body:
If the AFV changes its VCA (for example to fire a BMG) it is +3 for the first hexspine change and +1 for each additional hexspine change (just as it would be for firing a NT MA outside VCA).

If the AFV changes its TCA (for example to fire a CMG) it is either +2 or +1 for the first hexspine change (depending on whether the turret is a T (circle) or ST (square)) then +1 for each additional hexspine change (just as it would be for firing a T or ST MA outside TCA).

You may wish to review D3.5-3.52 for combat & D1.81-1.83 for CA. Changing VCA, takes a lot of value from vehicle-mounted MGs. So on a typical tank like a T-34 firing at infantry with FFNAM but not FFMO and a one spine VCA change would attack at six FP up two plus TEM. If it has to spin more than one hex or the TEM is, say, building you are starting to get into attacks that are not likely to be fruitful. Although they don't cower.

Firing the CMG only doesn't forfeit the BMG. The BMG is still available for a different attack. The word, "forfeit," implies the forfeited item is no longer available.

As an aside although HEAT does require special terrain AP does not. Also I can't think of any tank with HEAT that does not also have HE. You might use HEAT to get a double TH chance, but I have not seen that done unlike ammunition like APCR vs vehicles. It does not have to make a Motion attempt or "move" in a game sense. It will have to pass a bog check if appropriate. Despite there being a separate MPh it is assumed that vehicles make minor moves within hex without necessarily the game having a game action to match. For instance the traverse of a StuG III is around 20-25° (about 12° per side) but in ASL the vehicle can fire from the left-hand side of its VCA to the right-hand side, a sweep of more than 60°, without moving in game terms. Such "minor" VCA changes are abstracted in the game. The Char B1bis 75mm Gun had *no* traverse without actually turning the vehicle but again there is no game movement necessary, either within its VCA or not. Likewise vehicle-mounted weapons can change their TCA/VCA as part of an attack per C5.11 without using "movement" as a game action. It is just part of the attack. All this minor movement is hidden and assumed in the game.

I expect that there is even more "minor movement" that is assumed. For instance a unit, infantry or vehicle, in the board 10 walled town square (hex 10Y5) probably has to move from one side of the hex to the other in order to fire in different directions. Although in real life this would involve real movement, such movement is below ASL's level of abstraction.

With that out of the way, I will now point out a (slight) sleaze you can make with the changing CA DRM. For each "type" of DRM (TCA, VCA) only the most recent applies to an attack. So although you can't change TCA (for example) using the CMG then use the MA without Case A DRM, you can change TCA to close to the final arc then make a smaller TCA change for the second attack.

In this image if the T34/85 changed its TCA to fire its MA on the Pz IV the Case A DRM would be +3. But if it fired its CMG on the 4-4-7 then fired its MA on the Pz IV the Case A DRM would only be +1. The ASLRB authors knew this is a sleaze, so the target for the first attack *must* be Known. If it is not the TCA can't be changed the second time [D3.51].

D3.51, "If, after firing, another turret-mounted weapon (or the MA which has retained a Multiple ROF) wishes to fire at another target outside the current TCA, the Case A TH DRM would be applicable based only on the move from the current TCA to the new TCA (C5.12) but only if the preceding shot(s) were taken at a Known enemy unit; otherwise no further change in TCA is allowed during that phase."

This prevents TCA changes or VCA changes from accumulating. D3.51, with its "based only on the move from the current TCA to the new TCA," explains how multiple weapons interact.

Also note that a TCA change can't wipe out or reduce a VCA change and vice-versa. If in my example during the first shot the VCA changed as well as the TCA (perhaps to get the hull frontal armor pointing in a better direction), the first attack would have a +5 TH DRM, +2 TCA, +3 VCA, and the second attack would have a +4 TH DRM, +1 TCA for the most recent TCA change but also +3 for the most recent VCA change even though the VCA did not change as part of the second shot. 

C5.12, although part of the process, to my mind it does not explain what happens when different weapons cause different CA changes. C5.12 seems more geared toward Guns, where there is only one weapon causing CA changes.

Again I think the designers knew this was something of a potential sleaze where the CMG would be used to "bleed off" some of the CA change TH DRM, so they required that the attack be made against a Known target to partially mitigate that sleaze.

title: Firing with no chance of hitting but for acquisition bonus
question: If there’s mathematically no way for an AFV to hit its target (bounding fire with a +10 DRM for instance), can I still fire the AFV MA to get the acquisition bonus? Even Intensive Fire to improve the acquisition?
author: poifpoif
consensus_answer:
We say 'I'll take an Acq shot on hex ...." when it is one of these where we know we need something really, really low to hit.  Then we'll roll before even calculating exactly what we need and only look up the exact To Hit if we roll a 4 or less.  Presumption being that anything above a 4 would be a miss for sure, so not worth the extra time to figure out the exact roll needed.

Typically we're looking at a BU vehicle firing in the AFPh at a concealed target after moving, so usually +1 with a +4 with a +2, so minimum of a +7 shot.Note that you can’t acquire a concealed target (C6.5).

Note that you can’t acquire a concealed target (C6.5). But you still can use ATT and acquire its hex, which allows bracketing once the unit loses concealment or another, unconcealed, unit enters the hex.

The Area Target Type also has the double advantages that it ignores the TEM for the TH and a snakeeyes is an automatic critical hit unless the highest possible hit requires a DR ≤ 2. Since a moving vehicle only gets one attack in the AFPh regardless of Target Type an ATT attack may be the better choice. Consider a CE turreted AFV that moves within six hexes but not within two of an unconcealed infantry target in a stone building/rubble. In that AFPh the TH DRM are +4 cases A & B for having moved with both ATT and ITT and an additional +3 for TEM for ITT. With the ITT even a snakeeyes is an Improbable Hit, requiring a subsequent dr. For the ATT a three is a normal hit (which may not be great but is usually better than nothing) and a snakeeyes is an automatic critical hit. Different DRM (e.g. different TEM, concealment, point-blank range, BU/CE, hindrances, etc.) can change this calculation and may give different results for other situations. Also if you put down an ⅝ inch acquisition and the target may leave the hex but remain in LOS before you can fire to switch acquisition type, the ⅝ inch acquisition will not track the target. These are considerations for choosing what Target Type to use in the AFPh.

As others have said.  Usually we're firing ATT in those situations to generate the ATT ACQ.

And to be technically correct, you CAN gain concealment on a concealed target using ITT /if/ your attack successfully removes the concealment (C6.57).

title: Smoke fire is a miss
question:
Need some clarifications here.

An AFV attempts to fire SMOKE at the beginning of its PFPh.

1) He rolls higher than the TH number. It’s a miss, there’s no SMOKE placement, period. Right? 

2) If ROF is maintained however, he could try again right away without any drawbacks?

3) If ROF isn’t maintained, he could try to fire SMOKE again but only using an Intensive Fire?

4) If he successfully fires smoke and ROF is maintained, he’s not marked with a Prep Fire marker? So he could move during the incoming MPh? 

5) If he successfully fires smoke but ROF isn’t maintained, he receives a Prep Fire marker but could still fire his MA with an Intensive Fire? He won’t be able to move this turn however?
author: poifpoif
consensus_answer:
After your roll a to hit DR for ordnance using special ammo such as Smoke (WP, APCR, etc.), there are two numbers you have to look at. The first is the depletion number per C8. This is the number next to the abbreviation on the back of the counter, e.g. for "s8" the abbreviation "s" means "smoke" and "8" is the depletion number. If the TH DR is ≤ the depletion number the weapon successfully fired that type of ammo. Proceed to next step. If you rolled > the depletion number the weapon not have that type of ammo (is depleted) and is considered not to have fired for any purpose unless it malfunctioned. If the TH DR equaled the depletion number the attack is completed below but the weapon is out of that type of ammo for further attacks.

Now you have to add the TH DRM to the TH DR and compare the result to the value on the TH table for the range on the Area Target Type. If the TH DR + TH DRM ≤ the TH value, you have hit with that ammo.

As mentioned above only MTRs can maintain ROF while using the ATT. But Smoke (or other special ammo) can be fired as intensive fire as otherwise allowed, e.g. don't deplete the ammo, 

A unit may not move in the MPh if it fired in the PFPh, regardless of whether ROF is maintained [A3.3].

That simple. I guess I’m starting to overthink. So many rules and exceptions to remember.

title: E1.21 Freedom of Movement
question:
Does a gunflash allow a unit marked with a No Move counter freedom of movement? Does a gunflash qualify as a Known enemy unit?

I think the answer is “no”, but seek clarification.
author: Bombadil929
consensus_answer:
Does a gunflash allow a unit marked with a No Move counter freedom of movement? Does a gunflash qualify as a Known enemy unit?

I think the answer is “no”, but seek clarification.
No. The gunflash reveals the Location but not the unit [E1.8]. Per E1.81, "Fire at/observation of a Gunflash beyond the firer's NVR is treated as occurring vs a concealed target [EXC: if the target can be treated as being within NVR, as per 1.101]—regardless of whether or not the target is physically covered by a "?" or represented by a Cloaking counter."

If the attack by a unit that is now unconcealed then a starshell could be placed using the "LOS to gunflash" method, which would drift at most three hexes and thereby illuminate the Location in most cases (except terrain like jungle, etc.), which would in turn put the now-unconcealed unit to be treated as being within NVR and so allow removal of No Move.

title: AFV, Melee and the Movement Phase
question:
I was unsuccessful in destroying the German APC that moved in between two buildings (no street between them) to put my Broken Bazooka team and MMG crew back under DM.  However, he didn't have enough MP's to turn back around and head out. During my turn, I was able to pass my PAATC with a Squad and an 8-1, which failed to take it out.  It is now the Germans Movement Phase again.  The APC was still in Motion, but still had to turn one more click to head out from between the two buildings.  Since I was already held in Melee with it, I do not have to pass another PAATC, correct, and try and kill it when it turns that last click in order to vacate the hex, correct? 
So the only difference to the CCV values now is that I wouldn't get the Ambush (or Street Fighting) opportunity, correct?  

CCV would be 6 for the Squad and SMC combo, -1 Leader Bonus, -1 unmanned MG (APC is buttoned up), -2 Open Topped and +2 Motion.  All correct?
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
I was unsuccessful in destroying the German APC that moved in between two buildings (no street between them) to put my Broken Bazooka team and MMG crew back under DM.  However, he didn't have enough MP's to turn back around and head out. During my turn, I was able to pass my PAATC with a Squad and an 8-1, which failed to take it out.  It is now the Germans Movement Phase again.  The APC was still in Motion, but still had to turn one more click to head out from between the two buildings.  Since I was already held in Melee with it, I do not have to pass another PAATC, correct, and try and kill it when it turns that last click in order to vacate the hex, correct? 
So the only difference to the CCV values now is that I wouldn't get the Ambush (or Street Fighting) opportunity, correct?  

CCV would be 6 for the Squad and SMC combo, -1 Leader Bonus, -1 unmanned MG (APC is buttoned up), -2 Open Topped and +2 Motion.  All correct?
If the vehicle was In Motion, infantry in the hex would *not* be in Melee (unless there was some other enemy unit to cause Melee) [A11.15]. The MMC would still have to pass a PAATC to attack using CC-RF.

The +2 DRM is for non-stopped, not Motion. Motion is a state that only has meaning outside the unit's MPh. Technical detail but it is useful to understand the difference between Motion and non-stopped. A Motion vehicle is always non-stopped, but during its MPh a non-stopped vehicle is not In Motion.

Alternately you could attack the halftrack crew with TPBF, +2 CE DRM and -1 leader even though the vehicle is BU because it is OT [A7.211].

Even if the vehicle had been stopped and held the infantry in Melee, once it started the infantry would have been released but they would still have to take a PAATC. Melee does not free infantry from PAATC requirements. All attacks in the CCPh have no PAATC requirements. You only take a PAATC in the (enemy) MPh when making a CC-RF, when an enemy unit enters and you want to retain concealment or during the APh when Advancing into a Location with an unconcealed enemy vehicle.

So if the Squad/SMC were already in the same hex with the APC, after already passing a PAATC to get into the hex, your saying it's necessary to pass another PAATC to attack it as it turns in order to leave that same hex?

So if the Squad/SMC were already in the same hex with the APC, after already passing a PAATC to get into the hex, your saying it's necessary to pass another PAATC to attack it as it turns in order to leave that same hex?
Correct. What is not necessary is a second PAATC in the CCPh. There are no PAATCs in the CCPh. So if an enemy vehicle drives in, the friendly squad either isn't concealed or decides to give up concealment, and and the enemy vehicle remains in the CCPh, there is no PAATC to attack in that CCPh. Even if the infantry remains in the hex in the next (friendly) turn (either because held in Melee or because it isn't held in Melee but it decides to stay anyway), there would be no PAATC necessary to attack in the second CCPh. Because again there are no PAATCs in the CCPh.

One time where there is no need for a second PAATC is if the friendly infantry have already passed one in the same phase. Assume an enemy AFV enters a hex with only a concealed friendly unit. The vehicle can't declare an OVR as it enters because there are no Known enemy (i.e. friendly to us) units. The concealed unit wants to maintain concealment so it takes a PAATC, which we'll assume it passes. The vehicle can now declare an OVR, but it will be at half FP for the concealment. After the OVR is resolved the friendly infantry might want to CC-RF, and here it does *not* have to make a second PAATC. Once it has passed a PAATC in a phase it has a ticket (for that vehicle only; a second vehicle would require its own PAATC) to attack the vehicle for multiple times (as many as MP spent if you want).

This is actually a fairly complicated topic in its own right. Depending on what kind of SW was fired and whether we are talking about SFF or FPF. If a halfsquad/crew, for instance, fired a non-MG SW/IFE Gun as first fire (e.g. BAZ, PF, 37 Inf, MOL, etc.) it can only use its inherent as SFF or FPF even if it also possesses an unused MG SW/IFE Gun. If it used a MG SW/IFE Gun for DFF it can choose between that weapon or its inherent for SFF, but it must use that weapon for FPF (unless that weapon malfunctions/is eliminated, in which case it can only use its inherent even if it possesses another unused SW/Gun, MG/IFE or not).

I will not go through all the possibilities for squads because there are numerous permutations depending on weapons possessed and used for DFF.

title: When does the +1DRM for Artillery leave play?
question: So with an OBA strike, there is a +1DRM for shooting through or out of the Area of Effect, from whatever debri is kicked up from shells hitting the ground and/or buildings and whatnot. consensus_answer:

In the Defensive Fire Phase, Arty is called in and converted to FFE-1.  All targets hex's are rolled for on the IFT and under the +1 Debri field.  End of that Phase the FFE-1 is flipped to FFE-2.  The Prep fire Phase has no corrections, and the same hex's are hit again.  FFE-2 is flipped to FFE-C. title: B25.651 Gusts Example Error?
question:
I'm completely new to ASL, I'm reading the electronic version of the rulebook and have come across the example for B25.651 (emphasis mine),

The wind is Gusting and the Wind Direction is 5. There are three Blazes in 21FF1,
EE1, and EE3, and a Flame in DD2. FF1 is ineligible for the two-hex Fire Spread because
there is no Burnable Terrain within two hexes that is not already burning. So
only EE1 and EE3 are eligible and subject to the Random Selection DR to determine
which Blaze will automatically spread two hexes. The Random Selection DR is Doubles,
resulting in both Blazes gaining the automatic two hex spread. A Flame counter
is placed in CC2 from the Blaze in EE1. DD3 and CC4 receive Flames from EE3. Had
the Wind Direction been 3, a Flame counter would have been placed in GG4; had the
Wind Direction been 4, EE4 and EE5 would have received Flame counters. Had the
Wind Direction been 6, DD2 would have received another Flame counter and CC2
would have received a Flame counter. Had the Wind Direction been a 1 or 2, no spread
would occur.

How is it that hex DD2 receives an extra Flame counter from wind direction 6 but not 5? Or put another way, why is the Blaze in FF1 ineligible for spread if a hex can contain more than one Flame counter?

I can't find any errata for this or any other threads for that matter, so I'm wondering if I'm missing something?
author: Rezza
consensus_answer: As above apparently "not burning" in B25.651 means both no blaze and no flame. That's probably not something I would have guessed from reading B25.651, but it is a possible interpretation. From the EX it seems to be the one the rules writers had. It is the more literal interpretation, despite the fact that a second flame could be put in the hex with one already present.

replies.body: Because in the first case the only possible hex would be DD2, which is already burning, so another choice must be made. In the second case DD2 is burning but CC2 not, so it is eligible. There is at least one hex not burning, so the spread is valid.

title: Vehicle in Bypass and CC

author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
So even though the vehicle in question is in Bypass in Z14, that alone prohibits an Infantry unit from entering the building in Z15?
Is that because the vehicle is considered straddling both hexs?

Sorry. I thought you meant to enter Z14. You can enter Z15.

Despite being positioned on the map in an ambiguous way, the vehicle (or infantry performing bypass) is always in exactly one Location. In this case it must be in Z14. If there were another bypassable obstacle in AA15 you can't tell which hex it is in from the position alone; the player has to declare which. A vehicle in that position would never be in Z15 for any reason

If so, the Squad would then have to pass a PAATC to enter the building in Z15 in the Advance Phase to instigate a CC with the vehicle in bypass?
Are there any additional DRM's for that CC scenario?
Again, thought we were talking about Z14. The unit can enter Z15 all it wants. It can't attack Z14 using CC because it's not in the same Location. There's an EXC for needing to be in the same Location for village streets [B31.132], but otherwise the units must be in the same location (with street fighting allowing units to move into an adjacent street as part of the attack).

title: Bocage, Wall Advantage, and Smoke/WP fire
question:
I /think/ I know the answer to this, but I wanted to ask to make sure...

A buttoned up US tank is 5 hexes from a concealed German unit in a Woods hex behind bocage.  It is 1944 and the US tank has WP7 and s5.

Situation 1 (the easy one): If the German unit takes Wall Advantage (WA) during the Rally Phase and the US tank Prep Fires at it, it would have several options:  
1a) Attack on the ITT needing a 3 (8 To Hit with DRMs on the roll of +2 for Concealment, +1 for BU, and +2 for Bocage TEM) - it could use existing ACQ, but could not gain ACQ unless it effected the target to cause it to lose concealment.

1b) Attack on the ATT needing a 4 (7 To Hit with +2 for Concealment and +1 for BUT), with +2 on IFT effects at half FP.

1c) Attack on ATT with Smoke, needing a 5 or less (7+2 To Hit with +2 for Concealment and +1 for BU), but s5 cap.  6 or higher = no shot.

1d) Attack on ATT with WP, needing a 6 or less (as above, but WP7) ... so a '7' would be a 'have WP, but miss' and run out of WP.  If he hits, the German unit would lose concealment and suffer a NMC with a -2 DRM (i.e. as if stacked with a 9-2 leader).

Situation 2 (the harder one): If the German unit does /not/ take WA, then the US tank cannot actually see him during the Prep Fire Phase, but could still see the hex.  It could:
2a) Attack on ATT with Smoke, needing a 5 or less as above (7+2 To Hit, +2 for Concealment and +1 for BU).

2b) Attack on the ATT with WP, needing a 6 or less as above (7+2 To Hit, +2 for Concealment and +1 for BU).  A roll of '7' would be a Miss and run out of WP due to WP7.  If he hits, the German unit would NOT lose concealment unless he broke, as he would not be in LOS of any unit (NMC would be as if stacked with a -1 leader, as the woods is only a +1 TEM).

Correct to all?

Awesome, thank you.

Reading the comments I thought I'd add a clarification, just to be on the safe side for anyone else reading this.

You have a Hull Down AFV behind a Wall and the enemy tries to hit you. He does get a hit but it's a Hull hit. In this case nothing happens. He would have normally hit your Hull, but as you are Hull Down behind the Wall, the round just hit the Wall instead with no effect. This is why you don't get the Wall TEM because the Hull is already totally covered by it, and the Wall doesn't effect hitting you in the Turret (the Turret is "above" the Wall).
Got it. Thanks all.

And if the only TEM the AFV would have is the wall, you MUST just take the HD advantage (I /think/ ... you may be able to take the +2 TEM /instead/ of HD, but I think JRVs rule excerpt implies 'no' to this).  If you are in a woods hex behind the wall, I believe you have the option of either taking the woods +1 TEM to the To Hit roll, but NOT being considered hull down, or taking the hull down effects.  The case is almost always obvious to keep the hull down, but there was a discussion a while back I think about benefits of a + on the To Hit versus Hull down depending on the needed roll to hit you, etc.  So if you want to min-max this, work your google-fu and you should get some interesting reads (from what I remember... unless the to hit roll needed is something like a 4 or less, you're almost always better just taking hull down).

Also note that HINDRANCE and hull down /do/ stack ... so a hull down tank behind Smoke can be a real bear to hit ...
Being hull down almost always shaves at least half off your chances of being hit, which is usually better than any TEM you might claim.

title: stairwell symbol?
question: Are the fat white round symbol in X9 on map 51 a stairwell symbol?
author: Nslcole
consensus_answer:
That is a symbol for a single-hex two-story house - see B31.3.

Basically, it's single hex, but you treat it like a normal multi-hex building, instead of a normal (square) stairwell giving it three levels.

Basically, it's single hex, but you treat it like a normal multi-hex building, instead of a normal (square) stairwell giving it three levels.

The building stair symbols are the product of the evolution of the rules and the creation of more complex and historical maps, and have no logical sense when seen now. The number of levels of a building is a combination of different factors, such as the symbol, lack of symbol and number of hexes of the building.  Many historical maps have special symbols to create special levels in a particular building that would not match the generic rules.

A much better system would have been to have explicit symbols for the heights. Such as in no symbols for one level, fat circles for two levels and squares for three levels and just print each symbol in each building hex. Buildings with only stairs in particular hexes could have a specific stairwell symbol designed by SSR (no stairwell symbol would mean stairways in every hex), like the rooftops and factory SSR.

For some reason I thought an enemy unit couldn't claim Wall Advantage until after their MPh was over. So basically claiming in opponents DFPh.

The (very general) rule of thumb is: if you're in a hex with no TEM, you always have wall advantage until you don't :).  You don't have it if you're broke and alone in the hex and various other conditions (though being broken is the big one).

Where WA gets tricky is when you are in a hex with in-hex TEM (a building or woods, for example) and also have a wall/bocage/hedge.  If you don't mark your unit, you ALWAYS have the in-hex TEM.  You gotta declare if you are leaving the in-hex TEM to get coverage from the hexside terrain.  We had this come up twice in our current game ... once where I forgot to declare WA (so my stack couldn't shoot where I wanted them to shoot in DFPh) and once when my opponent did the same ... so, yeah ... this is common.

MPh and AdPh only apply to the phasing player, Rally Phase WA applies to both sides.  There are a few other times (if you're on the opposite side of a wall/hedge/bocage and the other player loses WA, etc.), but these are the most common.

The part where you can get 'cute' is that you can always drop WA if you have in-hex TEM unless you're Pinned.  So you can do cute things like get WA in Rally Phase, firing in the PFPh, then immediately drop WA and 'disappear' to any return fire (if you're behind a bocage)...only to reclaim WA during the AdPh.  If you're talking normal walls/hedges, there really isn't much benefit unless you're going to be firing a backblast wpn during the PFPh...

title: Movement options for an observer
question:
This is an issue that, for some reason, my brain just can't grok.  So I figured I'd ask and hopefully get it resolved once and for all.

Setup: We're talking an onboard observer with a radio and no pre-reg hexes or NOBA. Just a standard 100mm OBA module and a radio.

Situation 1: no AR or SR/FFE2/FFEC on map - This is easy.  During the PFPh, the observer can either attempt to establish radio contact and battery access (hereafter "Contact+Access") or move during the movement phase.  They can't do both.  They are allowed to advance assuming all other requirements are met.

Situation 2: an SR/FFE2/FFEC is already on the map - This is the one that confuses me.  During the PFPh, I get that the observer can remain in their hex, maintain Contact+Access and do 'OBA stuff'.  They then cannot move during the MPh, but can still advance if otherwise able.  But what if they want to move???

Do they still roll to maintain contact?  If they don't, is this a 'voluntarily loss of contact' and the SR/FFE2/FFEC is removed from the map (cancelled?)?  Just uncertain how an observer moves around and how that movement impacts any on-map OBA stuff...
author: kbernatz
consensus_answer:
This is an issue that, for some reason, my brain just can't grok.  So I figured I'd ask and hopefully get it resolved once and for all.

Setup: We're talking an onboard observer with a radio and no pre-reg hexes or NOBA. Just a standard 100mm OBA module and a radio.

Situation 1: no AR or SR/FFE2/FFEC on map - This is easy.  During the PFPh, the observer can either attempt to establish radio contact and battery access (hereafter "Contact+Access") or move during the movement phase.  They can't do both.  They are allowed to advance assuming all other requirements are met.

Situation 2: an SR/FFE2/FFEC is already on the map - This is the one that confuses me.  During the PFPh, I get that the observer can remain in their hex, maintain Contact+Access and do 'OBA stuff'.  They then cannot move during the MPh, but can still advance if otherwise able.  But what if they want to move???

Do they still roll to maintain contact?  If they don't, is this a 'voluntarily loss of contact' and the SR/FFE2/FFEC is removed from the map (cancelled?)?  Just uncertain how an observer moves around and how that movement impacts any on-map OBA stuff...

Rolling for radio contact is a prep fire "action," and as such it places a Prep counter on the unit (at least in your mind; the actual Prep counter need not be placed if the Observer is concealed/HIP per C1.6) just like any other attack, as you say. C1.22 gives us:

"Voluntary loss of Contact (i.e., failure to roll for Contact/Maintenance or voluntary rout; 1.6) causes the immediate loss of Access and Cancellation of the Fire Mission (if any). However, failing to roll for Contact/Maintenance is considered voluntary loss of Contact only if the Observer has no LOS to the SR's/FFE's Blast Height."

This does twist around the meaning of "voluntary" until it is hard to recognize, but in essence it says if the Observer does not roll for contact, battery access is lost and the current OBA counter only goes away if the Observer does not have LOS to current OBA counter's Blast Height. If the Observer *does* have LOS to the Blast Height, it is free to decline to roll during the PFPh/DFPh (and possibly move during the friendly MPh) and the current OBA counter will continue in the OBA progression (SR will remain SR, but FFE:2 will attack and become FFE:C) in its current hex. Note that the Observer can still Rout in the RtPh or Advance in the APh without immediate impact on OBA.

As a final point if the Observer does decline to roll, in the next phase it wants to perform OBA actions it will no longer have the DRM for maintaining radio contact. I will guess that is obvious, but I bring it up for completeness.

title: Foxholes behind Hedges
question: At scenario setup, if you set up a squad in a foxhole that's located behind a hedge, does it become HIP?  If the foxhole is not put on the board because it's out of LOS and can't be fired on until an enemy unit gets adjacent to it, how does it work with a Concealed squad at setup if it's in said foxhole?
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
At scenario setup, if you set up a squad in a foxhole that's located behind a hedge, does it become HIP?  If the foxhole is not put on the board because it's out of LOS and can't be fired on until an enemy unit gets adjacent to it, how does it work with a Concealed squad at setup if it's in said foxhole?
The foxhole is not out of LOS to an enemy unit that has LOS to the hex at the same level through a wall/hedge hexside [B9.21]. The foxhole sets up HIP because A12.33 says *all* Fortifications set up HIP. This is regardless of whether the in-hex terrain is concealment terrain or not.

The foxhole would be revealed at the end of setup «just prior to placing non-OB "?"» [A12.33], again assuming an enemy unit within sixteen hexes has LOS to the hex through a wall/hedge hexside (or, of course, if not through a wall/hedge hexside).

A HIP foxhole does not grant HIP to its contents. This is in contrast to a pillbox [B30.7] or a cave [rules cite available on request].

Despite the fact that the foxhole itself is not out of sight through a wall/hedge hexside to an enemy unit at the same level, units in it are out of LOS [B9.21]. There is a q&a on this:
A12.33 & B9.21 Since LOS is reciprocal, B9.21 seems to imply that a hidden entrenchment directly behind a wall/hedge cannot be seen across that wall/hedge by a non-adjacent, same-level unit. Is this correct?
A. No – the required LOS to the entrenchment's Location is all that is necessary to reveal it. 
[An93b; An96; Mw]

If the foxhole behind a wall/hedge is not revealed (PTO, night, long range viewer only, etc.) and that foxhole contains potential targets, this is a problem that is not addressed the rules. I believe the current fashion is to allow the attack but then if there is any effect to say that the target is out-of-LOS. So far as I know there is no officially-sanctioned solution to this problem.

replies.body: The foxhole behind the hedge is easier to see than a unit in the foxhole. As well, a foxhole being HIP does not entitle its occupants to be HIP. Note that all fortifications can set up HIP, but they tend to lose that status quickly. See A12 and/or the concealment gain/loss chart.

The foxhole would be revealed at the end of setup «just prior to placing non-OB "?"» [A12.33], again assuming an enemy unit within sixteen hexes has LOS to the hex through a wall/hedge hexside (or, of course, if not through a wall/hedge hexside).

A HIP foxhole does not grant HIP to its contents. This is in contrast to a pillbox [B30.7] or a cave [rules cite available on request].

Despite the fact that the foxhole itself is not out of sight through a wall/hedge hexside to an enemy unit at the same level, units in it are out of LOS [B9.21]. There is a q&a on this:
A12.33 & B9.21 Since LOS is reciprocal, B9.21 seems to imply that a hidden entrenchment directly behind a wall/hedge cannot be seen across that wall/hedge by a non-adjacent, same-level unit. Is this correct?
A. No – the required LOS to the entrenchment's Location is all that is necessary to reveal it. 
[An93b; An96; Mw]

If the foxhole behind a wall/hedge is not revealed (PTO, night, long range viewer only, etc.) and that foxhole contains potential targets, this is a problem that is not addressed the rules. I believe the current fashion is to allow the attack but then if there is any effect to say that the target is out-of-LOS. So far as I know there is no officially-sanctioned solution to this problem.
Got it, thanks.

title: Vehicles and ROF
question: I thought I knew this one. A vehicle that Prep Fires and keeps it ROF can then move in the Movement Phase, right?
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
To be clear, if you fire your MA in one hex and fail to retain ROF, you cannot fire your MGs in another hex [D3.3, D3.51]. 
My understanding here is that the non-MA weapons have to be fired in the first hex the MA fires in, regardless of whether it maintains ROF or not.

D3.51 "Once any vehicular weapon fires, its other weapons may fire in that phase only from that same hex [EXC: OVR; and MA retaining a Multiple ROF may fire again from another hex if the previous shot(s) were Bounding First Fire]."

The MA may fire again in a different hex if it retains ROF, but the MGs and other non-MA weapons are only allowed in the first hex from which *any* fire occurred.

This also means, as best I read it, that the MA must fire from that first fire-hex and retain ROF; you can't fire the MGs in the first hex but not the MA then move to another hex and fire the MA even if the MA has a ROF listed for it. It must fire from that first hex and retain ROF to be able to fire from a hex other than the first fire-hex.

title: What happens when an OBA SR lands in a part river, part land hex with the centre dot being river - is it lost as there would be no blast height for an observer to see if it lands in water?
question: A friend and I are playing the Dinant CG. His French OBA SR drift landed in a partial water/land hex, but the centre dot was in water. author: ivorgardiner
consensus_answer:
A friend and I are playing the Dinant CG. His French OBA SR drift landed in a partial water/land hex, but the centre dot was in water. I'm not clear on what difficulty you are having. The blast height of the SR (and more generally any FFE) rises two levels from the base level of the hex [C1.32]. There is no EXC for a Water Obstacle hex, so the blast height rises from level minus-one to level one, i.e. if the observer could see a unit at level one in the hex, the observer can see the blast height of the SR/FFE in that hex. Then for purposes of rules that require having LOS to the blast height (e.g. C1.22 covering whether failing to roll is voluntary loss of contact but also many others) the observer has LOS. This is no different than if the SR/FFE landed in another level minus-one hex, e.g. a Depression or Valley hex.

title: Berserk Dashing
question:
Apparently a Berserk (already Berserk since previous turn) unit can dash to the location (stone building) with the enemy unit he's charging at?
What can the enemy unit still do?
-Defensive First Fire PBF but halved due to area fire (dashing). Correct?
-If the Berserk unit survives and charges into the building, the enemy unit can still Final Protective Fire with TPBF. Correct? Can it do that 2 x since the Berserk unit had to pay 2 MF? Is this still halve due to area fire (dashing)?
author: neo.colpaert
consensus_answer:
DFF is halved (the Berserk status has no bearing on the Dash rule). In your case, it also is doubled due to PBF indeed.
The enemy in the building must DFF (normal DFF, SFF or FPF, depending on the fact that it fired previously or not) at TPBF. On your case, it would be a SFF.
No halving due to Dash (that only occurs in the road hex) but halving due to possible SFF/FPF of course applies.
You can DFF twice, as the building cost 2MF to be entered.
OK thanks, Robin. Completely understood. 🙂 In this case you could even choose to wait then with DFF until the Berserk unit enters the building since it would not be halved as SFF (not the first shot anyway), I suppose?

consensus_answer: C1.57.  A HE concentration FFE of at least 70mm is a two level +1 LOS Hindrance to any LOS into, through or from it.  It is only +1 per FFE, not +1 per hex.

A unit at level one is "plateau-ed" by level one obstacles in other hexes. "Plateau-ed" means they can't see anything at lower elevations. A unit in N7 on the first level would be plateau-ed by N8, O13 and O11 too, though just by a hair for the last. LOS from N7L1 to O25 could only see level one or higher in O25, which of course there isn't any. Concealment would not be lost for units in O25 from N7L1.

If N8, O11 and O13 did not block LOS, I count four out-of-season orchard hindrances from level one to level zero.

From N7 level two LOS would be clear and also unhindered by the out-of-season orchards.

Also a steeple can be overstacked, so your opponent could potentially move a full squad up there.

LOS rules are complicated.

The easy answer to your question is... 'it depends'.

Let's talk about above ground obstacles only...
For buildings, trees, etc., we'll assume these are all on ground level (level 0) and that the person viewing over them is at level 2.  A building or woods hex is a 'level 1 obstacle'.
At 1 - 4 hexes, the building/woods (hereafter just "woods") creates 1 blind hex.  This is also EDIT (in season) orchards, fwiw.
At 5 - 9 hexes, the woods would create 2 blind hexes (out of season orchards, like in Hatten, I /think/ always create only 1 EDIT (HINDRANCE) hex... but you should read the orchard rules to be sure)
At 10 - 14 hexes, the woods would create 3 blind hexes
15 - 19 ...
20 - 24 ...

etc.  every FULL multiple of 5 hexes from the lvl 2 viewer increases the blind hexes by 1.  If you're on a level 2 HILL and the potential obstacle is a crest line (so the level 1 crest line), /decrease/ the number of blind hexes by 1 (which means 0 - 4 hexes = 0 blind hexes).  If you're on level 3 and only need level 2 to see over the obstacle, also decrease the number of blind hexes by 1 ... but in this case, there is a 'min 1'( so 1 - 9 = 1 blind hex; 10 - 14 - 2 blind hexes, etc).

Finally, the thing to remember is that if you aren't on the 'crest' of a level you can never see below you.  Only if you're at the 'edge' of a terrain feature can you see down below you (this almost always matters just for hills, as you can't see out of an internal building hex in most cases ... but if you were on a rooftop and not 'on the edge' of the building, you also would be unable to see lower than your unit).
AWESOME! Thanks for the responses. Going to print this out for future reference.

Just to be clear, the rules for blind hexes only apply if the viewing unit is *above* the top of the obstacle. If the viewing unit is at the same level as the top of the obstacle, as is the case here, there are "infinite" blind hexes to lower levels. There is no LOS from N7L1 to O25.

I see a row called star Vehicle, and bunch of numbers, but I don't what that means: is that the number needed to kill the enemy tank?  Nothing says.  I've been up and down the excellent pdf rules I bought, but can't find anything on it.
author: bignickel
consensus_answer:
Thanks for comments all.  It basically seems that for normal squads without a SW, non-cc reaction fire is pretty useless unless the AFV blundered in CE.
That is in most cases right. The exceptions are going to be vanishingly rare. You might fire to put down residual if you expected a Human Wave, but then you would typically fire before the OVR. You can fire at the crew of a OT vehicle in-hex even if it is BU [A7.211], but is is unlikely that a BU OT AFV will perform an OVR. There may be other reasons, but I can't come up with one that would be common.

Even CC-RF is not all that good. The vehicle has a +2 DRM for non-stopped, so a squad attack would be with CCV of five and a +2 DRM in common cases. You might as well save your FP for following infantry (unless of course it looks like the vehicle is not planning to leave, in which case you might as well take a shot).

replies.body: In general, most IFT fire has no effect on AFVs. If a vehicle has Star armour (ex. Jeep, Truck), then yes, the Star row is the number needed to affect the enemy vehicle. Against an AFV, any vehicle with armour of 0 or greater, the IFT will only affect a CE crew via PTC, MC, etc.

Non-CC Reaction Fire is a fancy name for DFF that occurs after an OVR. It has certain advantages for Guns in that TH cases A & E are n/a and any hit is automatically on the rear facing. For IFT fire you might consider waiting for non-CC RF rather than firing *before* the OVR if the non-moving unit is concealed. Then the OVR would be at half FP for concealment. Otherwise if not concealed you are probably better off firing using regular DFF *before* the OVR in hopes of getting a result (e.g. Stun)  that would halve the FP for the OVR. If the vehicle is not vulnerable to the particular attack (e.g. BU CT AFV vs inherent FP) then non-CC RF doesn't change that; the non-CC RF attack will not have any more effect.

title: OBA Modules
question:
In a Campaign Game, a purchased OBA Module can only be used once for the day it was purchased, correct? I used my 80mm Battalion Mortar with Pre Reg fired in my first turn Defensive Fire Phase, which I drew a black Chit, and converted to a FFE1. There was nothing left in the area during my half of turn 1 for the FFE2 to cause damage to.
So in my next defensive fire phase, I can't attempt to use the same module at a different target, going through the whole process with a spotting round and hoping to draw the last two black chits in a row?
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer: During the course of one particular CG Date an OBA module is usable just like it is in a normal scenario, i.e. place ARs, SRs and FFEs in as many hexes as you like until your draw two red chits on "non-extra" draws [C1.21]. Most, perhaps all, CGs have a rule saying that OBA modules are "retained" after completion of a CG Date only if the OBA module was not used to place a FFE, e.g. Valor of the Guards CG10, but this might vary in other CGs.

replies.body:
Your question isn't too clear. If you're asking if you get only one fire mission from a module in a CG setting then that would be true only if there is an SSR stating this.

Sans SSR then it's just a normal module you can continue to use it for numerous fire missions as long as you have contact access etc.

Does this help?
Yup. So the pre reg is basically just a bonus at the start. There is an off board observer in contact, so no need for the radio check roll. Thanks.

During the course of one particular CG Date an OBA module is usable just like it is in a normal scenario, i.e. place ARs, SRs and FFEs in as many hexes as you like until your draw two red chits on "non-extra" draws [C1.21]. Most, perhaps all, CGs have a rule saying that OBA modules are "retained" after completion of a CG Date only if the OBA module was not used to place a FFE, e.g. Valor of the Guards CG10, but this might vary in other CGs.

I believe you're talking Hatten, right?

The pre-reg just makes the first (usually) shot easier ... you can directly place the SR as a FFE and it is accurate on a 1-4 (usually).  You still need to go through the DR for radio contact (EDIT: if not an offboard observer ... if an offboard observer, this is automatic)  and the chit draw for access prior to placing the  SR/FFE in the pre-reg hex.

Once it has been placed in your first use (DFPh in your example), the FFE1 is flipped to its FFE2 side.  During your PFPh, you /can/ adjust this as normal ... (up to 3 hexes, with a subsequent dr of 1-2 for accuracy) following all the normal OBA rules (I highly recommend you SLOWLY follow through the OBA flow chart for your first several uses ... it is extensive (and slow to use), but worth it until you internalize your options).  I.e. you COULD cancel that first FFE in your PFPh and attempt to place a new SR, for example ... but that would require a new battery access draw, I believe.  Oh... start of your PFPh, you'd have to roll to maintain contact (DR)...if you fail, the FFE2 continues and hits the current hexes, then is flipped to its FFE:C side (this happens regardless of where the FFE2 hits, fwiw).  Yes ... I realize this means that the "FFE1" side is used all of 20 seconds before it is flipped to its FFE2 side ... ASL is what ASL is 🙂 .

Assuming you fire the FFE so it becomes a FFE:C, then on your next DFPh/PFPh, you would roll to maintain contact (DR), followed by another chit draw.  If black, you could place a SR anywhere (I know), correct the FFE:C and keep it as an FFE (I think), but limited to 1-3 hexes of correction, correct the FFE:C up to 18 hexes and convert it to a SR (I think).  I never remember these as we almost always use option 1 (place a new SR) ... so you'd have to look at the flow chart and see what your options are.  They ARE limited.  If the SR lands off-map (like ours did in Hatten :< ) ... your options are even /more/ limited.

With Hatten, you never LOSE your artillery module if I remember ... you only have 1 red chit and it goes back in the pool after drawn.  I guess if you get all four black chits drawn you would 'lose' it, in the sense that only the red chit would remain ... but with Hatten you are pretty much guaranteed potentially up to 4 'shots' with your OBA.
Ah, so you still have to roll for radio contact even if it's an offload observer?

Ah, so you still have to roll for radio contact even if it's an offload observer?
No.
Ooops... I just read the C1.2 and didn't read the offboard observer rule.  As JRV notes - they automatically achieve radio contact and automatically maintain it.
The one odd case is aerial observers, which are sort of off-board [E7.61] but have an inherent radio.

title: Sniper choice
question: My opponents sniper is activated. It lands even distance from a Concealed unit in a wooden building and a Concealed unit in an as yet discovered foxhole. So, the sniper has to go to the unit in the foxhole, even though it's TEM is identical to the wooden building.  Does the sniper attack reveal the Foxhole, even though no other enemy can see it?
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
My opponents sniper is activated. It lands even distance from a Concealed unit in a wooden building and a Concealed unit in an as yet discovered foxhole. So, the sniper has to go to the unit in the foxhole, even though it's TEM is identical to the wooden building.  Does the sniper attack reveal the Foxhole, even though no other enemy can see it?
When selecting an alternate target HIP fortifications *may* be revealed by the owning player [A14.21] at his option. If the target player prefers the unit in the foxhole to be targeted, he need only remain mum. If he'd prefer that building be targeted he could reveal the foxhole, but that would give the Sniper player the choice between the two hexes because the TEM is the same, and it would not be guaranteed that the Sniper player would select the building.

title: Leader which becomes heroic
question:
An 8-1 German leader becomes heroic. My question is whether or not he now has a 1FP? He  is stacked with a HS manning a MMG, so can the stack attack as 6FP with a -1 DRM?

Also, I believe his morale is now a 9, correct?
author: Bombadil929
consensus_answer: One additional comment: if the leader is participating in the firegroup as a hero, it can't use its leadership to direct the firegroup. That means the firegroup can cower. Since heroes are immune to cowering, any cower DR automatically affects the halfsquad/MMG (unless participating in a larger firegroup, in which case depending on what the other participants are random selection may still need to be rolled). Alternately the heroic leader can still direct the firegroup, but then its one FP is not added, the leadership DRM applies but the heroic DRM does not.

Yes and yes. Note that the range for a hero using its inherent FP is only four hexes, so the German MMG & hero combo has six FP only out to four hexes. At 5-8 hex range there's only five-and-a-half FP and no heroic DRM.
