title: A general question about CX paragraph wording
question:
Gentlemen,

I am going through full ALS game rules for the first time (advancing from ASLsk), and have a following general question about the CX rules paragraph. >> I am wondering if I am missing something obvious or perhaps it is just the paragraph that is worded in an unnecessarily convoluted way?

"4.51 COUNTER EXHAUSTION (CX): CX units must add one to any labor task or attack DR they make or direct (+1 to To Hit DR for ordnance; +1 to IFT DR for all others). CX units must add one to any inherent SW (ATMM, MOL, PF) or SMOKE Grenade Availability Check dr they make. CX units must also add one to any CC attack they make, and deduct one from any CC attack made against them. CX units must add one to their Search/Recovery dr (12.152; 4.44), and Ambush Status dr (11.4), and may not advance into Difficult Terrain (4.72). A unit’s CX counter is removed if the unit breaks; or in its next Player Turn as soon as it: has completed all of its Prep Fire, or is designated as an Opportunity Firer, or moves (unless due to a Minimum Move or Deep Stream Entry it becomes CX again), or becomes TI; or at the conclusion of its next MPh—whichever comes first." 

until now all, more or less, clear. But then this:

"A CX counter is removed at the start of a MPh and does not affect that unit during that MPh other than prohibiting its use of Double Time during that MPh."

So, if it is removed at the start of a MPh, how the following could happen: "[...]or at the conclusion of its next MPh—whichever comes first."?
author: brachson
consensus_answer:
The last part of the rule is really to pick up a situation where a CX unit does nothing during its MPh.  

Normally the CX counter is removed when the unit moves - ie at the start of that unit's MPh.

But if the unit does nothing during its MPh, then that the moment the unit moves won't ever arrive.

In that situation, the conclusion of the unit's MPh will happen first (ie before it breaks, Prep Fires, is designated for Opp Fire, or moves).  

Not a common occurrence, but something which can happen.  It could probably have been worded in a slightly less cumbersome way (in the example I gave, the start and end of the unit's MPh effectively are the same moment).

title: Oddity in setup of PB CGI vs CGII
question: In PB for CGI, the full German company sets up in Le Port and the depleted in Benouville. However for CGII, they're switched. Is this intentional or an error in one of the set ups? I've looked for errata for PB, but not sure where to find it.
author: Sparrowfalls
consensus_answer:
In PB for CGI, the full German company sets up in Le Port and the depleted in Benouville. However for CGII, they're switched. Is this intentional or an error in one of the set ups? I've looked for errata for PB, but not sure where to find it.
Note that the elements of PanzerPionier Kompanie 2 are a Depleted Coy at the start of CG I and a Full Pltn at the start of CG II. Likewise PanzerPionier Kompanie 1 starts as a Full Coy in CG I and as a Depleted Coy in CG II. Rather than "swapping" company sizes, one company has gone from a depleted company to a platoon and the other has gone from a full company to a depleted company. Both units have decreased in size, presumably as a result of casualties over the three night scenarios of CG 1 that are not played in CG II. 

The differences sound correct; I don't think you are going to find an erratum for this. More broadly probably the best place to look for errata is the combined compilation on Klas Malmströms' web site.

title: CC vs a squad in a foxhole
question: If a US squad advanced into a Foxhole with a german squad under the foxhole, and eliminates the german squad in CCPh, are the US squad under the Foxhole counter or outside the foxhole?
author: Nslcole
consensus_answer:
As above, B27.44, "A unit may move/advance beneath a foxhole if otherwise able to enter that Location even if an enemy unit exists in that foxhole. The capacity of a foxhole counter is per side; i.e., two opposing squads can both occupy a 1S foxhole during CC."

The extra bit of text, "during CC," seems to be there just to confuse the reader. The intention seems to be that two opposing squads can both occupy a 1S foxhole at any time. If the friendly and squads in the same foxhole can't eliminate each other in CC, they remain in the foxhole in Melee. They might not have a Melee too, e.g. one squad entered during the MPh as part of a Human Wave, one or both squads are concealed, etc.

question: I have a stack consisting of 2 Squads and a Leader. They all move one hex as a stack for 1MF.  Can I then have one Squad attempt to throw Smoke into one hex and the other Squad attempt to throw Smoke into a different hex and still be at 3MF totally used for the stack and 3MF remaining to be used? A4.2 "units may choose to move together as a stack at their own risk and may break up the stack during the MPh to continue to move separately but all members of that moving stack must end their MPh before another unit not in that stack may move."

title: D5.5
question: An Immobilized AFV takes a hull hit. the final To Kill number is 5. The AFV survives the hit. Is the crew subject to TC ?
author: adolfinger
consensus_answer: That gave me time to look up the rule. Per D5.5 an Immobilization Task Check is needed only if that hit "would have destroyed or Shocked it with an Original TK or IFT DR of 5." In this case if the TK DR is four or less, the vehicle is destroyed. If the TK DR is five or higher, a five would be a double-secret Immobilization and anything else would be no effect, so there is no Immobilization TC. If the hit had been on the turret with a TK of five, that would cause an Immobilization TC.

title: Can an ATR fire twice in Movement Phase

author: Mozumbooo
consensus_answer:
Not all ATRs are SW. One sort-of exception is if the ATR is a vehicle MA, e.g. the British Morris CS9 Armoured Car or the Carrier B, it may use Intensive Fire. Per a q&a:

"C5.6 May a vehicular-mounted MG/ATR/light-MTR use Intensive Fire?
A. Yes, if it is MA. Such a weapon is considered a Gun (C2.1). [An93a; An95w; An96; Mw]"

This is probably not what was intended for the question. A vehicle-mounted ATR can't still can't use SFF (unless there is one that has IFE), which is disallowed by rule as above.

One final thing to observe is that Intensive Fire is not Subsequent First Fire and vice-versa. IF is an ordnance attack; SFF is a non-ordnance attack.

title: LOS from a Foxhole at end of Hedge?
question:
So, in the image above, a Concealed German unit is in a Foxhole (M17) at the end of a Hedge.  I'm thinking that if the LOS goes along that Hedge Hexside in N16/N17, he will not have a LOS to the stack of Americans when they enter Q17.  If the Hedge was widthwise, there would be no question, he would not have LOS until I got to an adjacent hex.
Does the same rule apply in this case?
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
B9.21 "A unit in an entrenchment cannot see (or be seen) across a same-level wall/hedge hexside/hexspine forming a part of the unit's hex to (or from) any non-adjacent same-level or lower Location"
So you are correct it could not see O17 or Q17. Because the hedge depiction has a non-zero thickness, albeit very small, there is a narrow cone that a unit in an entrenchment can't see. Close up it's probably just going to be the hexes directly in line with the hedge hexspine, but as you go farther out it's possible some LOSes not exactly along the hexspine are also blocked.

title: CC Reaction Fire (woods)
question: An AFV on a road moves adjacent to an enemy squad that is in the woods. The enemy unit may not employ CC Reaction fire from the woods, correct? (My understanding is that CC Reaction fire may only be utilized by a unit qualifying for Street Fighting or upon a OVR.)
author: Bombadil929
consensus_answer:
Yes, I played SL (a lot) when I was younger,  but what brought the question forward is the example below D7.22: “…., and the tank expends another MP to enter D3 where it is safe from Street Fighting since all ADJACENT Russian units are marked with First Fire counters”.

The question brewed up because the Russian in D2 is in the woods and ADJACENT. The wording of the example makes it sound like *only* the FF counter prevents it from CC Reaction Fire.

Anyway, I over thought the example. The rules are clear on it. 

In the D7.22 example it does sound as if the only reason the unit in C3 can't use CCRF/Street Fighting is because it is marked with a First Fire counter. I wonder if the writer of the example misunderstood the rules, because A11.8 clearly says a unit using street fighting has to be *in* a building. It's also possible the rules did not require the street-fighting unit itself to be in a building at the time the example was written but changed at some point without updating the example. We'll probably never know. However in this case the moving vehicle is between two buildings so at least that part of the street fighting requirements are met and are unlikely to happen with a woods-road, although it is possible I imagine.

replies.body:
7.2 seems pretty clear its only in street fighting for an adjacent hex:

7.2 Reaction Fire
Reaction Fire is conducted during the MPh by
the DEFENDER, who uses it to attack a vehicle in that DEFENDER’s
(or, if using Street Fighting [7.211], in an allowed ADJACENT) Location.

As above a unit adjacent to a woods-road hex may not enter the other hex for CCRF. It may CCRF if it is already in the woods-road hex of course, but without street fighting.

I think the game design reason here is that ASL streets in towns are "magnified" on the game map, i.e. they are mostly not 40+m wide in reality. When they are indeed 40m wide that is a boulevard  instead. However for other game purposes, particularly infantry fighting, street hexes need to be one hex wide. That in turn called for a rule that reflects the difficulty vehicles have with infantry in close-in fighting in towns. Hence we get street fighting. A solution like having roads go through buildings like they go through woods messes up the way infantry experiences city fighting. For infantry most normal streets create definite "fire breaks" that require special effort to cross. One only has to look at village terrain narrow streets [B31.1] to see how the woods-road solution would not work well in a city environment. For infantry fighting narrow streets hardly exist.

title: Street fighting
question:
After a squad performs a street fight vs a AFV,does the AFV get to attack back
against the squad? And if so,in which hex would that attack take place in?
author: JTV656
consensus_answer:
After a squad performs a street fight vs a AFV,does the AFV get to attack back
against the squad? And if so,in which hex would that attack take place in?
This depends on in which phase the street fighting occurs. During the MPh as CCRF per D7.211, "CC Reaction Fire occurs during the MPh when no vehicle CC attacks (of any kind, including "sN"; A11.622) are allowed" [D7.213]. This is repeated in A11.8, "Reaction Fire is identical to Street Fighting CC procedures except that the vehicle may not attack back; i.e., it has no CC attack options during Reaction Fire (although Crew Small Arms still applies)." During the CCPh normal CC occurs, including the vehicle being able to attack back. The attacks take place in the hex with the vehicle.

There is an erratum from the 93b Annual: 

U.S. Vehicle Note 30 M3(MMG) & M3(HMG) After "VCA." in the next-to-last line of the final paragraph, add "In addition to Removal as per D6.631, the AFV's Passenger(s) may Remove its secondary AAMG as (a) dm MMG [for the M3(MMG)] or (a) dm HMG [for the M3(HMG)]. The MA of both AFV may be removed (but only as per D6.631) as a dm .50-cal HMG." [An93b; An96; Mw]

The squad (/two halfsquads) may Remove only the secondary armament(s). The crew may Remove any/all of the three AAMGs.

Removal by a Passenger, when allowed, is part of the unloading cost [D6.631].

title: C.4 vs. C3.33:  Direct Rules Contradiction?
question:
Maybe we're just confused about possible differences between the concepts of Area Fire and Area Target Type, but these two rules seem contradictory to me: 

-- According to C.4:  "ORDNANCE AREA FIRE:  Ordnance Area Fire never halves the FP effect of any hit.  Instead, any shot affected by any provision of Area Fire caused by the target's status uses the Case K To Hit DRM (6.2)..."

-- But according to C3.33:  "AREA TARGET TYPE:  The Area Target Type must be used at all times by mortars and whenever ordnance [EXC:  LATW] attempts to fire SMOKE; otherwise it may be selected when firing HE...  All units hit by HE are attacked on the IFT using a single DR and half the FP of the firing ordnance;..."

So which is it?  My Marder wishes to use Area Target Type to fire at a Stone Building with Concealed troops inside.  Seems like Case K applies, so at Range 5 my To Hit is 7 while my To Hit dice roll incurs a +2 for Case K.  We prefer to use the IIFT, so if I hit, then do I get a 75L full strength 14FP result (with +3 on the damage DR for the Stone Building), or a half strength 7FP result (again with the +3 for the Stone Building)?
author: A2SimGamer
consensus_answer:
As above, Area Fire and Area Target Type are not the same thing. One place to see this is in the two separate entries in the index.

Because they are not the same, for any given ordnance attack it is possible that one or the other, both or neither apply to the attack. A BAZ firing out of a shallow stream uses Area Fire [B20.6] but not Area Target Type (it is an LATW that uses its own TH Table [C13.42]). A Mortar firing from open ground to an unconcealed target in open ground uses Area Target Type but not Area Fire. Per A7.23 concealment is a form of Area Fire so a German PaK 40 choosing the Area Target Type when firing against a concealed target would be using both Area Fire (i.e. it has a +2 TH DRM) and Area Target Type (i.e. its effects FP is halved from its normal FP). And a Pz IV firing at an unconcealed T-34 using the Vehicle Target Type would not be using either Area Fire nor Area Target Type.

replies.body:
You are confusing Area Fire and the Area Target Type - a quite frequent confusion.
Area Fire is firing at, for an example, a concealed target.
Case K TH DRM +2 applies, but otherwise the FP is not halved for the sake of Area Fire (e.g. if the concealed target is hit, the FP used is not halved).

Now, using the Area Target Type, if the target is hit, the FP is halved.

Now, if an Area Fire situation occurs while using the Area Target Type, case K applies.
If a hit occurs, the FP is halved due to the Area Target Type, but is not halved again, as Area Fire doesn't halve the FP.

title: Rout or surrender?
question: Will the russian surrender, or what routning options do he have?
author: Nslcole
consensus_answer:
Am I missing something?  G6 cannot be seen by the German unit.  That means the Russian does not have to surrender.  The Russian can still low crawl to G7, without having to surrender.  A possible route path to G9 might go through G6 using 5 movement points (G6 to G7 to G8 to G9).

20.21 RtPh: Any broken Infantry unit during its RtPh that is both ADJACENT to Known, Good Order, armed enemy Infantry/Cavalry and unable to rout away from it or only able to rout while being subject to Interdiction or resorting to Low Crawl (regardless of how it actually routs or if the possible unconcealed Interdictor is Known to it), will surrender to that enemy unit as its prisoner instead, (captor's choice of unit receiving surrender if more than one unit qualifies) after first abandoning all its SW [EXC: if pinned; 10.53 & G5.5].

The fact that G6 cannot be seen, negates the only clause.  But, we get further clarification from the words in parentheses "regardless of how it actually routs . . ."  If the Russian unit was to rout to G6, it would no longer be ADJACENT to the German unit.  20.21 would no longer apply.  A route path to G6 to G7 to G8 to G9, is a possible rout path.  Low crawl to G7 is allowed because there is an another option that would not leave the Russian unit both ADJACENT to the German unit, and unable to move away without being subject to interdiction.  

So, what rule makes the Russian surrender?

A20.21 forces it to surrender.

The unit has to rout to G9. That is its only rout target. It cannot Low Crawl to G6 because it would not have moved closer to G9, but that is actually not important. However per q&a:

A10.51 If a DM broken unit that must rout is within six MF of the nearest woods/building, must it attempt to reach the woods/building in a single RtPh?
A. Yes, unless it uses Low Crawl, but it need not take the shortest route (in hexes/MF) to do so. Even if it uses Low Crawl, however, it must still do so toward that woods/building (i.e., at no time may it increase the hex range between itself and that woods/building, and must end that RtPh closer to it than it was at the start of the phase).
So its choices are:
  1) Low Crawl to G7.
  2) Rout normally through G7 to G9, facing interdiction in G7 & G8.
  3) Rout normally through G6 to G9, facing interdiction in G7 & G8.

Referring to A20.21, the unit's only choices are to use Low Crawl or face interdiction. It surrenders.

The unit does not have to be subject to interdiction as it moves from ADJACENT to the KEU. It just has to face interdiction somewhere on all the paths it might take. A q&a regarding this:
A20.21 Assume that No Quarter is not in effect and that a broken unit is ADJACENT to a Known, Good Order, armed enemy Infantry/Cavalry, with a Building hex 3 hexes away which is its only possible rout target. Or is it captured even though it would no longer be ADJACENT to the enemy unit where it would suffer Interdiction?

The unit need not even have LOS to the (unconcealed) unit that will interdict it. Assume that the German halfsquad is in SMOKE but there is another unconcealed German squad in E8 able to interdict G8. The broken unit still surrenders. If the German in E8 were concealed it would have to reveal itself at rout start to force surrender.

title: 10.5 Routing
question:
A10.5: (During the RtPh a broken unit not in Melee may not remain in the same Open Ground hex in the Normal Range (10.532) and LOS
of a Known non-Melee enemy unit/its-SW/Gun)

So if a broken enemy unit  2 hexes away are in LOS of one of mine broken units in open ground, do I have to rout(The Broken unit can´t attack, but I ask because I don´t know if the enemy broken unit have normal range)?
author: Nslcole
consensus_answer:
What is the “normal” range of a gun? Or is it a prohibition to remaining in the normal range of the crew?
The unit manning the Gun has to be unbroken. Per A10.5, "During the RtPh a broken unit not in Melee may not remain in the same Open Ground hex in the Normal Range (10.532) and LOS of a Known non-Melee enemy unit/its-SW/Gun." The reference to A10.532 is intended to bound the Normal Range to sixteen hexes as per A10.532 even though nearly all Guns have an unbounded range in ASL. This reading is less-than-obvious to me, but there is a q&a explaining this:

"A10.5, A10.532, & A10.62 In rule 10.5 (routing) and 10.62 (desperation morale), what does the reference to rule 10.532 mean?
A. It is referring to Normal Range being limited to 16 hexes."

So the "Normal Range" for any unit/weapon as would force a broken unit in A10.531 Open Ground to rout is its maximum range or sixteen hexes, whichever is less.
Possibly because >16 hexes also has different rules for Concealment gain/loss. Which will hopefully help me remember this the few times it becomes a factor.

title: After attempting to move from ASLSK to ASL I noticed there is no strictly defined order of actions in the RPh
question: The SK definitely says "these steps must be taken in order". Is this order still implied or is the omission by design?
author: MadOgre
consensus_answer:
The SK definitely says "these steps must be taken in order". Is this order still implied or is the omission by design?
In ASL detailed order is defined on the "Advanced Sequence of Play (rev.)" (ASOP), which is a two-page, front-and-back chart included with the v2 rules. The v1 rules had a one-page, front-and-back chart.

title: Night rules: Gunflashes and KEU's
question: Is seeing a gunflash from an enemy unit the same as seeing a KEU for freedom of movement purposes?
author: Sparrowfalls
consensus_answer:
Christopher, Bring on the Night by JR VanMechelen (aka The Original JR) is a great resource for playing Night.  It's been printed in a Journal, I think, but you can also find it here on the Texas ASL site.  I re-read it before any Night scenario and am still picking up nuances after all these years.
Note however that there is at least one error in there. On page 4, under E. Jungle, the first line of the example says:

Example: There is no LOS between 34H7 and 34I8 if they are dense jungle, but there is one from 34G8 to 34I8.
However if that is a Dense Jungle, there cannot be LOS from 34G8 to 34I8 as Dense Jungle is inherent terrain (G2.2).

replies.body:
No; 'Known Enemy Unit' is defined as 'any unconcealed, non-prisoner enemy unit—even one which is broken or in Melee—which the unit in question currently has a LOS to)' - that's from the index but you can find a broader description in A12.11.

However, any unit *attacked* by whatever generated the gunflash now has Freedom of Movement if it didn't already, as per E1.21.
What was throwing me off was E1.101 that says units outside of NVR are out of LOS unless marked with a gunflash. So I thought maybe the LOS would be enough to trigger Freedom of Movement.

What was throwing me off was E1.101 that says units outside of NVR are out of LOS unless marked with a gunflash. So I thought maybe the LOS would be enough to trigger Freedom of Movement.

Right, that's a little confusing.  A unit outside of NVR can't be affected at all by your fire, unless marked with a gunflash or otherwise illuminated.  However, that gunflash in and of itself doesn't render it Known to you.  

A unit within NVR but still concealed is unknown to you, but you can at least shoot at it.  If it's within NVR and unconcealed and in a friendly unit's LOS, it can grant that unit Freedom of Movement.  Similarly, if it's unconcealed, in LOS, and illuminated (by IR or Starshell), it would grant FOM.

title: When one side has No Quarter in effect by SSR.
question: One side has declared No Quarter at scenario start by SSR. When this happens, does the other side already know it or do they "discover" it the first time they try to surrender and are eliminated?
author: Sparrowfalls
consensus_answer:
One side has declared No Quarter at scenario start by SSR. When this happens, does the other side already know it or do they "discover" it the first time they try to surrender and are eliminated?
Once No Quarter is in effect (whether by action or by SSR), units will not try to surrender by the RtPh method: A20.21, "units faced with No Quarter (20.3) never surrender via the RtPh method."

title: One more Mortar question
question: In Prep Fire, a Mortar attempts to fire WP and rolls higher than its WP exponent. Can you come back to that same Mortar after all other Guns have fired their Smoke/WP and fire regular HE rounds, or even move in the Movement Phase since it's first shot of WP was non existent?
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer: If that Original To Hit DR is > the Depletion Number, the firer had no such ammunition and is considered not to have fired yet for any purpose unless Gun Malfunction or Low Ammo (D3.71) occurs.

If it has smoke and WP (some US tanks, for example), you can even attempt WP...fail, go to other units and attempt SMOKE, then go /back/ to that first unit an attempt Smoke.  As long as you don't fire anything other than SMOKE, you can always go back and try another SMOKE type with the same unit.

title: Mortars, WP and ROF
question: So a Mortar that has a WP exponent can continuously fire WP rounds in a Fire Phase as long as it keeps its ROF, correct?
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
Note that special ammo, including SMOKE, can be fired as Intensive Fire by Guns (but not SW) too. So you can squeeze out an extra SMOKE counter that way too.

You probably are thinking the right thing, but the fire need not be "continuous" by the same weapon as long as SMOKE is fired before non-SMOKE ammunition. Other weapons might interleave in firing SMOKE.

Also a weapon *might* keep ROF but suffer a malfunction, which would also terminate its SMOKE streak. But I can't come up with a case where it does not also deplete its special ammo.

replies.body:
Note that special ammo, including SMOKE, can be fired as Intensive Fire by Guns (but not SW) too. So you can squeeze out an extra SMOKE counter that way too.

You probably are thinking the right thing, but the fire need not be "continuous" by the same weapon as long as SMOKE is fired before non-SMOKE ammunition. Other weapons might interleave in firing SMOKE.

Also a weapon *might* keep ROF but suffer a malfunction, which would also terminate its SMOKE streak. But I can't come up with a case where it does not also deplete its special ammo.

A captured German 81mm MTR with a non-qualified crew fired in 1942 extreme winter would have its breakdown number (ordinarily twelve) reduced by six to six. A TH DR of six (one for the colored die) using Smoke against an empty but doubly-acquired hex would hit and place Smoke and retain ROF but would malfunction. So there's another reason a weapon might not be able to continue firing SMOKE even though it kept ROF and didn't deplete.

Now I will admit I've only had this happen to me twice, so it isn't very common. But it is possible.

So a Mortar that has a WP exponent can continuously fire WP rounds in a Fire Phase as long as it keeps its ROF, correct?
And as long as it avoids special ammo depletion.

title: Routing movement
question: Recently in a game on a bocage filled board, I had to rout a broken unit. The unit had no LOS to a building or woods. I routed to other terrain. Now my question is does a routing unit have to use all 6 movement factors? I could not find any rule on this.
author: Kazootinner
consensus_answer:
Note that a lot of the rout rules, IMO, are 'fuzzy' and (as such) subject to potential abuse.  I.e. if a unit is 2 hexes away from a building (Open ground separating them), can they rout AROUND that open ground hex (moving first away from the building, but then back towards it), provided they can still reach it with 6 MF?  Or must they take the direct path (3 total MF), but be subject to Interdiction in the Open Ground hex?

A10.51 "As long as it reaches that hex during a single RtPh, it need not use the shortest route, but as long as it follows the shortest path in MF otherwise"

So the unit can in this case avoid the open ground.

If you have no valid rout target, can you designate a hex that allows your unit to "Rout forward", assuming they are not routing towards a KEU?  This is fairly clear 'yes', but can be quite odd-looking in some situations.

A hex need not be woods/building to be a valid rout target. Woods/building are *preferred*  but if not available or if ignorable and ignored, the rout target can be of another kind.

That said, a rout target, woods, building or otherwise, can be "forward" in some sense that is outside the rout rules. The rout rules don't concern themselves with whether the player can create a better situation out a rout than might otherwise be expected.

A lot of times we find ourselves making 'gentleman agreements' with respect to routing in the spirit of the rule versus trying to find ways to abuse the (albeit, limited) control you have over a broken unit that is routing.

You are of course free to do this if you want. I play the rout rules as written, and I will on occasion make a silk purse out of a sow's ear, but not often. As far as I know the rout rules are not "fuzzy" but sometimes a canny player can see multiple options for routing and choose the better of them. Likewise since you know the rout rules you can have a leader "pre-positioned" in likely rout targets before units break. I do this all the time. The line between good play and abuse is fairly narrow one.

One thing that did was changed in the routing rules is that Voluntary Break [A10.41] used to be allowed always. In the 1996 ASL Annual an erratum added that the unit had to be within LOS and normal range of an unbroken enemy unit. Without that Voluntary Break was subject to abuse. But routing "forward?" How would you ever define "forward?"

replies.body:
Recently in a game on a bocage filled board, I had to rout a broken unit. The unit had no LOS to a building or woods. I routed to other terrain. Now my question is does a routing unit have to use all 6 movement factors? I could not find any rule on this. 
A broken unit does not have to have LOS to its rout target, whether that is a building/woods or other hex. The target has to be within six MF in a direction that does not violate other rules such as moving toward a KEU, but it need not start in LOS. It is possible that if there are any "surprises" (e.g. enemy units that unconceal themselves) or the broken unit chooses to Low Crawl or for some other reason the broken unit might never have LOS to its chosen target. 

In the same way that sailors can "smell" land, broken units can smell preferable rout targets, i.e. woods or buildings.

That said, assuming there is no woods/building within six MF that the broken unit can reach or if they are all ignorable and ignored, it can choose *any* hex within six MF as its target if that hex is otherwise reachable (e.g. not closer to a KEU, not across an unbridged river, etc.). There is no particular distance that hex has to be other than within six MF.

As JRV says, this can mean you can designate your rout target (which you still must do prior to routing) as any hex anywhere on the board as long as it's is legal.  This can even let you "rout" forward!  Eg we had a situation where a unit broke in the middle of a field with no building or woods nearby and only one enemy in los (the one that broke it), but this enemy got vaporized in AFPh, so the unit could rout forward as there was no KEU preventing that direction from being a valid rout path.

A broken unit does not have to have LOS to its rout target, whether that is a building/woods or other hex. The target has to be within six MF in a direction that does not violate other rules such as moving toward a KEU, but it need not start in LOS. It is possible that if there are any "surprises" (e.g. enemy units that unconceal themselves) or the broken unit chooses to Low Crawl or for some other reason the broken unit might never have LOS to its chosen target. 

It's important to note that a unit can't rout to any building/woods within six hexes, it must rout to the closest  (in MF) building/woods. Once you determine the closest building/woods, you don't have to rout there using the shortest possible path, but you can't pick a different rout destination just because it would leave your broken unit in a more convenient location. Even if routing to the closest building/woods would force you to use Low Crawl or undergo Interdiction, you can't arbitrarily pick another destination. The only things that allow you to ignore the closest route destination are:

1) The destination is no further from a Known Enemy Unit than the hex the broken unit is routing from. In other words, if you break in a hex that is two hexes away from a Known Enemy Unit and the closest building/woods is two hexes away from that same unit, you have the option to ignore that destination.

2) The destination is part of the same multi-Location building your broke unit already occupies. Ignoring such a destination is optional; you can choose to route to another Location in a multi-Location building if it's in the closest building/woods hex and you'd prefer to do so.

3) There is no path to the destination that does not pass through a Blaze, an unbridged Water Obstacle, a cliff, an FFE, or a Known Minefield (although you can rout through an FFE/Minefield if you'd prefer to do so, or if the only legal rout destination forces you to do so).

If any of these conditions is true, you must then pick the next closest building/woods.

Once you've reached your rout destination, you can continue routing so long as: 1) you have MF remaining, 2) you enter only buildings/woods hexes, you don't violate any of the other rules of routing (you don't move closer to a Known Enemy Unit, for example).

This is an important concept that a lot of beginning players miss. To eliminate a unit for Failure to Rout, you don't have to take away every one of its conceivable rout paths, just its path to the nearest building/woods.

This is a lot harder than it sounds, though ... as a unit can ignore MANY 'closer' buildings as potential rout destinations if this would cause it to move closer to a KEU.  So while the closest rout target may be directly adjacent to it and you can prevent that by having a unit two hexes away in that same direction, all that really does is make that 'target' a non-target and they get to pick a different target building/woods.

In practice, our experience is that 99% of the time if you want to eliminate a unit for failure to rout, you will need to have to utilize several units and likely mostly surround the enemy.

title: Are PF's available only by SSR?
question: Just wanted to doublecheck on PF availability. Is it by SSR only or is it in any scenario dated post 9/43 the Germans have the capability? I originally thought it was the latter, but then was watching a few scenario playthroughs on YT that made no PF attempts and started wondering if I had it right.
author: Sparrowfalls
consensus_answer:
Thank you so much for mentioning that. That may explain why I didn't see any PF usage. There's so many things I've forgotten about the rules in the last two decades plus and C8.31 isn't even referenced, I don't think, under the PF and BAZ rules. I'm just going to have to sit down over the next few days and read every line of the rules instead of trying to reference isolated rule sections before playing a new scenario. :)

And in reverse, PF are also backblast weapons [C13.8], so if a defender has an opportunity to fire one, it is fairly likely because the target is in a building [C8.31], which in turn means the firing unit is also fairly likely to be in a building and so would be subject to backblast or would have to take the "stepping out" TH penalty. Against enemy AFVs it is often worth "eating the 'blast" and potentially trading your friendly infantry for the enemy AFV, but against enemy infantry (who would also get wall or building TEM TH DRM) it is frequently not worth the trade. PFs are perhaps not used against enemy infantry as often as they might be, but often they have the serious backblast downside and can be more dangerous to the unit firing them than to the target, especially against enemy infantry.

title: Bocage, Wall Advantage, Concealment, and LOS
question:
Questions concern when/if LOS exists to allow the possibility of fire by either side: 

1)  If several defending German units initially setup Concealed directly behind Bocage, is it correct to mark them during Defender Initial Setup either with or without Wall Advantage so that the attacking American will know before he sets up which concealed Defenders are in position to fire over the Bocage on Attacker Turn 1 vs. which concealed Defenders are out of initial LOS? 

2)  Would the answer to #1 above be any different for Germans who were in a Woods/Bocage hex as opposed to a Clear/Bocage hex?

3) Later, during American MPh, a 7-4-7 moves from L3 to M3 toward the Concealed German 4-4-7 in Q2.  My thought [per B9.541, 1st edition rule set] is that the German has no LOS over the Bocage to the American unit unless/until the German declares Wall Advantage.  Can the German claim Wall Advantage at any time during the American's move (if he wishes to First Fire at M3 from Q2), or must Wall Advantage have been claimed by the German earlier, either during his Initial Setup or during some previous move on his part?
author: A2SimGamer
consensus_answer:
1)  If a defending German unit initially sets up Concealed directly behind Bocage, is it correct to mark it during Defender Initial Setup either with or without Wall Advantage so that the attacking American will know before he sets up which concealed Defenders are in position to fire over the Bocage on Attacker Turn 1 vs. which concealed Defenders are out of initial LOS? 

If the unit is in a hex that has mandatory WA then marking the unit is not necessary until an enemy unit becomes adjacent. Until then the unit has WA regardless of being marked.

2)  Would the answer to #1 above be any different if the German were in a Woods/Bocage hex?

A unit in a hex that does not have mandatory WA can claim it during setup but also could delay claiming it until one of the five times that WA may be changed. One of the five times is during the RPh [B9.322], so potentially the unit might not claim WA during setup then immediately claim it in the first RPh, just to "mess" with the opposition.

3) Later, during American MPh, a 7-4-7 moves from L3 to M3 toward the Concealed German 4-4-7 in Q2.  My thought [per B9.541, 1st edition rule set] is that the German has no LOS over the Bocage to the American unit unless/until the German declares Wall Advantage.  Can the German claim Wall Advantage at any time during the American's move (if he wishes to First Fire at M3 from Q2), or must Wall Advantage have been claimed by the German earlier, either during his Initial Setup or during some previous move on his part?

If you are using the first edition ASLRB you may be missing substantial revisions to the WA rules...yes, it looks as though mandatory WA was introduced with v2. For most rules v1 & v2 are not all that different, but there are some places where they did change as here. title: Support weapons
question: Guys, if a unit routs can I choose to drop its sw
author: Thom6110
consensus_answer:
No. It must carry up to its IPC and it must drop the SW that weigh more than their IPC.
A10.4 : ... A broken unit may not portage anything in excess of its IPC, and prior to rout must abandon any items in excess of its IPC in its current Location—but must rout with any SW ≤ its IPC limits if it possessed such items when it broke.

In other words, you don't have a lot of control on brokies.
Footnote 6 of chapter A4.43 rule on Posession gives some design insight on that limitation.
Broken units are not allowed to transfer or drop their weapons because allowing them to do so expands the omniscient player’s control over broken units that he should have little or no control of.

First when attacking infantry you don't have a "TK" DR. It's an "effects" (or IFT) DR.

For the Infantry Target Type per C6.8 the TEM applies on the TH DR. For the Area Target Type it applies to the effects DR [C3.331].

Lol, it's not quite that bad.  Versus infantry in cover, the first shot upon rolling up is usually just for acquisition anyway.  Next turn you'll likely be looking at a 5 to hit (base 8, +3 DRM for the stone building, +1 DRM for buttoned up, -1 DRM for the acquisition), which is ~28%. Yep, because when you eventually will hit the said infantry in the building, it usually will hurt quite bad (12+0 is common with late war AFVs/MAs).
Be aware that you don't get acquisition if you fire in the MPh (if you don't have gyrostabilizers). You have to wait for the AFPh to do this.

And if the infantry are concealed (quite common in stone buildings), you'll have to fire Area Target Type if you want to build up acquisition...

Though firing ATT isn't horrible either, as you're more likely to hit (no TEM on To Hit, but the +1 for BU and +2 for concealment will apply to either target type), and still have a some chance of stripping concealment (6 FP +3 TEM will strip concealment on a 5 or less).  Usually we fire ATT until we get at least some acquisition and then switch to infantry target type if the target is no longer concealed.  The nice thing about ATT is that you can 'split' the To Hit DRM if it is large (+6 in this example .. +3 for TEM, +1 for BU and +2 for concealment).  Rolling on the ITT at +6 to hit is going to basically be 'potential critical (unlikely hit) or miss' versus rolling on the ATT, which splits the DRM into +3 To Hit and +3 to effects on the IFT.

title: Tanks in prep fire
question: Can a tank with a motion counter on it during prep fire phase fire it’s main armament
author: Thom6110
consensus_answer:
BTW, as a teachable moment, a tank that wants to fire in its PFPh but can't may be interested in using BFF. BFF does not occur as part of a MP expenditure but rather either "between" MP expenditures or after the last MP expenditure or before the first MP expenditure. The last case is the material one here. The vehicle can fire *before* any MP expenditure, almost like it fired in the PFPh. That means it isn't subject to DFF because there was no MP expenditure by the vehicle to target it with DFF.

Almost. A vehicle that announces a BFF attack before expending any MP can be challenged by the rarely-used DEFENDER Gun Duel [[C5.33]. The target of the attack (only) can claim the right to use DFF against the vehicle that is attempting to BFF before expending any MP. But units other than the target can't intervene. 

It's hard to come up with a case where this is super-useful, but it is a fun bit of trivia. 

This is good to know. Was the Gun Duel rule added to cover that circumstance, which could be interpreted as a loophole in the "no firing in PFPh for vehicles in motion" rule?

A Gun Duel [2.2401] allows a vehicle that would normally have to wait for all the attacks by the opposing player to shoot first in certain circumstances during the MPh.

In the MPh the *normal* course of events is: the ATTACKER announces a MP expenditure; the DEFENDER fires as much DFF as he wants; the ATTACKER can now use BFF. Consider the case where the DEFENDER has to spin a Gun around 180° in the woods. That's going to take a long time, as indicated by the +10 DRM (+5 doubled because in woods). You can practically see the commander of the vehicle drumming his fingers on the roof of the vehicle, waiting for this to happen so he can get on with BFF. This is obviously unnatural, and the vehicle would easily get off a shot before the Gun got turned around. ASL allows for the ATTACKER to get off the first shot when the firer-based DRM for the ATTACKER are lower than those of the DEFENDER.

At the start of a unit's movement there is another window where the rules allow out-of-normal-sequence fire. The ATTACKER vehicle can fire at the start of its MPh, before it expends any MP. Because it hasn't expended any MP, it can't be targeted for DFF. A DEFENDER Gun Duel potentially allows the target of a BFF attack to fire without having to wait for a MP expenditure by the vehicle.
Makes sense. Someone has put a lot of thought into these rules

title: Throwing smoke grenades and assault moves.
question: If a MMC attempts to throw a SMOKE grenade before moving it's one hex for an assault move, can the Defender First Fire at the unit in it's starting location during the smoke placement? If so, does the fire get the FFNAM -1 modifier?
author: Sparrowfalls
consensus_answer:
If a MMC attempts to throw a SMOKE grenade before moving it's one hex for an assault move, can the Defender First Fire at the unit in it's starting location during the smoke placement? If so, does the fire get the FFNAM -1 modifier?
You have to announce that you AM before you spend a MF. Your opponent doesn't get the -1 FFNAM if you AM.
But since you spend an MF in your starting location to try to place smoke, your opponent can shoot at you there.

Also be aware that you can't use up all your MF if you want to Assault Move, so placing smoke into an adjacent hex (2 MF) and then moving into the smoked hex (at least 2 MF) doesn't work as Assault Move if you only have 4 MF (ie a squad without a leader can't do this).

title: concealment in CC
question:
It´s the german turn. If 2 german squads advanced into a wood hex with a russian concealed squad you put a CC counter on. 
There are no ambush.

1) If the russian don´t attack i CC, and the germans get 11 with no effect does the CC counter stay on?
2) What opportunities have the russian squad in the next russian turn: May it fire, move, advanced?
3) What opportunities have the german squads in the next russian turn: May it fire?
4) If they do nothing at all the next turn will there be another CC with ambush?
author: Nslcole
consensus_answer:
1) If the russian don´t attack i CC, and the germans get 11 with no effect does the CC counter stay on?

n/a. However if the situation were different and the CC counter were placed, e.g. the Germans got into the hex by unloading from a vehicle [D6.5], the red-on-white color coding indicates that the CC counter is removed at the end of the CCPh [A.12, A3.8, probably also in the ASOP but I did not check].

2) What opportunities have the russian squad in the next russian turn: May it fire, move, advanced?

Because a Melee did not form in the previous CCPh, the Soviet squad may do anything it normally could, including fire (but limited by A7.212), move, etc.

3) What opportunities have the german squads in the next russian turn: May it fire?

Again without a melee the world is the German squads' oysters.

4) If they do nothing at all the next turn will there be another CC with ambush? 

There would be another round of CC but no ambush because no unit advanced in [A11.4].

If 2 german squads advanced into a wood hex with a russian concealed squad you put a CC counter on. 

This is not one of the times you place a CC counter. It's not harmful and some players place one in the APh but there is no rule instructing you to do so.

title: HIP and squad equivalents
question: SSR rule says ≤ 1 squad equivalent may set up using HIP. So does this mean two half squads and three leaders could all set up using HIP?
author: Sparrowfalls
consensus_answer:
It seems they wouldn't have made the rule that  ≤ 4 SMC are equal to 0 squad equivalents if it wasn't meant to be played that way.You are mixing up the rules and an SSR, so you are using flawed logics to press your point.

The debate is not about the rules of squad equivalency - nobody is contesting it - which isn't confined go HIP limitations (e.g. think vehicular PP).
Typically, an SSR - which is crafted for a soecific scenario - may miss some side effects allowed by the rules.
As said, your suggestion is legal.
Did the SSR designer think of it? I have doubts. 
I don't think I was pressing a point as much as curious why it's problematic to play RAW in this case. 🙂
However, in the spirit of pressing my point, I would say in the context of Defiance on Hill 30, it would make sense to word the SSR the way they did because it enables a SMC to be designated a spotter for the US mortar and start HIP. This also neatly explains the reasoning for the departure from other SSR's that word HIP as squad equivalents plus stacked leader. 🙂
Though, hmmm.... there would be no reason to say squad equivalents plus stacked leader if less than 4 leaders count as zero units. So, yeah, you may be right about it not being the intent.🤔
With all rule sets, though, my goal is to arrive at the correct answer rather than ramming through my point of view and I take seriously the advice to discuss this in advance with an opponent since they may not see it the same way. 😀

title: Human Wave unit starts in crest status: how does it move?
question: A Human Wave unit starts in crest status of a Gully. Can it both exit its crest status and move to the next hex in one impulse, or does it exit crest status in one impulse then move to the next hex in a second impulse?
author: jrvjrv
consensus_answer:
You exit a foxhole in the same hex as the foxhole itself; if you were Human Waving out of a foxhole, that would clearly be a 1MF impulse (unless other members of the HW had an irreducible 2+ MF expenditure).  However, when you leave Crest Status you're either going into the depression or into another hex; there isn't an intermediate still-in-the-hex-but-not-in-Crest-Status state.  

Well there sort-of is and sort-of isn't "an intermediate still-in-the-hex-but-not-in-Crest-Status state" because the unit exiting crest can be attacked by DFF in the Depression hex without benefit of crest TEM [B20.93], and if it breaks/pins it drops INTO the Depression.

The issue is further clouded by the Human Wave rules where a unit may do exactly one of exiting an entrenchment or moving to a forward hex [A25.232]. 

This also has some implications for regular movement. If exiting the crest status and moving to the adjacent hex are separate expenditures, I can exit, see what the result of DFF is, then choose which hex to move into, whereas if it's one expenditure I can't delay my decision until after I see the result of DFF.

Anyway you see my difficulty at least. Maybe I should form a support group.

"Crest Infantry may exit the Depression hex to a non-Depression hex along the same side of the Depression which they occupy as if they were leaving a foxhole* (one MF & COT or normal APh capability)."

(*emphasis mine)

title: Defensive Fire Opportunities vs. Infantry Overrun?
question:
The German stack in Y14 attempts to use its Leader Bonus to Assault Move conducting an Infantry OVR [A4.15] of the American Heroic Leader (which by Scenario Special Rule has 2FP) in building hex Y13. 
 

Assuming that the German stack passes the requisite NTC check to be allowed to conduct the Infantry Overrun in the first place, and ignoring potential defensive fire from Z12, how many times does the American Heroic Leader get to fire as the Germans move into his hex? Four defensive fire attack opportunities sounds right.

title: Stack of units with leader entering a minefield
question:
What is the procedure followed when a stack of squads with a leader enters a minefield.

The example refers only to unit. We played it that each unit is rolled for individually with the leader checking first. We did not apply leader modifier to the minefield check.

No terrain or movement modifiers apply to the check on any unit but does the leader check first and apply his modifier to other results of their minefield checks.
author: csonson
consensus_answer:

I describe it as "ancient" because mmp declared all q&a as defunct I think with the v2 rulebook. In theory they put everything they wanted in the rules, and anything left out was, perhaps, deliberate. It would seem to me that the drive train would need to be engaged to turn the vehicle, and that would make it susceptible to potential reliability issues. 

The turret probably would not require drive train engagement for a TCA change, but I think a VCA change would.

Thanks!

Regards,

JB
author: gmdjeb
consensus_answer:
Per Chapter D footnote 5 the Mechanical Reliability DR is a game mechanic meant to represent not the literal seizure of the engine or similar but rather an abstract notion that in reality probably meant the vehicle was not even present on the battlefield. As such the game designer wants to keep the number of such DRs made to a "reasonable" level, and so decided to only make the DR on start DRs or Motion attempts. You have to view it more as an abstract game mechanic than a literal representation of the physics of engines or drive trains.

Amazing what one learns by reading the footnotes! Although in this case I think the note is just being too smart:

A more realistic rule would be to simply make a dr at the start of a scenario which a vehicle with poor mechanical reliability would have to pass in order to be included in the scenario. The drawback to such a system is that play balance can be destroyed before the game even begins.

Destroyed is a very strong word, and who knows if it would more more realistic! (ASLRB words, not mine). Designers can set the balance according to the rule itself. My impression is that the DR riffs quite well with the idea that the engine might seize up when you start it. 

How the actual odds of stalling relate to the odds of rolling boxcars is left for optional homework.😀

author: neo.colpaert

Now, if you are in LOS of the enemy, normal movement through woods will lose "?", though advance and assault movement will not.

author: Fly by Night

title: Remove DM during Melee?
question:
A broken MMP Guard has a DM marker and it is attacked by its prisoners during CCPh.
Both units remain so they are now in Melee (I guess).
As I understand it, unarmed units do not force DM status.
Is the DM marker removed in the next RPh or is it not as the unit is in Melee?
author: esparver73
consensus_answer:
A broken MMP Guard has a DM marker and it is attacked by its prisoners during CCPh.
Both units remain so they are now in Melee (I guess).
As I understand it, unarmed units do not force DM status.
Is the DM marker removed in the next RPh or is it not as the unit is in Melee?
I think as written the DM counter is removed in the RPh as long as some outside condition does not leave it on (e.g. being ADJACENT to an armed enemy unit, being in Open Ground [A10.531] and in normal range of KEU, etc.). Removal of the DM is not an activity by the unit, and so A11.15 would not prevent it. The unit would regain DM status when the prisoner attacks again in CC. This might be seen as a flaw in the rules but since the unit can't rally while in Melee (other than by HoB result) and since it will regain its DM status in the CCPh from the prisoner attack if a flaw it isn't really a major one.
Terrain also plays a factor. If the occupied hex is building or woods, the DM counter must be removed. Otherwise it is the players choice.

title: DFPh Final Fire with MG marked as First Fire
question:
During the MPh a stack of an MMP with an MG fires its MG (not the IFP) without ROF and is marked First Fire. No more fires during the MPh.
In the DFPh, can the MMP fire without the constraints of the First Fire marker on the MG (to a non-adjacent hex)?
author: esparver73
consensus_answer:
During the MPh a stack of an MMP with an MG fires its MG (not the IFP) without ROF and is marked First Fire. No more fires during the MPh.
In the DFPh, can the MMP fire without the constraints of the First Fire marker on the MG (to a non-adjacent hex)?
I'm going to assume you mean "MMC" instead of "MMP." MMP can always fire because they control the rules and can change them as they desire.

This depends on if the MMC is a squad or not. If it is a squad per A7.351 it does not give up its inherent FP when it fires exactly one SW. This fire capability is independent from its use of that SW. Per A.15 a unit may fire in both enemy MPh and DFPh without being considered as having fired in two phases. The "first fire" counter is regrettable in that when placed it is ambiguous for a squad as to whether just one SW capability has been used or both fire capabilities. Per a q&a these are used independently:

"A8.4 During the defensive fire phase, a squad & MMG want to make fire attacks. The squad (only) is marked with a def first fire counter. Is it legal for the squad to fire his MMG at full FP vs a non-ADJACENT unit and then (provided it didn’t cower) have the squad use final fire at an ADJACENT unit? Would the answer be different if the situation was reversed? (MMG only is marked with a first fire counter, squad fires at non adjacent unit and then MMG final fires at adjacent unit.)"
A. Yes. No."

Various third party producers and now MMP have printed "First Fire SW" and "First Fire Inherent" counters that fix the flaw and allow squads to be marked unambiguously.

One thing it has taken me many years to realize is that fire during the DFPh is not exactly like fire during the enemy MPh. During the enemy MPh a MG that is marked with First Fire (and the inherent not) can be fired again either with or without the inherent, but then all fire capabilities are marked Final Fire. During the DFPh a MG that is marked with first fire (and the inherent not marked) can fire at an ADJACENT target, then the inherent can be fired after the MG as normal fire, i.e. not necessarily against the same or even an ADJACENT target and not at half FP.

As stated. Although the inherent fire is not necessarily against the same target, it might be. The MG, being marked with a first fire counter, would have to be against an ADJACENT target. title: Hidden Fortification in solo play
question:
The rules inform how to handle HIP in solo play (A12.3) but I can't find anything about hidden Fortifications (pre-designate secretly buildings as "fortified").
Does someone have a tip on how to adapt this to solo play, please?
author: neo.colpaert
consensus_answer:
Due to health reasons, I only play ASL solo. My method for anything hidden is to identify alternate locations, the exact number depends on the map, avenues of approach, etc. I then assigned probabilities to each location, usually uniform but sometimes variable depending on the likelihood I think appropriate. The probabilities for the locations must total 100%. As an example of variable probabilities for three locations I might have them be a d6:1-3, d6:4-5, and d6:6. Uniform would be d6:1-2, 3-4, 5-6.

When a location comes into an enemy LOS, I roll. If the roll passes (say, a roll of 2 on a d6:1-3), the hidden unit appears - if that's what's supposed to happen. It may just mean that the hidden unit can take a shot and then reveal itself. But the hidden thing is there. Usually, a ? is placed.

If the roll fails, the hidden thing is in one of the remaining locations. I adjust probabilities for those locations so they total 100% and play on.

I used this method for hidden squads, vehicles, fortifications, and so on. I've found over the years that this method works really well. It keeps some tension in the game as to what's where and makes solo play more enjoyable. 
That's what I had in mind as well, Rick. You can perhaps alter the chance of finding a hidden fortification when you first find nothing. The 1-3 yes can then become a 1-4 yes after 2 or 3 buildings.

title: Flame Tanks
question:
Couple of questions on situations involving Flame tanks.

1)  Can you use Flame Tanks with Bounding Fire?  So, can they move to a target, stop, Flame on, then start and move on?  From what I have been able to decipher, this is allowed, but at half FP.

2) In regards to Flaming Concealed Units, is this at Half FP also?

3) Can Flame Tanks use Intensive Fire?
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
Couple of questions on situations involving Flame tanks.

1)  Can you use Flame Tanks with Bounding Fire?  So, can they move to a target, stop, Flame on, then start and move on?  From what I have been able to decipher, this is allowed, but at half FP.

2) In regards to Flaming Concealed Units, is this at Half FP also?

3) Can Flame Tanks use Intensive Fire?

1) Yes. A flame tank is not halved for bounding first fire [D3.31], but is halved for non-stopped/Motion fire [D2.42]. For the example you give since the tank Stopped it fires at full FP during the MPh (but could be halved for other reasons, e.g. concealment, long range). 
2) Yes [A22.1].
3) Not with their flame thrower. Only Ordnance can use Intensive Fire. A Churchill Crocodile could use Intensive Fire using its 75mm MA, but that's probably not what you meant. And why can't it use Sustained Fire?

question: A Broken Squad in a Foxhole cannot rout out of the Foxhole and into an adjacent building if there is an enemy unit adjacent to that Foxhole, correct?  Spending 1MF to come out of the Foxhole is bringing them closer to the enemy unit, therefore eliminated, yes?
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
Hmm, I understand the combined MF, which is detailed in the Foxholes section to avoid Interdiction, but being adjacent to the Known Enemy unit as it spends the first of those 3MF to do so, should demand elimination, no?  Is there a rules reference I'm missing?It expends the 3MF in the building hex it is routing to.
Hmm, you seem to think that it expends the exit MF and the building MF in the Foxhole's hex, which is quite a strange way to read the rule - no need for another reference, all is clearly written in A27.41.

title: Area Fire on Concealed Unit in a Foxhole
question:
Just want to make sure we played this right.

My opponent Fired on a Concealed Squad in a Foxhole with the +2 DRM for shooting at Concealed units.  He hit.  So its still Area Fire, which is then halved on the IFT Column. So now the +2 for the Foxhole comes in as a DRM on the IFT roll to see if any result would remove the Concealment, correct?
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
My opponent Fired on a Concealed Squad in a Foxhole with the +2 DRM for shooting at Concealed units.  He hit.  So its still Area Fire, which is then halved on the IFT Column. So now the +2 for the Foxhole comes in as a DRM on the IFT roll to see if any result would remove the Concealment, correct?
First this sounds as if the firing unit is attacking with ordnance. If that is correct, the firing unit has to choose a Target Type, or if he fails to declare a target type, C.9 will be engaged and the Target Type will be chosen by rule.

You can use any of the three Target Types against any target, concealed or not. There are advantages and disadvantages to each. First the Target Type determines what is hit. The Vehicle Target Type targets exactly one vehicle. So if you use the Vehicle Target Type against a unit in a foxhole you probably aren't going to hit anything. But there is no rules reason you couldn't declare the attack as such. In a situation such as you have you will probably choose the Infantry or Area Target Type instead.

If you choose the Infantry Target Type there is a +2 TH DRM for concealed (Case K) as well as a +2 TH DRM for foxhole TEM (Case Q). If there is any acquisition that applies only to unconcealed units. Plus any other TH DRM, e.g. target size, armor leader, point-blank range, etc. If hit the target is attacked at the ordnance's *full* FP, i.e. not halved [C.4]. If the target loses concealment (or if there is another, unconcealed target in the Location), then acquisition is placed/improved.

If you choose the Area Target Type there is a +2 TH DRM for concealed (Case K). The +2 DRM for TEM is taken on the effects DR [C6.2, C3.331]. Plus any other TH DRM as applicable, but note that point-blank range is n/a for Area Target Type. If hit the target is attacked at half FP for Area Target Type but not halved again for concealment The penalty for concealment is the TH DRM. The +2 DRM for TEM (foxhole) now applies to the effects DR. Regardless of whether there was any hit or effect, acquisition is placed/improved.

To emphasize per C.4 FP is *not* halved for ordnance for concealment. Concealment is a TH DRM for ordnance instead.

replies.body:
Depends... if he fired on Area Target type, then you are correct.  The +2 for concealment applies on the To Hit and the +2 TEM applies on the effects. He can also gain ACQ from this shot.

If he fired on the Infantry Target Type (or did not specify), then the shot applies the +2 for concealment /and/ the +2 for TEM to the To Hit roll, but if he hits then the effects are at full effect with no TEM.  However, if he does not strip concealment then he gains no ACQ (whether he hits or not).

At least this is my understanding...

Plus any other TH DRM as applicable, but note that point-blank range is n/a for Area Target Type. If hit the target is attacked at half FP for Area Target Type but not halved again for concealment The penalty for concealment is the TH DRM. The +2 DRM for TEM (foxhole) now applies to the effects DR. Regardless of whether there was any hit or effect, acquisition is placed/improved.

To emphasize per C.4 FP is *not* halved for ordnance for concealment. Concealment is a TH DRM for ordnance instead.

This goes to something that is quite often confused. Area Target Type is a choice made when firing ordnance. Area Fire is a combat condition where for some reason the weapon firing has difficulty. Area Fire can apply to both ordnance and non-ordnance attacks. You can use the Area Target Type without Area Fire being applicable. You can have a situation that involves Area Fire without using the Area Target Type. They are *not* synonymous nor even related, although it is somewhat common to use the Area Target Type when firing at concealed units because that allows the firing unit to gain acquisition even if the target's concealment is not lost.

Things that cause Area Fire: Concealment, fire out of stream or marsh, fire from crest through non-crest hexside, Spraying Fire, Snap Shot, Dash and some others mentioned in the index. There may be yet others that are not in the index. The cases covered by Area Fire (note again, not Area Target Type) are a real hodge-podge of odd cases. Many do not ever apply to ordnance, e.g. Spraying Fire or Snap Shot. Some apply to particular ordnance or with particular rules, e.g. most ordnance cannot fire from a stream but LATW can (as Area Fire, i.e. with a TH DRM per C.4), and most ordnance cannot fire from crest (but some can, B20.95) of a sunken road, gully or stream but can fire from crest from a wadi [F5.4].

As a quick summation, Area Target Type and Area Fire have similar-sounding names but are completely different things. Don't cross the streams.

I had no idea that you could choose Infantry Target Type on a Concealed Unit. I can only assume that this is rarely done since it makes it that much harder To Hit. That and you don't get to place an Acq.

Getting acq is a frequent reason. But there's no difference in ITT vs ATT for DRM for concealment. Both get a +2 DRM for case K. Now that can make a difference based on where you end up net for DRM. As one simple example imagine firing at a concealed unit in brush at range six. The TH# for ITT is eight and for ATT it's seven. With the +2 for concealment that's a hit on the six for the ITT but a five for the ATT. Given that, ITT may be the better choice. But if the target is in stone building instead of brush the DR needed for ITT is three but still five for the ATT. Of course the TEM now applies to the halved effects DR, so depending on your size gun the ATT or ITT might be the better choice.

And since you get the point-blank fire DRM for ITT and not for ATT, if you are making an attack with an AFV the ITT can make sense when you run the AFV up adjacent to the target. The +2 TH DRM for concealed is offset by -2 for point-blank range, and if you get a hit you get full FP.  It probably pays off best when the gun is relatively small. For instance a 37mm Gun firing against a stone building the effects of a hit will be a two FP attack up three using the ATT, while the ITT will be four FP flat. Of course the ITT will use TEM on the TH DR and the ATT will allow gaining acquisition, so it's not all sunshine and lollipops.

title: prisoner escaping from broken guard with other units present.
question:
During the previous enemy turn a German guard halfsquad broke and routed with its prisoner to M6. The prisoner took a NTC to escape in the CCPh but failed. During the German turn the concealed 4-6-7 and an unconcealed 8-1 assault move into the hex. 

Is there any way for the GO 4-6-7 and/or 8-1 to recover and/or attack the prisoner of the broken guard, given that the prisoner is not escaping? 

During the CCPh the prisoner rolls its NTC to escape. This time it succeeds. Am I correct there are no ambush drs even though there is a concealed unit in the Location because the point at which the escape NTC is rolled [ASOP8.14B] happens after the step for Ambush [ASOP8.12B]?
author: jrvjrv
consensus_answer:
A20.5: "...are either transferred above another guarding unit in the same manner as a SW (4.431) or abandoned."

A4.431 only allows transfer between GO units, though A4.44 lets a GO leader Recover a SW from a broken unit. I was thinking that might be extended to prisoners, but taking a look at the rules, I think not.

Ambushes are easier: They only happen if a unit advances into the hex, and since the prisoners didn't advance, there's no Ambush.

If it is 'as a SW', I can't see why the GO leader wouldn't be able to 'recover' the prisoner per the normal SW recovery/transfer rules.
There is a difference between recovery and transfer.
The rules state "transfer" in A20.55 and that is between GO unpinned units.
Such is not the case here.

title: Firepower 1 halved
question: When a unit has Firepower 1 and it's halved again, does it still retain firepower?
author: neo.colpaert
consensus_answer:
When a unit has Firepower 1 and it's halved again, does it still retain firepower?
To expand on previous answers, it probably depends on why this is important to you. If a unit/firegroup wants to attack on the IFT, and it does not have at least one FP, its attack would not be sufficient to use any column on the IFT table (attacks use the column equal to or to the left of their total FP [A7.3]) and so the attack would automatically fail. It's an interesting question whether this automatically failing attack would still get a LOS string (which might matter if you had something, say ordnance, that also wanted to attack); I would say it would as long as the attack was not entirely out of range, but I don't think the rules cover this exact situation. But if a unit that by itself had < one FP firegrouped with another unit or units, and their combined strength was ≥ one FP, then the attack would be performed normally, and in that sense the unit's FP is "retained." If you have eight pinned 1-2-7 vehicle crews firing at a concealed target in the AFPh without using opportunity fire, their total FP is one, and they have a legitimate attack on the IFT. In CC it is the ratio of FP that is important, so for example a unit with fractional FP can still attack other units in Close Combat. For example a unit with ½ FP for attack (say a pinned SMC alone) could attack another unit with one FP (say an enemy 1-2-7 vehicle crew) at ½-to-1 or 1-to-2 odds. In the context of Rout a unit with < one FP (e.g. a pinned 1-2-7 vehicle crew) is still an armed unit and so can't be routed towards [A10.51] but could not interdict [A10.532]. In sum it depends on the context of your question to say whether the unit "retains firepower."
In this case it was a single unit whose already reduced firepower of 1 was again halved due to area fire and could not be combined with other units in a FG. No shot possible then, I suppose.

replies.body: Nope.  Falls off the left side of the IFT chart.

It had 0.25 FP.
Useless if alone (less than 1 FP has no effect), but added to other FP of a Fire Group, it may help.
In CC it would still count for forming odds.

author: Fly by Night

A Hull Down Tank behind a Stone Wall, Crew Exposed.  What are they DRM's for an IFT attack?  +2 for the Stone Wall and +2 for the Armor? Or just one or the other?
PRC aren't eligible for hexside terrain (mostly): " PRC [EXC: Motorcyclists] never receive a TEM for a wall/hedge" [B9.3].

replies.body:
A Hull Down Tank behind a Stone Wall, Crew Exposed.  What are they DRM's for an IFT attack?  +2 for the Stone Wall and +2 for the Armor? Or just one or the other?
PRC aren't eligible for hexside terrain (mostly): " PRC [EXC: Motorcyclists] never receive a TEM for a wall/hedge" [B9.3].

title: Observation: LATW with their own TH table still pick a Target Type
question:
For a long time I have had it in my mind that a LATW with its own TH table (e.g. BAZ, PF, etc.) does not pick a Target Type. I thought the choosing of a Target Type was synonymous with using the standard TH tables. I recently researched this and found I was mistaken. Despite using their own TH table these weapons do choose a target type. This is not directly stated that I see but hinted at in C13.1, "LATW may never use the Area Target Type." 

This is an interesting question when there is a AFV and a non-vehicle (e.g. a Gun) that are vulnerable to the ammunition being fired by the LATW, say. HEAT. For some reason I had it in my mind that for example, potentially, a BAZ might fire at a Location with both an AFV and a Gun and hit both. Per above this is not possible because the BAZ has to choose either ITT or VTT, which will prevent it from hitting one or the other.

I never researched this before because it was so rare that there might be two eligible targets of different types in the same Location that it never came up as an issue. But having finally looked at it, the answer makes sense. If no Target Type is announced then C.9 applies, but most often the situation never arises. In the future I will try to remember to get my opponent to specify his Target Type before he rolls his TH DR where this applies.

title: ASL Rules for original Squad Leader
question: Can you use the ASL rules with the original components from SL, CoI, GIAV?    I found a set of mint rules, but don't want to spend the money on Valor at this point.
author: PinehillJoe
consensus_answer:
I agree with others here that it would be very difficult to play with ASL rules using only SL-GIA counters. The missing info markers alone might drive you batty, not to mention GIA will not give you all the proper HS counters you will need. However, if you were up for all the DYI modifications (an extensive list to be sure) in order to play a few scenarios (probably solo) to see if full ASL is for you without having to cough up $100+ for BV, then go for it. MMP has a resource that lets you DL Jim Stahler's conversions of some of the classic SL scenarios to ASL. Most (if not all) use the original SL boards 1-4.

Again, I am only talking about testing the waters of ASL. If you intend to take the plunge (and eventually play FTF with live opponents), using the classic SL kit just won't cut the mustard. Also, keep in mind JR V's comment that online VASL is an option if you already have the ASLRB.

title: Assault Move and Concealment
question: Almost sure the answer is no, but need to verify.  You cannot Assault Move into a Foxhole from and Adjacent hex and maintain Concealment, even if said Foxhole is in an Orchard, correct?  Spending 2MF before moving only works for Routing into a Foxhole to avoid Interdiction, correct?
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
Almost sure the answer is no, but need to verify.  You cannot Assault Move into a Foxhole from and Adjacent hex and maintain Concealment, even if said Foxhole is in an Orchard, correct?  Spending 2MF before moving only works for Routing into a Foxhole to avoid Interdiction, correct?

As long as it doesn't move in Open Ground (relative to some enemy unit, so the A10.531 definition of Open Ground, not the terrain type) and doesn't perform some other sort of action (e.g. recovery, throw smoke grenades, etc.), assault move allows a unit to maintain concealment. A unit will maintain concealment if it assault moves out of an entrenchment into its own orchard hex then into an adjacent orchard hex.

You can do this as assault movement because inside an entrenchment and outside are the same Location. You cannot exit a pillbox and then move to an adjacent location as assault movement because that's two Locations (unless there is a trench/bunker situation).

I'm not sure what "spending 2MF before moving" means. It only costs one MF to exit an entrenchment (EXC: A-T ditch). Also I consider all use of MF in the MPh as "moving." So recovery, throwing smoke grenades, using stairs, entering/exiting crest or entrenchment, etc. is all "moving" to me. This is not a formal definition, so perhaps you think of it a different way.

title: Another Concealed Tank Question
question:
So we are playing Hatten in Flames Scenario #6 now, and another Concealed Tank situation came up.  Actually two.  My Opponent has the Americans and had one of his Tanks Hidden in Place in one of the Forest Hex's.  SSR gave him the "as a Gun" bonus, so his first shot that killed one of Pz IV's enabled him to come on board still Concealed.
I was able to get a half squad and then one of the HT's adjacent to it in the Movement Phase, which he chose not to shoot his AAMG or turn his turret to engage, knowing this would remove his Concealed Status and my Panther already had a -2 Area Acq on him.
Question one:
If the half squad Infantry Advanced Fired on it, it would be at half FP (Area Fire), but would it be with a +1DRM for the Forest, or a +2 for the Armor benefit, which I wouldn't know about yet unless I got a result?

Question two:
 What happens if an Infantry unit Advances into a hex with a Concealed AFV?  Its unknown, so I wouldn't think a PAATC is required.  Or would a PAATC be required to then engage it in the CC round or since its Concealed, does it get all the benefits that a Concealed enemy Infantry unit would gain if I advanced into its hex?

TEM DRM vs CE DRM is defender's choice, D5.31.

Question two:
 What happens if an Infantry unit Advances into a hex with a Concealed AFV?  Its unknown, so I wouldn't think a PAATC is required.  Or would a PAATC be required to then engage it in the CC round or since its Concealed, does it get all the benefits that a Concealed enemy Infantry unit would gain if I advanced into its hex?
Per A11.16 PAATC only applies for an unconcealed vehicle. Note that the vehicle might not be Known (to the advancing unit) because, perhaps, it is out of los in bypass, but what matters for PAATC is whether the vehicle is concealed.

Once in the Location no PAATC is made in the CCPh. You would roll for ambush, which you would do anyway because it's a woods hex. The tank would get +2 for vehicle and -2 for concealed.

CC is sequential because of the vehicle. If there is no ambush the vehicle would retain concealment and the enemy infantry would attack first. Because the target is concealed, that gives a -1 to the CCV for the infantry's attack.

title: ESB & BFF
question: A tracked vehicle uses its entire MP allotment to enter a hex. It makes an ESB DR for one MP to stop and rolls a final twelve or more. It is immobilized. Can it use Bounding First Fire in its new, immobilized (i.e. stopped) state?
author: jrvjrv
consensus_answer:
A tracked vehicle uses its entire MP allotment to enter a hex. It makes an ESB DR for one MP to stop and rolls a final twelve or more. It is immobilized. Can it use Bounding First Fire in its new, immobilized (i.e. stopped) state?
I am pretty sure that failing an ESB DR ends the vehicles movement. If not, then I see no reason Bounding First Fire cannot occur.
Bog has a statement that after a bog result the vehicle ends its MPh [D8.21]. ESB does not have a similar statement that I see.
