So I don't quite see that ESB would change that....

title: Radio Breaks Down, when is FFE:C removed?
question:
A unit's radio breaks down at the start of his PFPh.  OBA is already an FFE:C.  When is the FFE:C removed?

I believe from reading the rules, the FFE:C is removed at the end of the following RPh, so the FFE:C stays on board this turn.  No attack rolls are made during the PFPh, but if a unit moves into the FFE:C area or becomes more vulnerable within the FFE:C this turn, it is attacked.

Is that correct?

Thank you,
author: Viking_CTO
consensus_answer:
A unit's radio breaks down at the start of his PFPh.  OBA is already an FFE:C.  When is the FFE:C removed?

I believe from reading the rules, the FFE:C is removed at the end of the following RPh, so the FFE:C stays on board this turn.  No attack rolls are made during the PFPh, but if a unit moves into the FFE:C area or becomes more vulnerable within the FFE:C this turn, it is attacked.

I don't think that is what should happen, but it's difficult to extract that from the rules

C1.34 "At the start of each friendly PFPh/DFPh in which an Observer has gained/maintained Radio Contact and had that battery's FFE:C onboard, he must attempt to gain Battery Access as per 1.21. Regardless of the outcome, that previous Fire Mission is now Canceled."

My belief is that in C1.34 "regardless of the outcome" includes cases where the Observer does not attempt radio contact or fails. The "failure" is both to gain radio contact and/or to gain battery access. Then the Fire Mission for the FFE:C is now Canceled and is removed per C1.35. I find it difficult to believe that if radio contact fails or is not even attempted the FFE:C remains on board but if radio contact is achieved the FFE:C is removed. But it's definitely worth a q&a.

That would definitely make sense, but as you say, its hard to extract that from the rules. C1.22 muddies this further (for me anyway):
"The involuntary loss of Contact does not automatically cause loss
of Battery Access, but failure to regain Contact in the next friendly PFPh/
DFPh (whichever comes first) will prevent the Conversion, Correction, and
voluntary Cancellation of that battery’s onboard SR/FFE counter; the FFE
would continue to be resolved as per 1.5-.51, and, if still existing at the end
of the RPh in which it is a FFE:C, would at that time be Cancelled (1.34);
a SR would remain in place. 

Thank you JR.

title: Re-assembly and Concealment loss
question: So I'm putting my MMG's and HMG's back together in my Defensive Fire Phase after jumping out of the Halftracks last turn.  Two squads were Unconcealed when disembarking, but the third squad was not, which then advanced into a building.  I can't find in the rules that re-assembly of a Support Weapon is a Concealment loss action, but I'm thinking since its in the Defensive Fire Phase, it does lose its Concealment, Yes?
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
So I'm putting my MMG's and HMG's back together in my Defensive Fire Phase after jumping out of the Halftracks last turn.  Two squads were Unconcealed when disembarking, but the third squad was not, which then advanced into a building.  I can't find in the rules that re-assembly of a Support Weapon is a Concealment loss action, but I'm thinking since its in the Defensive Fire Phase, it does lose its Concealment, Yes?
SW assembly is generally considered to fall under the "any other action" [A12.141]. There is no specific statement of assembly but it seems the most likely answer. ASL does not precisely define actions so if you are strongly against this interpretation the only option I know would be to submit a q&a.

replies.body:
Yes, it's a concealment loss activity.

And you won't find it in the rules as a concealment loss activity, rather there is a list of the things that are NOT concealment loss.
On the Chapter A Concealment chart, re-assembly is not listed as an exception to losing Concealment. So yes, loses concealment.

title: Can a unit on a Hillock see past a Hillock summit down to ground level?
question:
Can Baddington see the wreck?

I have my doubts because of F6.43.  It requires a unit to be "higher than the topmost height of an intervening hillock hex" (I interpolate:  a hillock summit is a hillock hex (F6.6)) "in order to have a LOS past that hillock hex to an elevation one or more full levels lower than that hillock hex's topmost height".

In the image, Baddington is at level 1/2.  The intervening hillock hex is the hillock summit, the topmost height of which is level 1.  The wreck is at level 0.

I think Baddington would need to be at level 1 1/2 or higher to see the wreck through the hillock summit.

Is that right?
author: Malcolm C
consensus_answer:
Can Baddington see the wreck?

I have my doubts because of F6.43.  It requires a unit to be "higher than the topmost height of an intervening hillock hex" (I interpolate:  a hillock summit is a hillock hex (F6.6)) "in order to have a LOS past that hillock hex to an elevation one or more full levels lower than that hillock hex's topmost height".

In the image, Baddington is at level 1/2.  The intervening hillock hex is the hillock summit, the topmost height of which is level 1.  The wreck is at level 0.

I think Baddington would need to be at level 1 1/2 or higher to see the wreck through the hillock summit.

Is that right?

As far as I understand the hillock rules a unit "behind" a hillock (i.e. adjacent to and at the base level of the hillock and ½ level below the top of the hillock) cannot see beyond that hillock to a lower elevation. Per F6.43, "A  unit must be higher than the topmost height of an intervening hillock hex in order to have a LOS past that hillock hex to [a target hex] elevation one or more full levels lower than that hillock hex's topmost height," where I have introduced the phrases "viewing" and "a target hex" to give the two hexes names for clarity. In your EX the hillock is at level one and the target is at level zero, i.e. the target hex is one full level below the topmost height of the hillock, and the viewing unit is *not* higher than the intervening hillock, so there is no LOS. 

The fact that the viewing unit is on a hillock itself and the intervening hillock is actually a hillock summit is covered by F6.6, "A Hillock Summit is treated as a normal hillock that rises from Level ½ instead of from Level 0," i.e. we can reason about such a situation as if the hillock summit was just a regular hillock. 

As you say the viewing unit would have to be above that hillock to see past the hillock (summit) to a level at least one full level below the summit. Technically that could be any amount above (a quarter level, a sixty-fourth), but since the smallest interval we have had to date is a half level, as of today the viewer would have to be at level one-and-a-half to see the wreck.

title: Clearance q&a
question:
Clearance activities in ASL are a hodge-podge of slightly different procedures with the commonality of making a Clearance DR [B24.7]. There are differences in which phases they can be declared, whether they require MF/MP or not and in which phase the DR is made. When I wrote this question I was in particular interested in whether units under No Move could attempt to cut a jungle path [G2.7, apparently allowed], but I added a bunch of other questions:

>> May a clearance task that requires expenditure of MF be
>> performed by a unit without Freedom of Movement?
>
>
  No.
>
>
>> May a clearance task that does not require MF expenditure
>> be declared during the friendly MPh? During the friendly DFPh?
>
  Yes. Yes. 
>
>
>> Some clearance tasks (e.g. rubble, fire, and roadblock) are subject to
>> Hazardous Movement. Per B24.7 a unit is engaged in the clearance task
>> "until it makes a Clearance DR, is pinned, or is no longer Good Order."
>> Does the end of engagement in the clearance task also end the unit being
>> subject to the Hazardous Movement DR?
>
  Yes.
>
>
>> Flame clearance is both declared and performed in same the friendly MPh
>> or the same friendly DFPh. It does not seem to require any MF
>> expenditure [B24.72]. The unit is subject to Hazardous Movement
>> [B24.72], but since the declaration and the Clearance DR are performed
>> in the same phase without the expenditure of MF, there would seem to be
>> no opportunity to fire on a unit trying to clear flame subject to the
>> Hazardous Movement DRM, assuming the unit is not subject to Hazardous
>> Movement once its engagement in the clearance task ends.
>
  Correct.
>
>> Does a unit attempting to clear flame expend any MF?
>
  No.
>
>> If not can such a unit be fired on anyway as DFF before it rolls its
>> Clearance DR and if so, how many times?
>
  No.
>
>> Is there any possibility to fire at a unit making flame clearance during its DFPh?
>
  No.
>

title: LOS Hindrance - Would a Squad in a foxhole count?
question:
Here's the situation.  I have a Squad in a Foxhole, which gets a +2.  There are two enemy squads in two adjacent hex's of the Foxhole.  Those two enemy squads are also shrouded in +3 Smoke and one of those enemy Squads are under a CX. 

Question:  Does the +4 for shooting out of the Smoke combine with the +2 TEM for the Foxhole for a +6 total and negate the possibility of shot according to B.10?
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
Here's the situation.  I have a Squad in a Foxhole, which gets a +2.  There are two enemy squads in two adjacent hex's of the Foxhole.  Those two enemy squads are also shrouded in +3 Smoke and one of those enemy Squads are under a CX. 

Question:  Does the +4 for shooting out of the Smoke combine with the +2 TEM for the Foxhole for a +6 total and negate the possibility of shot according to B.10?
There are many kinds of DRMs on the IFT. Hindrances [A6.7] are those DRM that are marked as such on the terrain chart "LOS Obstacle/Hindrance" column and/or in the body of the rules. SMOKE is a hindrance per A24.2. On the terrain chart you will find that entrenchments are not an obstacle or a hindrance, i.e. they have "—" listed in the LOS Obstacle/Hindrance column, but have a TEM (under the TEM/Indirect column) of +2/+4, i.e. it is an IFT DRM but not a hindrance. CX is not listed on the terrain chart nor is it indicated as a hindrance in the rules so it is an IFT DRM but not a hindrance either. As noted above B.10 does not use any IFT DRM but those that are hindrances.

replies.body: A foxhole (and being cx) is not a Hindrance.  The +6 is for Hindrances (only) and then it blocks LOS.

Ah, Ok.  So if both Squads end up shooting at the German Squad in the Foxhole, it will be a combined attack of 24 +7 (+4 for shooting out of Smoke, +2 for the Foxhole and +1 for the CX'd Squad), Correct?
Correct if 1) the squads have a combined twelve FP and are shooting with Point Blank Fire [A7.21] in either the PFPh, the DFPh or as DFF during the enemy MPh and are not halved for any form of Area Fire and 2) those are the only DRM that apply.

There are some terrains types that are both a hindrance and a TEM. Graveyards and crags are two examples. As far as I know there are none that are in-hex hindrances (like SMOKE, A24.2) and also have TEM, so usually only one aspect of their terrain behavior applies to any one attack.

Although, depending on whether you consider it one attack or two, an attack that affects multiple Locations (e.g. spraying fire) might use the hindrance aspect for one target and the TEM aspect for another.

author: neo.colpaert

I think you have to play the rules as written, and don't try to read too much into them nor expect much from them. An SSR that wants to use the convoy rules with restrictions can add restrictions if it likes.

I think you have to play the rules as written, and don't try to read too much into them nor expect much from them. An SSR that wants to use the convoy rules with restrictions can add restrictions if it likes.

title: Railroad Embankments
question: Setting up Scenario 5 from Hatten in Flames.  I need a crash course on Railroad Embankments.  Reading the Hillocks entry is confusing as F***!  So its a +1 TEM shooting over it and it doesn't appear to block any LOS unless say a squad is in a Foxhole or some such, correct?  And units on the EMRR are in Clear Terrain, but get a +1 Height Advantage?
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
Setting up Scenario 5 from Hatten in Flames.  I need a crash course on Railroad Embankments.  Reading the Hillocks entry is confusing as F***!  So its a +1 TEM shooting over it and it doesn't appear to block any LOS unless say a squad is in a Foxhole or some such, correct?  And units on the EMRR are in Clear Terrain, but get a +1 Height Advantage?

Hillocks are often called "thick walls," and that captures the behavior for units at ground level. You can see over them if you are ADJACENT but if not you can't see past them. When both units are on them, it's as if they don't exist, and that's also true of all other half-level (wall, hedge) obstacles at ground level. When one unit is on one and the other unit off, it's complicated. A unit on one can see over the hillock it is on, completely over another half-level obstacle (although a unit immediately behind a wall/hedge still gets the benefits) and just behind another half-level obstacle but not beyond that.

title: Rolling into a hex with an HIP Tank
question:
So my Panther rolled into a hex that had a HIP Immobilized American M10.  I have used 6MP so far.  What happens and/or what all are my choices and what are my opponents choices?  D2.6 is a little confusing.
My tank is coming from J28 into K28.
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
Still at a loss.  How does Overrun work against a Tank?
An AFV is not vulnerable to OVR, but its vulnerable PRC will be attacked "collaterally," i.e. as if they were the target of the attack [D7.12]. Effectively a N FP up two attack. 

Note that the entry of a hex by a vehicle against a HIP vehicle does not result in concealment loss (nor a PAATC to retain concealment as infantry might [A12.41]) or being pushed back into the previous hex [A12.4]. I believe the only reason the moving vehicle realizes that there is a HIP vehicle there is that it has to pay one extra MP [D2.14]. From that the moving player should realize that there is a HIP vehicle in the hex.

Because all the enemy units in the hex were concealed, an OVR can't be declared on entry and can be declared as a separate expenditure after entering the hex [D7.1]. That means the M10 can fire on the entry MP *before* any OVR can be declared. To fire its Gun the M10 must turn its CA to include the hexside entered [C3.2EX] and would pay Case E. A random turret facing would be hit [D3.2]. The aamg can just fire.

After DFF on entry the Panther might declare regular BFF or it might make another expenditure for an OVR.
Detail Overload.

OK, so my opponent would have to tell me that it cost 2MP to get into that hex, and he doesn't have to put his HIP tank on board Concealed, unless he wants to take a First Fire shot at me, correct?  Which, in this case would prove futile if target facing is taken into account and he doesn't roll a CH due to the Panthers frontal armor value, correct?

So if my opponent does not fire, his tank remains HIP?
If after I'm notified it will cost me 2MF, I know its in there, can I stop?  Can I fire?  Area Fire I presume? Can I just keep going and move into another hex?
I'm also currently CE, so would he get TPB fire using his AAMG?  If so, he would get to shoot first, correct?
And he would get to shoot again if I then spend a MP to stop, correct?

So many questions, sorry in advance;-)

If the M10 is immobilized, why is it marked, "moved?"

The M10 has some options: maintain HIP, toss Smoke or fire. The aamg would be a 12 FP up two and the MA would be +2 change CA, +2 moving, +2 in-hex, -1 large target. In addition, the 76L APCR TK# with modifications for range is 25. It can penetrate Panther front both on hull and turret. The 76L AP TK# at range zero is 18, meaning it can't penetrate hull front without a critical hit but can penetrate turret front.

If he doesn't achieve any result, in my response, what all am I able to do? Is my Panther stopped or still moving? If still moving, how would the Sn-woofet work?

The Panther is naturally not stopped, unless the Panther received an immobilization result, a Shock result or a Stun result. It spent two MP to enter, and neither of those MPs is a stop MP.

In order to fire the sN at any time you have to be BU [D13.34]. After DFF the Panther BUs (which is done "between" MP expenditures, D5.33) then makes its next MP expenditure, which would be to attempt sN. There is a +1 usage DRM for being BU [D13.3]. The Panther might also use vehicular smoke grenades D13.35. I believe the odds of getting them are less than the sN but it would allow the Panther to remain CE, if that was desirable.

If I have to spend another MP to stop, he would be able to get a third shot in. Correct?

Perhaps. If he fired a first shot, lost ROF, and a second, Intensive Fire shot, the M10 could not fire a third time

Thinking about this now, perhaps if the M10 does not keep ROF after the first attack, it might hold the Intensive Fire attack until the Panther commits to an action. If the M10 fires its Intensive Fire attack (and so no longer has any more MA attacks) the Panther can exit, stop and shoot from ADJACENT, which is a fairly good shot. If the M10 is holding its Intensive Fire the Panther risks the Intensive Fire attack when it exits and possibly when it stops, although depending on the circumstances the Panther may be in a position to make and win a gun duel.

The residual FP from the M10's aamg will attack the Panther if it makes another MP expenditure in the hex while CE.

It might stop and use BFF with its MGs and/or MA, changing from triple-and-quartered MG FP to triple-and-halved MG FP. It might "spin" (use CA change MP) to burn off MP so it can remain in hex to prevent other fire out. There are lots of options, none of them being super-great but all being at least somewhat reasonable.

Why couldn't he do MA+AAMG as shot on 1st MP, then MA (IF or ROF) on 2nd MP?  I.e. I don't think he has to pick between MA and AAMG as which he fires (he could fire both).

Not if the M10 used Intensive Fire.

Your best bet (if you didn't want to OVR) might be to exit the hex after the M10 shoots, since his 3rd shot would hopefully be IF + several rotations ... so even though you're exposing your ass to him, he should have a fairly low chance to hit.  Then you can stop and spin and return fire or run away.

Certainly an option. 

If he doesn't fire and remains HIP then perhaps the best solution is to try for sN smoke in the hex and then run away (or OVR him or BFF MGs at TPF either halved (if you stop) or quartered (if firing while in motion) ... I think.).  
I think all of the Panther's options are not great but not terrible either. I have not tried to calculate or simulate any of them, so I really don't know which is better. Likewise with the M10 I did simulate one option but I did not go through the other options for comparison. That's a lot of work.

Well, it ended poorly for my Panther, as JR V predicted.  My opponents first shot with AP (his first first shot with APCR missed) rolled Snakes, turning my poor baby Panther into a burning wreck.
Which brings up another question.  So now the M10 has to shoot out of burning wreck Smoke, so +3.  Does the wreck in the same hex as the M10 cause any issues firing out for the M10 or Firing in for me?

You might also be able to try for a Gun Duel if he decides to shoot, right?

True. The Panther has a +4 Gun Duel DRM (Case B & C) while the M10 has +2 (change CA) so unless there are Armor Leaders the M10 wins the Gun Duel, at least for the first shot. The Gun Duel might be more interesting for a later shot. Say the M10 changes TCA, fires its MA but loses ROF. The Panther might then exit into L27 (turn the Panther turret backwards). The Panther will probably not be interested in an attack while moving, so the M10 has to consider whether to make a DFF attack now. Its DRM are +2 moving target, +2 intensive fire, +3 TCA change, -1 acquisition, -1 target size, which is not a great chance of a hit. The M10 would really like to wait until the Panther stops to get the point blank DRM (Case L). But if it does wait, the Panther should declare the Gun Duel. The M10's Gun Duel DRM are +2 Intensive, +3 change CA, -1 acquisition, net +4, while the Panther's are +2 Case B & +2 Case C, assuming the Panther does not BU and there are no ALs. The Gun Duel DRM being the same, first shot goes to the lower TH DR, with a tie possible.

And what is the sequencing of when you can BU?  After he announces it is +1 MP to enter the hex, do you get a chance to BU before he DFF or after?  And would it be possible between the 2 MPs spent or does he get both MP shots before you have the option to BU?
CE change can be done as a separate action during the MPh. So when the Panther announces entry into the hex, that's one action, and it must be fully resolved, including DFF & BFF for that MP expenditure, before any other action can be taken. The Panther can't enter the hex, discover the awkward situation and BU before the M10 gets a chance for DFF on that MP expenditure with the Panther CE.

title: A Hedge question and a HIP/Rout question
question:
Question 1:
So I took an Advance Phase shot for Acquisition with one of my Panthers against one of my Opponents M18's, which was behind a Hedge.  I rolled Snakes, but with all the other DRM's, (orchards, hedge, small target) I just missed, but....
this particular Panther had a 9-1 Amor Leader. So even with all the +DRM's, the To Hit still came out to a 2.  Thats a hit, correct.  I took in account that it was behind a hedge, and I hit in the hull, so thats the +1DRM.  It it were a wall, only then would it not be a hit, unless I hit it in the Turret, correct?

Question 2:
So the earlier Broken German Squad ran towards the Rubble, got my opponent to unconceal those dues in the forest in order to Interdict, which my squad passed, but upon hoping the hedge into the next hex, revealed one of his HIP immobilized M10's.  Is my Squad now eliminated for failure to rout?
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
So the hull down aspect, is that applied even if it's just a hedge? I applied the the +1 TEM for it in the To Hit. I thought only Walls and the like forced it to be a turret hit in order to hit, but a bush?

No, hedge does not provide HD. Walls provide HD, but a vehicle can be HD in other ways such as bocage [B9.5], by height [D4.22], by being Dug-In [D9.54] or by amphibious movement [D16.3]. You specifically mentioned walls but the rule on CH switching to turret applies to all these and perhaps some more I didn't think of. You may lump them all together as "wall-like," and in that case my expansion of the question from "walls" to all HD made have suggested that hedge provides HD, but it doesn't. Sorry for the confusion.

Question 1:
So I took an Advance Phase shot for Acquisition with one of my Panthers against one of my Opponents M18's, which was behind a Hedge.  I rolled Snakes, but with all the other DRM's, (orchards, hedge, small target) I just missed, but....
this particular Panther had a 9-1 Amor Leader. So even with all the +DRM's, the To Hit still came out to a 2.  Thats a hit, correct.  I took in account that it was behind a hedge, and I hit in the hull, so thats the +1DRM.  It it were a wall, only then would it not be a hit, unless I hit it in the Turret, correct?

The Basic TH# is read off the C3 To Hit Table. You haven't told us enough to know the value but I will make a wild guess that you are firing using the Vehicle Target Type at range 1-6 and the value is 10. The Basic TH# is modified by C4 Gun & Ammo To Hit Number Modifications to get the Modified TH#. You have not told us enough again but I am going to guess that there are no modifications off the C4 table, and the Modified TH# is also 10.

I will guess at the DRM for the attack: Case C (Bounding Firer, +2) plus Case B (Firer in the AFPh, +2) plus Case P (target size, +1) plus Case Q (TEM, +1) for a total +6. It's possible that Case I applies (BU, +1) and you mention Hindrances, Case R (either +2 or +3, depending on whether the Panther is BU). That's a total +9 DRM, i.e. any TH DR + TH DRM will be > the Modified TH# of 10.

If that were the case a natural snakeeyes becomes an Improbable Hit [C3.6], and you make a subsequent dr. If this dr = 1, the result is a Critical Hit, a 2 is a turret hit and a 3 is a hull hit, with 4-6 a miss.

However in your case there is one more DRM, a -1 Armor Leader, making the TH DRM a net +8. A TH DR of two with the +8 DRM is ≤ the Modified TH# of 10, so the result is *always* a hit. But because the only number that will give a hit is a snakeeyes, the result is not an automatic Critical Hit [C3.7]. Instead you make a subsequent dr. A subsequent dr=1 is a Critical Hit; a dr=2-6 is a normal hit.

Against a Hull Down target (whether by wall or by other means), a Critical Hit is against the Turret [C3.9]. Any non-critical-hull hit would be a miss instead.

Question 2:
So the earlier Broken German Squad ran towards the Rubble, got my opponent to unconceal those dues in the forest in order to Interdict, which my squad passed, but upon hoping the hedge into the next hex, revealed one of his HIP immobilized M10's.  Is my Squad now eliminated for failure to rout?

Told you not to rout that way. (I am guessing this question relates to a situation in Hatten in Flames; in HiF rubble hexes are treated like buildings in being rout targets.)

This depends on how the HIP vehicle was revealed. As I recall your broken unit would take three MF to cross the hedge and another three MF to enter the rubble. If your opponent dropped concealment before the broken unit attempted to enter the hex, the appearance of a new enemy unit would force the broken unit to refigure its rout path but starting with three MF. In your particular situation the squad can probably find a safe place to rout with its remaining three MF. If it could not, it would be eliminated for FTR.

If the HIP tank lost its concealment involuntarily because the broken unit attempted to enter its hex, the broken unit would be eliminated [A10.533]. The broken unit must end its RtPh and is eliminated for FTR; no refiguring of rout is possible.

I was thinking the M10 was in H27 in the rubble, but re-reading your question it may have been in G27 across the hedge in the orchard. The same answers apply, but if in G27 and the M10 voluntarily revealed, the unit would have five MF instead of three with which to refigure its rout. It the M10 was involuntarily revealed the unit is eliminated per A10.533.
You're playing HF4, "Liehr Launches First," and the M10s must be in Orchard to be HIP.

consensus_answer:

C5.34 (case C³), "In addition, those weapons with a Backblast (13.8) must use this +2 To Hit DRM when firing from ground-level rubble/building unless the firer predesignates that he will risk Desperation penalties (13.81) or is using Opportunity Fire."

title: Advancing to 2nd level rooftops ( factories in RB)
question:
It seems amazing that MMC  with  heavy SW ( r MMG,  HMG) SW  can just advance to the ROOF of a  2 level factory in RB.

Let's break it down to useful "notions".

447  with MMG     
as above  PLUS   CX

426 with MMG
as above PLUS  CX 

Now , I presume the move or advance to a  2nd level rooftop is  2 MF  ( 1 is virtual- inside the factory).  

In the  447.   base  4   MF

Case 2:   -1  MF  (CX)   ,  -1  (  +1 pp over inherent)=   so has  2 MF  to  advance 2  locations ( unless it teleports).

In  426   base  3 MF

Case 2  :  as  above  but  1 MF   to advance,  thus  unless it costs 1MF  to advance , it cannot.

I hope someone can shed light on RB factories and advance,,,
author: Oberst_Hausser
consensus_answer:
B23.87 "Infantry expend two MF (for a 1½-level Factory) or three MF (for a 2½-level Factory) to ascend to the Rooftop or vice-versa."

The rooftop is another Location above the standard building levels, so it costs one MF to move from level zero to level one, one MF to move from level one to level two and one MF to move from level two to the rooftop level.

As for whether a particular unit possessing particular PP with a particular CX status can make a move or advance, this is all standard rules based on available MF, MF cost, and CX status. There is nothing different for accessing a rooftop, including a factory rooftop.

For movement if the MF cost is less than available MF and a move of only one Location is made, the unit may assault move (or normal move at its option). If the MF cost is equal to MF available the unit must use non-assault movement. If the move is greater than available MF and the unit has at least one MF available, it may make a minimum move [A4.134]. Double Time [A4.5] can be used with all the standard gains and provisos.

For advance if the MF cost is less than available MF and less than four MF, the unit may advance normally. If the MF cost is greater-than-or-equal-to available MF or greater than-or-equal-to four MF and the unit has at least one available MF and is not CX, it may make an Advance vs Difficult Terrain [A4.72].

title: D17. 25 VCA change Aerosan
question: Why does the Aerosan have to start, stop and start again for VCA change in the 2nd example (towards hex X7) since it does not have to do this in the first example?
author: neo.colpaert
consensus_answer:
Why does the Aerosan have to start, stop and start again for VCA change in the 2nd example (towards hex X7) since it does not have to do this in the first example? 
In the first EX the VCA is changed as the Aerosan enters a new hex (VCA declare as part of the declaraion to enter the nex hew). In the second EX the Aerosan is making two VCA changes in the same hex.

One can only make a one-hexsping change after each Start MP - that's why it has to Stop and Start again to make the second VCA change...

D17.25 VCA CHANGE: When changing its VCA outside of the MPh (2.401; C3.21-.22), an Aerosan is limited to a VCA change of one hexspine only. During the MPh, it may change its VCA one hexspine per hex (as a separate MP expenditure), either after entering a hex after having announced the change prior to entering the new hex or after expending a Start MP.

title: Can reinforcing units search [A12.152] from offboard?
question: I don't see anything that would prevent them from doing so, but I'd like other players' opinions. Obviously the unit would be TI and so unable to enter in the MPh and/or APh and would be lost.
author: jrvjrv
consensus_answer:
I agree, A2.52 prevents it, but even if you could do it, it would likely be fatal to the searching unit.  It would be marked TI and unable to Advance onto the board, and if that was its required turn of entry, it would be eliminated by A2.5:  "ENTRY: All forces scheduled to arrive on a certain turn must enter the mapboard on that turn..."

Hmmm, at least I assume that's fatal - what's the consequence of failing to enter?  Is the unit considered eliminated, or is it simply not in play at all?  I assume the former; the latter could be a little gamey for CVP victory conditions, etc.  The point is moot re JRV's original question but I'm curious about the more general case of failure to enter.
It depends the entry instructions.
Sometimes they say : "... enter on Turn X or later".
If they are due on a precise Turn and don't enter, they are lost and count as CVP, I think.

replies.body: I'm not sure I understand the question. If they are still offboard, what would they be searching for?

author: adolfinger

I misread some of the rules. I'm going to have to re-think this.

To me there are some additional factors that complicate trying to apply the q&a to the question. The rules, in particular G11.51, make it sound like it could be paraphrased, "if it's a continuous slope from the entrance hex, then it's a continuous slope from the cave." But this paraphrased reading would lead to certain technical problems with caves. In particular a conflict with A6.3, elevation necessary to see INTO a depression. The q&a refers to the G11.5 EX, cave A and LOS INTO hex 25DD2. 

The technical problem here is that a unit at level three in hex 25BB5 (as it would be in a cave) does not have LOS INTO a depression at level one in hex DD2 per A6.3. A unit at level four in hex 25BB5 would have such LOS per A6.3, and a unit at level three in 25CC5 also would have such LOS. So does the apparent existence of a continuous slope per B.5 (one level change per hex) based on the cave entrance hex, 25CC5, override the inability of a unit at level three in hex 25BB5 to see INTO a depression at range four (25BB5 to 25DD2) when a unit in 25BB5 at level three (in a cave) is only three levels above the base level of 25DD2 (level zero IN the depression), or does A6.3 prevent LOS INTO the depression despite meeting the B.5 definition for continuous slope from 25CC5 combined with the G11.51 paraphrase? 

I think actually G11.51 handles this question. G11.51 has additional verbiage beyond the B.5 definition of continuous slope: "If the LOS from a unit in a cave whose CA Hexside is also a hill (only) Crest Line hexside lies along a Continuous Slope when disregarding the Cave counter's hex, then a Continuous Slope is considered to exist from that cave along that LOS." I have bolded the extra "hill (only)" because I think it is meant to prevent G11.51 from overriding A6.3. If 25DD2 had been a level zero hex without a Depression across hill Crest Line across the 25DD2/25DD3 hexside there would be continuous slope from a cave in 25BB5 but because entry to 25DD2 is *not* across a "hill (only)" hexside, G11.51 does *not* create continuous slope even though the LOS from the 25CC5 entrance hex meets the B.5 definition of continuous slope.

Circling back to the original situation without a cave, I would be reluctant to read the q&a as stating that a depression hex is excluded from B.5 continuous slope definition even when there is no cave and no reference to G11.51 without a second, clarifying q&a discussing that particular combination of terrain, e.g. a unit at level four in hex 25BB5. I think the q&a comment on depressions voiding continuous slope is only in the context of G11.51 because of the specific wording of "hill (only) Crest Lines" that G11.51 uses.

But I could be wrong, and the intention is to void all B.5 continuous slope that involves Depressions. The problem with that is it changes the definition of B.5 from "A Continuous Slope is a change in elevation such that, in each hex successively crossed by the LOS, the elevation changes by one level in a continuous gradient" as it reads currently to, "A Continuous Slope is a change in elevation across hill (only) Crest Lines such that, in each hex successively crossed by the LOS, the elevation changes by one level in a continuous gradient." That would seem to me to require an erratum, especially since not everyone owns Chapter G.

Gully rules aside, I think that G11.51 means that if you remove the cave counter and CC5/BB5 is a hill crest line that has a Continous Slope, then units in the cave also have that LOS.
Imagine that BB5 is Level 4, then units in the cave would have the LOS even though technically these units are not "above" the hill but "under" the hill top. I think the rule is for this case.

title: Sleeze Freeze and AFV CC
question:
Still trying to wrap my brain around this tactic.
I have an AFV wanting nullify an squad/MMG. I do a VBM, ending in the hex with the enemy squad/MMG.

Can the squad choose not to use CC reaction fire?
If so, it can avoid the PAATC roll then in the upcoming CC then. Correct?
What happens if the squad attempts to use CC Reaction Fire when the AFV enters in Bypass and it fails the PAATC? It's then Pinned and this will then become a DRM in the upcoming CC, correct?
If it Passes the PAATC but fails to cause a result in the CC Reaction Fire, what happens in the upcoming CC?

I've been flipping back and forth between A7.212, A12.42 and D7.21 trying to decipher all this. Any help appreciated.
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
AFV in bypass will force loss of  ? 

AFV stops in hex  will  force loss of  ? 

A vehicle entering a hex, either in bypass or not, does not cause automatic loss of concealment.

If the vehicle is "broken" [A12.1] it will never cause loss of concealment. 

If the vehicle is not "broken" and enters without bypass or woods-road, the defending units must either voluntarily surrender concealment (including HIP) or pass a PAATC unless immune [A12.41]. If immune to PAATC concealment is retained.

If the vehicle enters using bypass, concealment is retained. If the vehicle *ends* its MPh in bypass, concealment is lost without opportunity for PAATC and even if immune to PAATC. [A12.42]

"If the squad chooses not to make a CC-RF attack, it does not have to make a PAATC if the vehicle is in bypass. If.."

Correct, it does not have to make a PAATC for an attack it does not make. If the vehicle enters without using bypass/woods road it may have to take a PAATC to prevent concealment loss. If the vehicle enters using bypass and remains, concealment is lost (there's no PAATC nor benefit to being immune).

That's   generally not the problem, CC-RF  is  a  "last ditch stand"  - good luck-   the problem is you lost ?  and the bad guys are about to 
AFPh, or OPPORTUNITY FIRE  or  encircle you..

If you don't win the CC ( if you are still alive) the bad news is  TPBF awaits... Unless the AFV exits there is  NOTHING you can do about it.
Could be, but how bad that is very much depends on the particular vehicle. First the BMG can't be used in-hex from bypass [D2.35], and any turret-mounted weapons often get case A as well as an extra +1 DRM for firing from bypass in the side CA [D2.321]. French tanks are not much of a threat from bypass, and even German vehicles are not as dangerous from bypass because they can't use the BMG.

But even with that said, I do not like to be in a position where my vehicle is engaging in multiple rounds of CC. My first preference would be to have infantry following along closely behind the tank (not necessarily armored assault) to fire in the AFPh. I would also consider advancing some infantry in even in the face of the ambush drm. Sending in a vehicle without support would be my least-preferred choice unless I was willing to sacrifice the vehicle for a great benefit.

title: Low Crawl Towards Woods
question: The nearest woods location is 4 MF away by direct route. It is possible to make the same rout by a different path using 6MF which is completely fine. My opponent claimed that he could low crawl 'toward' the woods location using the hypothetical 6MF path. I felt like it didn't work that way, since that path did not make the woods location any closer to the low crawling unit. Which is correct in this case?
author: drmark64
consensus_answer:
The nearest woods location is 4 MF away by direct route. It is possible to make the same rout by a different path using 6MF which is completely fine. My opponent claimed that he could low crawl 'toward' the woods location using the hypothetical 6MF path. I felt like it didn't work that way, since that path did not make the woods location any closer to the low crawling unit. Which is correct in this case?
You have to move closer. 

q&a: "A10.51 If a DM broken unit that must rout is within six MF of the nearest woods/building, must it attempt to reach the woods/building in a single RtPh?
A. Yes, unless it uses Low Crawl, but it need not take the shortest route (in hexes/MF) to do so. Even if it uses Low Crawl, however, it must still do so toward that woods/building (i.e., at no time may it increase the hex range between itself and that woods/building, and must end that RtPh closer to it than it was at the start of the phase).

title: Two Bocage Questions
question:
Question 1:
BackgroundWe're playing SME and are on day 2 of the Campaign.  Germans set up their 81 MTRs to pound the US front line and are behind bocage. They are Emplaced Guns and start HIP. During the GE PFPh, they both fire.  One loses ?? the other only loses HiP. 

Question During the CCPh, Infantry/Dummy units that can only be seen via a Bocage hexside gain concealment per B9.55. This rule says nothing about Guns or Emplaced Guns, which have their own entry on the concealment loss/gain table.  Following the table, the Gun that lost concealment does NOT gain it as there is an enemy unit that has LOS to it (albeit through a bocage hexside).  Is this correct?  If so (i.e. the Gun does NOT gain concealment), does the manning crew gain concealment per B9.55?  So you end up with a CREW being concealed, but the GUN being unconcealed?  Is this even possible?

Question 2:
Background As above, its day 2 of the Campaign and a German HS has grabbed the bridge Strategic Location that also borders a bocage hexside.

Question Can a unit ON a bridge (over a gully) claim wall advantage???  We didn't think so, since they have limited movement and must enter/exit via the road, which is NOT the bocage hexside, but we didn't find anything in the rules that prevented it.
author: kbernatz
consensus_answer:
Question 1:
BackgroundWe're playing SME and are on day 2 of the Campaign.  Germans set up their 81 MTRs to pound the US front line and are behind bocage. They are Emplaced Guns and start HIP. During the GE PFPh, they both fire.  One loses ?? the other only loses HiP. 

Question During the CCPh, Infantry/Dummy units that can only be seen via a Bocage hexside gain concealment per B9.55. This rule says nothing about Guns or Emplaced Guns, which have their own entry on the concealment loss/gain table.  Following the table, the Gun that lost concealment does NOT gain it as there is an enemy unit that has LOS to it (albeit through a bocage hexside).  Is this correct?  If so (i.e. the Gun does NOT gain concealment), does the manning crew gain concealment per B9.55?  So you end up with a CREW being concealed, but the GUN being unconcealed?  Is this even possible?

Although Emplaced and Unemplaced Guns and their manning infantry are listed separately on the Concealment Loss/Gain chart, the crews remain Infantry. As you say per B9.55 when the crew is capable of claiming WA from bocage against all unbroken enemy units, it is considered out-of-LOS and in-concealment-terrain. This is without regard to whether it possesses a Gun. It gains concealment per the "(none in LOS) IN CONCEALMENT TERRAIN" column of the Concealment Loss/Gain chart, but on the "EMPLACED GUN (and manning Infantry)" or "VEHICLE (and PRC)/UNEMPLACED GUN (and manning Infantry)/ CAVALRY/ HORSE/ BICYCLE" row.

I.e. I think that neither should gain Concealment or, at the very least, the crew gains Concealment and not the Gun, as the Gun does not qualify as being out of enemy LOS.

Weapon and possessing unit always share concealment.

You are correct that the "Emplaced Gun (and manning Infantry)" row is the one to use in your case. But per B9.55 the *column* to use is "(none in LOS) IN CONCEALMENT TERRAIN."

I think you are driving the rules argument the wrong way. You can't use the row labels on the Concealment Loss/Gain table to determine if B9.55 applies. The relevant row labels on the Concealment Loss/Gain table are, "INFANTRY (not manning a Gun)," "EMPLACED GUN (and manning Infantry)," and "VEHICLE (and PRC)/UNEMPLACED GUN (and manning Infantry)/ CAVALRY/ HORSE/ BICYCLE." B9.55 says only "Infantry," i.e. it matches none of the three Concealment Loss/Gain row labels. If the categories in the Concealment Gain/Loss table rows have to match for B9.55 to be applicable, B9.55 would never be applicable because "INFANTRY (not manning a Gun)" is not the same as "Infantry". B9.55 determines which *column* applies for Infantry, and the row is determined by whether the Infantry possesses an Emplaced Gun, an Unemplaced Gun or no Gun at all.

title: Using LMG in SFF/FPF after firing two PF
question:
Hello friends,

Question: A ger.fullsquad (carrying an LMG) fired two Panzerfaust-rounds as First Fire during enemy MPh, therefore forfeiting its inherent FP until the CCPh (A7.351), except during SFF/FPF where it can fire half of its inherent FP (A7.353).

After that, an enemy fullsquad moves adjacent to the ger.FS. 

Which Options regarding weapon combination does the Squad have to fire on the adjacent squad as SFF/FPF?
Can it fire it's LMG again? Is this LMG using sustained fire or firing without penalties, as the LMG technically didn't receive a First Fire counter asnit didn't shoot. 

Best regards, thank you for your answers in advance
author: Awazungu
consensus_answer:
As a minor technical niggle the squad need not be adjacent (or ADJACENT) to use its inherent (but again in this situation not the LMG) as SFF. 

Hm, I think I disagree for this special situation. The squad already fired 2 PF, so lost its inherent FP as per A7.351 "A squad using two SW/Gun loses its inherent FP until the CCPh [EXC: 7.353]." 
Now the EXC comes into play, allowing it to use its inherent FP in SFF/FPF after all: "A7.353 In both of the above cases, Subsequent First Fire (8.3), FPF (8.31), and Final Fire (8.4) vs adjacent units retain halved inherent FP for those attacks (regardless of how they were used during First Fire)"
SFF is covered in A8.3: "Subsequent First Fire cannot be attempted against any target at a range > that to the closest armed, Known enemy unit, nor outside the firer's Normal Range." If you want to fight the "rules are in apparent conflict" fight, rule number A8.3 is > A7.353 and higher number rule wins. But since A7.353 references A8.3 by number, I would also expect that A7.353 expects that all the provisions of A8.3 are in play.

Regarding FPF this is only covered in the q&a. There is no rule support for it that I see. If you don't use q&a then you're right. But if you do again similar to the above I would expect the q&a would rule over the printed rules.

replies.body: I think the LMG will be used as sustained fire when the squad is using SFF. If the enemy squad only uses 1 MF to enter the adjacent hex then you only get one shot as SFF. If another squad moves adjacent then you can use FPF (incl the LMG as sustained fire).

When firing as SFF, if choosing to use the LMG, it will receive Sustained Fire penalties, even though it did not fire as First Fire.
When using FPF it is mandatory to use the LMG, and it will again receive Sustained Fire penalties.

Hello Marti, how do you explain (rule-based ;-)) the use of that LMG please?

title: Yet another slope question
question: Can these two squads see each other? Does hex T32 have any effect on LOS?
author: Jgolch
consensus_answer:
Sorry for "resurrecting" this thread, but I want to fully understand the image situation and the slope role (I assume the US unit is at level 0 and the German one is at level 1).

I understand that the units can be seen because, while the slope raises the observer slightly it doesn't raise it enough (it's not a full level) to create a blind hex which would otherwise be created even if the German unit were at level two, since in this case there is always at least one. Is that correct or am I missing something?
You have this somewhat backwards. Raising the German higher either reduces blind hexes or keeps them the same. If there were a blind hex when the German was a full level above the S32 obstacle there would also be one when it is ¾ of a level higher (or a half level higher, e.g. on an EmRR). 

To clarify the KGP map colors, the German is on level six; the American is on level five [KGP SSR1]. This does not matter because all calculations for blind hexes are the same when the relative elevations are the same.

A unit viewing across a slope hexside is treated as if at level ¾ above the hex level, i.e. level 6¾. Because the German is (treated as if) at a height > than S32, T32 and U32, it can see over those hexes to a lower elevation [A6.4]. The German will not be "plateau-ed" by those hexes. So now it is a matter of calculating blind hexes. Level-six hex U32 creates one blind hex for a viewer at level 6¾ to level 5, which is T32, so not interesting. T32 creates one blind hex, which is S32, so not interesting. That leaves hex S32. An non-crest-line obstacle in S32 would create one blind hex, so if S32 were a woods or building, hex R31 would be blind. However S32 *is* a crest line. A crest line has to be at least five hexes away to create one or more blind hexes [B10.23], so the number of blind hexes for S32 is zero. There is a minimum of one blind hex for *non-crest-line* obstacles, but S32 is a crest-line obstacle so that minimum does not apply.

replies.body:
Can these two squads see each other? Does hex T32 have any effect on LOS?
Yes. No. Slope hexesides not on the viewer's or viewee's hexside have no effect on LOS. 

This remains true even if the two units are at the same base level and neither benefits from a slope, e.g. assume R31 is the same level as W34 and the LOS is traced from R31 to/from W34.

My way of thinking of slope rules is as follows. This is not meant to be literal, but rather "imagine for effect." The slope hexside is a thin and wobbly ladder that goes from the hex center to the hexside. Because it is a thin and a ladder, it has no effect on LOS past it. Because it is wobbly you dare not look in a different direction because the ladder might wobble and you'd fall off. It only lets you climb to level ¾ above the base level to see past terrain in that direction. Units that are in direction other than the covered hexside can only fire at you when you are off the ladder, and you can only fire at them when you are off the ladder.

It's actually a dumb model but it is a understandable synopsis of the LOS rules. It does not cover other behavior like TEM or MF cost, etc.

Being on a slope hex looking through the slope simply allows you to see units in a lower elevation than your elevation, even if you are not in the crest hex. It is a way to allow the flat cake effect in some maps (notoriously KP).

Probably a mix of the two. In any case all help is welcome.

Just think that the unit in the slope looking in the slope direction has a level 0.75 higher than without the slope. If the terrain of the unit is Level 1, looking through the slope the LOS is taken from Level 1.75. 

The effect of this is that you can see over obstacles if your height is higher than the obstacle height. So a unit in Level 1 cannot see over a one hex building of height 1, but from a slope you can because you are higher than the obstacle. Then apply the usual blind hex calculations.

The purpose of the slope is to allow maps with extensive hill terrain to be usable in the ASL system, to eliminate the layer cake effect, where units can only see downhill from the slope hexes. Without slopes, units would have to be always in slope crest-line hexes to fire, making the system behave weirdly with hills levels of many hexes, like in the KGP module. With the slopes you can move around the hills and still see downhill.

This slope problem would not exist if the hill terrain had been conceived from the start as slowly rolling downwards from the top, and LOS was only broken for terrain on the other side of the hill or for obstacles in the hill itself.

The height advantage could have been ½-level, ¼-level or even 0.0001 level to give LOS to lower levels. But since the unit is considered at ¾-level slopes also give LOS over half-level obstacles & hindrances (walls, hedge, rubble, brush and wrecks) that are at the same base level as the unit. For that reason ¾-level was chosen (I assume; I was not there at the time!).

Bingo.

There is another place where LOS over a "same level" crest line to lower elevations was deemed desirable: caves. Crest-line caves are considered at the level of their entrance hex [G11.112], and in most cases would be "plateau-ed" by their entrance hex if something weren't included in the rules. In real life caves would almost always have LOS down the slope they were set in. One could imagine using the slope "trick" and saying caves are considered some amount higher than their entrance hex, e.g. ¼-level. This was not done, and presumably because the cave being close to the ground level of the slope it would have a very restricted LOS to lower elevations. Instead it is declared that the entrance hex (only) does not prevent LOS to a lower level [G11.5], i.e. it does not "plateau" LOS. If the LOS goes over another hex (besides the entrance hex) at the same level, the LOS is plateau-ed. I remember this by thinking that the cave is ¼-level higher but only to its entrance hex. That isn't the way the rule is written but it does produce a similar effect.
Again, this caves rule would not have been needed in the first place if hills in ASL had a gentle slope from its highest point to the bottom. But the rules are as they are.

title: Shellholes confusion
question: Let’s say an infantry unit begins the Movement Phase in a hex adjacent to a shellhole hex.  The units moves into the hex and decides to “enter” the shellhole and ends its movement. Is the unit subject to FFMO/FFNAM?
author: Jgolch
consensus_answer:
My conceptualization of shellholes vs foxholes is that a shellhole does not represent a single hole in a corner of a hex (unless it is a *monster* shellhole as might be generated by, say, a sixteen inch shell). Instead shellhole terrain represents multiple shellholes that cover a random and substantial portion of a hex. Think Paschendaele.

https://collection.nam.ac.uk/images/960/103000-103999/103603.jpg

Thus you can enter the hex and zig-zag around the shellholes, but when the music stops there's always one to fall into. But this also explains why shellholes are hard to create. Unless you are using a terrific big weapon, it takes much more than one shell to pockmark an entire hex.

In contrast foxholes are small holes that are set up in a militarily significant and therefore non-random part of the hex. A bit like wire, the abstraction for foxholes says that where ever your unit is in the hex, it's not near the foxhole you want to use. Murphy's Law for Foxholes. So you have to move around in the hex to get into that foxhole, i.e. spend one MF to enter. And again a bit like wire Murphy's Law for Foxholes says that when you want to leave the hex, the foxhole is not near where you want to go, so you have to spend a MF in the hex to "exit" the foxhole.

And again a bit like wire Murphy's Law for Foxholes says that when you want to leave the hex, the foxhole is not near where you want to go, so you have to spend a MF in the hex to "exit" the foxhole.

And this difference makes that in the game the random shelling of an hex is a very good protection for your infantry while a military significant non-random entrenchment can be a death trap for your own units. The trenches I have visited from the Spanish Civil War always have some evacuation corridors to withdraw the casualties or to abandon the position if necessary, without being exposed to enemy fire. Which is totally logic.

Something like shown here: https://www.longlongtrail.co.uk/soldiers/a-soldiers-life-1914-1918/the-evacuation-chain-for-wounded-and-sick-soldiers/
Trenches in ASL are superb for rout. Foxholes are not trenches. Note that escape from foxholes is also safe if you can wait until just the right moment when firing has died down then run for all you are worth, i.e. you are routing. What they are not good for is when you want to make a deliberate move at a time of *your* choosing, i.e. in the MPh. I find the ASL rules for foxholes understandable, explainable and even reasonable. I only wish there had been designer's notes on the matter.

Let’s say an infantry unit begins the Movement Phase in a hex adjacent to a shellhole hex.  The units moves into the hex and decides to “enter” the shellhole and ends its movement. Is the unit subject to FFMO/FFNAM?
If the unit decides to enter the hex at one MF, it is subject to FFMO. But at that point it does not have to spend any more MF to "enter" the shellholes. Unlike entrenchments there aren't two separate semi-Locations in the hex. After the completion of any DFF for the one MF spent to enter the hex, if the unit ended its MPh (i.e. did not expend any more MF), it could not be attacked any more during the MPh. If it were then attacked in the DFPh it would receive the +1 TEM for shellholes. A unit can be considered "outside" the shellholes only during the MPh, and only by explicitly expending one MF to enter the hex. Again this is very different from entrenchments.

As Tankboy says, it depends on how the unit expended the MFs.

1) They have to announce Assault movement PRIOR to /any/ MF expenditure, so if they don't say they are using Assault Movement, they will /always/ be subject to FFNAM, even if only moving 1 hex or even NOT leaving their hex (spending MFs for smoke, etc).

2) If they say they are spending 2 MFs to enter the hex, then they are in the shellhole and NO FFMO.

3) If they say they are entering the hex but do NOT specify that they are expending 2 MFs or 'entering the shellhole', then they are in Open Ground (all other things being equal) and may be subject to FFMO if all the conditions for that apply.

And this difference makes that in the game the random shelling of an hex is a very good protection for your infantry while a military significant non-random entrenchment can be a death trap for your own units. The trenches I have visited from the Spanish Civil War always have some evacuation corridors to withdraw the casualties or to abandon the position if necessary, without being exposed to enemy fire. Which is totally logic.

Something like shown here: https://www.longlongtrail.co.uk/soldiers/a-soldiers-life-1914-1918/the-evacuation-chain-for-wounded-and-sick-soldiers/

For example choosing to keep heads down during the RPh would TI the unit (so no fire from them) but act as an additional Area Fire on attacks vs them. That would be useful during own's turn in a defense situation when instead of prep firing a heads down would reduce the risk on the opponent def fire but still keep the unit there for the next defensive fire.

Just think: a "heads down" rule could also get rid of skulking. 😀

It has the choice to only pay for Open Ground and risk FFMO.

title: Critical hits for Infantry Target Type 3.7 (C9)
question:
Is it correct that you have to throw an extra dr of 1 or ≤ half of the 
Modified TH# after scoring a critical hit for Infantry Target Type?
Is this only on an original TH DR of 2 or also on a final TH DR < half the Modified TH#?
author: neo.colpaert
consensus_answer:
There are four possible situations here: the unit is hit by WP but not in the Location where the WP counter is placed, the unit is not hit but in the Location where the WP counter is placed, the unit is both hit and in the Location where the counter is placed, and the unit is neither hit nor in the Location where the counter is placed. In the first three the unit must take a WP NMC; in the last there is no WP NMC. The unit may be subject to a CH if it is hit but not if it is not hit.

JRV, I'm not following the bolded one above?  Do you mean a unit at ground level in, say a Pillbox, where WP hits units outside the Pillbox?  Or do you mean a unit at level 1 or 2 (for example) with WP hitting a unit at Ground level in the same hex?  I.e. I'm confused how it can be hit and subject to the NMC if not in the same Location as where the WP is placed.

Consider a level two building. Level two has an unconcealed unit. Level one has a concealed (but not HIP) unit. The LOS to level zero has six grain hexes, and there is a unit in it, HIP, concealed or unconcealed. The firing unit is not a MTR and fires WP at range, say, eight hexes. Because this is not a cave the ATT is used. The ATT could in theory hit all three levels but because LOS is blocked to the ground level (six grain hexes), it can't be hit. The Base TH number for ATT at range eight is seven, modified by case C4.4 (SMOKE ammunition range ≤ 12 hexes) to nine. The DRM are +0 vs the level two unit and +2 vs. the level one unit. On a TH DR of nine or eight the top unit is hit but not the middle unit. By C8.52 the WP counter is placed at ground level, i.e. level zero. The level two unit and the ground unit both take WP NMCs, the first because it was hit and the second because a WP counter was placed in its Location. The level one unit was neither hit nor had a WP counter placed in its Location and so does not take a WP NMC. If the TH DR had been seven or less, both the top and middle (concealed) units would be hit, and all three would take a WP NMC. On a snakeeyes (critical hit) the top and middle would be eligible for CH effects but not the unit at ground level because, being out of LOS, it was not hit; its WP NMC was "indirect" by the counter being placed at ground level.

If the attacking unit had been a mortar then on a TH DR of seven or less the unit at ground level would also be hit [C3.33], and it could potentially be subject to a critical hit. If the TH DR of eight or nine the middle unit would not be hit, and so the out-of-LOS unit would also *not* be hit.

If instead of a concealed the level one unit had been HIP, the cases for the non-mortar attack remain the same. For the mortar now a TH DR of eight or nine hits the level two unit and also the ground level unit (because the hardest-to-hit-non-HIP target has been hit) but not the level one unit because it is not out-of-LOS and its final TH DR with the +2 TH DRM for concealment (HIP) is > nine.

Pillboxes are actually a tricky, special case that goes beyond what we have covered so far. Per B30.34 they may never contain SMOKE and thus never get the WP NMC except when a WP gets a CH and the placing/firing unit "is ADJACENT-to/within-the-CA-of the pillbox." 

24.31 CASUALTIES: The chemical agents in WP caused discomfort and 
could result in demoralization/casualties. All units (including friendly ones) 
except a non-CE, CT AFV in a Location with a WP counter must take a 
NMC when the WP is placed (by any means) [EXC: non-moving units in 
First Fire] in that Location (not when it drifts or they move into it) or when

Consider a level two building. Level two has an unconcealed unit. Level one has a concealed (but not HIP) unit. The LOS to level zero has six grain hexes, and there is a unit in it, HIP, concealed or unconcealed. The firing unit is not a MTR and fires WP at range, say, eight hexes. Because this is not a cave the ATT is used. The ATT could in theory hit all three levels but because LOS is blocked to the ground level (six grain hexes), it can't be hit. The Base TH number for ATT at range eight is seven, modified by case C4.4 (SMOKE ammunition range ≤ 12 hexes) to nine. The DRM are +0 vs the level two unit and +2 vs. the level one unit. On a TH DR of nine or eight the top unit is hit but not the middle unit. By C8.52 the WP counter is placed at ground level, i.e. level zero. The level two unit and the ground unit both take WP NMCs, the first because it was hit and the second because a WP counter was placed in its Location. The level one unit was neither hit nor had a WP counter placed in its Location and so does not take a WP NMC. If the TH DR had been seven or less, both the top and middle (concealed) units would be hit, and all three would take a WP NMC. On a snakeeyes (critical hit) the top and middle would be eligible for CH effects but not the unit at ground level because, being out of LOS, it was not hit; its WP NMC was "indirect" by the counter being placed at ground level.

If the attacking unit had been a mortar then on a TH DR of seven or less the unit at ground level would also be hit [C3.33], and it could potentially be subject to a critical hit. If the TH DR of eight or nine the middle unit would not be hit, and so the out-of-LOS unit would also *not* be hit.

If instead of a concealed the level one unit had been HIP, the cases for the non-mortar attack remain the same. For the mortar now a TH DR of eight or nine hits the level two unit and also the ground level unit (because the hardest-to-hit-non-HIP target has been hit) but not the level one unit because it is not out-of-LOS and its final TH DR with the +2 TH DRM for concealment (HIP) is > nine.

title: CC, Snakes and Withdrawals
question: So we are playing HF1, my opponent advances into my building for CC.  No Ambush gained. He rolls Snakes. So he can choose to withdraw from CC per the rules. If he chooses to withdraw. Does he still eliminate my Squad? Or, does he have to choose to stay in order to cause my elimination, but also take whatever I roll?
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
I think we played it that he either withdraws (only) or kills + takes the return fire...but not sure if that is 100% correct, as we had a similar question when this came up in one of our Hatten matches.
You are mixing Ambush [A11.41] rules with Infiltration rules [A11.22]. With Ambush you have the choice to either withdraw immediately with no attack or to attack and possibly be attacked. With Infiltration you both get the result and do not need to face any *pending* attack (but any completed attacks are still valid).

So we are playing HF1, my opponent advances into my building for CC.  No Ambush gained. He rolls Snakes. So he can choose to withdraw from CC per the rules. If he chooses to withdraw. Does he still eliminate my Squad? Or, does he have to choose to stay in order to cause my elimination, but also take whatever I roll?
If he is the ATTACKER and CC is not sequential (i.e. not Ambush, Prisoner or Vehicle), the ATTACKER rolls all his attacks first even though CC is "simultaneous" [A11.12]. If in that process he rolls a snakeeyes ("infiltration") he may *immediately* withdraw, both getting the result and also avoiding being attacked, because the ATTACKER always rolls "simultaneous" CC first, and the immediate withdrawal means the DEFENDER won't have the opportunity to roll and declared attack.

To note here is that the mechanics of "simultaneous" CC are not simultaneous. There is a definite order to them, and allows an ATTACKER to both score a result and also escape an announced attack with Infiltration.

In (sort of) contrast, if one side rolls Ambush it must either withdraw immediately or attack and risk being attacked. It may be attacked if it attacked and there are any survivors and if it did not roll a snakeeyes in any attacks it made. Ambush alone does not prevent an enemy counterattack (unless all enemy units are eliminated, of course) but Infiltration on top of Ambush can, just like with simultaneous CC.

title: Tank shoots for No Smoke
question: I should know this, but if a Tank attempted to fire Smoke, rolls higher than his exponent, the shot doesn't occur.  If no further attempts to fire, can the tank then move in the Movement Phase?
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
As a clarification, if it rolls higher than the depletion number for special ammo a weapon isn't considered to have fired unless it malfunction or low ammo occurs [C8.9].

As trivia, a vehicle can use one type of vehicular smoke dispenser in the MPh then fire WP in the AFPh.

If the tank tried to fire smoke during the PFPh and rolled higher than the depletion number, it isn't considered to have fired.
So, unless it fires anything else, it can move during the following MPh.

title: Building Locations VC
question: Let’s say a scenario in RB requires control of a certain number of building locations.  Am I right to assume that a two hex building (no stairwell) has four locations (because rooftops and cellars don’t count)?
author: Jgolch
consensus_answer:
Let’s away a scenario in RB requires control of a certain number of building locations.  Am I right to assume that a two hex building (no stairwell) has four locations (because rooftops and cellars don’t count)?
In Red Barricades cellars are full building Locations with all rights and privileges thereof [O6.1]. If the building is not a factory, in Red Factories (and Red Barricades before) it has six Locations for control purposes. Where you say, "no stairwell," I assume you mean to say it has "no *printed* stairwell," because in that case there is an inherent stairwell in both hexes [B23.22]. Per RF SSR3 rooftop Locations do not count for control, as you say.

If the building is a factory it has two Locations for control; it does not have a cellar.

title: Pushing Guns down Narrow Streets
question:
My opponent set up a 57mm AT Gun in the middle of downtown Sainte-Mère Église with the idea that he would push it out to the suburbs down Narrow Streets. Per C10.3 the Gun can't be pushed into bypass. The village terrain rules  give no exceptions for narrow streets. Is the only option to push the gun into a building, or have I missed something?

From a reality standpoint I don't see any reason that a Gun couldn't be pushed down any lane/path big enough for a farm cart, but by rule I think the Gun has to be pushed into the building.
author: jrvjrv
consensus_answer:
If a Gun were allowed to be placed on a Narrow road, how would one apply the B31.122 TCA Change and B31.123 VCA change?
If vehicles can do it, why not the Guns? 😈

replies.body:
I'd say you are correct in the rules, and another reason to hate the infantry bypass rules

If I were to consider a rules fix, I'd treat the gun as a vehicle, and have it bypass in the same manner (and be pushed hexside by hexside)

Another example of adding more and more complexity to a simple basic scheme that was not designed to support that complexity.
European streets are not 80 m width even in cities, which is what SL map 1 reflects. And Russian 628 units needed then a 2 range to be able to shoot to the building in front of them, no matter what the real ranges of weapons are. So the basic scheme is just an abstraction not a simulation. Adding then more and more layers in the name of reality means fiddling with years of previous rulings, mapboards and scenarios and it is impossible to just make it all fit together. So no bypass for guns.

I agree, Martí.
We all will feel some tension between our idea of reality and the limits of the rules.
At some point, we have to accept that ASL is just a game, which requires some simplifications to remain playable.
I think that some already existing chrome could have been done with - but most of it is confined to HASL stuff.

...have I missed something?

I don't think so - I'm surprised this hasn't come up before.  Allowing pushed guns in bypass has a knock-on effect in other rules so I can see why it's not allowed but from a realism standpoint it doesn't feel right.
Could easily be an exception applied to the Narrow Streets rule (as ASL /loves/ its exceptions).

Could easily be an exception applied to the Narrow Streets rule (as ASL /loves/ its exceptions).
There would be many effects in interaction with many rules, so the exception would not be easy to implement.

The biggest problem with allowing Gun Bypass is that you don't know/choose when you when you will stop in most instances. Which means it could easily end up having to end its move in Bypass, which would also mean the pushing Infantry ends in Bypass....

I think the best solution that could be done is allowing a negative DRM on the pushing if it could move to where you're pushing it to via a narrow street. Even that would get gamey, and possibly a little complicated to write, but it won't tie things up in the Bypass conundrum.

Could easily be an exception applied to the Narrow Streets rule (as ASL /loves/ its exceptions).
The "problem" is that ASL does not allow infantry to end the MPh in bypass, unlike vehicles. When pushing a gun you never know when the music is going to stop, and you have to find a chair. You could allow the infantry and gun to remain in bypass, but now you have a strange EXC that might, somehow, be exploited for sleaze. And you'd have to answer the question of whether the infantry was at specific vertex or along the one (or two?) hexsides because, unlike with vehicles, infantry bypass is allows targeting *any* of the vertices.  You might have the gun and crew enter the bypassed building if it can't get out of bypass as with a Pin result, but again there's sleaze in them there hills. And what happens when instead of just a crew pushing the gun, there is a crew, a halfsquad, two squads and a leader pushing the gun. Do they all remain in bypass? Do they all enter the building? In my opinion it could be done but there's no *easy* extension of the rules, i.e. one that allows the action without some other implications to the system.

title: OVR vs a manned Gun
question:
Hi everyone ! 
We had for the first time this week a try on OVR during a scenario, but it was vs Infantry. 
After the game I went into details in the OVR rules and flowchart, it's a bit dense but I'll be okay ! 

One question though : what happens when an AFV declares an OVR vs a manned Gun ? 
I saw a lot of rules when it happens vs an unmanned/abandoned Gun, but what's happening otherwise ? I know the Crew can use OVR Prevention, but how is it dealt afterwards ? Resolution against the Crew and then the Random Gun Destruction ? 

Thanks in advance 🙂
author: Flyingkiki
consensus_answer:
Thanks a lot for your answer ! 
Okay so OVRing a manned Gun is a bit like following the principle of the C11 chapter, where you cannot attack a Gun directly : it needs a Direct Hit. Which, in the case of the OVR, is represented by a KIA on the crew, as per A9.74. 
Does it seem correct phrased that way ? :)
I don't know that I'd phrase it that way, but you might think of it that way sort of. Guns that are not mobile (NM, RFNM, unlimbered) can be affected without eliminating the crew ("a Direct Hit") or even breaking it [A9.74], so that's different. I'd say the idea is parallel but not exactly the same. I can't say I've ever seen it come up, and if it did it's entirely possible I overlooked A9.74. Eliminating or more usually breaking the crew is almost always enough.

A crew manning a Gun is Infantry, so it is resolved as infantry. Typically the crew manning a Gun gets the emplacement TEM. Sometimes the Gun is not emplaced or is emplaced but prefers a different TEM (e.g. stone building, trench, foxhole). In order to be subject to Random SW/Gun Destruction [A9.74] the crew would have to be eliminated by a KIA, or the Gun would have to be unlimbered, NM or RFNM.

title: Cloaking in RB - how many makes a dozen?
question:
So, it's time to get reserves in to form of cloaking.  How many can I get you say.

What say 12 is the maximum?
author: Oberst_Hausser
consensus_answer:
So, it's time to get reserves in to form of cloaking.  How many can I get you say.

What say 12 is the maximum? 

This is most cryptic. What are you trying to ask? What is the maximum number of cloaking counters needed per RG? Per CG date? Per campaign game? Since they are set up using the principles of cloaking [O11.6194b], one cloaking counter is given per squad [E1.411] plus five Dummy Cloaking counters [O11.6194b], so the maximum per RG is the maximum number of squads in an RG (twelve) plus five, which is to say seventeen. Of course there could be multiple Infantry RGs purchased per day, and over the course of a campaign game multiple days, so the maximum number of cloaking counters that might be needed in a day or over the course of a CG is "large."

title: Failure to Voluntarily Rout?
question: It's the Polish RtPh and No Quarter is in effect for the Poles. The broken German squad must rout and the leader opts to voluntarily rout with it. The Polish 2-4-8 in the cellar drops HIP. The German squad can still rout to the first level, but I was wondering: if the building was Level 1 only, and the squad is eliminated for failure to rout, what happens to the leader? The rules say a squad fails an Interdiction MC, the leader is eliminated, but seems less clear on what happens before the rout starts. Is the leader eliminated also can he opt to remain in the hex?
author: Holdit
consensus_answer: But that's specific to this example. In the general case the issue could arise, and I don't know the answer. Per A10.5, "Broken units must rout away (ATTACKER first—one unit at a time [EXC: Voluntary Rout; 10.711]) during that RtPh or be eliminated for Failure to Rout [EXC: Surrender; 20.21]." There is no indication that unbroken units are eliminated for failure to rout, so I would suppose that the leader ends the RtPh where the broken unit was eliminated. That would be how I would play it, but a q&a from mmp might decide differently.

So in this case the broken unit would rout to R6, then gain LOS to the surprise in the cellar, which would probably cause it to refigure its rout.

title: MG TH and ROF
question: I used a MMG to attack a moving AFV with a TH attemt and got ROF. Can I late in the MPh use the MMG to First Fire, Subsequent First Fire and Final Protective Fire vs a moving Infanrty unit or can I only use the MMG as ordnance?
author: Nslcole
consensus_answer:
Yes you can.
You also could attempt another TH DR.

If you lost ROF, you still could Subsequent First Fire/Final Protective Fire (vs infantry, an unarmored vehicle or an AFV with vulnerable PRC).
If marked with First Fire (not Final Fire), the MG could even fire during the DFPh at an ADJACENT target (at halved FP, doubled for PBF, etc.).
You could not, however, if ROF is lost, fire the MG as ordnance again, as SW don't use Intensive Fire (and a MG that would fire on the IFT at half FP may not fire as ordnance).

title: When Does Defilade Exist?
question: If a unit is on a level 1 hex and draws LOS to a level ground hex, when, if ever, do intervening level 1 hexes of the same hill block LOS? The rules use the term "blind hexes" rather than defilade but they're extremely unclear.
author: MajerBlundor6
consensus_answer:
A unit only can see over an obstacle to a lower level only if they are at a higher level than the obstacle.
So a unit at level one cannot see a unit at level 0 if a level 1 obstacle is between them.
Blind hexes are considered when the obstacle is lower than the higher unit.

See A6.2 example :

EX: Woods are a level 1 obstacle to LOS. If the firing unit is beneath level 1, it cannot see through ground-level woods to a target hex at level 1 or lower. The target unit would have to be at an elevation > the top of the obstacle to possibly establish a LOS to a hex at ground level beyond that obstacle.

Defilade is not a notion in ASL and you should not introduce it in your analysis.

That's the great irony of ASL. It tries so very hard to be a weeds up, hyper-detailed simulation of real world combat but then utterly fails to include fundamental, real world, military 101 concepts such as "defilade" which are intuitive to so many of us. 😆 

Anyway, I truly appreciate your attempt at an answer, but I still have absolutely no idea as to whether or not a unit on level 1 ground can see a unit at level 0 if there is intervening level 1 ground forming the same hill. It sounds like the intervening hex would block LOS but I'm not entirely sure since the rules also reference X number of intervening hexes to block LOS.  🤔
