title: Broken units and DM tokens
question: Does any broken unit automatically get a DM token when being fired at with enough FP to potentially cause a NMC? Whatever the attack DR result?
author: poifpoif
consensus_answer:
Does any broken unit automatically get a DM token when being fired at with enough FP to potentially cause a NMC? Whatever the attack DR result?
Correct. If an IFT attack *might* have inflicted a NMC that is enough. On a one FP flat a broken unit is marked DM regardless if the attack DR is a twelve, and even if the firing weapon breaks.

On a one FP up two the answer depends on whether the unit/weapon can cower. If it can cower, no DR can result in a NMC because an original snakeeyes cowers off the IFT and so no DM is placed, regardless of the actual IFT DR. If it can't cower the broken target is marked with a DM, again regardless of the actual DR. Those BMGs firing at long range can DM a broken unit hiding in a wooden building.

For ordnance a hit would have to be achieved first, but the actual *effects* DR doesn't matter. Ordnance doesn't cower, of course, but you would have to factor in TEM for the ATT.

title: Bump-scouting [A12.15] when already in the same hex?
question: An enemy concealed unit moved into a hex with a friendly concealed unit. In the CCPh Strength Factors were revealed, Insurance Cards were exchanged and Ambush was rolled, after which both sides looked at the situation and decided that losing concealment for making a CC attack was not in their best interests (complicated situation; ask if you are really interested). Come the next turn the friendly unit would like to strip concealment from the enemy to give outside units an opportunity to attack. It does not have enough FP to do so reliably in the PFPh. Searching would clearly work but seems a bit heavy-handed. But bump-scouting seems only to work if the unit is entering the Location. Does the friendly unit really have to leave the Location then attempt to re-enter in order to bump-scout?
author: jrvjrv
consensus_answer:
Why did the moving unit not lose concealment straightaway, according to Chart A12.121 (note A specifically notes Detection) & how did they stay in the same hex subsequently?
Or did you mean to say they Advanced into the hex?
I did not mean to say anything; I did not specify how they came to be in the same hex at the start of the CCPh both concealed. It wasn't especially important to my question. In my particular case it was the obvious way, one Advanced on the other. But this can also happen if G.4 applies, which allows units to move into hexes with HIP enemy units without invoking Detection. It might also occur if Personnel unloads from a vehicle. It's not clear what would happen if a CS/cs result from a concealed AFV (e.g. eliminated by mines) would result in concealed surviving PRC, but if so that might be another way. Perhaps there are other ways this might occur too.

edit: it can also happen with a pillbox. I said they ended up in the same hex, not Location, and for a pillbox the limited CA can allow enemy units to enter the hex during the MPh while remaining concealed and without invoking Detection even if the unit in the pillbox is concealed. In that case, however, the outside unit can attack the inside unit without the usual halving for concealment in CC [B30.7], which affects the decision matrix. Of course with a pillbox there's no opportunity for bump-scouting. The unit in the pillbox may not exit into its hex during the MPh if there is an enemy unit there [B30.6], although the mechanics of this are a bit vague when there are concealed units involved.

title: WA Non adjacent fire
question:
I don´t seem to find a post about this.

It´s the german PFPh and a german squad have WA in G3.
A german Hero and 2 HS in G4 fires on the enemies in G2.

Do the enemies in G2 get Wall Tem or are they considered to be in Open Ground?
author: Nslcole
consensus_answer:
Only one Location can ever have WA over the same hexside, so they are in Open Ground because the Germans already have WA (B9.321).
The unit in G3 can fire on the target in G2 using in-hex TEM only, but it doesn't share its WA with units in other hexes. In fact if G3 were a multi-level building hex and there were Germans on an upper level, the target in G2 could use the wall TEM against an attack from the upper level despite the ground-level having WA. WA for one particular unit does not grant WA for all units firing through the hexside. See my above post quoting B9.31.

replies.body: Only one Location can ever have WA over the same hexside, so they are in Open Ground because the Germans already have WA (B9.321) edit versus the adjacent Germans, but see below for non-adjacent.

I don´t seem to find a post about this.

It´s the german PFPh and a german squad have WA in G3.
A german Hero and 2 HS in G4 fires on the enemies in G2.

Do the enemies in G2 get Wall Tem or are they considered to be in Open Ground?

If the units in G3 were firing, the targets in G2 would not get the wall(/hedge, which I will not repeat hereafter) TEM. But WA only helps a unit that has the wall as a hexside of its hex. It does not affect units that do not have the wall as a hexside of the hex. This is written in a rather convoluted and indirect fashion in B9.31, "A target unit not claiming WA receives only in-hex TEM, but may instead use wall/hedge TEM vs enemy units which do not have WA over the hexside." The target unit in G2 may only use the in-hex TEM vs the enemy units in G3, but may use the wall/hedge TEM vs the enemy units in G4, because the enemy units in G4 are "enemy units which do not have WA over the hexside" even while the enemy in G3 *do* have WA over the hexside.

Restated, to deny the wall TEM to a target immediately behind that wall, the firing unit has to have WA over the wall on one of its hexsides. It is not sufficient for some other unit to have WA over that wall. WA is not transferable to units which do not have the wall on one of their own their hexsides.

That perhaps makes you the only one.

This is another example, which may be even more surprising.

All German units are in hex 10Z9, but they are displayed "spread out" so you can see the contents of the stack. 10Z8 is an orchard hex.

Here the German squad has WA over the 10Z9/10Z8 hexside. But the vehicle, being in a hex with positive TEM, cannot gain WA [B9.32]. Also per B9.32, "Units in a Location do not need to share the same WA status," and that is the case here. If the squad in 10Z9 fired on 10Z8, the TEM would be +0 (orchard), but if the halftrack fired, including in a firegroup with the German squad, the British squad would have the option to use the wall TEM despite not having WA (and of course would do so). The WA of the German squad cannot be transferred to the German halftrack even though they are in the same Location and the wall in question is a hexside of their own hex.

If the German stack were in 10Y9 instead, the halftrack could have WA, and indeed would be required to have it.

I've been trying to think of a way to summarize the rule, and this may be it: if the firing unit does *not* have WA over the hexside, the target can use the hexside TEM at its option (even if the target also does not have WA).

title: PSK against a Jeep with a half squad and Sniper effects
question:
Playing Apples to Apples, my half squad with a PSK hit a Jeep with a loaded half squad.  How is this resolved?

Shortly after, my opponent activated my Sniper.  My Sniper landed on a Half Track loaded with a Squad.  What happens to it and the Squad?  It was not designated as Buttoned up.
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
The Sniper has two eligible targets:  the half track crew and the passenger squad.

Random Selection determines which gets attacked.

If it is the squad, it can be broken (by a dr 1) or pinned (by a dr 2) and can remain as a passenger (D6.62).

If it is the crew, the sniper will inflict either a Stun or STUN (ie Stun + recall) result (see D5.34 and D5.341).
As fate would have it, Random roll was 4 and 4.  So the Crew was STUNNED/Recalled and the Squad was Broken.  Do they stay loaded on the Half Track or are they allowed to bail out before the HT moves off the board in the MPh?

title: Halving FP for a MG with ROF as SFF vs DFPh?
question: I think I have had this wrong for a long time. See if this is right. A four FP squad with a two FP LMG fires on an ADJACENT target at twelve FP. The target is not eliminated and spent > one MP. The LMG keeps ROF. The defender could use DFF (not SFF) to fire again with the LMG alone at four FP. The squad could use SFF with its inherent only at four FP. It could use SFF with both its inherent *and* the LMG for six FP, firing the LMG as Sustained Fire even though the LMG retained ROF [A8.3]. Alternately the squad and LMG could fire in the DFPh against the ADJACENT target at eight FP, four FP for the inherent marked with First Fire, four FP for the LMG not marked with First Fire. In the DFPh the LMG would *not* be treated as using Sustained Fire because it retained ROF. Treating an unmarked MG as using Sustained Fire when firing together with inherent that is marked with First Fire only applies when using Subsequent First Fire and not in the DFPh.
author: jrvjrv
consensus_answer:
Following along these same lines, could the LMG, after maintaining its ROF, fire at a unit that is further away than the unit it (and its owning squad) previously fired at? 

Yes, the LMG fired alone is not restricted by SFF restrictions because it is using DFF, not SFF. It can fire beyond the nearest KEU. It can fire at long range.

Also, could the LMG wait until the Defensive Fire Phase to fire at any unit, even though its owning Squad has previously First Fired?
Yes, as long as you don't mean something silly by "any" like, for example, a unit out of LOS. In the DFPh a unit/weapon not marked can fire normally, and a unit/weapon marked with First Fire can fire at an adjacent (or same hex) target.

title: LOS hills
question: Shouldn't the 4-6-7 in 3F9 be able to see the building on hill 3I10 since this is now a building on level 2?
author: neo.colpaert
consensus_answer:
LOS is always traced to the base of the obstacle or terrain feature, not to all its height. 
If the building in 3I10 had a second story, there would be a LOS to that second story, which would be 2 levels from the ground. Or if it had a rooftop, which would be 1.5 levels from the ground, or a slope, which would be 1.75 levels from the ground. But the building's Level 0 is always out of LOS of that unit.

replies.body:
LOS is always traced to the base of the obstacle or terrain feature, not to all its height. 
If the building in 3I10 had a second story, there would be a LOS to that second story, which would be 2 levels from the ground. Or if it had a rooftop, which would be 1.5 levels from the ground, or a slope, which would be 1.75 levels from the ground. But the building's Level 0 is always out of LOS of that unit.

The building in 3F9 is at level one and rises to level two. Units in it are at level one. In the same way if the building had been in E10, it would be at level zero as would all units in it and its "obstacleness" would rise to level one.

It is a one story building on level 1: units in it are at level 1 - nobody is dancing on the roof.
Level 1 hills block LOS to/from level 0.
The building "goes up" to level 2, but ASL usually cares about the base level, which is level 1. So no LOS, sorry.
OK understood. The building should have a second story with a unit in it or rooftop with a unit on it to have LOS.

title: Asterisk * and Mortars
question:
What's the purpose of a "*" suffix next to a Mortar caliber? 

According to the rules:
“*”, “L”, or “LL” suffix means that certains To Hit modifiers are used at various ranges, due to varying muzzle velocities or inherent accuracy, and also serve to change the To Kill capabilities of these Guns/SW as listed on the respective col- umns of their To Kill Tables. 

Mortars, however, don't really use TK tables.
author: poifpoif
consensus_answer: As above it affects the TH numbers. See the C4 Modifications to the Basic TH# on the C3 To Hit Table. Because nearly all MTRs are short barrel length, the Modified TH# [C4.5] for MTRs out to twenty-four hex range is seven, a fact which you can memorize as long as you realize there are some exceptions. The American M2 4.2-in. Mortar is a "normal" length gun, and some small MTRs (e.g. the Soviet 50mm RM obr. 40 and the German 5cm leGrW 36) run into caliber-size modifications at longer range too.

title: D14.31 Impulse Movement, D7.1 OVR and A12.41 concealed infantry (AFV entering hex)
question:
My platoon of Italian tankettes starts in motion 25DD5 (level 2 open ground) and 25DD6 (base level 2; AFV in the wadi at level 1), like so:

On their first impulse, they each move one hex forward to 25CC6 (level 3 open ground) and 25CC7 (base level 2; AFV in the wadi at level 1), like so:

The platoon spends 5 MPs for that impulse:  the most MP spent by any unit in that impulse (4 MPs +1 COT for the move from the level 2 open ground of 25DD5 to the level 3 open ground of 25CC6) (D14.31).

The tankette in 25CC6 secretly wants to OVR the Indian unit in that hex but because the hex contains only unknown enemy units it is exempt from the usual requirement of announcing the OVR as a combined expenditure with that of entering the hex (D7.1).

The Indian 4-4-7 tries to keep its concealment by taking a PAATC (A12.41) but fails and is revealed and pinned (I haven't placed the pin marker to avoid clutter):

What I want to do next is move onto impulse 2, in which the tankette in 25CC6 conducts an OVR for 3.25 MPs and the tankette in 25CC7 moves to 25BB6 (base level 3; AFV in the wadi at level 2, having ascended one level):

The cost of that impulse would be 7 MPs:  the most MP spent by any unit (4 MPs for the elevation change from 25CC7 to 25BB6 +2 MPs for the wadi +1 MP COT).

But can I?

A12.41 splits the MP cost of entering 25CC6 from the MP cost of the OVR.

D14.31 says that in each impulse each participating unit "may perform a maximum of one MF/MP expenditure" and that the impulse ends "when every participating unit has completed its single MF/MP expenditure".

Does A12.41 result in the MP cost of entering 25CC6 falling into Impulse 1 and the OVR MP cost falling into Impulse 2?

If so, the left hand tankette can move two hexes forward for 12 MPs over two impulses whilst the right hand tankette moves one hex in the first impulse and overruns in the second.

If the cost of entering 25CC6 and the OVR both fall into the first impulse, that impulse costs 8.25 MPs and the second impulse move by the left hand tankette can't happen.

(This and my earlier question arise in the course of a very enjoyable play of Showdown at Tug Argan Pass)
author: Malcolm C
consensus_answer:
As per the answer above the units need not expend MPs for the same purposes. One can imagine a "chain" OVR where the lead vehicle in a Platoon OVRs a target while a trailing AFV trundles along behind in one impulse followed by a second impulse where the leading AFV exits and the following AFV performs its OVR. 

Another option in this case is to have the second vehicle Delay while the first one performs its OVR. In this case you said you wanted to enter 25BB6 with the second vehicle, but this option is available for situations where you do not want to.

Note that Platoon Movement is the only time that Delay MP can be spent while not Stopped [D2.17]. I see players trying to declare Delay MP while not Stopped and not using Platoon Movement; don't try that when playing me.

Since each tank paid one MP to do so, the platoon thus expends one MP for this Impulse, for a total expenditure of three MP so far in the MPh." (emphasis added).

title: FT vs hex occupied by enemy squad and friendly AFV
question:
The Stopped FT equipped Italian tankette in 25H6 wants to Bounding First Fire its FT against the entrenched 4-4-7 in 25I7, which is in the same Location as the Non-Stopped Italian tank (which is part of the same Platoon).

There is no Melee in 25I7:  this is a drive-by.

A22.34 says that a FT attack against an AFV is resolved on the HE & Flame To Kill Table, but only if the AFV is predesignated as the main target (it isn't).

Although it seems somewhat counter-intuitive, am I right in thinking that the FT attack will not affect the friendly AFV at all (the AFV has no Vulnerable PRC to suffer a Collateral Attack)?

Here is the same situation without the 25I7 stack expanded:

and without units (to show the terrain):
author: Malcolm C
consensus_answer:
Friendly units are attacked "only if specifically allowed to by the rules governing a particular circumstance (e.g., Prisoners, Melee, OBA), Area Target Type vs enemy units [C3.33])" [A7.4]. This is not any of those circumstances. The friendly unit is not attacked.

title: Sniper attack on a Half Track?
question: So my German SPW Mortar carrier went on an Area Fire tear on some Russians, activating his Sniper twice.  First to no avail, but then rolled a 2 on the second activation.  I'm not sure what happens here.  Does the SPW crew become Stunned, or does the Inherent Infantry HS manning the Mortar become Pinned?
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
So if the crew dismounts, they will carry the little stun with them then?

The rules don't really mention what happens when a crew dismounts when it has a Stun/STUN status. One assumes they carry it around with them or record it; you have to record the crew anyway because it is Special, i.e. it is a dual-purpose, Infantry-and-Vehicle crew. It has no affect on performance while Infantry.

If a vehicle is stunned in its turn can its pinned or broken passengers disembark normally as if the vehicle wasn't under the effects of stun?

A. No, a Stunned vehicle cannot do anything.

title: non reciprocal ADJACENT status ?
question: are Russian HS ADJACENT to Germans ? Think yes .. but are Germans ADJACENT to Russians ? and if not , how are affected issues like rout, surrender by disruption ( B26.41 puzzles me more and  more ) , PBF and perhaps something else ?
author: adolfinger
consensus_answer:
I can't think of a way for one unit to be ADJACENT and the other not ADJACENT.
Probably true.  Whenever there's a seeming asymmetry re ADJACENT, if one is clearly ADJACENT, then it's mutual, generally.

EX:
At first glance, one unit in an OG hex is lower-case adjacent to one in an abutting Marsh hex (because the OG dweller could not enter that Marsh hex in an APh).
B16.4 Infantry/Cavalry may enter a marsh hex only at the cost of their entire MF allotment (inclusive of a broken unit’s RtPh allotment); a marsh hex cannot be entered during the APh, nor can it be entered via Low Crawl (A10.52) [EXC to all: along a bridge]. Entry of a marsh hex from a lower elevation is a Minimum Move (A4.134).
That unit in Marsh is ADJACENT to the one in OG, though (because it could  enter that OG hex in an APh).

But the Index defintion doesn't require symmetry, only that one unit be ADJACENT -- when so, both are.
ADJACENT (Locations [and units in them] are considered ADJACENT if any Infantry unit in one Location could conceivably—ignoring any enemy presence—advance into the other during the APh and a LOS exists between the two Locations, excluding SMOKE Hindrance [B.10] and NVR [E1.101]
(Assuming Infantry and mutual LOS in this case.)

".8 ADJACENT: Hexes (and the units inside them) are "adjacent" if they share a common hexside. I think you have this right. The tank, not held in Melee nor a Melee unit, could use TPBF if otherwise allowed in the PFPh, MPh or AFPh. The infantry, as long as it is held in Melee, could not attack until the CCPh.

Note that some interesting things might happen in the meanwhile. If the tank decides to expend a start MP but fails a Mechanical Reliability or stall DR, it still releases the infantry from Melee, which would allow DFF by that infantry.

title: Riders in Bypass
question: Can they disembark off a Tank in Bypass? Even if they dont have enough MF to move out of Bypass?
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
D6.5 states that an unload does indeed only cost 1 MF but it also states that that 1 MF puts the unit, "beneath the vehicle." Aside from Bailing Out [D6.24], could you indicate where it is stated a unit may be placed anywhere else, and would this not put the Riders in voluntary bypass with no means to exit?

When a Passenger/Rider is put "beneath" the vehicle it is in the ground level Location. The vehicle is in that same Location but by the vehicle bypass rules is allowed to remain in bypass. The Infantry is not. Per D6.5, "Passengers/Riders of a vehicle in Bypass which unload (even if they do not have enough remaining MF to move into the obstacle) or which during their MPh Abandon/Survive/Bail-Out (5.4-.6, 6.24) are assumed to be in the terrain of the vehicle's CAFP (2.36) for purposes of any Defensive First Fire vs them. Immediately after all such First Fire is resolved, they are assumed to be in the woods or building terrain of the obstacle itself." So the infantry for a brief moment are at the CAFP after unloading then after all DFF they "fall into" the obstacle. There is no cost beyond unloading, i.e. the nature of the terrain is ignored.

title: Defensive options for AFVs?
question:
So we're playing an early war scenario where there are a bunch of Pz I's versus superior (in terms of armor + gun size) French tanks.  It has proven to give us some good learning questions when an outclassed AFV faces another.

I /think/ we have a fairly good grasp now, but wanted to run this by the consigliere and see what we might have gotten wrong or were missing...

What can the weaker AFV due when confronted by the superior one...
1) Go for Deliberate Immobilization (need hull hit with a +5 DRM, but might be able to DI it in a bad location and then just avoid it)

2) Use defensive smoke dischargers to try to lay smoke during the enemy MPh.  This can be done either before or after a DFF shot (we think) and does NOT count as DFF.  But only get one attempt per enemy MPh.

3) Attempt to go into Motion during the enemy MPh provided the enemy tank didn't start in your LOS and you make the dr.  This has to be done BEFORE any DFF shots, but can be done before or after smoke discharger use.  Only get one attempt per enemy MPh, so make it count.  Not sure if this can be done AFTER the triggering vehicle is done moving and other units have moved (i.e. can you 'come back' to the AFV and declare a Motion attempt at the end of the enemy MPh, provided you haven't DFF'ed?).  If you succeed, remember that you can change your VCA and TCA.

4) Avoid engaging the enemy armor and let your infantry deal with them.  If you /have/ to engage them, look to get point blank rear shots via the 'swarm'.  Consider always staying in Motion since you're essentially rolling for a critical hit anyway.  Intensive Fire to get as many shots as possible when it makes sense.

I think that mostly covers the options (obviously some are going to be very situational and specific to the scenario, so I don't expect this to ever be a complete list).
author: kbernatz
consensus_answer:
A MG can't use Deliberate Immobilization [C5.71]. This takes that option off the table for the Pz I. Also French AFVs will often be small, making the DI shot that much worse.

For the particular pairing you suggest, early war French AFVs vs German Pz Is, the Germans may have some other advantages. Most often the French tanks will be radioless, meaning they are effectively slower because the platoon often has to make the same extra expenditure (crossing a wall/hedge, climbing a hill) multiple times. Often members of the platoon will hinder each others shots and/or prevent itself from having LOS (perhaps a member of the platoon can't make it past an obstacle). The factors make radioless vehicles less effective unit-for-unit. The French tanks are also often RST or 1MT, meaning they must be BU to fire, although that particular advantage is lost vs a Pz I (or Pz II). All this says the Germans should be more maneuverable than the French and more able to gain an advantage by movement.

That said the Pz I is not going to be killing many French AFVs (unless they are FT-17s, and even then). The typical French armor is around four AF, and the Pz I's basic TK# is four. Even with range and rear target that's not a recipe for slaughter. Based on this the German is probably looking for opportunities to use his tanks against infantry, and looking to avoid the French tanks using his superior maneuverability.

title: SSR KGP12?
question:
Hey everyone,

 My long-distance opponent (he's in Germany) and I have decided to play Schwerpunkt's scenario SP 23 Assault on the Hotel Continental.  It's SSR #4 states "British tanks are not subject to Recall.  SSR KGP 12 applies instead.

Neither one of us owns either of the KampfGruppe Peiper modules.  Anyone out there who does own it clue us in on SSR KGP 12?

Many thanks in advance.
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
Wouldn't want you not to be able to play without having to invest in yet another HASL 🙂 ...

"KGP12. GERMAN STUN/RECALL: A vehicle of the German OB (including a captured U.S. vehicle) does not suffer Recall due to MA disablement. A Recall due to attack effects (D5.341-.342) suffered by a German Inherent crew is always treated as a Stun result only [EXC: an armor leader may be Eliminated as per D5.341]; i.e., no Recall ensues. However, the +1 DRM effects of all Stun results vs a German Inherent crew are cumulative. In addition, when these total +DRM equal one < the vehicle's CS# (D5.6), its Inherent crew's abilities are limited to those of a SMC crew (A21.22); when the total +DRM equal the CS#, the crew is Eliminated and the vehicle abandoned (leave the "+#"  counter on the vehicle). Infantry wishing to re-crew that vehicle during play must first, using Hazardous Movement in the vehicle's Location (and position—e.g., not in an entrenchment), expend one MF separately to reduce the total "+#" by one; and only when that total "+#" equals zero (or "1" if OT or unarmored) may the vehicle be remanned."

Enjoy your game.

title: Firelanes
question:

author: Nslcole
consensus_answer:
A9.223, "The MG malfunctions whenever its Fire Lane Residual FP attack DR is also an Original Malfunction DR." This is unlike regular residual, where the residual attack is completely disassociated from the unit/weapon that made the attack. For this reason it can be pretty scary to put down a firelane with B11 or worse weapons.

As another matter of trivia, the MG has to be "Good Order." "Good Order" for a weapon means it is fully manned (no lone leaders putting down firelanes), not malfunctioned (that's pretty much a gimmie) and not subject to Ammo Shortage. The last doesn't come up that often but for example if you are playing a CG and have isolated setup areas it can be a factor.

title: Impact of rolling Gust in weather die roll
question:
Does the affect of the Gust rolled in a turn impact the entire turn? 

Once the Gust is enacted on the roll we immediately took the impact by lowering any existing smoke and potentially rolling to fire spread. 

But would the impact continue through the turn such as the placing ordinance smoke/WP and the same for smoke grenades would not be available for the turn?

Thanks all.
author: rhunter1148
consensus_answer: Gusts have no effect other than at the specified times in the ASOP, i.e. during the RPh [Step 1.12A] and the AFPh [Step 5.13A]. In particular Smoke Dischargers and SMOKE grenades can be used normally, SMOKE may be fired during the PFPh, enemy MPh, and DFPh normally. Any SMOKE placed during the turn would be affected in ASOP Step 5.13A.

title: B9.323 Mandatory WA
question:
I don`t think I get it right. 
Emplacement is not in-hex tem, as I read B9.323

So if a Emplaced gun set up behind a Hedges in a Brush or Open grund hex, has the gun Crew to take the WA of +1 tem (not the +2 emplaced tem), as it can`t claim at least +1 in-hex tem?
author: Nslcole
consensus_answer:
To add to the topic. If a Gun can normally setup HIP in concealment terrain, if forced to use WA to shoot through bocage does the player need to show the WA or is the recorded secretly? 
Per B9.324 a hidden unit may not claim WA. A unit would have to have WA to have LOS and shoot past the adjacent hex [B9.521]. Per B9.322 coming out of HIP is one of the times a unit can claim WA, even if an enemy unit has just moved adjacent [B9.324].
B9.324 now reads (per J8 errata), "A HIP unit that desires to claim WA during setup must secretly record such WA status [EXC: 9.323]." It can also set up without WA (unless mandatory) and claim it as it is put on board per B9.322.

As a side note Guns can normally set up HIP in *any* terrain as long as they are emplaced, A12.34.

C11.2, "In all cases, however, the Emplacement TEM cannot be used in addition to any other positive TEM; the Gun's owner may choose one or the other, but not both." Likewise a Gun in woods can (and probably will) use its emplacement TEM instead of woods TEM (although if fired on by Indirect Fire, the -1 airburst will be cumulative). A Gun in a stone building or rubble or in a pillbox could also use its emplacement TEM instead, but it is hard to imagine when this might be a good idea.

title: Guards broken by a Sniper
question: My opponent activated my Sniper, which proceeded to break the half-squad Guarding 3 Squads of POW's.  The POW's failed to pass a NTC in order to attack the now Broken Half Squad.  Would the DM come off in the next Rally Phase?  I guess they are technically still Enemy Units, but I'm not sure that they would be able to impose/maintain the DM status on the Guards.
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
The prisoners are still prisoners until they attempt to escape. As such I don't believe they don't cause DM. I would apply the reasoning that prisoners not in the act of escape are not units because they don't have the ability to move independent of their guard [index: unit definition]. It is not super clear that prisoners in the act of escape are units, but at least in your case it seems likely that the DM would come off.

If in the act of escape they might be units or not, but when they make a CC attack vs the guard that would put the DM on [A10.62].

On further search there's the other reason the DM would come off and not be put on, even if ADJACENT to an escaping prisoner: A10.62, "A broken unit is also automatically under DM whenever a Known armed enemy unit is ADJACENT to it (even if it does not end the phase ADJACENT to it)." A prisoner is not armed, even an escaping one. If a prisoner attacks its broken guard in the CCPh, the guard becomes DM, but that would not be sufficient to DM a broken unit in the same hex or an ADJACENT hex that was not attacked.

title: Unit rout into a Tank Hex
question:
I have a unit that is DM in a building and needs to rout across a road to the next building. 
On the road. I have a tank that is stationary. 
Can I rout across to the building via the tank hex without claiming Low crawl? As there are enemy troops a few hexes away within normal range and LOS to the tank/road hex. 
Thanks for clarifying
author: alexisW
consensus_answer:
Lou is correct.

Anything that provides a positive TEM/Hindrance DRM means that the hex is NOT 'Open Ground' per the definition in Rout (see A10.531).  Note that things like the unit being CX, BU MA, Pinned, in Motion, etc. also prevent a unit from Interdicting (basically anything that adds a DRM or halves the unit's attack strength negates the unit from being an Interdictor per A10.532).

replies.body: I would say yes because the hex is no longer considered Open Ground due to the presence of the friendly tank. See B.9 ARTIFICIAL TERRAIN. Disclaimer: I haven't played ASL in over a decade.

Lou is correct.

Anything that provides a positive TEM/Hindrance DRM means that the hex is NOT 'Open Ground' per the definition in Rout (see A10.531).  Note that things like the unit being CX, BU MA, Pinned, in Motion, etc. also prevent a unit from Interdicting (basically anything that adds a DRM or halves the unit's attack strength negates the unit from being an Interdictor per A10.532).

As above, a stationary AFV provides TEM (usually; see D9.3 for some other odd exceptions) and so allows rout without the possibility of Interdiction. If the AFV had moved that turn but is currently not in Motion, its TEM becomes effective at the end of the AFPh, i.e. right before the RtPh. 

If the AFV were not present or was not qualified to exert the +1 TEM per D9.3, the broken unit could still rout through the hex without using Low Crawl (unless forced to surrender); it would just have to take Interdiction.

One of the more interesting things I have read about color blindness is that while it is in some sense a disability, in another sense it is an ability. People and animals with full color vision are more easily fooled by color camouflage. There are a variety of stories where during WWII units liked to have a colorblind member to "see through" camouflage. It's hard to tell (from a quick web search) if this is something that was made up after the fact or did actually happen. But it has been demonstrated enough to suggest that there is an advantage to being colorblind in exchange for the disadvantage. Unlike something like, say, not having a right hand, which has very little upside, being colorblind is an "engineering" tradeoff; you lose something to gain something else. See, for example, https://phys.org/news/2015-11-colour-blindness-aid-efforts.html.

title: Rowhouse question from CSW
question:
Not sure if people also follow CSW here, but thought I'd share this here before I consider submitting an errata request to the eASLRB maintainers.

Someone had a situation with two Soviet squads in SEPARATE, but adjacent rowhouse hexes (i.e. they both were in rowhouse hexes, but of distinct and separate rowhouse buildings).  By a strict reading of the rules, they could not form a FG together because they both were in rowhouse hexes and didn't have another unit in the FG who wasn't in a rowhouse hex.

Note that this is distinct from the movement rules (rowhouse hex to rowhouse hex), in which the rule explicitly calls out 'of the same building'.

The general consensus was that the FG /should/ be allowed, since they are not in the same rowhouse building.  IMO, it makes sense either way (one could 'zen' it that rowhouses don't have as many openings for supporting fire, so units in rowhouse hexes...same building or not ... wouldn't be able to effectively coordinate fire.  But one could also 'zen' it that the intent was adjacent and in the same rowhouse building, NOT separate buildings altogether.  Thoughts?
author: kbernatz
consensus_answer:
The relevant sections you are referring to are:
A7.5 FIRE GROUP (FG): Two or more units/weapons joining together to 
make a combined fire attack are a FG. Two SMC manning the same SW are 
not a FG as they are considered one combined firing unit. A FG may consist 
of units from more than one Location only if each participating unit occu-
pies a Location ADJACENT to another participating unit of the same FG. It 
is possible to have a FG composed of a virtually unlimited string of ADJA-
CENT Locations; provided each Location in the FG contains a unit that is 
participating in the attack. ... 

and

adjacent (hexes are considered adjacent if they share a common hexside): A.8

ADJACENT (Locations [and units in them] are considered ADJACENT if 
any Infantry unit in one Location could conceivably—ignoring any enemy 
presence—advance into the other during the APh and a LOS exists between 
the two Location ...  

and

 part of B23.71 Infantry in a Rowhouse may move/rout/ad-
vance/Withdraw-from-CC directly into another Rowhouse hex of the same 
building only at the ground or Rooftop (23.8) level; if at the ground level they 
must specify which side of the building they are “bypassing”. Such units mov-
ing/routing on the ground level expend three MF (one to “bypass” in the hex 
it is leaving where it would be attacked by any OBA/Residual-FP and two to 
enter the building), and can be Interdicted or Defensive First Fired upon with 
FFMO/FFNAM DRM by any unit capable of doing so that can trace a LOS 
to the vertex of the hexside crossed by the moving/routing unit on that side of 
the building. ... Units in different Rowhouses may not form a FG unless each is ADJACENT to 
another unit that is not in a Rowhouse but that is part of that FG. Each hex of 
a Rowhouse building is always considered a separate building for Rout and 
Mopping Up purposes but not for Building Control.

So, I don't think your comment is correct.  Units in adjacent rowhouse hexes at the ground or Rooftop levels ARE 'ADJACENT', as they can clearly advance to the adjacent rowhouse hex of the same building at 3 MFs.

And the FG text requires two conditions... the 'ADJACENT' as you note, plus "not in a Rowhouse but that is part of that FG".  Note that the FG text never includes the 'of the same building' clarifier that the move/advance/rout language uses.  One uses 'Rowhouse' and the other uses 'Rowhouse hex', which might be the nuance that covers this??  I honestly don't know.

Per the rules you quote units in rowhouses are typically  not ADJACENT because typically no LOS exists. The rowhouse bar usually blocks LOS between the two hexes. The units can Advance from/to but are still not ADJACENT, even at ground level. There are some odd hexes where the rowhouse bar does not extend the to the middle point of the hexside, and the rowhouse bar can be breached (e.g. by DC or AFV), and so the units are in fact ADJACENT. Then they can form firegroups. But in most cases the LOS is blocked and no firegroup can be formed between units in adjacent (but typically not ADJACENT) rowhouse hexes through a rowhouse hexside.

Rooftops are different. Personally I don't think of units on rooftops as being "in" the building. Regardless of my personal feelings on the matter, units on rooftops do have LOS to each other even in adjacent rowhouse hexes and would be able to form a firegroup.

ADJACENT requires a LOS. There is no LOS over an intact rowhouse black bar, hence the units you refer to above are "adjacent" but not "ADJACENT", and therefore cannot be part of the same FG.

ADJACENT is normally a requirement for moving as well, which is why rowhouses need a further explanation on the nature of a move from one ground level, rowhouse location to the another, adjacent, ground level, rowhouse location, namely, that the movment is a special form of bypass via the vertex.

B23.71 defines a Rowhouse as a structure containing Rowhouses - perhaps not an ideal choice of terminology! For me, the first clause of B23.71 limits the scope of everything that follows to a single building with no applicability to separate buildings.

title: ROF and a FF Squad ?
question: I First Fired a Squad along with its LMG.  The LMG kept Rate.  Does the fact that the Squad has already First Fired limit the LMG's options to fire only at the nearest in distance enemy?
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
it just can't combine with the squad's firepower any longer.
The LMG can combine with the squad's inherent SFF, but if it does it will be treated as if using SFF/sustained fire itself. A8.3, "Whenever a unit uses Subsequent First Fire, it must use all MG/IFE in its possession (up to the unit's normal operation capabilities; 7.35-.353) as Subsequent First Fire or forfeit their use for the remainder of that Player Turn (barring FPF)."

There aren't many circumstances when a player might choose to do this. Ordinarily in such a situation the player will fire a MG without the squad's inherent SFF until the MG runs out of ROF. One case where you might consider it is if an 8-3-8 possesses a MMG. The MMG would fire at four FP without the squad but the 8-3-8 (SFF) and the MMG (forced to use SFF per A8.3 above) would fire at six FP even though the MMG is also using sustained fire. I can't think of a case where you might do this with a LMG but perhaps someone else can come up with one.

replies.body: NRBH, but only the squad is marked First Fire - the LMG can fire freely as long as it keeps ROF; it just can't combine with the squad's firepower any longer.

The MMG would fire at four FP without the squad but the 8-3-8 (SFF) and the MMG (forced to use SFF per A8.3 above) would fire at six FP even though the MMG is also using sustained fire. title: ASLsk2: To Hit Dice Roll Modifiers Chart, Case 16. and 25
question:
Hi there,
we are investigating on that question so hardly since 1-2 hours:

In the above mentioned chart it says:

16: (...) 1-hex range (2-hex range +1) +2

and

2: 1-hex range vs. stopped vehicle (2-hex range: -1): -2 (...)

Those both somehow should apply to stopped targets or moving firerer

A) What the hell should that mean? I really can't interprete that rule precisely. Somebody have an explanation?
B) I also searched in the GOB but couldn't find a referring rule in Chapter C5/C6. To which rule of FullASL does that ASLsk-Rule refer?

Thanks for answers guys!
author: Awazungu
consensus_answer:
I thought it is somekind of Calculation (1-hex range....) but it actually means "A hex range of 1"

Correct, it should not be read as, "One minus the hex-range vs stopped vehicle..." It should be read as, "One-hex (with a dash joining the two words) range vs stopped vehicle..." 

The basic idea for ASL is that the TH chart is divided into six-hex-range segments (0-6, 7-12, 13-18, although the first is actually seven hexes), but in fact there is a substantial improvement at ranges of one hex and two hexes. In ASL this is adjusted by having a -2 TH Point Blank Range DRM at a range of one hex and a -1 TH DRM at a range of two hexes. In ASLSK the designers decided to change the way this was calculated (but not the end result) by having separate segments for range one and range two on the TH chart for infantry target type. So far so good, but when a vehicle is the target there is no special columns for ranges one and two, so the #25 DRM is added. This means that ASLSK is in a half-way state, where the ASL DRM is an ASLSK DRM when using the vehicular target type but baked into the TH chart when using the infantry target type.

And there is a further complication that when the firing vehicle is not stopped, the Point Blank Range DRM does not apply. This is handled in the #25 DRM by the parenthetical for the vehicular target type, but when using the Infantry Target Type the adjustment baked into the TH table has to be subtracted out by the #16 TH DRM.

Note that you can't be using the ASLSK#2 chart for all this. None of these adjustments are necessary in ASLSK#2 because there are no vehicles. You must be using the ASLSK#3 (or later) chart.

Personally I think the ASL way is simpler when there are vehicles. I suspect that when the designers created the ASLSK#2 TH chart they didn't realize they were going to have to jump through so many hoops to get the right values in ASLSK#3. But that is speculation.

This means that if the firer is shooting at a vehicle (using the Vehicle Target Type), it can add a -2/-1 (range 1/2) DRM.

title: Berserk and the APh
question: So my opponent just Defensive Fired at my Adjacent Russian Squad, making them go Berserk.  Reading 15.431, my newly Berserk Squad, which had previously Prep fired, cannot Advance into Combat?  They have to wait until their next Mph?  Is there some significance for that?
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
The reason for not advancing is fairly obvious. They're represented as doing all-out charge at their target, with 8MFs, which matches the maximum any infantry unit will ever go (possible EXC - downhill skiers), without ever going CX. Advance is supposed to be a more cautious creeping forward (back, sideways...) that can't be shot at. For simplicity's sake, units can occasionally be denied a charge at all when they go berserk at an odd time. I'd think some sort of exception for guys going berserk late in their own turn would make a certain amount of sense, but then you'd have to remember that this one hasn't charged yet, and possibly let guys fire at them (since it is a charge)... and you'd tie the turn sequence in knots fast.

On ambushing, I'll also note that you have a potential ambush whenever someone advances into appropriate terrain. So, if someone charges into a hex, and then someone else advances into the same hex (easier now that the defender is too busy to fire), you can have an ambush with berserk units. Have fun with the +1 berserk modifier though.

title: Concealment issues
question: Having a rules meltdown with Concealment.  We are setting up 126 Commando Schenke.  The Russians get 13 Concealment counters in their OOB.  How does that work again?  All the Russians will set up in buildings (concealment Terrain), so will they be Concealed automatically and 6 Dummy Stacks may then be placed on board?  Or do the 13 OOB given Concealment counters go on the real Squads?
author: Fly by Night
consensus_answer:
So since the Germans set up on map as well, if I wanted to create 2 or 3 Dummy Stacks, I would use whats left of the OOB given Concealment counters to Conceal real squads, leaving the ones that won't be seen after the German set up to be concealed then, correct? And if I leave a real squad up close and in LOS of a German Squad, even though in Concealment terrain, they would not be automatically given a Concealment counter? Correct?
Correct on both counts. A unit in LOS at start can't get a free "?", disregarding HIP for Guns, but can have an OB-granted "?" placed on it if in concealment terrain.

You can also leave units unconcealed where they won't be seen to gain free "?" after all setup is done. Your opponent can see the top counter, but can't peel apart the stack. This sometimes suggests stacking things in odd ways at start, for instance a stack with a halfsquad, a HMG and a 9-2 leader might be set up with the HMG possessed by the 9-2 and the halfsquad on top. You just have to remember to exchange the HMG to the halfsquad in the first turn RPh. You could even fake this by putting a halfsquad on top of two OB-granted "?".

title: Question about British Carrier A and British Mark VIB
question:
I have a question about the British Carrier A with a BMG as MA, and the British Mark VIB with a CMG as MA
If I use those MGs can I:
-	make a TH attempt on the VTT, and after I have exhausted ROF make a IF shot? 
-	make a IFT shot(first fire) on a squad who moved 2 hexes, and if I exhausted ROF also make a subsequent first fire shot if I wish?
author: Nslcole
consensus_answer:
I have a question about the British Carrier A with a BMG as MA, and the British Mark VIB with a CMG as MA
If I use those MGs can I:
-	make a TH attempt on the VTT, and after I have exhausted ROF make a IF shot? 
-	make a IFT shot(first fire) on a squad who moved 2 hexes, and if I exhausted ROF also make a subsequent first fire shot if I wish?

You may use IF (q&a below) but not SFF. SFF is only available to Infantry. Per A9.3 it could use sustained fire in the DFPh.

"C5.6 May a vehicular-mounted MG/ATR/light-MTR use Intensive Fire?
A. Yes, if it is MA. Such a weapon is considered a Gun (C2.1). [An93a; An95w; An96; Mw]"

Note: there is a q&a saying an IFE Gun may use SFF: "C2.29 May an IFE-capable Gun that has exhausted its Multiple ROF use IFE again as Intensive Fire?
A. No; it could only use Sustained Fire, and only if also using Subsequent-First/Final-Protective Fire or Final Fire (since the use of Sustained Fire is permitted only to a DEFENDER MG/IFE-Gun and only during the MPh/DFPh). [An92; An95w; An96; Mw]"

It's not clear if this also applies to an IFE-capable Gun on a vehicle (i.e. not infantry-manned). It's also not clear if this extends to MGs. Even though the IFE/MG kwould be a Gun (as in the first q&a), A8.3 only grants SFF to Infantry. I would say the q&a does not grant license to a vehicle to use SFF, but a q&a might easily prove me wrong.

title: Commissars and the Human Wave
question: Are Commissars eligible to initiate a Human Wave?
author: Fly by Night

Stuka makes a successful sighting Task Check. Placed adjacent to its target.

A) Can I make a Light AA shot now?

author: drmark64
consensus_answer:
I am a bit confused on when to resolve Light Anit-Aircraft in general.

Stuka makes a successful sighting Task Check. Placed adjacent to its target.

A) Can I make a Light AA shot now?

If this were a different kind of aircraft (i.e. not a Stuka), then yes per E7.401. However per E7.403, "A Stuka making a Point Attack, unlike a FB, may attack from its present hex before receiving Light AA fire." Since the Stuka was placed adjacent to its target I assume it is making a point attack, and so the answer here is, "no."

It resolves its MG attack.
B) Can I make a Light AA shot now?

Yes.

It moves to the target hex. Because of the unique nature of the Stuka no Light AA is possible now.

As per above light AA waits until after the Stuka attack.

If makes it's MG and Bomb attacks.

C Light AA now?

Yes, after the Stuka attack.

I didn't find a rules section that outlines when Light AA attacks are made. A pointer to the correct section would be appreciated.

As mentioned above, E7.401 has the mechanics: "After it passes its Sighting TC, and after all Light AA fire (7.51) against it has been resolved, it may fire on its initial target. The aircraft then moves to the next hex along the predesignated Hex Grain toward that target and, after receiving all Light AA fire in this hex, may (if it chooses) make another attack DR on a new target hex four hexes distant." E7.402 changes this slightly for point attacks, but for most aircraft, AA is resolved after being placed in/moved to a hex and before attacks by the aircraft. Stuka point attacks change the order in that after being placed/moved to a hex, the Stuka may attack before any light AA is resolved.

title: Desperation Morale and berserk

DM morale only applies when attempting to rally units.

By the way, Berserk units may fire normally during the AFPh?

consensus_answer:
I can never remember which is the one without APh, berserk or human wave. Any memo?
Human Wave units *often* can't Advance, but not always. If Human Wave units are marked with a CC counter (which they are after entering a Location with an enemy unit [A25.234]) they can't Advance [A4.7]. Berserk units may never Advance [A15.431] but I don't know of any memory aid to keep the two straight.

Because there is no other rule saying the DM DRM applies to TCs (including berserk TC), this omission is inconvenient but has no practical effect.

title: Cx units in a FG
question: If not all but some units in a FG are under a Cx token, I guess the whole FG suffers the Cx malus?
author: poifpoif
consensus_answer: The application of DRM that apply to some units but not others is covered in A.5, "Whenever an attack is made against multiple defending units, if a modifier applies to some but not all of the defending units, that attack is made with only one DR by applying the appropriate DRM only to those units—thus getting two or more Final DR from the same Original DR. Conversely, whenever an attack is made by multiple attacking units/weapons, if a modifier applies to some, but not all, of the attacking units, it applies to the attack only if detrimental to the attacker. This often advocates the breaking up of a FG into separate attacks—not all of which are so penalized."

This often advocates the breaking up of a FG into separate attacks—not all of which are so penalized."

Something to be careful about is where multiple hexes in a FG are affected by /different/ +1s...  

E.g. one hex may have a CX unit, another may pass through a hedge hexside and another might pass through an orchard.  It isn't that the entire attack only adds a +1, the attack would add +3.

title: WP in a hex with ground and 2nd lvl units
question:
We had this come up in our last session and we weren't sure of the answer.

Basically, a US MTR fired WP at a concealed unit on the 2nd lvl of a building.  There were also concealed units on the ground level of the hex, but these were out of LOS of the MTR.

The MTR rolled a successful hit versus the concealed stack on the 2nd level.  Since these were the hardest to hit units in the MTRs LOS and given that Area Target Type effects the entire hex, we felt that this also meant the units on the ground level were hit.  This seems to be supported from C3.33.

However, in looking up the Smoke rules, it states that Smoke is /placed in the ground level/ of the hex (exception for interior buildings but this wasn't the case for us).  We get that this means the smoke hindrance extends from Ground level up to lvl 4 for the WP (versus from lvl 2 up to lvl 6), but we weren't sure if this means that ONLY the concealed unit at ground level is subject to the NMC and loss of concealment.

I.e. does the unit on the 2nd lvl also suffer the effects of a "Hit" by WP?
author: kbernatz
consensus_answer:
If the only in-LOS unit was at level two and there were out-of-LOS units at levels one and zero, after a hit on at least one in-LOS unit, the WP would drop to ground level and cause a WP NMC there, but the unit at level one would only be hit and affected if the hardest-to-hit in-LOS unit were hit.

One of our players pointed to A24.31 as the reason why the 2nd level actually does NOT suffer the NMC... pointing to the first red-font text below. 

 24.31 CASUALTIES: The chemical agents in WP caused discomfort and 
could result in demoralization/casualties. All units (including friendly ones) 
except a non-CE, CT AFV in a Location with a WP counter must take a 
NMC when the WP is placed (by any means) [EXC: non-moving units in 
First Fire] in that Location (not when it drifts or they move into it) or when 
hit by ordnance WP [EXC: if the WP does not rise to that elevation (24.4)]. 
See C1.71 for OBA. The NMC causes DM status (10.62), and also causes loss 
of concealment if the affected unit is in LOS of a Good Order enemy ground 
unit. Leadership, CE DRM and TEM apply as negative DRM to the NMC 
(treating grenades as if a Direct Fire attack for TEM purposes). However, if 
a CH (or Air Burst when using Indirect Fire) is obtained with WP, TEM are 
applied to the NMC as positive DRM instead. A CH with WP grenades oc-
curs if the colored dr of the MC DR is a 6.

Specifically, the language of 'in a Location with a WP counter' combined with the fact that the COUNTER is placed at the Ground Level made him feel that only the ground level person would suffer the WP NMC (and regardless of whether he was 'hit' by the original TH roll, as A24.31 never says they have to be HIT by the WP...only that they are 'in the Location with a WP counter').

However, the second red-font text made us confused because that implies that ALL levels 0 - 4 of a building would be impacted by the WP ... otherwise, why have the "exception: if the WP does not rise to that elevation" clause?  Since the WP clearly rises to levels 1 /and/ 2 of the building, it would seem to us that a successful Hit on the level 2, which then "places" the smoke at ground level per C8.52, also would impact ground level and 1st level ("8.52 SMOKE ammunition is always placed at ground level in any target hex which is hit on the Area Target Type, except Interior Building hexes, even if the only visible part of that hex is the upper level of a building. ").

As a follow-on quiz, what would happen if there were *no* non-HIP units in LOS on the second level, but there was an unconcealed unit out-of-LOS at the first level and a concealed, small Gun out-of-LOS at ground level. What are the possible results if the attacker is a MTR or a non-MTR firing WP or HE with LOS only to the second level? What are the DRM to the attack (for the target hex only; assume there are no out-of-hex DRM like hindrance, CA change, etc.)?

Per C3.33, if firing HE there would be no effect ... this is actually covered by the bocage example referenced in B9.521, as there are no 'hardest to hit' target available.  If firing WP, the DRM would actually be BETTER for them (as they wouldn't apply the +2 for concealment ... a rule I hate, fwiw) and it would effect ground level (for sure) and still-to-be-debated, level 1 :).

We went through a number of permutations during this discussion, so you'll have to be more specific about whether the hypothetical unit on level one is hit or not. If the level one unit is in LOS of the firing unit and is hit, the level one unit takes the WP NMC. If the level one unit is not in LOS but the firing unit is a MTR which hits the hardest-to-hit-non-HIP-unit in LOS, all out-of-LOS units are also hit (by super-power of MTRs per C3.33) including the level one unit, and the level one unit takes the WP NMC. Otherwise the level one unit is neither hit nor in the Location where the WP counter is placed (SMOKE counters are always placed at ground level; C8.52), so it does *not* take the WP NMC.

It may be helpful to understand that the obscuring gas from white phosphorus is not super-harmful unless in a very confined space, i.e. although it is not pleasant, it is not a poisonous gas in the same way that mustard gas or phosgene is. However if a piece of solid (non-gaseous) white phosphorus comes in contact with flesh, it burns painfully and continues to burn until removed. If a person is near where a WP shell hits, there is some chance he may come in contact with a piece of solid WP. Most smoke rounds also have bursting charges, i.e. they spread out when they land, so a unit at ground level is more likely to come in contact with a piece of solid WP. Hence in ASL units that are hit take the WP NMC and units at ground level take the WP NMC. The ability of MTRs to hit units that are out-of-LOS in ASL adds another layer of potential confusion to this subject.

But units on Level one wouldn't take the NMC?   
C3.33 helps : " All (including friendly) non-Aerial units in the target hex can be hit (even by WP), except for those immune as per 3.4 [EXC: a mortar also hits all target-hex units that are out of its firer's (Spotter's, if one is being used; 9.3) LOS if that shot hit the non-hidden enemy target that currently was the hardest for it to hit (i.e., that received the highest net TH DRM for that shot)]. "
So, as ATT is used, if the 1st level unit is in LOS, a WP hit - barring DRMs such as concealment or size for a Gun (in a fortified upper level location) , etc. which would result in a miss - will affect it.

title: Orchards hindrance to fire coming from above.
question:
Something that is bothering me. With obstacles, you might have blind hexes, but it doesn’t seem to matter in any way for hindrance purposes.

Then the Orchards weird exception… If they’re out of season, they do seem to cause hindrance against fire coming from above. If an orchard is in season, however, it becomes an obstacle for any fire coming from a higher level and « generates » 1+ blind hex, but they do seem to loose their hindrance ability.  So unless you’re in the blind spot, it seems that out of season orchards offer a far better protection than in season orchards against fire coming from a higher level.

Am I missing something?

consensus_answer:

Those generates blind hex(es) but don’t seem to block LOS beyond the blind hexes. From what I understand.You are missing the fact that the firer on your example is not at higher level than the orchard/building obstacle. They are on a 1 level hill and the orchard is a 1 level obstacle.
A6.2 ... LOS extends into or out of obstacles, but not through them into hexes beyond the obstacle except in certain cases wherein the target/firer are at an elevation ≥ the height of the obstacle or are adjacent to a hexside obstacle.If the firer or target is lower than the obstacle, the latter blocks LOS - excepted if one or the other is higher than the obstacle, and that is when Blind Hex rules kick in.

A6.4 BLIND HEXES: Assuming an otherwise clear LOS, even if a firing (or target) unit is at an elevation > the height equivalent of any intervening full level obstacle, a number of potential target hexes that are both directly behind that obstacle and also equal to the full level height equivalent (i.e., ignoring any half-level) of that obstacle are considered Blind Hexes to the firer. Blind Hexes cannot be seen by the firer unless the Blind Hex is at an elevation ≥ the full-level height of the obstacle (in which case it is not a “Blind” Hex after all). This “blind” area can increase as the range to the obstacle increases (6.41), and/or decrease according to the extent of elevation advantage over the obstacle (6.42).

replies.body: SMOKE, fog and mist are types of hindrances that can be translucent. Other hindrances are really solid obstacles that are relatively thin, so that a unit can move only slightly to get a clear LOS to a particular target. Terrain hindrances such as grain, brush, graveyards, marsh, crags, wrecks and the like are obstacles where it is possible to change position by a small amount (less than one hex) so they can be seen past. None of these are very tall, so they are all half level hindrances. There's nothing "magical" about this. There just aren't many things that are very tall but thin enough that looking around them requires only a minimal change, i.e. within the same hex rather than moving to another hex, to see past. Towers  are an example of something that can be a full-level (or higher) hindrances.
Note also that any time an out-of-season orchard hex would be a hindrance to a target at a different level (disregarding continuous slope), it would be an obstacle if in-season.
Huts are full-level hindrances.
Bridges are full-level hindrances to where only one unit is below the bridge level.

One thing to remember is that ASL uses "pancake-style" elevation rules as a simplification.  What this means is that every level of elevation can be thought of as a pancake, with a vertical drop off at is edge.  If you are in the center of the pancake, then everything lower then you will always be below your view because this style of LOS assumes the world is flat (so no curving your LOS).  To get to elevation level 1.5, it's just two pancakes stacked on to of each other; lvl 2 is three pancakes; etc.

Only when you're at the edge of the pancake can you see to lower levels...

Only when you're at the edge of the pancake can you see to lower levels...

And that's why they created the slopes, to allow the KGP map to be playable. Slopes allow you to see lower terrain in multiple level hills without being on a crest line.
Another common description is the "wedding cake" model. Flat hills but potentially with additional flat hills on top of them. And frosting, not syrup.

title: unhooking under fire
question: vehicle and manning  crew unhook and  are attacked by residual FP and defensive fire ; if I don't miss something as per D5.43 manning  crew is attacked on the MP unhooking vehicle expenditure even if itself do not expend MF ( disembarking is inherent in unhooking ) right ? And what happens if pinned or broken ? Unhooking fails and the gun remains onboard  but the is crew  anyway considered dismounted ? and in later turns does the crew have to load again on the vehicle to try to unhook the gun?
author: adolfinger
consensus_answer:
A truck carrying a crew and towing a Gun enters a hex and stops. Defensive First Fire against both the truck and the crew (D.8 Collateral Attack) is ineffectual but leaves Residual FP. 

The crew unloads and attempts to unhook the Gun. The crew will be attacked by the Residual FP with -1 FFNAM (and possibly -1 FFMO since the truck is unarmored). The truck is also attacked by the Residual FP. I *think* this is resolved with one DR on the IFT.

If the truck is destroyed then the Gun is also destroyed but the crew is not affected because they are Infantry not PRC (D5.43). If the crew is pinned or broken then the Gun remains hooked to the truck. Any unpinned Good Order MMC (or five SMC) can attempt to unhook the Gun not just the original crew (C10.111)

If the truck is destroyed then the Gun is also destroyed but the crew is not affected because they are Infantry not PRC (D5.43). If the crew is pinned or broken then the Gun remains hooked to the truck. Any unpinned Good Order MMC (or five SMC) can attempt to unhook the Gun not just the original crew (C10.111)

What Eric said.  Unhooking a Gun does not require the crew to 'unload' immediately prior.  We had a situation where we unloaded and tried to unhook a Gun, the crew broke and routed away, rallied the next rally phase with a good roll, then came back during our next MPh and successfully unhooked the Gun.  The Gun was towed by a ht and the fire that broke the crew was only a MG, so we were lucky that the vehicle + Gun did not need to vacate the hex or be in direct threat...

title: Beaching by drift on APh
question:
If a raft get beached in it's own APh by water drifting, do the units on the boat start IN the boat on the next PrFPh? 

Meaning, can I shoot them using full FP on the "star vehicles" row on the PrFPh?

Or do they "exit" the raft so they have to be fired as normal infantry?

Playing Gavin's Gamble. What a roller coaster of scenario.
author: alfonso_martin
consensus_answer:
If a raft get beached in it's own APh by water drifting, do the units on the boat start IN the boat on the next PrFPh? 

Per the Advanced Sequence of Play, Advance occurs during step 7.21A while drift is resolved in step 7.22A or 7.23D. So the units that are on a boat that drifts do not have the opportunity to Advance off. 

I don't think that a manned boat can be beached involuntarily. A manned boat can be beached voluntarily if it drifts into a river-edge hex but could remain afloat at its option. An unmanned boat can beach by random dr.

I’ll help you with this shot. You need to roll 10 or less. Throw the
dice. “We got a 5, colored die is 1.” Now let’s see
author: Wild Admiral
consensus_answer:
The difference between adding +1 to the TH Number and substracting -1 to the dice roll can be in a Critical Hit on the ITT, for example.

Imagine your Initial TH is 9. You Original DR is a 3+2=5. ITT CH is on a Final DR strictly less than half the Final TH.
What's the difference?

A) You apply the modifier as a -1 drm to the dice roll. Your Final TH is 9, your Final DR is 4. 4 is less than 9/2=4.5, so there is a CH.
B) You apply the modifier as a +1 to the TH. Your Final TH is 10, your Final DR is 5. 5 is not less than 10/2=5, so there is no CH.

Respect the difference!

The two places you must use DRM as DRM are the infantry target type (for critical hits) and CC vs vehicles (for blazing wrecks). You can be sloppy most everywhere else and still get the right result, for instance treating DRM on the VTT as (reversed) changes to the TH #. But it is a bad habit.

Table C4 is not a DRM, it is a modifier to the TH Number.
One other note - this is especially important for Infantry CH's, which can happen based on the Modified TH Number and the final DR.

title: Help in understanding CC Reaction Fire + Street Fighting
question:
We're playing Hatten and I suspect our German opponent has bought the dreaded Flame Tanks to come play with our boys in green.  We've got the center of the map, mostly, with some of the buildings rubbled.

His tanks, which I believe are the FT Hetzers, are just off the top of the picture (East in Hatten map geography), so they can move up during their MPh and fire at our front line units in their AFPh (where they would not be halved).  For arguments sake, let's say he gets aggressive and moves a tank up to H13, I13, J12, K13 or K14.  My understanding is as follows:

If in H13, no Street Fighting applies and we cannot use CC Reaction Fire against a tank that moves here.  We might be able to get a shot across the hedge if we get AT assets up there. So in H13, we could not do anything against the tank other than wait for our CC phase or use other AT assets.

In the other hexes, when he enters these hexes we have the option of declaring CC Reaction Fire against his tank due to Street Fighting.  We would have to make a TC (leadership applies) and, if it fails, our units would lose ?? and be Pinned.  If it succeeds, we MUST immediately make a CCRF attack against his moving tank (where we get to attack in CC, but he does not).  Regardless of outcome, we then get returned to our starting location (if we succeed, I /think/ we also keep ??... as it counts as an 'Ambush', correct?).

The CCRF counts as DF, so can either be first fire or subsequent first fire, though its use as final protective fire incurs a MC penalty, if I remember correctly.  If we have a squad alone, we start with a CCV of 5, with a DRM of +2 if we attempt it before he Stops; I don't think the -1 for no MG applies as they have that crappy 1 factor remote controlled MG... and the -1 for Street Fighting Ambush, so a CCV of '6'.  If we have a leader with us, it goes up to a 7 or 8 (if a -1 leader).

Correct?
author: kbernatz
consensus_answer:
Can CC reaction fire be performed during the Defensive fire phase by a unit not marked by First Fire vs an AFV that just moved ADJACENT on a road and stopped during the MPh ?

Can street fighting be attempted vs a stopped AFV oa an ADJACENT road during the Prep Fire phase ?
No to both.

Reaction Fire, both CC and non-CC, can only be performed during the enemy MPh. D7.2, "Reaction Fire is conducted during the MPh by the DEFENDER." Since in your example the AFV just moved ADJACENT it could have been attacked in just-finished enemy MPh. Once you reach the DFPh it's too late.

Street Fighting may only be conducted either as part of CC-RF i.e. during the enemy MPh [D7.211] or in a friendly CCPh after an Advance [A11.8].

title: Night Visibility Range movement
question:
The more I play the more uncertain I am.

If a Concealed unit Non-assault moves in an non-illuminated NVR, does it lose Concealment?
My reading of the Concealment Loss rule suggests it does not.
author: csonson
consensus_answer:
Perhaps I should have phrased it like this instead: "Is advance movement a form of assault movement"?

As answered above, no. Assault Movement is a form of MPh movement. Advance is a change of one Location in the Advance Phase. Although they share many features, in particular changing Locations and having to think about MF costs for such a change, there are many, many differences. You can't Recover SW in the APh, for instance. There's no enemy attacks in the APh beyond passive attacks like minefields and OBA FFEs. You don't exactly expend MF in the APh; rather you consider the cost and if it exceeds a particular amount you have to use Advance vs. Difficult Terrain. In the rules you don't see the phrase "advance movement" in general; instead "movement" or "movement in the MPh" is contrasted with "Advance." See A.3 for example. So although Advance is akin to movement in the MPh in that infantry units can translate their position on the board (and, for the purposes of this thread, the concealment loss rules are somewhat similar), there are a large number of differences between the two.

title: Night Rules: +1 LV Hindrance. Star Shells and Parachutes
question:
We are playing "Night Drop" scenario. As we haven't played Night Rules for quite a while it's a learning curve again.

Query 1: E1.9 says "Night Rules remain in effect in an Illuminated Location..."

I believe this means that the +1 LV Hindrance is in effect in illuminated areas also; that illuminating a location merely allows units to be attacked beyond the NVR and use acquistion (during the Player Turn). Is this correct?

Query 2: When there are no other defenders on board in a Paratoop drop scenario, after the Paratoop drops are set up and drop locations determined may the Defender fire star shells as at the beginning of the Movement Phase if it has a LOS to a Parachute counter?

Query 3: Does each hex of map range count as 2 hexes NVR for sighting of Parachute counters? I.e a parachute at 5 NVR can only be seen by a defending unit 2 hexes away until it lands.
author: csonson
consensus_answer:
Query 1: Yes .. + you lose "?" when non assault moving in illuminated locations, + you blind units in illuminated locations to un-illuminated locations even in NVR
Query 2: Yes E9.31 units have LOS to Aerial troops.  E1.91 Initial Use only requires LOS to an enemy unit.  However paratroops are not KEU until they land E9.4. (can't use method 2).  
Query 3: Yes.  E.5 AERIAL RANGE applies to all Aerial targets.  There's also a Q&A

E0.5, E1.1 - Suppose NVR is 3. Suppose a drifted Parachute is two hexes from a light-AA-capable enemy unit with an otherwise clear LOS to that Parachute. Suppose there are no Starshell/IR counters close enough to matter. Does E.5 Aerial range limit NVR in this case? Specifically, is the Aerial Parachute beyond NVR of the light-AA-capable unit?
A. Yes, beyond NVR. {3}

replies.body:
I believe this means that the +1 LV Hindrance is in effect in illuminated areas also; that illuminating a location merely allows units to be attacked beyond the NVR and use acquistion (during the Player Turn). Is this correct?

Correct. I believe that when a Location is illuminated it is treated as "being within NVR." The illuminated location doesn't "merely" allow attacks. There are lots and lots of other effects. Just to mention one, a broken friendly unit cannot rout toward a KEU in an illuminated hex. 

Query 2: When there are no other defenders on board in a Paratoop drop scenario, after the Paratoop drops are set up and drop locations determined may the Defender fire star shells as at the beginning of the Movement Phase if it has a LOS to a Parachute counter?

Per E1.91 the initial starshell can be fired if the unit has LOS to an enemy unit. What is vague is whether a parachute counter is an enemy unit. I think you have to read into E9.11, "A parachute serves only to mask the identity and provide a common Morale Level for its "occupants"; it does not render them concealed in any way," that a (5/8) parachute is not only an enemy unit, it is a KEU. This should allow starshell placement, as well as letting the DEFENDER remove a No Move counter.

Query 3: Does each hex of map range count as 2 hexes NVR for sighting of Parachute counters? I.e a parachute at 5 NVR can only be seen by a defending unit 2 hexes away until it lands.

Correct. Per E9.31 paratroopers that have not landed are aerial targets.

title: Covered Arc and Vehicular Bypass Movement (VBM)
question:
The Stuart is bypassing the Light Jungle in 34F8.  The AT Gun is in 34I8 with its covered arc facing 34H8 and 34I9.

Is the Stuart outside the AT Gun's covered arc?  I think so because the hex in which the Stuart is located (ie the Light Jungle hex 34F8) is outside the AT Gun's covered arc.

But for LOS purposes, the Stuart is considered to be at the Covered Arc Focal Point where 34F8 joins 34F9 and 34G9 (both of which are within the covered arc).  Arguably the CAFP is within the covered arc:  it is effectively on the boundary between CA and outside CA.  By that reasoning, maybe the Stuart is within the CA by being at that CAFP for LOS purposes.  I don't think that is right - but it is the argument which led me to make this post to seek the community's views.

Is the Stuart in or out of CA?
author: Malcolm C
consensus_answer:
Can I ask by 'whole hex' does that also mean if a unit , AFV/Inf , 
that uses bypass in LOS ( vertex), but the bypassed hex (center dot) is a blind hex to the firer ... 

Is that 'insufficient' ?  or still a legal target  ?

C.5B only requires the hex to be in CA. Per C3.2 the definition of CA does not require LOS; a hex/Location can be within CA without being in LOS. In your EX it is somewhat unlikely that the hex (center) is in LOS (and even if it is, there are plenty of situations where that would not be true) but that does not prevent having LOS to or fire at the vertex.

Thanks, phew been playing it correctly 🙂 
oh those lil doubts after decades ...

replies.body:
Although the LOS can be traced to the vertex of the bypass hexside, and for a vehicle just the CAFP, the unit in bypass is actually in exactly one of the three hexes that meet at that vertex/CAFP. In your EX there is only one hex that is bypassable, F8, so there's no ambiguity in that regard. The vehicle is in hex F8. In the general case if there had also been bypassable terrain in G9 and/or F9 the player would have to specify which hex the unit was in. For a vehicle as you have it, of course G9 would be right out, but for infantry tracing LOS to that vertex G9 might be possible if there were bypassable terrain in that hex.

Once the hex the target is in is determined, C.5B says that the entire hex containing the target must be in CA.
"C.5B FIRE WITHIN CA: A firer that must fire within a given CA must have the hex containing the target completely within its CA—merely having the vertex (or hexside) aiming point forming a part of the boundary of its CA is insufficient."
