What?  No!  Crest lines only possibly create Blind Hexes at ranges >= 5.  B10.23.  This is fundamental.

He is marked with a FF counter (gunflash) and is now visible to all units that can see hex CC6, regardless of range.  He is NOT "Illuminated" (E1.8).

Yes, but be careful how you define "visible".  Units beyond NVR can attack him, but he is not a Known enemy unit to them.

10) Cloak L contains a single 6-6-6 squad. If the US player ends his move in CC7 and Advancing Fires at the German player in CC6, he attacks at a strength of 8 (6 halved to 3 for movement, +1 for assault fire, then doubled for PBF to 8 )

That is not how Assault Fire is calculated.  Apply all multipliers, round up any fractions, and then add 1.  The American is halved to 3, doubled to 6, rounded up to 6, and add 1 = 7.  Also remember that each squad performs this calculation separately.  If there were two squads the total would be 14.  If there were three the total would be 21.  Any SW are also not subject to this calculation, they are merely halved or doubled as applicable.  A German 5-4-8 with a LMG firing at point-blank would be (5 halved, doubled, round up and add 1) = 6 + 3 for the LMG for a total of 9.

A consequence of this calculation is that any individual squad qualifying for Assault Fire will have a minimum FP of 2, no matter how many times they are halved for whatever reasons.  Any tiny fraction of FP is rounded up to 1, and then add 1.  So three such squads firing together would have 6 FP, whereas without Assault Fire they might be struggling to scrape together 1 FP!  This is one of the strongest advantages of Assault Fire.

title: subsequent first fire after OVR
question: My Infantry not yet fired is OVR, survives, then CC Reaction fire back -and is marked with first fire and CC - the AFV survives and leave the hex.  can I subsequent first fire,   later in the enemy MPh ( ex. vs  enemy infantry that come close ) ?
author: adolfinger
consensus_answer: Note that you could use CCRF more than once because the AFV spent at least 2 MP to do the OVR. The second CCRF would be at worse odds, however, and the infantry is marked Final Fire.

title: VBM and Reaction Fire - what did we do wrong/right?
question:
Ok... my brother and I are continuing our ASL adventures with Elst.  We're in CG day 2, with full ASL rules, and slogging away around the center of the town.  Due to routing, etc., he ended up with a huge nest of nasty SS in a single stone building.  Due to me being a fool, I ended up with multiple tanks with broken main armaments.  A match made in heaven for VBM to allow my grunts to move up, obviously (ok... probably not versus SS Germans, but ...hey... we're still playing around to learn what is 'good', 'bad' and 'just plain st00pid').

We're looking at hex FF13 in Elst: .

The starting situation is: .  I've left off other units, etc. to make the question/situation clearer, just FYI.

During the Prep Fire phase, I successfully fire smoke onto FF13.  I then activate the tank in DD14 and move as follows:
start (1 MP); CA change CCW (1); VBM into EE14 (DD13-EE14 edge, for 2 MP); activate sD (succeed even with +1 for BU, for 1 MP)*; CC change CW (1)**; VBM still in EE14 (EE13-EE14 edge, for 4 MP)*** ... then it got confusing for us.  This put him at 10 MPs expended.  He wanted to move into FF13 along the EE13-FF13 hexside.  Since FF13 also had SMOKE, the cost would be 4 MPs to enter that hexside, but he needs to change his CA for another 1 MP.  That puts it at a total of 15 MPs, so he needs to do ESB.  I roll a 9, +1 for the extra MP +2 for British and he is immobilized.  He stays in VBM in EE14.  This I think we got correct.  The question that we had was ... what is his CA???  Is the 1 MP CA change considered part of the VBM 'cost' to enter FF13?  Or is the CA change done first?  Or did we screw  up and he didn't need a CA change, even though he wasn't entering the obstacle in FF13, but was 'turning' to VBM it along the EE13-FF13 hexside?  We ended up ruling that the CA cost was part of the total MP cost to enter the hex, so his CA remained facing FF13: 

NOTES:
*) In hindsight, depositing smoke here was stupid..I should have done it at the EE13-EE14 hexspine.
**) We weren't certain if CA changes in Smoke are effected... i.e. 1 MP or 2 MP per CA change.  No change to a 'new location' so we went with just 1 MP.
***) We really weren't sure if the Smoke changes the VBM cost.  The VBM movement rules certainly imply that Smoke cost impacts VBM (and is clear that the +1 is doubled to +2). But is the vehicle actually entering a 'new location'?  Smoke is +1 MP/MF upon entering a NEW LOCATION.  We thought it made sense that it should double the cost (so total cost = 4 MPs), but we were quite uncertain.

So I then activated a second tank (also with broken MA) and tried, again, to get into VBM into FF13: .

He came dashing in and made it to FF13 where he then faced the onslaught of German defenders attempting to eliminate him so that he didn't prevent their fire to outside their own hex.  The Germans had three squads and a 9-1 leader: .

First, he had the leader direct the PSK, stepping out of the building to avoid everyone suffering the 1 IFT roll.  We felt his too hit roll was: 11 (0 hex range) -3 (SMOKE) -1 (firing out of SMOKE) -2 (Moving Vehicle) -2 (avoid backblast) +1 (size) +1 (Leadership), or needing a 5 or less.  He rolled a 10, x10'ing the PSK.  He then decided to attempt CC Reaction Fire with the squad + leader.  He passed the PAATC and attacked in CC.  No Ambush as not Street Fighting and no response by tank (?? we weren't sure on this, but didn't think so).  We determined his CCV as: 5 (squad) +1 (leader) +1 (leadership) -2 (moving) = 5.  He tried for an ATMM, but failed.  He rolled an 8, so no effect.  We marked them First Fire and CC (correct?).

He then had the other 6-5-8 attempt a PF check.  He succeeded and we determined his To Hit roll as: 10 (0 hex range) -3 (SMOKE) -1 (firing out of SMOKE) -2 (Moving Vehicle) -2 (avoid backblast) +1 (size) = 3.  He rolled a '4'.  He then tried to have that squad CC Reaction Fire on the tank, but failed the PAATC (leadership could not apply, as not part of same FG, correct?).  The last 4-4-7 missed both its PF check and PAATC.  Both these squads were marked First Fire and Pinned (correct?).

We stopped here, but some follow-up questions.
1) If I end my vehicle in Motion, he does not put the enemy into Melee and if I advance any squads in (I have 2 squads and a HS in DD14 that have yet to move), I would have to roll for Ambush with the Germans having a net +2 DRM (BU vehicle vs Pinned), correct?

2) If I spend a top MP with the vehicle (which would require another ESB check *gulp*), would it put a Melee on the hex NOW?  Or only at end of CC Phase?  I think the latter, right?  So stopping doesn't prevent an Ambush roll if I advance in later :(.

3) If I don't stop, his squads are not prevented from leaving that hex during his MPh, so they could assault move to FF12 to get out of the SMOKE, etc. ... unless I advance in squads and don't have them all killed by his CC fire.

4) If the German Squads had fired 2 PFs (or the PSK and then a PF check), would they also have been able to conduct CC Reaction Fire?  The Overrun Flow Chart implies 'yes' (they'd have been marked First Fire after the second SW, and the flow chart seems to imply  that units marked First Fire can still conduct CC Reaction Fire, but would be at a -1 CCV DRM due to halved FP...correct?).

5) The charts list an ATMM as a 'support weapon', but how does that apply if a squad uses one in CC?  The one German CC failed to generate one, but we weren't sure if it mattered that he already fired a PSK earlier (i.e. the ATMM would be a 'second SW usage' by that same squad)?  Do ATMM actually /count/ as a SW usage?  The ATMM rules don't seem to imply this, but the '1G' on the Support Weapons Chart made us wonder (though I see now that it does NOT have note A or B associated with it, which is clear that those prohibit, potentially, inherent FP). title: Pinned unit withdrawal in close combat
question:
We had a disagreement concerning pinned units in close combat.

From what I gather from the infiltration rule (A.11.22) : "Any Infantry/Cavalry unit(s) attacked by an Original 12 CC DR may likewise withdraw from CC immediately thereafter, assuming it has not been eliminated by that 12 CC DR"

But the ambush withdrawal rule referenced state A.11.41 states that ambush withdrawal is non available for pinned unit.

"Any Infantry (unless pinned/berserk/Disrupted)..." 

Should we consider "any infantry" from A.11.22 or  "Any Infantry (unless pinned/berserk/disrupted)" from the rule A.11.41 it referenced ?

author: gruhl
consensus_answer:
Q&A:

A11.22
It seems to me that the literal reading of A11.22 says that a pinned unit may withdraw from CC if the opponent rolls a 12. Can

A. A pinned unit may never withdraw.

title: Cloaking loss during APH
question: If a cloaked & Concealed unit Advances into a Shellhole, in LOS of a enemy Unit in a illuminated hex, do they loose Cloaking and concealment ?
author: rudialberts
consensus_answer:
You cannot be "cloaked and concealed".  It's one or the other.

E1.31 LOSS: An Infantry unit loses Cloaking/"?" at night if it uses Non-Assault Movement in a Location that is already Illuminated when that unit expends MF in it, or if it enters an enemy-occupied Location during the MPh. Otherwise, it does not lose Cloaking/concealment at night when moving/advancing.

It doesn't matter whether it's Open Ground or not.  It doesn't matter whether it's Illuminated or not.  It doesn't matter whether anyone has LOS or not.  What matters is: it's the APh.

Units do not move during the APh.  They advance.

The only circumstance I can think of where you might lose Cloaking/"?" during the APh in a Night scenario is if you advance onto an A-P minefield (or into a FFE), and the resulting attack causes at least a PTC, and you are within NVR (which includes being in an Illuminated Location) and LOS of a Good Order enemy unit.

question:
76L Gun in bldg....

So, A7.25 Opportunity Fire says, near the end "Ordnance can use Opportunity Fire only if fired by Infantry, and cannot change its CA until actually resolving its To Hit attempt during the AFPh when it would be subject to applicable Case A To Hit DRM."  I also imagine it would not be subject to the +2/+3 (bldg.) in the AFPh, though, since it Op Fired and waited to fire until then.  So seemingly not much of an "advantage" since the +6 still has to be used, in spite of ignoring the +2/+3 for AFPh.

C3.22 says "Changing CA without Fire:  A Gun may change its CA without firing only at the end of a friendly fire phase (not MPh), and only if at that time its crew is still able to fire it without using Intensive/Sustained Fire [EXC....etc.].  Such a change in the PFPh cancels any movement possibilities for that Gun (even a vehicular Gun) and its crew for the rest of that Player Turn, but does not prevent that Gun from attacking in the AFPh-presumably now without any Case A DRM."

Hmm, so what's this?

Possibilities (correct?):  
Gun doesn't change CA, fires in PFPh, no penalties
Gun doesn't change CA, fires in AFPh, pays B +3 (bldg.)
Gun marked Op Fire, fires in AFPh, pays B +3 (bldg.)
Gun changes CA, fires in PFPh, pays A +6
Gun changes CA in PFPh, fires in AFPh, pays B +3 (bldg.) (according to C3.22)
Gun marked Op Fire, changes CA, fires in AFPh, pays +6 (according to A7.25) 

If this is correct, why ever Op Fire?
author: GamerKirk
consensus_answer: OK, that makes sense, and so to avoid the +6 and sub with +3 according to C3.22 by changing CA in Prep Phase but firing in AFPh may or may not be worth it depending on ROF value.

No, if you have Prep Fired, you have Prep Fired.  You cannot fire in the PFPh and then fire again in the AFPh, regardless of ROF.  To put it another way, if you fire in the PFPh, you are marked with a Prep Fire counter when you have taken all the shots you are eligible for and interested in taking.

title: Ignoring building hexes in rout
question:
Can you ignore select building hexes in rout (A10.51) if you are not routing out of a building altogether? My sense is no. I ask because I have a stack of routers who’d love to rout to a hex in that same building with a leader, but he is more than one adjacent building location away. Can they ignore some hexes in that building to get there or must they stop at the first they can get to?

I understand if they are looking to vacate the building altogether, they can ignore all, but in this situation, can they be selective?
author: PaulusBorgia
consensus_answer:
As I understand it, and it has been a while as I said on your last post, routers can ignore woods and buildings hexes if they are part of the same "complex".
As far as I understand you cannot leave an area of connected woods hexes as long as other locations of this wood area are valid rout destinations. You can only leave buildings. Refer to the last EXC in A10.51.

You are right ... I guess my answer was not clear. What I meant, and I think this was what the OP was asking ... was that the routing unit can ignore legal rout spaces in the same complex. For instance, take the situation if a unit is adjacent to an enemy to the north and must rout, and there is a building/woods complex adjacent to the broken unit to the south. The router doesn't have to stop in that first building hex, even if it is no longer adjacent to a known enemy unit,  but can continue to rout through the complex to a leader or anywhere else for that matter ... as long as it is not moving closer to a KEU and it has the MF to get there.

replies.body: As I understand it, and it has been a while as I said on your last post, routers can ignore woods and buildings hexes if they are part of the same "complex". So you can continue to rout toward the leader if you have the MF and you are not getting closer to any known enemy unit.

Not sure if I can answer the original question, but I would think that nobody forces you to leave the building as long as you still have a valid destination therein.

For instance, take the situation if a unit is adjacent to an enemy to the north and must rout, and there is a building/woods complex adjacent to the broken unit to the south. The router doesn't have to stop in that first building hex, even if it is no longer adjacent to a known enemy unit,  but can continue to rout through the complex to a leader or anywhere else for that matter ... as long as it is not moving closer to a KEU and it has the MF to get there.

The one hesitation I have on Al Cann’s last example is this from 10.51: “ EXC: A broken unit in a building need not consider a hex of the same building in which it begins the RtPh as its closest building hex.”

I think this means if you’re entering a new building you must stop in the first hex entered (“in which it begins the RtPh” being key).

I think too the lingering question of my OP is still can you start in a building complex and ignore other hexes in it to get to a preferred one that is otherwise legal (and say, contains a leader you need to rally)? The hesitation I have here is this: “if it prefers to rout out of that building altogether and toward another building/woods.” That seems to be the restriction?

Okay, when routing, you need to select a destination. This should be the closest rally terrain (building or woods) to the target. There's a few conditions:

1) You cannot end ADJACENT to a unbroken Known Enemy Unit.

2) The selected destination cannot be closer to any KEU in the routing unit's LOS.

3) You can ignore anything that is no further from KEU in LOS.

4) You can ignore a Location in the same building as the routing unit.

If there's a different building, or woods, in an adjacent hex, and it's further away from all enemies in LOS, that (or another such Location) is your target, because you can't ignore it. If it's no further away from the enemy, you can ignore it. If it's further away, but is part of the same building the routing unit is already in, you can ignore it.

You could elect to ignore a Location in your building, but not ignore a different Location in your building, and rout there, as long as you aren't getting closer to a KEU in LOS. However, the fact that once you reach the destination you can keep routing as long as each new Location entered is building/woods, means you probably will never need to do that to pick your initial destination.

What James says.  The key thing is that (assuming all other applicable rout rules are complied with) you can ignore Locations of the same building, but you cannot ignore Locations of the same woods mass.  There is no specific requirement to "stop in the first hex entered", as long as there are ADJACENT woods/building Locations available to continue routing in.

title: Berserk unit approaching, Fire group & FPF question
question:
Newbie looking to get some clarity. My stack of Germans (9-1 leader, 4-6-7 with LMG, and two other 4-6-7 units) is in a ground-level building. A Russian 4-4-7 across the road goes berserk and does the mad movement phase charge. My Germans choose to shoot at the berserkers with the two 4-6-7s without LMG in the road outside the building, hoping to direct the LMG unit and leader against other non-berserk targets in the Defensive Fire Phase (or other regularly moving units).

Despite the good shot (-2 for FFMO & FFNAM) shot at the berserks, it fails to break or affect them, and the berserk Russians enter the building. Can the German LMG unit and leader now take a shot at them with TPBF, foregoing their other preferred targets?

Looking at the mandatory FG rules, I believe so. Mandatory FG applies to the same location and movement factor expenditure, yes? So I couldn't have taken two separate shots at the Russians in the hex outside the building, but once they are inside, the units that haven't shot yet could, right? And even the ones that had shot already could shoot again. Would the ones who'd shot previously be using subsequent first fire? Or final protective fire?

In either case, would the whole group firing now (factoring in the area fire for the previous shooters) have 33 FP (4 + 3 + 2 + 2, for 11 multiplied by 3 for same location fire)? With a -2 on the shot for FFNAM and the leader? My only hesitance in using the previous shooters is whether they would be forced into FPF in which case they do the morale check with the shoot.

In this situation, does everyone have to shoot? Or could some units be left out of it (again, hoping to wipe the berserkers and free up units for another target)?
author: PaulusBorgia
consensus_answer:
Don’t forget to dash your berserkers across the road! This way they only take 1/2 firepower in the street. 

Funnily enough, it's OK to use dash if you are already berserk when performing the charge (A15.431) -- but if you are making a dash and become berserk while doing so, you immediately lose the benefits of dash (A4.63)!

replies.body:
All units must fire when a berserk unit enters your hex ... the strength of the defensive fire is tripled. However that tripled fire is subject to modifiers ... no modifier if the unit is firing D1F, /2 if the defending unit is firing SFF or FPF. It becomes a bit of a math exercise if you have units in that mandatory FG that "are not on the same page" regarding their firing status, like your example indicates. MGs also must be used in that mandatory FG and they would be subject to sustained fire breakdown if they already fired in the turn and did not retain ROF.

What I don't remember is if your FG is forced to fire twice, for instance, if the berserker took an extra MF to enter your hex ... like if your stack was in a building. I don't think that is the case, but it has been a while since I played and my RB is not handy. I'm sure one of the grognards will chime in and correct me if I am wrong.

Well, in most circumstances, the answer would be "sure".  However, because the Russian squad has entered the German Location, A8.312 applies.  All of the German MMC must fire (First Fire for the squad with the LMG, Subsequent Fire Fire for the other two squads). title: Kindling NA
question: When a scenario indicates kindling not allowed, can natural flames and blazes still occur? This restriction only applies to human endeavor, yes?
author: PaulusBorgia
consensus_answer:
A notorious example of "sleaze" of that sort is one of the scenarios in , where kindling is N/A, but it's advantageous to the German player to burn a particular building, so (unless house-ruled otherwise) the German player can park an unarmored vehicle upwind of the building, have the crew abandon it, and then blast it with a Pazerfaust

I don't know about that; you are explicitly not allowed to attack your own units except in a handful of specific cases (A7.4).

The Germans may have abandoned the vehicle, but unless the Americans actually capture it, it still belongs to the Germans.

Now, you can argue that with no crew the vehicle is not a unit (the Index definition of "unit" is a little vague when it comes to vehicles); and if it's not a unit, it can't be a "friendly unit", and therefore is exempt from A7.4.  I suppose that argument has some merit.  It seems a long road to travel just to (probably) start a blaze that (might) spread to where you want it to go.  I can't help but feel that there must be better ways to use your units.

With all due respect, Bruce, I didn't come up with this: http://www.gamesquad.com/forums/index.php?threads/have-you-played-kgpi-clash-at-stoumont.107538/page-2

Step 1: German player stops halftrack in immediate upwind hex from desired hex to burn.
Step 2: Inherent crew voluntarily abandons halftrack. (D5.41)
Step 3: Inherent crew self-destructs halftrack, making it a non-burning wreck. (D5.411)
Step 4:  Any PF-capable German unit in range that can find a PF can legally shoot the wreck (D10.1: "A non-burning wreck may be attacked by either side, treating the wreck as if it were the original vehicle . . . .") (emphasis added).
Step 5: Hope for a good TK roll to make it a burning wreck (B25.14)
Step 6: Keep fingers crossed for a good spread roll (B25.6)

I take no position on the desirability of the strategy, but clearly someone thought it made sense in the specific scenario at issue for it to get tried.  My point was simply that there are ways a player can engineer around the prohibition on kindling if they have the resources and a burning desire to start fires.

replies.body:
When a scenario indicates kindling not allowed, can natural flames and blazes still occur? This restriction only applies to human endeavor, yes? 
Correct, it's purely deliberate kindling efforts that are barred!  You can even still take actions that are highly likely to cause fires so long as you aren't actually "kindling" them.  A notorious example of "sleaze" of that sort is one of the scenarios in , where kindling is N/A, but it's advantageous to the German player to burn a particular building, so (unless house-ruled otherwise) the German player can park an unarmored vehicle upwind of the building, have the crew abandon it, and then blast it with a Pazerfaust, which is highly likely to make a burning wreck, which can then spread to the building.  (I believe there are also several scenarios where kindling is N/A, but one side or the other has flamethrowers, Molotov cocktails, or other things in their OoBs that are likely to "naturally" start fires in the course of regular play and that's fine.)

When a scenario indicates kindling not allowed, can natural flames and blazes still occur? This restriction only applies to human endeavor, yes? 
Yes.
It refers directly to B25.11.
B25.11 KINDLING: Any unpinned, Good Order Infantry unit stacked with a leader (or a SMC alone) may deliberately attempt to start a Flame in the Burnable Terrain it occupies during its own PFPh, provided the SMC passes a NTC for that purpose.

A notorious example of "sleaze" of that sort is one of the scenarios in , where kindling is N/A, but it's advantageous to the German player to burn a particular building, so (unless house-ruled otherwise) the German player can park an unarmored vehicle upwind of the building, have the crew abandon it, and then blast it with a Pazerfaust

Now, you can argue that with no crew the vehicle is not a unit (the Index definition of "unit" is a little vague when it comes to vehicles); and if it's not a unit, it can't be a "friendly unit", and therefore is exempt from A7.4.  I suppose that argument has some merit.  It seems a long road to travel just to (probably) start a blaze that (might) spread to where you want it to go.  I can't help but feel that there must be better ways to use your units.

Incidentally, it has to be said that the "Kindling NA" SSR which has become so ubiquitous is a profound example of lazy scenario design.  There are a small number of scenarios (generally older ones) where allowing one side to kindle at will "breaks" the scenario by making it essentially unwinnable for the side not using the matches.  Many players have interpreted that to mean "kindling is always a terrible thing and should never be allowed".  Those players are just not thinking.  How many times have you tried to kindle in a scenario where it is allowed?  I would guess that the answer for most players at most times is "zero".  It's usually not easy to deliberately kindle.  If it's a small scenario, you are probably devoting a not insignificant part of your force and a not insignificant part of your available time to do something that if it works might prove to be of some benefit.  Again, I would argue that usually you've got smarter things to do.  Indeed, in many cases, I'd personally welcome my opponent trying this.

What should happen is that the scenario designer should consider the likelihood of kindling and what the impact might be if it succeeds.  Any experienced player ought to be able to play this out mentally; in addition, actual playtesting ought to highlight potential issues like this.  If the result of these efforts is "hmm, allowing kindling is a red flag in this specific scenario" then restricting it via SSR is sensible.  What actually happens is that most scenario designers can't be arsed to think about their designs and just slap on the restrictions as a default action.  (I have even seen scenario designs where kindling was a tactic known to have been used in the historical action that the scenario is modelling, but the designer slapped on the SSR anyway.)

I don't care who "came up with it".  If a thing is illegal, it's illegal.  That being said, with the added step of the deliberate self-destruction of the vehicle (which you didn't mention in your first post), there's no question of the legality; any wreck is indeed fair game to be shot at.

There's a lot of caveats.  It's a minimum of 2 turns of effort just getting the vehicle where you want and then abandoning it (unless the vehicle is already, by chance, in the desired Location).  It may take longer if those PF can't be found, or the units firing them aren't very good shots.  Then there are all the vagaries of the spreading fire rules.  If CVP are important, then you're giving your opponent a bunch for free.  Your original post also said that the vehicle should be "unarmored"; for that vehicle to have a crew, there has to be a weapon on it, in which case that weapon is being thrown away (unless it can be removed/scrounged or was already malfunctioned).  This is a thought exercise, not a practical tactic; even if it worked exactly as desired, I'd still call my opponent an idiot for doing it.

That being said, with the added step of the deliberate self-destruction of the vehicle (which you didn't mention in your first post), there's no question of the legality; any wreck is indeed fair game to be shot at.

I didn't mention it because I wasn't trying to provide a step-by-step guide on how to do it until you showed up and needed to try to be a know-it-all.  I was just providing a high level example of a very "gamey" way of getting around kindling restrictions in one very specific situation.

This thread is a rules discussion; if you're going to contribute with only vague assertions, you should expect people to challenge those assertions.  It's nothing to do with being a "know-it-all" and everything to do with being precise.  If you don't like it when people expect you to be precise, perhaps you should not contribute to threads where precision is expected?

title: Motion Status Attempt dr
question:
D2.401 says: "... makes a Motion attempt dr <= the number of MF/MP expended in its LOS by that unit during its MPh. The enemy unit must be one that had not been in the vehicle's LOS during that Player Turn prior to entering it during that MPh."

I had the following situation: An american M18, which was not in LOS to a german PzIVH at the beginning of its MPh, drives down the road and becomes visible for 1 MP between two buildings. Then it continues driving around the corner, stops (for 2 MP in LOS) and wants to start shooting on the PzIVH. Here I want to make the Motion Attempt. What is correct:

1. dr must be <= 2 (last visibility).
2. dr must be <= 3 (enemy unit's cumulated visibility).
3. Motion Attempt is not possible here, because the only chance was the first visibility for 1 MP.
author: phxhf
consensus_answer:
Interesting. So it probably doesn't matter if LOS is lost after the first contact, but I don't see the rule which would allow me to count the MPs out of LOS as well. D2.401 clearly states "dr <= the number of MF/MP expended in its LOS", and not "dr <= the number of MF/MP expended after LOS was first established" ...?
In any case, I'm much relieved it isn't option 3. 🙂

replies.body: I don't see anything in the rules that would support 1 or 3, so I'll go with 2.

You count the total MP spent in LOS - the enemy vehicle doesn't even have to be in LOS when the attempt is made, IIRC (e.g., it spends 6 MP in LOS and the moves out of LOS and ends it MPh, you can automatically go into Motion).

Interesting. So it probably doesn't matter if LOS is lost after the first contact, but I don't see the rule which would allow me to count the MPs out of LOS as well. D2.401 clearly states "dr <= the number of MF/MP expended in its LOS", and not "dr <= the number of MF/MP expended after LOS was first established" ...?
In any case, I'm much relieved it isn't option 3. 🙂

I don't see the rule which would allow me to count the MPs out of LOS as well.

That would be because there is no such rule.  Only MF/MP expended in LOS count for the dr.

Note that they don't need to be spent contiguously, either.  If the enemy vehicle expends 1 MP in LOS, 3 MP out of LOS, another 2 MP in LOS, then (if you want to make the dr at that point) there is a total of 3 MP expended in LOS that you are making the dr against.
Perfect! That makes sense. Thanks.

But a location isn't a hex... a hex CAN be a location if it has no subdivisions.

There's no "can" about it.  A hex always contains at least one Location.

Within a single Location, there may be different "positions".  That's not a clearly-defined game term, unfortunately, you just have to infer it from the particular rule being referred to.  Examples are "in bypass of an obstacle" and "in an obstacle"; "in an entrenchment" and "outside of the entrenchment"; "in a depression" and "at crest level in a depression".  In all cases units are always in a single Location, but at different positions within that Location.

One thing many players trip over is Wall Advantage.  WA is not, repeat not an example of different positions within the same Location.  A unit claiming WA is always in the obstacle just as if it were not claiming WA.  However, a unit claiming WA can never claim the obstacle TEM.

title: IFE
question:
In Rule C2.29 the last sentence states "When using IFE , a weapon is not considered ordnance and is subject to sustained fire - not intensive fire - penalties per A9.3. Does this mean the vehicle with IFE shoots of the IFT as normal. 

If it does not retain ROF (which is lowered by 1 using IFE) it can shoot a second time but uses the rules of Sustained fire as if it were a MG Or do the rules of sustained fire A9.3 apply to every IFE shot taken (which would not make sense).

Thanks you for the support.
author: rhunter1148
consensus_answer:
This issue--IF vs. Sustained Fire--comes up frequently, for instance see this recent GS thread: post.

As for me, I keep notes on ASL rules questions that I've encountered before. Here are mine on IF vs SF: (note: these are my notes and not assured to be correct)

C5.6: The DEFENDER cannot IF a Gun if that Gun begins the DFPh unmarked by any fire counters--he can only use up his ROF (even if there's an adjacent target). [Why? Because after taking those ROF/Final Fire shots, it'll be marked with a Final Fire counter, and hence won't be permitted to use IF (A8.4).] If you begin the DFPh marked with a First Fire counter, you can IF vs. ADJACENT targets, A8.4. 
After exhausting its normal ROF, a Gun can use IF:
•	In its Prep Fire Phase. (C5.6)
•	In its Movement Phase as Bounding First Fire (vehicular only). (D3.3, D3.32, D3.51--you must take the IF shot from the same hex that you lost ROF in).
•	In its Advancing Fire Phase by an Infantry unit marked with Opportunity Fire. (A7.25, C5.6)
•	When marked with a First Fire counter during the enemy Movement Phase--at any range target: IF is not Subsequent First Fire, A8.1.
•	As OVR Prevention during the enemy Movement Phase (non-vehicular Gun only). (C5.64) [If you're using OVR prevention, you have to be able to change the CA of the Gun in question to the correct hexside in order to IF; if you can't, then the crew attacks (without its Gun) with FPF as CC-Reaction Fire instead.]
•	When marked with a First Fire counter in the DFPh--but only at a same-hex or adjacent target. (C2.241, A8.4-.41)

C5.6: In the enemy's MPh there is no range restriction on Intensive Fire. The rule, "Subsequent First Fire cannot be attempted against any target at a range > that to the closest armed, Known enemy unit, nor outside the firer’s Normal Range." - only applies to Subsequent First Fire - not to Intensive Fire.

replies.body: Yes, IFE is resolved automatically on the IFT, no To Hit required. And Sustained Fire applies after ROF is used up.

In Rule C2.29 the last sentence states "When using IFE , a weapon is not considered ordnance and is subject to sustained fire - not intensive fire - penalties per A9.3. Does this mean the vehicle with IFE shoots of the IFT as normal.

If it does not retain ROF (which is lowered by 1 using IFE) it can shoot a second time but uses the rules of Sustained fire as if it were a MG Or do the rules of sustained fire A9.3 apply to every IFE shot taken (which would not make sense).

You're correct -- that would not make sense.  Fortunately it's not what the rule is suggesting.  It's just reminding you that if you lose ROF and want to shoot again, you're not using Intensive Fire, you're using Sustained Fire, and therefore the rules for the latter apply (A9.3).

So, borrowing Bruce's suggestion from the storage thread, I googled 'difference between Intensive Fire and Sustained Fire' as this is something that has always confused our group and GameSquad had something that I did not appreciate...

Basically the permutations are:

1) Opponent's MPh, Gun Defensive First fires, loses ROF and is marked with a First Fire counter. Gun can still make an IF Defensive First Fire attack at a moving enemy unit (since it is not yet marked with a Final Fire counter). Since IF is not SFf, there are none of the SFF range restrictions on such an IF shot

3) A Gun begins the DFPh unmarked by any fire counter. It fires and loses ROF and is now marked with a Final Fire counter. It can not make an IF shot since it is marked with a Final Fire counter [C5.6 with the Journal#7 errata] 
from Game Squad forum post

title: Commissar Rally SMC
question: The rules say that an MMC that fails to rally is replaced by a lower quality unit. Further on in the same rules it says an SMC that cannot be replaced is eliminated. This makes me question the intent. Is it the intent that an SMC would be replaced if it fails to rally?
author: drmark64
consensus_answer: Yes, a leader that fails to rally would be replaced with the next-lower type (see the end of A19.13). A 6+1 could not be replaced, and would be eliminated.

replies.body: Yes, a leader that fails to rally would be replaced with the next-lower type (see the end of A19.13). A 6+1 could not be replaced, and would be eliminated.

This makes me question the intent.

The rule gives you exactly three possibilities, and spells those possibilities out explicitly.

If the unit that fails to rally is an MMC that can be replaced by a unit of lower quality, then it is so replaced.
If the unit that fails to rally cannot be replaced by a unit of lower quality, and is a MMC, then it suffers Casualty Reduction.
If the unit that fails to rally is a SMC, then it is eliminated.

What "intent" are you questioning?  None of that is remotely vague.

Yes, a leader that fails to rally would be replaced with the next-lower type

That is not correct.  Any SMC that fails to rally displeases the Commissar, so he shoots him.  Only MMCs are subject to (possible) Replacement from Commissar action.  (It is true that SMCs can, in general, be Replaced by ELR failure, but not in this case.)

title: Confirmation on rules from our last session
question:
Unlike last time, we're fairly certain we got these right ... but wanted confirmation.

1) We have a 2 hex fortified building (ground level) with cellars from RB (meaning, also fortified).  Our understanding is that, provided there is at least 1 good order squad in a location, we can't advance into it /even if coming from another location within the building/.  This seems to have been answered this way on-line and agrees with the rules (which don't distinguish between exterior and interior 'walls' of the building vis a vis fortified).

2) We had a Melee where the Soviets fired into it, got lucky and broke the German squad but not their HS, but also created a Heroic Leader.  Our understanding was that, during CC, the German player had an option: have the leader stick with the squad and try to withdraw (and suffer the same fate as the squad) or have the heroic leader attack separately (able to apply his heroic drm, but not his leadership drm).  He chose the latter.  Soviets rolled poorly in CC, but managed to kill the broken, withdrawing squad (-4 DRM), but failed to kill the Heroic leader.  He failed to kill any Soviets.  So the heroic German leader and the remaining Soviet units are now all locked in Melee for the next player turn, correct?  I.e. a single SMC can still hold full squads in melee (we think 'yes' as the SMC overrun requires expending MPs to ENTER the hex, etc., and doesn't talk at all about not holding people in melee).  

3) The German squad that was broken in melee doesn't surrender during the Rt phase because it was already in melee.  Instead, it must attempt to withdraw EVEN though it will end adjacent to a known enemy unit while broken.  And this withdraw can be to an Open Ground hex, etc. with no other negatives (interdiction, etc.).  This seemed fairly clear in the rules after some digging around, but we just wanted to make sure it wasn't a "Squad must surrender" situation.

4) And the one that we weren't 100% certain on ... but we had a squad with a leader using armored assault under a Soviet T-34 M43.  We knew there was a hidden AT gun somewhere so wanted to minimize the # of MPs the tank spent in potential LOS at the end of the movement, so decided to delay down to 7 MPs remaining before conducting the armored assault movement (which was going to be 6 MPs + the 1 MP to stop, only the last hex being in potential risky LOS).  We didn't see anything that prevented the tank from delaying before, during, or after each armored assault hex ... but just wanted to confirm that one could 'delay' with the tank but NOT the squad during an armored assault (since it is kind of like platoon movement as you're moving multiple units simultaneously).  I think we got this right, provided the tank did not move away from the infantry during the course of the move ... but we weren't 100% certain on the delay aspect.

Units in RESERVE are set up following the CLOAKING provisions (E1.4) but cannot move or take whatsoever action until revealed (Inor 7.202). They can be revealed (direct attack apart) by enemy proximity (4 hexes) AND LOS or by enemy proximity (2 hexes) with no LOS. In these cases are the CLOAKED units revealed Concealed or UNconcealed? Is this LOS dependent?
Thanks
author: Qwirz
consensus_answer:
This would be something that the campaign rules would have to specify. In Red Barricades they are placed on the map concealed.

O11.6194 b) Reserve: ... put that Cloaking counter's contents (if any) unconcealed on-map.

However, Inor is not RB, and it's disingenuous of LFT to say "use the standard rules".  Reserve deployment is not a "standard rule", it's a rule specific to each CG individually.  It should be stated explicitly, just as it's stated explicitly in Chapters O, P, Q, R, etc.  The exception would be if the CG states upfront "use all CG rules from Chapter  except as modified herein" which is what the HoB CGs typically stated.

Note that the Reserve deployment rules are not even part of the CG SSR ... they are part of the CG "purchasing reinforcements" rules, which by definition are specific to an individual CG in most cases.

Excellent clarification. I checked my rules and you are correct. Unconcealed it is. Interesting for me I grabbed my old Red Barricades rules. And unconcealed is written in pen. There must’ve been an update at some point.

title: Heroic Leader
question:
Playing Gavin Take, Gavin gets a HOB and becomes heroic. Yeah! superman/john wayne. I'm confused how this works. When he is leader of a FG, is his modifier a -4? I don't think so because the rules state you don't combine the hero -1 with the leader's modifier. Do you add his Hero 1 fire power to the FG? (if within range) and if you do, can he still lead the fire with the -3 (or -4 depending on the 1st question)?

What's the benefit of him becoming heroic?

Thanks for any help.
author: deschubert
consensus_answer:
What's the benefit of him becoming heroic?

Notwithstanding the other comments, which are fair, there are benefits to being a Heroic leader.  Suppose, for example, he has to rally a pile of broken units, but there's a good chance that enemy units may come up to threaten him.  An ordinary leader doesn't have many options; a heroic one can attack back, and with (at least) 9 morale can even risk FPF shots.  He can fire a MG (or various other SW) at full effect, or even fire a Gun if the crew have gone elsewhere.  He'll never pin (except in a few specific instances).  He's now Stealthy, if he wasn't before.  He can't be encircled.  et cetera

title: Vehicle bypass and CC Reaction questions
question:
Several questions came up in our current playing of OA28 Where Iron Crosses Grow.

We had a situation where a HiP German squad (4 factors) + MMG + 8-1 leader popped up to mow down a German 6-2-8 and 9-1 leader (2 KIA on an 8-3 attack and kept ROF :<) so a Soviet T-85 with malfunctioned MA rolled into its hex (forest) and ended in bypass+motion.

Our questions that came about were:
1) The leader applied his leadership DRM to the MG + squad that fired on moving 9-1 and 6-2-8, so can he apply this to the PAATC for the squad to attempt Subsequent First Fire Reaction CC versus the T-85 as it enters its hex?  We believe the answer is 'no', but were not sure (since it is the same squad, but different 'fire'?)

2) Can the squad (which fired the MMG that kept its ROF) attempt to gain a PF in a non-CC Reaction attack?  We don't think so since the squad was marked with First Fire (IFP) and had also fired the MG (though the MG still had ROF).  This would be firing IFP + 2 SWs, which we didn't think was allowed (even though the MG was not marked as First Fired due to keeping ROF).

3) Could the leader attempt to gain a PF in this situation?  We believed 'no', as he used his leadership to modify the squad + MG fire, so would be marked First Fire along with the squad.  A leader cannot use both his leadership DRM to assist others and fire a separate SW was our understanding.

4) What can the tank fire at the squad with?  If in bypass, can it use its BMG?  Can it use its CMG if pointed outside of the hex?  Or does the CA have to be turned to include the hex being bypassed?  I guess to put it another way, what can a tank fire at a 'same hex target' that it is NOT overrunning?  We know an Overrun doesn't care about CA, but it seemed like vehicle bypass does.  So, in our situation, the BMG could not fire (will always be pointed out of the hex) and the tank needed to rotate its turret to include the bypassed hex in its CA to fire the CMG.  The MA is malfunctioned, so moot in this case.

5) Is there any FPF Reaction ability against bypassing vehicles (or just versus their vulnerable PRC?)?  The rules allow for FPF Reaction versus OVERRUNNING vehicles, but not apparently just against same hex bypassing vehicles.  E.g. our T-85 moved into the hex and they attempted CC Reaction while it was still in motion (since that was the intent ... to leave it in motion).  Once they failed to kill the T-85, we stopped to fire our MGs then restarted (to end in Motion).  Could they have done anything with the squad + leader (marked CC and Final Fire) on the stop MP and start MP?  We didn't think so because the T-85 crew was BU and there didn't appear to be a proviso for them to attempt multiple CC Reaction attacks on each MP.

6) We advanced a soviet squad (now a HS) into the hex for CC.  Should we have checked for Ambush with the Squad advancing into the hex (marked with a CC already due to the bypassing tank)?  We didn't think so, since it was reinforcing an existing CC situation ... but wasn't marked with 'Melee', so wasn't sure.  Since the tank was in Motion, the German squad + leader would not have been locked in Melee, which is why we sent in the squad (even though it was CX at the time).  We didn't roll for Ambush because the existing CC marker, but weren't sure if this was correct.

7) How is CC resolved in this hex: We felt the squads did their simultaneous CC first (Germans casualty reduced the soviet...soviet did nothing), THEN the Soviet T-85 got to attack (using only its CMG, halved for being in Motion).  We think we did this correctly, but wasn't sure if ALL the CC attacks should be simultaneous.

8 ) If the T-85 wants to overrun the woods hex (they are already in Motion and in bypass in the hex), how does this occur? Per D7.13 seems like they have to exit the hex and re-enter it, correct? They would then attack with 11 strength (2 str due to no MA + 9 (18/2 for MGs) = 11 total strength)?  When does the Bog check occur (before or after the overrun)?  Does it affect both the Soviet and German units (locked in Melee)?  Seems like the TEM (+1) would apply...so it would be an 8+1 attack, or 4+1 if they bog.

-K
author: kbernatz
consensus_answer:
1) The leader applied his leadership DRM to the MG + squad that fired on moving 9-1 and 6-2-8, so can he apply this to the PAATC for the squad to attempt Subsequent First Fire Reaction CC versus the T-85 as it enters its hex?  We believe the answer is 'no', but were not sure (since it is the same squad, but different 'fire'?)

??  A PAATC is not any type of "fire".  It's a PAATC, i.e., a test of the unit's morale.  Of course the leadership modifier is applicable (it's not even optional).

2) Can the squad (which fired the MMG that kept its ROF) attempt to gain a PF in a non-CC Reaction attack?  We don't think so since the squad was marked with First Fire (IFP) and had also fired the MG (though the MG still had ROF).  This would be firing IFP + 2 SWs, which we didn't think was allowed (even though the MG was not marked as First Fired due to keeping ROF).

You are correct, it's not allowed for the reasons you state.  It's also not allowed because a PF cannot be fired as Subsequent First Fire (C13.31).

3) Could the leader attempt to gain a PF in this situation?  We believed 'no', as he used his leadership to modify the squad + MG fire, so would be marked First Fire along with the squad.  A leader cannot use both his leadership DRM to assist others and fire a separate SW was our understanding.

Correct.

4) What can the tank fire at the squad with?  If in bypass, can it use its BMG?

No, because the obstacle that is being bypassed is not (cannot) be within the vehicle's VCA.

Can it use its CMG if pointed outside of the hex?  Or does the CA have to be turned to include the hex being bypassed?

"Can a tank fire a weapon at something that the weapon is not pointing at?" is not really a question that you need anyone to answer for you, is it?

Of course the vehicle's TCA must include the hex being bypassed if you want to fire at it with a turret-mounted weapon (excluding rear-machine guns and other oddities not applicable to a T-34/85).

5) Is there any FPF Reaction ability against bypassing vehicles (or just versus their vulnerable PRC?)?  The rules allow for FPF Reaction versus OVERRUNNING vehicles, but not apparently just against same hex bypassing vehicles.

Consult the OVR Flowchart for full details but the short answer is yes, FPF Reaction Fire is permitted even when no OVR takes place.  D7.2 "Except as stated otherwise, a DEFENDER may use Reaction Fire as often as it is able to use the various forms of First/Final Fire."  The D7.2 rules are not a masterpiece of clarity but the Flowchart sorts out all the options.

6) We advanced a soviet squad (now a HS) into the hex for CC.  Should we have checked for Ambush with the Squad advancing into the hex (marked with a CC already due to the bypassing tank)?

Absolutely there should be an Ambush dr, because there is not yet a Melee.  The side with the vehicle is severely penalised in this dr, with at least a +3 drm (+2 for a vehicle being present, +1 for being BU).

7) How is CC resolved in this hex: We felt the squads did their simultaneous CC first (Germans casualty reduced the soviet...soviet did nothing), THEN the Soviet T-85 got to attack (using only its CMG, halved for being in Motion).  We think we did this correctly, but wasn't sure if ALL the CC attacks should be simultaneous.

Not even close to correct.  Ignoring the issue that the Russians have almost certainly been ambushed, there is no simultaneous CC when there is a vehicle present.  A11.31.  The side that doesn't own the vehicle always goes first (unless by some miracle they have been ambushed).  Then you go back and forth until everyone who wants to, or is able to, has made an attack.  Because it's not sequential, any results are applied immediately -- if a unit is eliminated before it gets its turn to make an attack, well, then it doesn't get to make an attack.

8 ) If the T-85 wants to overrun the woods hex (they are already in Motion and in bypass in the hex), how does this occur?

The short answer is they have to leave, turn around, and come back in.

When does the Bog check occur (before or after the overrun)?

Before.  If the vehicle bogs, the OVR FP is halved.  D7.11.

Does it affect both the Soviet and German units (locked in Melee)?  Seems like the TEM (+1) would apply...so it would be an 8+1 attack, or 4+1 if they bog

Well, the odds that the Russian HS is still alive is pretty poor, so it's quite unlikely that there's a Melee.  Indeed, the Germans might have absconded to a different Location with their ambush result.  They may well plug the T-34 with a PF before it even gets a chance to turn around.  But for argument's sake, if there was indeed a Melee, then like any other attack into a Melee, all units involved are subject to the results.

8 ) The AFV has to exit and re-enter. The Bog check is rolled after the Overrun is declared but before resolution. Overrun FP is halved if it Bogs or is otherwise immobilised or destroyed. Everybody in the Melee is affected, and TEM applies.

title: Ammunition Shortage Summary
question:
We're playing a scenario with Ammunition shortage and I want to make sure we're understanding everything correctly (it is OA28 Where Iron Crosses Grow, with the German side starting with the shortage).

1) If a German MMC attacks on the IFT and rolls a 12, it suffers Unit Replacement after resolving the attack (conscripts or other squads unable to replace are broken instead of disrupted, unless berserk)

2) No German MGs can use Fire Lanes

3) The German AT Gun and tanks (starting B12) would be considered to have a circled B11, meaning a To Hit roll of 12 malfunctions the gun and a To Hit roll of 11 places a Low Ammo marker on the gun.  Once marked with a Low Ammo counter, the gun is considered to have a circled B10/X11, meaning it malfunctions on a To Hit roll of 10 and is permanently broken on a To Hit roll of 11 or 12.

These are the only effects of Ammo Shortage, correct?
author: kbernatz
consensus_answer:
Ammo shortage means your weapons aren't "good order".
Mandatory Fire Group doesn't apply to them.
ie. MG attacks  then squad attacks same target same MF different attacks.

Interesting.  I've not previously noticed that "Good Order" phrase in A7.55 before.  Note that being exempt from Mandatory Fire Group doesn't mean that you cannot form a FG, only that you are not required to do so.  Generally you would want to form a FG if your final DRM is positive, and you would want to fire separately if your final DRM is negative.  (Dealer's choice if the DRM is zero.)  Note that A7.54 only excludes Berserk units from participating in multi-Location FG, so clearly it's OK for them to participate in a single-Location FG (although such participation would prevent any Leadership from applying  -- A15.42, last sentence).

title: 1.211 OBA battery's draw pile
question: Is it correct that you have to discard each chit drawn for battery access? Which should mean then that your amount of chits is getting lower turn by turn giving you less opportunity to gain battery access? Extra chits on the other hand should be mixed back in the pile. But how do you recognize an extra chit then when drawn?

title: Pillboxes and CC
question:
In B 30.6 is mentioned:  CC is resolved in the normal manner between Infantry units in and outside of a pillbox [EXC: Hand-to-Hand CC is NA; no Melee results (30.1; A11.15)].

What is meant by "no Melee results"?
author: neo.colpaert
consensus_answer:
The most significative effect is that you can fire at units not in Melee without hitting those on your side.
And a unit can leave that hex during MPh (if from in the Pillbox, either by an existing tunnel or moving upon the pillbox).

replies.body:
The most significative effect is that you can fire at units not in Melee without hitting those on your side.
And a unit can leave that hex during MPh (if from in the Pillbox, either by an existing tunnel or moving upon the pillbox).

If there is an enemy unit in the outside Location, a unit in the inside Location cannot move out of the Pillbox (barring usual exceptions), only advance out of it. The usual restrictions on moving upon an enemy unit apply.
Even if units from both sides survive the CC units are not held in Melee, no Melee marker is placed.

title: Drifting Smoke during a wind change?
question:
Had many burning tanks in our last scenario and Mild Breeze to start.  This was easy... 2 Grey Dispersed smoke counters in the wind direction from each burning tank beginning with the first AFPh (B25.14 and A24.61) after the vehicle was eliminated.  What confused us was the language in A24.61:
24.61 DRIFT: Original SMOKE sources (other than SMOKE Grenades which do not last long enough to drift) are differentiated 
from drifting Dispersed SMOKE by using white counters for original SMOKE (EXC: a Wreck/Terrain Blaze needs no original Smoke counter) and gray counters for drifting SMOKE. Whenever there is a Mild Breeze, Dispersed SMOKE drifts from any original SMOKE source (EXC: to/from non-rooftop Locations of an Interior Building hex) at the start of the game’s first RPh and at the start of every AFPh. Drifting SMOKE consists of a number of Dispersed SMOKE counters equal to the Hindrance DRM of the original SMOKE.

What is meant by 'game's first RPh'?  Clearly not the RPh of player 1 on game turn 1 and that's it, right?  Shouldn't this be 'at the start of each ATTACKER'S RPh and at the start of every AFPh' ???  I.e. just like when Wind change occurs (only during the Attacker's RPh)?

This came up because we managed to roll a '2' during the wind change roll, resulting in a 1 hex shift CW for the wind.  We were confused as to whether the drifting smoke immediately shifted to the new direction or if it was removed entirely from the board (per the rule later in B24.61: "Drifting SMOKE is removed immediately when the original SMOKE source is removed or when the wind changes direction or force. ") and not replaced until the AFPh?

I.e. we could see two options within the rules:

1) Wind Changes 1 CW ... just shift the drifting smoke counters to the correct new direction (due to adjusting smoke each Attacker's RPh)

2) Wind Changes 1 CW ... remove the drifting smoke and replace them in the AFPh in the correct new direction
author: kbernatz
consensus_answer:
Because that is what the rules say...  
A24.61: Drifting SMOKE is removed immediately when the original SMOKE source is removed or when the wind changes direction or force.  (emphasis added)

replies.body:
What is meant by 'game's first RPh'?  Clearly not the RPh of player 1 on game turn 1 and that's it, right?  Shouldn't this be 'at the start of each ATTACKER'S RPh and at the start of every AFPh' ???  I.e. just like when Wind change occurs (only during the Attacker's RPh)?

This phrase is to cover a situation where there are fires as part of the scenario setup. Basically, since the fires are burning before the start of the game, there needs to be smoke drift occurring on the first turn.

Ahh...
Ok.  So Drift occurs at start of a scenario and then every AFPh afterwards...correct?
Right.

So it sounds like the correct interpretation of drifting smoke during a wind change is that the smoke is removed in the RPh (when the wind changes direction/force), then reappears in the immediate following AFPh.  So there is one set of fire phases (Prep and DF) where the drifting smoke will be gone.

Why would the wind be gone?
Since the rule states, Smoke drifts in the ADVFPh  That phase has to be put in to have it ALREADY be drifting.

Because that is what the rules say...  
A24.61: Drifting SMOKE is removed immediately when the original SMOKE source is removed or when the wind changes direction or force.  (emphasis added)

title: Do Vehicles with MGs as MA use ACQ counters?
question:
Reading C6.5, I'm confused if the "(including the MA and SA ... of vehicles)" is only clarifying that a Gun that is either a separate 5/8" counter OR a vehicle MA/SA Gun gets ACQ or if it is adding that a Gun /or/ any MA or SA of vehicles gets ACQ.  I /believe/ it is the former (that vehicles armed with a MG MA do /not/ get ACQ), but just wanted to confirm.

We're gonna try the DB scenario Uncommon Occurrence and have some early war tanks with CMG only, so trying to figure things out.  My understanding is:
1) CMG MA Tanks do NOT get ACQ.
2) Against enemy tanks, they still need a To Hit roll, which is modified by range as if <=40 mm.
3) Their base TK# is 4, modified by range as if <=25mm.
4) Unclear if their lower die is doubled if firing while in Motion w/o Gyro...but believe 'yes' (don't see anything that would remove this).
5) They are not subject to multiple hits on doubles.
6) If firing at long range (13 - 24 hexes), doesn't something happen to their TK#?  Halved?  I thought I read that somewhere, but couldn't find it...so maybe I'm imagining a rule that doesn't exist?
author: kbernatz
consensus_answer:
formatting got all screwed up ...grumble... hopefully fixed now

Interesting...

How would you interpret C4.2?
 4.2 SMALL CALIBERS: Smaller shells generally lost velocity faster 
than larger shells, affecting trajectory, stability, and ultimately, accuracy. 
Any weapon (including MG) ≤ 57mm is subject to a -1 modification to its 
Basic TH# for every 12 hexes (or fraction thereof) beyond 12 hex range. 
A weapon ≤ 40mm is subject to an additional -1 modification to its Basic 
TH# at > 12 hex range.

At first, I thought a MG would be less than 40 mm, but reading C4.2 it seems to only mention MGs with the first -1 modification.

Agree on the need for greater than 20 mm in C6.5... and that it precludes MG "Guns" from getting acquisition.

A9.61 is interesting... thank you for pointing that out.
9.61 AFV KILL: Unlike Small Arms Fire, a MG attack may conceivably 
destroy a poorly armored AFV during a fire phase by attacking it alone (i.e., 
not as part of a FG) on the To Hit Table (using the Vehicle Target Type) and 
the AP To Kill Table. Such an attack must be made within Normal Range of 
the MG, without any form of halved FP penalty imposed, and predesignated 
as an AFV To Kill attack vs a specific AFV. If hit in an unarmored Target 
Facing, the AFV is attacked on the H Vehicle line of the IFT instead of on the 
AP To Kill Table. If the resulting To Kill DR is < the Final Kill Number for 
that Target Facing the AFV is eliminated (and burning if ≤ half of the Final 
Kill Number), and if the To Kill DR equals the Final Kill Number the AFV 
is Stunned (even if BU; D5.34). See C3.8 (Multiple Hits), C3.9 (Location of 
Hits) and D3.54 (Vehicular MG Fire vs AFV) for related information.

This explicitly states that it must be "without any form of halved FP penalty imposed", so think that rules out pretty much all bounding fire unless there is an exception (like you note in D3.53-3.54).  I find it interesting that it references Multiple Hits, when that seems to be quite clear that it has to be at least 20 mm... and no MGs are 20 mm (50 caliber being 12.7 mm).

D3.53 The Case B To Hit DRM does not apply to vehicle MG; the FP of any MG firing during the AFPh is halved instead, unless it is MA attempting a To Kill DR as ordnance (A9.61).

I think D3.53 is saying "if you're firing a vehicle MG MA at another vehicle, it is not considered halved during AFPh, which therefor allows it to actually have a TK# against that vehicle" ...  maybe ... or it is saying "Instead of halving, you apply the Case B DRM".  I could parse this sentence a couple different ways...  I think the section has two clauses:

3.53 The Case B To Hit DRM does not apply to vehicle MG; the FP of any MG firing during the AFPh is halved instead, unless it is MA attempting a To Kill DR as ordnance (A9.61).

Note that D3.52 appears to covers Bounding Fire...
3.52 Any BMG/CMG/IFE firing outside its current respective CA must 
add a DRM to its IFT DR equal to the pertinent To Hit DRM of Case A 
(Bow MG = NT, CMG = T or ST depending on Gun Type; 1.3). A vehicle 
which uses MG Bounding First Fire must use half FP instead [EXC: Gyro-
stabilized CMG vs Acquired Target; 11.13] because a Bounding First Firer 
must always fire within its current CA (C5.13).

So the sole exception is that if you have a MG MA, you can still make TK rolls in the AFPh, and they allow this by saying "MG MAs aren't considered halved if firing as ordnance and trying to kill something with a TK#".  At least that is my best guess...

It's very clearly stated in C6.5 that only Guns of >= 20mm qualify for acquisition.

Similarly, per C3.8, Multiple Hits are restricted to Guns >= 15mm and <= 40mm.

A9.61 tells you everything you need to know about MGs vs AFVs.

There is a curious EXC though; although A9.61 says it's NA if the MG FP is halved, if the MG is a vehicle's MA, then you're allowed Advancing Fire TH/TK attempts (even though the vehicle's MG FP would be halved for firing in the AFPh).  Presumably also that means it's legal to make TH/TK attempts with a MA MG as part of Bounding First Fire/Motion Fire.  The reason this is "curious" is because it's only kinda-sorta mentioned in passing in D3.53.  I would prefer that a pretty fundamental EXC like this to be more explicitly called out, preferably within the rule that it's an EXC to!

Presumably (again) it means it's also legal for a MA MG to make a TH/TK attempt for any reason that halved FP would apply, such as a concealed target.  Presumably. (But not long range because A9.61 specifically says "within normal range".  Still ... that D3.53 EXC seems pretty broad.  When does it apply, when doesn't it apply?  Since the rules don't say, good luck on finding a definitive answer.)

title: Clearance rubble
question: When a building has totally collapsed and reduced to rubble and this rubble is completely cleared and the token(s) removed, which terrain do these hexes become then, please? Open ground? But how do you mark that then on the map?
author: neo.colpaert
consensus_answer:
Per B24.71, you can only clear rubble from non-building hexes. Should you manage to clear each hexside of a non-building rubble hex, the rubble counter (and trail breaks) are removed and the hex goes back to whatever terrain it was before.

Which is ... odd ... if that terrain was woods/orchard.  Hey, turns out those trees weren't knocked down, they were just bent down under the rubble, and have all sprung back up to their normal height!

Although we should "never say never", I am pretty confident that this is one of those things that has never actually occurred in any game ever played (or ever likely to be played).

title: Backblast LATW
question: Is there a backblast for LATW's in a Lumberyard hex? I didn't find this in the rules. I suppose not?
author: neo.colpaert
consensus_answer:
Is there a backblast for LATW's in a Lumberyard hex? I didn't find this in the rules. I suppose not?

Jan, Backblast (and the associated Desperation penalty) applies to a Lumberyard - by B23.211 it's considered a building for most purposes: 

"A lumberyard is considered identical to a wooden Single Story House in all respects except for Rout (A10.51), Rally (A10.61), Victory Conditions (A26), and EC DRM for Kindling/ Spreading (25.5) purposes, the ability to fire mortars and AA Guns therefrom, and the hex may not be OVR by vehicles."

I don't see an exception for lumberyards under C13.81 so you can eat the backblast or step outside as you see fit.

title: EmRR (Hatten in Flames)
question:
We're about to jump in and start our first CG (Hatten in Flames, CG1).  I'm sure we'll have many mistakes, but ... hey ... I'm also sure we'll have fun along the way.

One thing I'm trying to wrap my mind around is how the elevated embankment RR (EmRR) works.  An earlier post by Bruce said to 'treat it like a full hex wall and you'll be mostly right' (paraphrased) makes some sense, as I've been trying to digest the hillock rules.

It seems like a unit on the EmRR can see over one wall/hedge completely, then see over a second wall/hedge to the hex bordering that wall/hedge.  E.g. a unit in HT Z7 would have LOS to AA7, BB6, CC6, DD5 and EE5, but not FF4 (assuming none are in entrenchments).

I think I've got that down.

But the parts that I'm having a hard time wrapping my head around are the following:

1) If a unit is behind the EmRR (i.e. not in its hex; say in hex Y8), how does the EmRR impact LOS?  My instinct is that it doesn't ... that one can trace over the "first" hillock and then to the second wall/hedge/hillock to the hex adjacent to this second wall/hedge/hillock.  But since there are no other hillocks, I guess this would be only if your LOS somehow managed to cross the EmRR twice (which would be fairly rare on this congested map, I would imagine).

2) If a unit is behind an EmRR (say Y9) and takes fire (say from CC7), would it have any TEM or hindrance other than the out-of-season orchard in AA8?  This is where I'm confused because my instincts is 'no', but if we treat it like a wall, then wouldn't there by a +2 TEM or something?  See also #4 below (i.e. I think I figured it out in typing out these questions, lol).

3) If the unit was in a foxhole in Y9, then there would be no LOS between it and hex CC7, correct?

4) If the unit was ON the EmRR (say hex AA10), would it gain any TEM from fire on it from hex CC7?  There would be the +1 hindrance from the out of season orchard in BB9, but F6.5 and F6.51 confuse me.  F6.51 implies that you need a FULL 1 lvl height advantage (hillock only has 1/2 lvl height advantage), but F6.5 talks about gaining the +1 for tracing across a hexside of a hillock?  Would this mean that a unit in Y9 would gain the +1 or HD status, but a unit in AA10 wouldn't (because no 'hexside' in the case of a EmRR)?

5) If rubble were to somehow end up on an EmRR (NA in Hatten, as 'falling rubble' is NA, I believe), would the hex become a full 1 hex LOS blocking hex?  Or would it still be treated as a 1/2 lvl obstacle (falling rubble)?  Don't think this can occur in Hatten, but the EmRR does run next to some buildings which is why I started thinking about it.
author: kbernatz
consensus_answer:
1. The whole HT EmRR is a single Hillock, so units ON the EmRR can see all over it. A unit in Y8 can see over the Hillock in Z7 and the over the next wall only to the first hex in CC6.

2. Check F6.5. The Z8 Hillock hex provides a +1 TEM to units in Y9 fired from CC7, because Z8 is 1/2 higher than Y9.

3. Correct.

4. Correct, ON AA10 gives no TEM and also no HA (needs a full height). Instead, in Y9, the Hillock provides a +1 TEM.

5. Rubble adds a half-level, so I guess it would become a 1 level obstacle.

title: Hidden Minefields and routing units
question:
(trying to break up questions so others can find them more easily in the future ... realized I didn't do a good job of that in the past and I know BGG moderators try to encourage this)

So we had the following situation come up in our last session.
A German squad broke in a hex where it was next to a same level forest (2 MF to rout into) and a forest on the next elevation level (4 MF to rout into).  The squad needed to rout and my opponent stated that the forest on the next elevation was the routing units destination hex.  I was like "no, it has to be the other forest since it is 2 MF vs 4 MF".  He countered, "no, trust me...it has to be THIS hex".

Me, being dense, didn't put 2 and 2 together to reach 4 and kept saying, "no, that is 4 MF".  So, finally, he said "Wait... <clicks a few buttons in VASL to reveal a minefield...  ... he can choose to avoid routing into a known minefield, hence it is the other forest hex.".

Which got us into a discussion: does one have to reveal that there is a known (but hidden) minefield in that hex to prove that it isn't a valid rout target for that unit, or should I have just put 2 and 2 together when he acknowledged the rule, but then stated "no, that isn't his rout target".  In reality, not much different between him exposing the minefield and (for all practical purposes) admitting that there is a minefield in that hex, but we were wondering what the powers-that-be had to say on this.
author: kbernatz
consensus_answer:
I don't think so.

I do think so.  "known minefield" is a phrase in the middle of the paragraph A10.51.  It has no definition, it doesn't form a definition, it's just a phrase used in a sentence.  There's nothing about it to make the reader think "aha, I have to go look up exactly what that means".  It's words from English used in a sentence written in English that an English speaker would be expected to understand using the common English grammar rules.  It's a minefield that is known.  Known by whom?  The only relevant possibilities are the unit currently routing, or the player who controls the unit that is currently routing.  There's nothing in that phrase that even implies that a non-hidden counter placed on the board is a requirement.  There's no reference to B28.45.

"Known Minefield" is a phrase used in B28.45 and the very fact that it is capitalised indicates that this is a GAME TERM.  There is no common English grammatical reason for it to be capitalised otherwise.  Since the reader knows that it is a GAME TERM, he knows to look for its definition either in the Index or in the rules paragraph(s) that it appears in.  As a GAME TERM it's even possible that the definition need not conform to the common English usage.  (Compare the game definition of "voluntary" in C1.22 as opposed to the actual normal meaning of the word "voluntary".)  The very fact that it's non-use in A10.51 is the alarm bell that should ring very loudly to everyone looking at the nonsensical Q&A quoted above.

Now, if MMP want to issue errata to change "known minefield" in A10.51 to "Known Minefield", or something similar, then the above Q&A will become true and while still extremely silly that's the way it will be.  I would hope that they don't do this because of the silliness of it, but if they do I will shrug and say "OK, that's how we play it now".

I've said all this elsewhere before but it bears repeating: MMP have said multiple times over the years that unofficial Q&A is exactly that, unofficial.  (You know it's "unofficial" because it's not published in an MMP publication or on the MMP website.  The only "Official Q&A" that MMP has ever published since the introduction of the 2nd ed. rules are the Q&A found in the pages of the BRT Gamers Guide -- and yes, a couple of those Q&A apply to the rules generally, not just to BRT.)  Essentially, unofficial Q&A are a guide to understanding the rules but are absolutely not the last word, and the primary reason that they're not the last word is because they want the right to change their minds before carving it in stone.

Given these facts, unofficial Q&A fall into 4 categories:

1 - They repeat, perhaps more clearly, what the rules already say.  These are by far the most common, easily 90% or more.
2 - They provide an answer to a question that the rules simply don't provide.  Sometimes a situation occurs where the choices are A or B and the rules support both choices equally (or if you prefer, support no particular choice).  We need to make a choice, the Q&A does that for us.  These are pretty rare but they are quite important.  Hopefully, these eventually turn into new errata items (i.e., the rules are expanded).
3 - In forming the answer to the Q, the decision is made that the printed rule is in error and that it needs to be changed.  The clue to identifying these is that typically the phrase "this is errata" or something very similar will be in the answer.  Also quite rare, but obviously also important.  The rules are corrected.
4 - The answer flat-out contradicts the rules but gives no hint why, or suggests that errata is pending, or anything like that.  The usual phrase for such Q&A is "this is wrong".  In fairness, these are by far the least common.

The only way to identify which category any given Q&A falls into is to know and understand not just the rules, but how the rules are constructed.  Most importantly, apply critical thinking!

building or woods hex (even if overstacked) unless that route is through/into a known minefield or FFE, or is not traversable (e.g., through a Blaze, unbridged Water Obstacle, Cliff, etc.).

That seems kind of gamey/counter-intuitive.  You would think the German defenders would know the location of their own minefields (esp. since it was legit right next to their starting hex, lol). B28.1 doesn't seem to allow voluntary exposure, so would the German player be forced to rout his OWN unit into his OWN minefield because it wasn't "Known" to the enemy?  That seems kind of gamey/counter-intuitive.

I agree.

I do not believe the phrase "known minefield" as used in A10.51 has the same specific meaning as "Known Minefield" as used in B28.45.  The difference in capitalisation is a big clue here.  It's also worth remembering that B28.45 didn't exist until Chapter F was first published; there it was rule F.7.  It was copied back into Chapter B in the 2nd ed. rules.

I think it's much more likely (and much more sensible) that the A10.51 meaning (when the rule was originally written) is simply the normal meaning of the phrase, i.e., a unit can choose not to rout into a minefield that it knows about.

In the situation as described in the first post, the owner of the routing unit would normally be forced to choose the least-MF-required option, but in order to choose otherwise he must be able to explain to his opponent why that rule can be ignored.  "There is a A-P minefield in that hex and the broken unit is therefore ignoring it."  The rules don't technically require anything more than that, but I would place a minefield counter in the hex (with the strength factor hidden) and play on.  I mean, you could tell your opponent that the minefield is there, not place the counter, and then hope that he immediately forgets it ... but I think that would be just silly.

The nature of the game requires occasional compromises such as this when you're dealing with concealed and hidden things.  The classic example is the Attacker moving a concealed stack into a Location where his opponent has a still-hidden minefield.  The Defender can demand proof that the stack contains at least one real unit even if he has no LOS, because if it is a Dummy stack the minefields don't make an attack.  This is essentially giving away "unearned" information (especially if it is a Dummy stack) but the game doesn't work properly otherwise.  Sometimes you just have to shrug and accept it.

There is a Perry Sez on this:

A10.51 & B28.413

Must a unit that is routing rout through a hidden minefield of its owning side, or may the it ignore it? If it may ignore it, must the mines come on board? If the mines don’t need to come on board, must a reason be given to the other player as to why the hex was ignorable (even though it may be obvious)?

A. Routing units cannot ignore hidden minefields and routing towards a minefield is not a reason for putting it on board.

 

During rout can a unit ignore a hex where there are hidden mines friendly to its side? If the above answer is no, can the owning player reveal the mines in order to avoid forcing the broken unit to rout into them?

A. No to both.
