So, are there Dogfight rules in Squad Leader and what does it say? :P
Yes, there was air-to-air combat in SL, but it was extremely abstracted:

139.151 (from Crescendo of Doom): "During each Rally Phase in which opposing aircraft are on the board simultaneously, those aircraft must engage in air-to-air combat. Air-to-air combat is resolved by each player making a single die roll with the player making the lowest roll eliminating one opposing aircraft of the owners choice."

Ties resulted in no losses. There were DRMs of -1 for each friendly fighter and -1 if the combat took place in a friendly Player Turn.

Thanks for that. It's so different that it can't be used as a reference.

Another question: Does Stuka hold FB in Melee? Rules:

Aircraft in Melee cannot engage in any other activity and are forced to engage in Aerial Combat again in the next Player Turn if opposed by an undamaged FB with functioning MG.

I read "no".

This relates to the ultimate issue of starting a Dogfight in opponent's CCPh. Check this out, I have a Stuka, he has a FB:

1. My CCPh: He starts a Dogfight that goes into Melee
2. His MPh: Melee, so I can't make ground attacks
3. His CCPh: He leaves Melee (because my Stukas cannot hold him)
4. My MPh: He makes ground attacks against my units
5. My CCPh: He starts a Dogfight that goes into Melee. Rinse and repeat.

See how sleazy that would be? He can both bind me AND make ground attacks, while I can do nothing. If only the Attacker could start Dogfights then he'd have to make a tough choice in step 3. Either we both fight in Melee until his next CCPh, or we both can make ground attacks.

Stuka's should be easy meat in dogfighting. Also, dogfighting tends to make aircraft lose altitude, which tends to take divebombers out of their attack band. Not so much sleaze as one way of showing why Stukas were really only useful when unopposed in the air.

title: So A-P mines makes A-T mines unfindable?
question:
If there are both A-P and A-T mines in a hex, is there any way to find out about the A-T mines before a tank drives into it?

Because if there were A-T mines only, and I Searched the hex and find a "minefield", I could step into it and if no dice are rolled, I could deduce they must all be A-T mines.
But if there are A-P mines, I can't make any assumptions about any A-T mines correct?

This is probably all "well, duh" stuff, but mines are new to me and I'm trying to figure out how to determine what kind of minefield is there... 
If I knew there were only A-P mines, I could clear a path with a tank...

Maybe it's supposed to be that way and I should just avoid that hex or try a Clearance with infantry.

Btw, In lieu to spending all MFs, infantry can also move normally into a minefield hex, take the boom and still make a Clearance attempt during that turn, right?
author: Hipsu
consensus_answer:
Since A-P mines and A-T mines would be two separate minefields, I would place two counters after a successful search. I cannot find a rules reference, unfortunately.
Searching reveals the presence of minefields, but not their strength or type (A12.152), so I think only one counter would be placed. Placing two counters would be revealing the types of mines present: a violation of this rule.

As for clearing, I would say you are correct. Move normally into a minefield hex, survive the boom, and declare Clearance attempt. Using all your MFs to enter a known minefield only gives you the bonus of no minefield attack.
No. A unit that wishes to clear mines must become TI (B24.74), but units that become TI cannot move during that Player Turn (A4.8).

EDIT: A closer reading of B24.74 reveals that a Good Order unit is allowed to spend all of its MF to enter a minefield location and become TI so as to allow a clearance attempt in the same Player Turn. This would be an exception to A4.8, but I don't see that a unit that entered a minefield location without spending all of its MF in that move would be allowed to declare mine clearance and become TI. Sorry for any confusion from my previous answer.

title: Did I count this off right?
question: I guess bypass is giving me trouble. I know, this is a video, but I'm not going to post it in the videos! Frack that.

title: Fire vs Motion truck with Passengers
question:
In my game tonight, I IFT fired against a truck carrying passengers which was in motion.  After much rule searching, I'm still at a loss for exactly how this works.  Most of what I found stated that IFT attacks suffer no penalties, but that just seemed odd.  I wound up using Area Fire (because I wasn't firing at the truck specifically) and halving the FP.  I wound up still breaking multiple passengers in the truck.

Can someone give me some clarification as to how this sort of attack works?  Thanks!
author: paulus22
consensus_answer:
One more thing...what about an IFT shot an open-topped, armored vehicle?  

Armored vehicle means IFT shot has no effect on the vehicle itself.
If the crew is CE, the IFT shot will affect them with their CE TEM, usually +2.

If the crew is BU, they are immune to IFT shots except under certain circumstances. For example, I am pretty sure an adjacent firer with a 3 level height advantage can still affect the BU crew.

5.31 CE DRM: ...An OT AFV’s normal (usually +2) CE DRM can be reduced by Elevation Effects as per 6.61, and by Air Bursts (B13.3); see 5.311....

5.311 UNPROTECTED CREWS: The Inherent crew (as well as each Passenger) of a vehicle receiving fire (including Fire Lane Residual FP) [EXC: Sniper attack] through an unarmored Target Facing/Aspect (C3.9; including any OT AFV receiving either Air Bursts or fire from a higher elevation whose elevation advantage is > the range [5.31]—and, vs mines, the PRC of any AFV with a hull AF of 0 [B28.43]) is Vulnerable even if BU, and receives no (or a reduced; 5.31) CE DRM. Consequently the crew is not susceptible to Stun/Recall from such an attack; it is instead subject to PTC/MC/K/KIA results. If it breaks it must rout from the vehicle using normal Infantry rout procedures [EXC: it expends all its initial-RtPh MF to be placed beneath the vehicle]. The vehicle automatically Stops (no Stop MP is spent) when its crew breaks. If the crew routs or is eliminated, the vehicle is marked with an Abandoned counter. If an OT AFV’s crew would receive a CE DRM reduced by Elevation-Effects/Air-Bursts to < its normal CE DRM, that AFV is instead treated as unarmored and the attack vs it—but not vs its PRC—is resolved (with no Air Burst TEM) either as per A7.308 (for non-ordnance/Indirect-Fire-HE) or > the range to the halftrack. In this event, the +2 CE DRM applies but is reduced by one for each full level elevation advantage > the range (to a minimum CE DRM of 0) as per 5.31, and even BU Passengers may return fire...

replies.body:
D6.7 TRUCKS: All unarmoured, fully wheeled vehicles (such as a jeep) are generically covered by truck rules. the only difference in transporting Personnel by truck (or unarmoured halftrack) is that both the vehicle and its Passengers are subject to all forms of attack (ie, its PRC are always vulnerable). A non-ordnance or mortar attack is resolved on the * Vehicle line of the IFT (A7.308) against both the vehicle and Collaterally (D.8B) against its passengers/crew with the same DR [EXC: if that attack destroys the vehicle; D8].

So you attack the truck on the IFT and if it survives you then use the same DR to resolve the Collateral attack against the Passengers/crew (see D5.311).

The D.8 Collateral attack table shows that a "G" (= General) collateral attack occurs when an IFT attack is done vs an Unarmored vehicle.
Here is the rules' definition of such an attack - which confirms Damon's answer.
D.8B GENERAL: When a vehicle is subjected to (but not destroyed, etc., by) FP which is not required to pre-designate it as the target, any Vulnerable PRC in/on it are subject to a General Collateral Attack as per D.8 above, but modified normally for range, Hindrances, TEM/CE DRM, etc. - just as if the Vulnerable PRC were the only target being attacked. Additionally, the Vulnerable PRC of any other vehicle in the same Location are also subject to the same General Collateral Attack (but possibly with different modifiers due to their CE/Motion status, etc.). A General Collateral Attack is just a special name for the application of the original attack to a vehicle's Vulnerable PRC. (See Collateral Attack Table and Example to follow).
Does the truck's Motion status have any effect on the attack?
I don't believe so. I can't see any FP modifiers or DRMs listed on the QRDC that apply to a Motion vehicle...
Likewise, you don't suffer any IFT direct fire penalties vs the CE PRC of a ht or AFV, etc.

Likewise, you don't suffer any IFT direct fire penalties vs the CE PRC of a ht or AFV, etc.
... but modified normally for range, Hindrances, TEM/CE DRM, etc. - just as if the Vulnerable PRC were the only target being attacked. Emphasis added. I presume that that is because it is only a truck, and not a HT or other AFV?

Reopening this old (but helpful!) thread to ask a follow-on question. 

One of the points I took away from the OP was the he felt it was counter-intuitive that there would be no penalty against the firer for a small-arms attack vs PRC (i.e. using IFT) on a moving/motion vehicle analogous to case J on the To-Hit table. I agree with him that it does seem counter-intuitive. One would expect it to be somewhat harder to fire at targets on a moving vehicle compared to if that vehicle was stationary.

Does anyone have any insights on why the IFT would not have any modifiers for firing at targets on a moving vehicle whereas the To-Hit table and Close Combat table do?

Thanks!

I guess that small arms fire against a truck is a matter of spraying bullets around the area where the truck is, while firing a round of ordnance means hitting the moving truck with your shot, and attacking in CC means getting in close contact with a moving truck and dropping some grenades or so, so the difficulty levels are different.

Does anyone have any insights on why the IFT would not have any modifiers for firing at targets on a moving vehicle whereas the To-Hit table and Close Combat table do?

But there are modifiers for firing on the IFT at targets in a moving vehicle.

The modifiers are "you don't suffer FFMO/FFNAM DRM".

Small-arms fire is always assumed to "fill the hex".  Whether your vehicle is stationary or travelling at top speed, the bullets etc. are everywhere you go within the hex.  Nevertheless, the vehicle is marginally safer than being exposed to exactly the same firepower while on foot.

I don't see the issue here.

Hi Bruce,

The comparison that came to mind when I wrote the question was the following:

case 1: MMC firing small arms during PFPh into a location with a stopped vehicle with vulnerable PRC.

case 2: MMC firing small arms during PFPh into a location with motion vehicle with vulnerable PRC.

Intuitively, case 2 should have less chance of affecting the PRC than case 1 but the IFT table doesn't differentiate between the two. It could be that the "fill the hex" reasoning applies in these two cases thus justifying that they have the same modifiers.

I'm not trying to nitpick here - I just find it easier to memorize the table modifiers when I have a good grasp of the logic behind the effects.

Thanks!

case 2 should have less chance of affecting the PRC than case 1

Says who?  The rules don't deal with "should".  That stuff is personal opinion; the only opinion that matters to the rules is that of the people who wrote them.  (Or to put it another way, the rulebook is not a democratic institution.  Why are you trying to cast a vote?)

It's harder to hit a motion vehicle with ordnance because the ordnance has no effect unless you actually hit the vehicle (or in the case of the Area Target Type, land your rounds somewhere near the vehicle).  Inherent Firepower (small arms) doesn't have to "hit" anything -- it represents a volume of space (one hex) being filled with a certain quantity of bullets, grenades, etc. -- so being "hard to hit" is almost irrelevant.  [I said "almost" -- obviously there are various possible modifiers that might apply (concealment, SMOKE, etc.) -- but "moving" isn't one of them, so far as vehicles are concerned.]

So if you need a rationale to help you remember the rule, the rationale is "the hex is filled with fire -- moving or not, I'm still going to burn".

title: Quick questions before it erupts in Stalingrad
question:
1. If a squad spends movement points in a minefield without moving (e.g. to place smoke, recover a weapon), is it attacked by the minefield ?

2. Rocket artillery is limited to one fire mission. Does that mean that it fires twice ? (a mission being the time between ARs, including two FFEs)

3. If that is the case, and if a pre-reg hex has been bought, how does one determine the landing point ? It seems that the first extent of error roll will be halved, but the second one will not, nearly voiding the pre-reg effect. Is that right ?

4. Are units on map-edge hexes adjacent to units set up as reinforcements ? e.g. creating the need to rout.
author: Merrimac
consensus_answer:
1. If a squad spends movement points in a minefield without moving (e.g. to place smoke, recover a weapon), is it attacked by the minefield ? 

No; minefields only attack on entry/exit of a minefield hex (B28.41).

 2. Rocket artillery is limited to one fire mission. Does that mean that it fires twice ? (a mission being the time between ARs, including two FFEs) 

Correct; see the Index for the definition of "Fire Mission."

 3. If that is the case, and if a pre-reg hex has been bought, how does one determine the landing point ? It seems that the first extent of error roll will be halved, but the second one will not, nearly voiding the pre-reg effect. Is that right ? 

I'm not sure what "second" EoE you are referring to.

 4. Are units on map-edge hexes adjacent to units set up as reinforcements ? e.g. creating the need to rout. 

If I understand your question, the answer is "no" because there is no LOS between onboard and offboard units (A2.51).

replies.body:
1. If a squad spends movement points in a minefield without moving (e.g. to place smoke, recover a weapon), is it attacked by the minefield ?

No, just entering and exiting.

2. Rocket artillery is limited to one fire mission. Does that mean that it fires twice ? (a mission being the time between ARs, including two FFEs)

Yes.

3. If that is the case, and if a pre-reg hex has been bought, how does one determine the landing point ?

It can't be accurate. Put the AR in the pre-registered hex. Then roll for error. Extent of error is halved for pre-registration.

It seems that the first extent of error roll will be halved, but the second one will not, nearly voiding the pre-reg effect. Is that right ?

It can't be corrected, so, where is lands is where it stays.

4. Are units on map-edge hexes adjacent to units set up as reinforcements ? e.g. creating the need to rout. 

They are 'adjacent' but not 'ADJACENT'. So they do not impact routs, also LOS does not exist.

title: Question(s) about Wall TEM/LOS/WA
question:
I have a series of specific questions about a situation that came up in a PBEM game. I've been reading chapter K, and I *think* I have an understanding of how things work here, but something wonky happened and I wasn't absolutely sure how to apply the rules. I'm going to just describe things as I think they work, and you guys tell me where I go wrong.

Here is the initial state from which I will begin asking questions:

Of note is the Russian squad in the lower right, and the Finnish half-squad three hexes away, which has wall advantage. This Russian squad then moves into bypass along the y10/z10 hexside, for 1 MF, non assault movement:

(how do I make the images larger?) Now, the half-squad in x8, the one marked WA, can sight right along the hexspines, along the x9/y9 wall. Since the wall is only a half-level obstacle, and the HS is sighting along it, the wall does not obstruct LOS. The Russian squad gets no protective benefit from any wall, because it isn't up next to a wall. The shot here, if the HS takes it, would be a 2 neg 2 shot.

Next, the Russian squad moves into hex y10. Now I'm feeling really confused. This isn't Deluxe ASL, so units get WA over every hexside. So the Finns have WA over w9 and x9...but what about y10? There is this line of wall between the two units. I think that this is a situation in which both the Russian and Finn unit get the +2 TEM....but does it matter if the Russian unit has completed its MPh yet? I think the total shot here for the Finns would be a +1, for wall TEM and NAM. But I'm not sure, because of the Finns' WA...does WA extend to y10? My gut says no.

Thanks in advance for the feedback.
author: Rindu
consensus_answer:
Hmmm...there is consensus that there is no LOS to the bypassing unit, but I'm still confused about that one. Let's see...since the target unit is in bypass, the firing unit can pick a vertex to trace LOS to...thus I presume the firing unit would trace to z10-y10-y11 (offboard). (unless that is impossible.) 

When I consider this, along with the page B7 illustration and rule B9.2 and the example, I'm confused as to why the Finnish HS can't fire on the Russian squad in bypass. Spenser Armstrong says the y9/y10 wall blocks it, but B9.2 says that "a wall/hedge lying length-wise (on a hexspine) exactly along a LOS is [an obstacle] only if ...the vertex opposite of the viewing/target hex has walls/hedges on all of its three hexspines." But there is no wall at x9/y10. 

So I do see that LOS is blocked to z10, but I'm still confused about the bypass part. :(

Your gut is correct.  WA is only relevant to fire between adjacent units who share a wall hexside (not hexspine).  So WA is relevant between AA9 & AA10 in your first picture.  It is not relevant between X8 and Y10 because they do not share a hexside, they share a hexspine.

Hope that helps.  I find that the illustrations and examples in the rulebook are sometimes as useful (if not more useful than) the actual rules on stuff like this.

S

Since the wall is only a half-level obstacle, and the HS is sighting along it, the wall does not obstruct LOS. The Russian squad gets no protective benefit from any wall, because it isn't up next to a wall. The shot here, if the HS takes it, would be a 2 neg 2 shot.

No.

*If* the Finn HS has a LOS to the Bypassing Russian at the Z9/Z10/ZZ10 vertex (hard to tell in the picture but it's possible), any shot would be 2(+1) [+2/wall TEM; -1 FFNAM]. The Wall still applies because the LOS crosses it and that Wall hexside is not a wall that the Finn HS has WA over.

Otherwise, the Finn HS does not have a LOS *hex* Z10; the Y9/Y10 hexside wall blocks LOS between those two hexes.

When the Russian squad reaches Y10, the Finn HS can see it.

 Next, the Russian squad moves into hex y10. Now I'm feeling really confused. This isn't Deluxe ASL, so units get WA over every hexside. So the Finns have WA over w9 and x9...but what about y10? Your gut is correct; X9/Y9 is not part of the Finn HS's WA because it is not a hexside of its HEX. So both units receive the +2 Wall TEM (though the moving Russian also has to apply FFNAM, for a net +1 DRM should the Finn HS fire at it).

1. No LOS from X8 to a unit bypassing Z10. LOS down the wall hexside only goes to Y10, or anyone bypassing Y10. Since the unit is bypassing Z10, even though it is the same vertex, no LOS exists. Counter-intuitive, but hexsides often behave in strange ways.

2. You have it correct. You can only get Wall Advantage over hexsides of your hex.

LOS from X8 -> Z10 is blocked in the example.

LOS from X8 -> Y10 is clear.  Unit not using Hazardous Movement in Y10 will be subject to a Net +1 TEM modifier from fire from X8 in the example.  +2 Wall, -1 FFNAM.

Hmmm...there is consensus that there is no LOS to the bypassing unit, but I'm still confused about that one. Let's see...since the target unit is in bypass, the firing unit can pick a vertex to trace LOS to...thus I presume the firing unit would trace to z10-y10-y11 (offboard). (unless that is impossible.) 

When I consider this, along with the page B7 illustration and rule B9.2 and the example, I'm confused as to why the Finnish HS can't fire on the Russian squad in bypass. Spenser Armstrong says the y9/y10 wall blocks it, but B9.2 says that "a wall/hedge lying length-wise (on a hexspine) exactly along a LOS is [an obstacle] only if ...the vertex opposite of the viewing/target hex has walls/hedges on all of its three hexspines." But there is no wall at x9/y10. 

So I do see that LOS is blocked to z10, but I'm still confused about the bypass part. :(

For LOS to a unit in bypass, you can only pick vertexes the bypassing unit actually moves through.  You can't pick the Z10-Y10-Y11 vertex because the Russian unit doesn't actually go there.  It only crosses Z9-Z10-AA10 and Y10-Z9-Z10 before leaving bypass into Y10.

I think the Finns in X8 have LOS to the first of those vertexes, but not the second, as LOS crosses the Y9-Y10 wall before it gets to the vertex.
Thanks, Dave!

Also note that for the sake of speed play, you don't need to put the WA counter in X8 until it is needed to avoid confusion. If there is no possible TEM in the hex the unit is assumed to have WA. If there was a TEM you have to specify WA if you want it. Also if there is a enemy unit adjacent to a shared wall hexside.

title: Night related questions

Ah, Night.  I love it, but the rules are trying.  Apologies in advance for any errors, I'm not claiming expertise, just trying to think through.

I've familiarized myself with the Night rules by reading the excellent Night articles in the Out of the Attic #1. I still got some questions though.

1. That special Fire Lane thingy.. When exactly can it be placed? E1.71 says "Once any starshell/IR has been fired" but does that mean "at any time during the enemy MPh, just as long as the first Starshell has been fired some time previously" or "when any starshell is fired, the very next thing to do is to decide if one wants to start firing that Fire Lane, but once something else happens, the chance is lost until the next starshell."?

Subsequently it's clear of course; every turn at the start of the enemy MPh.

Also, I know the Fire Lane reaches beyond the NVR but can the actual Bore Sighted location be beyond the NVR?

Also, even though LMGs can lay Fire Lanes, they cannot Boresight so that means they don't get this benefit?

I don't see any reason it would need to be immediately after the first starshell, since there's no mention of immediacy. 

I don't think the BS Location can be out of NVR since Locations out of NVR are out of LOS and BS Locations are required to be in LOS (C6.4)

LMGs can't boresight, they can't use this.

2. The first Starshell.
One of the events allowing the placement of the first starshell says:
"E1.91: a Gunflash is placed due to an enemy FFE or an attack vs an enemy unit."
The Line of Sight box in the chapter E divider calls this a "Friendly Gunflash".
So, what about an enemy Gunflash? Why is it not listed? Can anyone give a thematic reason?

No, I'm not sure there's a thematic reason per se.  By and large, it's not terribly relevant.  Only a terrible attacker is going to be firing out of NVR early, and keep in mind, you can place starshells based on sight of a unit, not a KEU, so you'd like see them before you'd see their gunflashes.

I would think slightly differently as to how it works were it not for the divider clarifying to "Friendly Gunflash."

3. Jitter Fire 
"E1.55: Jitter Fire cannot occur in a scenario until at least one Gunflash has been placed due to an attack vs an enemy unit."
Again that friendly Gunflash. Does this mean that if only one side has fired a shot, then only that side can be affected by the Jitter Fire?

Could it be that the quoted rules in questions 2 and 3 are phrased like that to emphasize that the firing must be against an enemy unit, as opposed to say, an empty hex, to prevent any sleazy early Starshells when the enemy is still far away? But it got somehow misinterpreted in the chapter divider as "Friendly Gunflash" by whoever wrote that?

I don't see "Friendly Gunflash" under Jitter Fire.  In fact, I see the opposite.  On the divider, it clarifies to "first attack."  So, in this case (and contrary to starshells), once any attack is made vs a unit (no firing vs an empty hex), Jitter Fire is activated for everybody.

Generally, "vs. an enemy unit" would mean any attack since "enemy" is always relative.  I think...

4. Cloak and Ambush
"E1.43: Cloaked status is lost... ...for making any attack other than a successful Ambush."
But a successful Ambush in itself it's not an attack. If I manage to Ambush you I get to choose if I want to fight or immediately withdraw. Does this rule actually mean a successful attack after a successful ambush? So I may kill his units and still keep the Cloak?

Yep.  Stab 'em in the dark and stay Cloaked.  And if you can strip their concealment first...  I had a concealed 10-2 and 838 running around Cloaked for most of my last Night game.  Typically -5 on Ambush, only needing 2 less...  Oh, it was brutal.  :D

E1.8 mentions that that a firing unit reveals it's location but not necessarily itself. What are the situation(s) where it does not reveal itself? Is it the next rule, E1.81, which talks about firing beyond NVR? So if a unit fires it doesn't lose its concealment if outside the enemy's NVR?

Correct.  No ? loss for firing unless you're inside NVR or Illuminated.  Units firing into Illuminated areas have a huge advantage...Reciprocity does not apply.

We are going to play scenario H - Escape from Velikiye Luki. In the SSRs it says "The Majority Squad Type of both sides is Normal." but right after it continues to state: "All German units are Stealthy while all Russian units are Lax."
Why the contradiction? Someone explain this to me.

I think you're looking at an old version of the scenario, actually.  In the version in ASL Classic (the newest one), SSR 5 says only "All Russian units are Lax (E1.62); all German units are Stealthy."  MST is not defined.  So, you seem to have struck erratta.

Don't think yuo're missing anything.  I'm trying to strain my brain and figure out a way it could matter, but coming up empty.

Or, here's a hypothetical example question: How many MFs does it cost for an uncloaked unit to enter hex 3I10 from I11 during night with snow on the ground?

I'd say 5 MF from I11 (4 + 1 for elevation change through an unplowed road hexside but + 0 for entering a concealment terrain through a road hexside), and 6 MF if entered from J10 (no 4 + 1 + 1).

I think you've got that right.

Hope this helps.

title: The roads in A5/A6 and GG5/GG6
question: Where are the roads in these hexes supposed to be? In only one hex, in both hexes...? My question arises from entering units from off-map from these hexes, as I'm not sure if I can use the road for both hexes or only one of them.
author: esparver73
consensus_answer:
2.51 OFFBOARD SETUP: Units designated by a scenario as having to enter the mapboard (rather than setting up on it) must still be set up offboard on the turn of entry as the first act of the RPh of that Player Turn. This is done by placing any randomly chosen unused board(s) adjacent to the mapboard edge(s) the ATTACKER’s units are to enter. The offboard player then places all forces scheduled to arrive during that turn on any whole hex(es). If only part of a board is in play, only the actual road hexes on the unused portion are “off board” road hexes. Fire and LOS between the mapboard and any setup board is not allowed (including the overlapping Blast Area of a FFE). However, offboard units may move normally on the offboard map so as to enter the mapboard on a hex which is not adjacent to the one they set up in, provided they were not scheduled to enter via a specified hex which is not blocked. All terrain on an offboard setup map is considered Open Ground except for off-map half-hexes which are butted against a half-hex of some other terrain type and hex rows Y, Q, and I which are road hexes if the board is butted lengthwise. If the board is butted widthwise, all offboard hexes with a coordinate of 5 are considered road hexes. Roads share the same status as the majority of on-board roads of the adjacent board (i.e., paved, plowed, or muddy). Entrance of an offboard setup hex on the way to entering the mapboard always costs the standard Open Ground MF/MP rate per hex (or standard road movement rate if on a road) except where scenario weather conditions increase the cost of such basic movement.

Only hexes on the offboard map (when aligned so that the A or GG edge is being entered from) with a coordinate of 5 are considered road hexes, so you could use either of the 'on board' (GG5/6, A5/6) hexes as road hexes, but only units which had set up or entered from the 'offboard B/FF-5 hex' would be able to claim road rate.

So both 5 & 6 hexes on map are road hexes, then, and as the share a road depiction in their hexside I could go from one of them to the other one as using the road.

title: Railroad hexes in Valor of the Guards?
question:
Hi!

I have been trying to understand how ground level rail road hexes are to be treated in the Valor of the Guards.

There is a conversation in the gamesquad forums:

http://forums.gamesquad.com/showthread.php?75880-VOTG-SSR-5-Entrenchments-in-RR-Hexes

After reading that, and the "perry sez" mentioned there, it would look to me like this:

Ground level "open ground" rail roads (which do not contain other terrain like shell holes or debris) are treated exactly like paved roads (*), EXCEPT that they are nothing like paved roads. After all exceptions and clarifications, they are actually like this:

- For the purposes of infantry, they cost 1 MF, and prevent straying at night. Otherwise they are exactly like open ground.

- Fortifications (except mines) may not be set up in those hexes.

- For the purposes of vehicles, they cost 2MP for tracked (or halftracked) vehicles. (either 2MP from another such hex, or 1+1MP from a non-railroad hex).

- Debris and shell holes modify those as in the Debris and shell hole rules.

Am I correct here?

(*) The rulebook says that they are like paved roads, and then goes on to add exceptions until there is nothing except "do not stray at night" left. Well done, Rulebook. Well done..
author: petrip
consensus_answer:
The closest we get to something official is post #74:
http://forums.gamesquad.com/showthread.php?75880-VOTG-SSR-5-Entrenchments-in-RR-Hexes/page8

When I've played it, we've allowed manholes beacause there was no official erratum. One thing in favour of allowing them in RR hexes is that it takes care of the otherwise orphaned manhole location up in the northeast. You may play it however you and your opponent want to, with or without an erratum.

One nuance is that there is no exception for them acting like paved roads when it comes to determing if the hex has a sewer entrance; they are still active for that. Makes for a lot more manholes than would otherwise be on map.   

Or has there been a Q&A/errata that I missed? I asked MMP about ages back and never got a response.

The thread I linked to above seemed, to me, come to the conclusion that there would NOT be sewer entrances there. At least that was how I interpreted the discussion there.

title: Alternate hex grain Fire Lane snap shot vs. Banzai/HW

So, two Japanese units in X5 and Y5 declares a Banzai charge. On first impulse they move to the street. At this point the US MMG shoots at the unit in Y6 and declares an alternate hex grain Fire lane (pictured). Notice, the FL wasn't there before.

author: Hipsu
consensus_answer:
It would not affect anyone in X6 because that hex is not within the firelane.

title: US M5 76.2 mm AT gun Notes Please
question:
Hi All

Looking at a scenario with the above gun in it and do not have the Chp H notes. Could someone please post a summary?

Thanks in advance
author: Shadow Cat
consensus_answer:
While the M1 57mm AT gun was being developed in 1941, the Army also decided to start work on a more powerful weapon. To bring it into production as quickly as possible, the designers used the barrel of the 3-in. (76mm) AA gun and the carriage, breech and recoil mechanisms of the 105mm howitzer. The result was rather large and heavy for an AT gun (its weight in action was almost twice that of the German 7,5cm PaK 40), but it worked better than might have been expected from such an improvisation. However, while the M3 3-in. AA gun and the M7 3-in. gun of the M10 GMC had semiautomatic breech blocks, the M5 had a manual breech block which lowered its rate of fire. 2500 were built before production ended in 1944. The M5 was not used as a divisional AT gun but rather in tank destroyer battalions (towed), with four guns (each towed by an M3 halftrack) per platoon. In early 1945 most towed battalions were converted to SP, making the towed gun relatively rare in the last few month of the war. Since the M5 3-in. was used solely in towed TD battalions it was sometimes referred to as a tank destroyer instead of an AT gun. Apparently it was not used in the PTO.

APCR is not available in Italy.

RF for use in the ETO (other than Italy) is 1,3 for 6-8/44,  1,2 for 9/44 - 2/45,  and 1,4 for 3-5/45.

Dates and RF for use in Italy are 11/44 - 5/45 and 1,4.

The gun was not used by U.S. forces in the PTO.

title: CC, rolling Snake-eyes and effect
question:
Hi,here's the situation:
2 German units locked in melee with 2 Dutch units. No ambush, so both sides roll at same time. Germans roll under kill number but dutch roll snake-eyes (double 1). We re-read rules but I don't think we played it right...

Our result: Dutch kill germans (and created 7-0 leader) and instantly retreat. As is allowed by my reading of the rules. Germans score zip as the Dutch withdraw (as per rules sorry NRBH while Germans don't kill as they are know alone in hex. 

Is this right, my gut says no!
author: bluetiger80
consensus_answer:
I know it can be a bit hazy. I used to play this wrong because I had learned a bad habbit from Starter Kits and that was rolling the dice simultaneously in CC. You're not supposed to do that. The ATTACKER rolls first so the result to your question depends which one was the ATTACKER. Here's what I wrote in my SKs to ASL guide:

If your CC DR is 2 or your opponent's CC DR is 12, you may immediately withdraw from the CC/Melee. 

Infiltration momentarily suspends the simultaneous nature of the CC, so what happens next depends on if you’re the ATTACKER or the DEFENDER (remember, the ATTACKER rolls first even in a simultaneous CC).
- First, remember to resolve the possible Field Promotion. (A18.12)
- If the ATTACKER rolls 2 he must first choose if he wants to withdraw before the DEFENDER resolves his attack. If he does, the DEFENDER does not get a change to strike back. That DR of 2 is still resolved against the DEFENDER but even if the DEFENDER was eliminated the ATTACKER does not gain control of that CC location. 
- If the DEFENDER rolls 2, he must suffer the ATTACKER’s roll first regardless.
- If the ATTACKER rolls 12, the DEFENDER does not roll for his attack if he chooses to withdraw.
- If the DEFENDER rolls 12, the ATTACKER’s roll is still resolved even if he chooses to withdraw.

So, if Dutch was the Attacker he would have to make a decision before seeing what German rolls. He would either kill Germans, then withdraw immediately or kill the Germans and stay but then the Germans would get a change to roll too and in this case both would have died.

If Dutch were the defender, both would have died because the German rolled first.

But in any case (German or Dutch player turn), any surviving Dutch (whether having being attacked or not) can withdraw.

title: Can claiming TEM of a Fortified building location nullify earlier shots that contributed to the Encircling attempt retroactively?
question:
Good luck trying to decipher the subject lol.

Situation: German squad in a stone building. Russian 447 shoots at it and rolls something high. The German yawns. Then a Russian 627 shoots from the other side and claims that the German is now Encircled. The German reveals a Fortified building location and claims that the FP of the first shot wasn't actually enough for NMC, thus no Encirclement.

But, is it too late for the German now because he didn't reveal the additional TEM for the first shot? I'm not sure if there exists some rule that prevents "tinkering the past".

My opinion: No Encirclement for obvious logical reasons, but I just read a Series Replay where Encirclement was placed in this kind of situation but it could have been just that in the 1st ed. rules maybe there were no requirement for NMC and any amount of FP was enough? Probably the case but still got me thinking about this question.
author: Hipsu
consensus_answer:
I agree with Spencer.

It seems blatantly obvious to me that A23.911 unambiguously states that the existence of the FB is revealed when *it is fired upon*  and it would change a result of said attack.  Negation of encirclement is a change to the result of said attack.  Merely announcing an attack is not actually making the attack.

From a common sense standpoint I would play that it is not encirclement and you can reveal the FB after the second attack die roll. I do not think it is obvious that the rules support this. 

It can be argued that when you try to prevent the encirclement during the second attack (the one that finished encirclement) you are trying to change the effect of the previous attack from "was enough to start encirclement" to "was not enough to start encirclement". Changing the effect of the previous attack is not allowed by B23.911.

It could even be argued that encirclement is not changing the effect of an attack since no single attack causes it. It is an effect of multiple attacks combined, in which case B23.911 does not apply.

Edit: changed A23.911 to B23.911

There are a few cases where the targeted player knows something the the firing player doesn't.

-Concealed unit with a FT
-Hidden fortification when E1.16 is in effect (Night & PTO)
-Fortified location

In any of these cases, an attacker makes attacks that may not be what they announce.  If they announce 4+3 against a Fortified Location, the defender knows it's 4+4.  If they call 4+3 against that FT squad, the defender knows it's 4+2.  They may fire into a jungle hex and anncounce 4+1 (or 4+2 for dense) and the defender knows it's 4+2 (foxhole) or 4+3 (wood pillbox) or 4+5 (stone pillbox) or simply not capable of having an effect (NCA of a pillbox).  In any of these cases, the shot is not what the attacker declared it.  That doesn't change what the shot was and it doesn't create a duty for the defending player to reveal unless the result changes. 

If you allow Encirclement because one player said 4+3 and wasn't corrected, do  you have to forfeit the FT or the fortification later because you didn't correct?  Of course not.  The attacker's declaration of the shot isn't relevant, what the shot actually was is all that matters.

Even if you fire into a jungle hex and announce 4+1 (or 4-1 with a 9-2 leader) and you roll snakeyes, your opponent doesn't have to tell you anything about the pillbox whose NCA you just bounced rounds off.  

Stuff only shows up when it changes a result, not a declaration.  The Encirclement result cannot be changed until the sealing shot, so the Fortified Location shows up at that moment and not before.  That first shot was always a 4+4, whoever might not have known it.

S

replies.body:
B23.911 [...] A Fortified Building is not revealed until an enemy unit atempts to enter it, or it is successfully Searched (A12.152) or fired on with a result which would be different due to the increased TEM of a Fortified Building.

Your case is the latter: even though after the first shot there was no need to reveal the FB, as the roll was high, after the second shot the German reveals the FB as revealing it changes the result of the firing. Without FB, the result of the second firing would be Encirclement. With FB, there is no encirclement.

B23.911 [...] A Fortified Building is not revealed until an enemy unit atempts to enter it, or it is successfully Searched (A12.152) or fired on with a result which would be different due to the increased TEM of a Fortified Building.

Without FB, the result of the second firing would be Encirclement. With FB, there is no encirclement.

I agree.  Just because you didn't happen to need to announce the shot was actually +4 and not +3 doesn't mean it wasn't. 

It's an interesting question and one I hadn't thought of. Thumbs up.

You're Encircled unless the fortified TEM is claimed before the second attack's DR is made. Note that as soon as the second shot is announced, which means that Encirclement is going to happen, the Fortified Location must be announced as per the last line of 23.911 because the upcoming result is going to be 'different due to the increased TEM'. Essentially, you have to warn the opponent that it cannot happen before he rolls the dice. If you wait until after the second DR, then A.2 kicks in.

There are a few cases where the targeted player knows something the the firing player doesn't.

-Concealed unit with a FT
-Hidden fortification when E1.16 is in effect (Night & PTO)
-Fortified location

In any of these cases, an attacker makes attacks that may not be what they announce.  If they announce 4+3 against a Fortified Location, the defender knows it's 4+4.  If they call 4+3 against that FT squad, the defender knows it's 4+2.  They may fire into a jungle hex and anncounce 4+1 (or 4+2 for dense) and the defender knows it's 4+2 (foxhole) or 4+3 (wood pillbox) or 4+5 (stone pillbox) or simply not capable of having an effect (NCA of a pillbox).  In any of these cases, the shot is not what the attacker declared it. title: Dug-in AFV
question:
The Russian player in Red Barricades is buying some dug-in AFV (D9.54). Can he scrounge any MG from the AFVs? BMG, CMG?

An MG not scrounged can be used, including BMG?

Thanks.
author: esparver73
consensus_answer:
The Russian player in Red Barricades is buying some dug-in AFV (D9.54). Can he scrounge any MG from the AFVs? BMG, CMG?
Only non-burning wrecks and abandoned vehicles may be scrounged (D10.5), so the Dug-In AFV would first have to be abandoned (and marked with an Abandoned counter). Once abandoned, only the BMG and AAMG (if present) could be scrounged (D10.51).

An MG not scrounged can be used, including BMG?
A Dug-In AFV is considered HD (D9.54), and a HD AFV cannot fire any bow-mounted weapon other than its MA (D4.223), so the BMG cannot be fired.

A11.52 CAPTURE OF VEHICLE IN CC: Infantry may not attempt to capture a manned AFV or a Motion/non-stopped vehicle (or its PRC), but may attempt to capture or eliminate an Abandoned AFV as per 21.2. An unarmed, stopped/non-Motion vehicle without Personnel Escort is captured instantly in any CCPh in which it is alone with opposing Infantry. The old board 2 hermit shack.

consensus_answer:
Which hex does the residual firepower go in when you fire at a unit using rowhouse bpyass at the bypass point?

Well, B23.71 says that that is spent as "one to 'bypass' in the hex it is leaving..."

so I'd say the hex it's leaving.

S

Also from B23.71 - If broken, pinned, or repulsed at this vertex, the unit is returned to its last-occupied Location as if it had attempted to enter a concealed MMC's Location during its MPh.

That indicates to me that the bypass MF is in the original Location and not the new building Location, so residual goes into the original Location, the hex the unit is leaving.

I have a slightly different take on the matter because if you keep reading the sentence Spencer quoted:

"Such units moving/routing on the ground level expend three MF (one to 'bypass' in the hex it is leaving where it would be attacked by any OBA/Residual-FP and two to enter the building)..."

In my mind there is a two step process here - one MF is spent bypassing in the 'starting' location and then two MF are spent in next row-house hex the unit is entering.

So it would depend on the point at which Defensive Fire was declared as to where the RFP would be placed. Is DF being declared as the unit is bypassing through the hex vertex or is it being declared when the unit enters the next row-house hex?

If DF is declared as the unit crosses the hex vertex then RFP would be in the 'starting' hex.

If DF is declared on entering the building then RFP is placed in the 'second' hex.

Just my 2c which probably isn't worth much as there are wiser ones then I here abouts...
If declared when the unit is entering the building, the LOS must be traced to the building center hex and the TEM DRM used.

title: 10 - The Citadel, scenario specific questions (the canal)
question:

One of my German squads went berserk while still south of the Canal. Do you think it would try to cross the Canal with those SSR provided "inherent boats" or rather try to go around across the bridge? We played that the bridge was so far away that the berserker would use the boats (They are not stupid, just mad).

Besides it invoked a funny mental image of the dudes inflating boats in a berserk fury! :D

Another question: Do you think LLMCs are applicable while in the canal? We played yes, because the the SSR didn't say otherwise (it's brutal BTW). On the other hand if they were actual boats using actual Ch.E rules the LLMC doesn't apply right?

---

There seemed to be a weakly defended crossing point at the middleish area so I decided that almost everybody should cross with the boats. There were effectively only one Cupola and a couple of squads guarding the Canal. I managed to neutralize the guards and SMOKED the cupola and over I went.

Guess what.

Half of my OB at the bottom of the Canal.

That damn Cupola made some awesome 6+2 shots from inside the SMOKE and kept rate. I never really thought how much the Hazardous Movement would offset the +4 SMOKE DRM. I just though "He'll never hit anything once I smoke it HA HA!. And the LLMC didn't help my mega stacks, oh no. Sigh.
Btw, I lost that game. It's pretty funny now, actually, but it wasn't funny yesterday. :)

Another means of dealing with pillboxes is to fire AP/APCR/APDS (of sufficient caliber) at them.  

B30.35  "AP:  Neither the CA nor the NCA Defense Modification applies to an AP/APCR/APDS attack against a pillbox/its-contents, provided the Basic TK# of that ammo type being fired is > twice the Defense Modification that would otherwise apply."

replies.body:
Question #1: A6.7 mentions a couple of times that the shot has to go through the hex to be a hindrance, so I am going to say that in hex hindrances don't affect shots involving the pillbox.

Question #2: Broken units can remain adjacent to enemy units standing outside the pillbox. That's the way I have been reading that.

Question #3: How does one deal with pillboxes? There are a few ways to deal with them.

AVOIDANCE: If the pillbox can be avoided on your way to the victory conditions, consider this option.

FIREPOWER: Put lots of bullets on it. Decent leadership and lots of firepower can make the +5 TEM of a concrete pillbox seem inadquate. 30fp +5 TEM is equivalent to 8fp no TEM.

SMOKE: If you can obscure the pillbox long enough, you will marginalize its effect on the game and also make it vulnerable to Close Combat.

CLOSE COMBAT: This isn't such a bad option. Remember that units in the pillbox can't see and shoot at units in the same hex. Nobody gets locked in melee. Generally the units in the pillbox can be ambushed easier but other than that neither side has the advantage.

1. I think it is just written that way to be crystal clear. In hex TEM does not apply, hindrances and SMOKE still apply.

2. I have always played that they are not required to rout, nor are they eliminated for failure to rout.

3. Pillboxes can be tough to crack, especially as part of a defensive network. Use SMOKE, SMOKE, with a side helping of SMOKE. Try not to approach a pillbox from its CA - come at it from its side instead. AP fired from a large enough Gun does not get the pillbox TEM on its TH roll. Once in hex, CC and DCs are deadly. Or just roll a CH with a 150 HE attack.

Mark is right : terrain hindrances never affect units in the hex and brokies can remain in the PB even if there are enemy units in the PB hex.

Additional tactical advice : you can enter the PB hex through its NCA, so the occupants cannot Defensive First Fire against you.

Something to keep in mind if Pillbox Control is part of the victory conditions:  since the Attacker is *outside* the Pillbox during Close combat, even if he wins the Close Combat he does not yet Control the Pillbox. This can be important when you're timing your final rush - you want to be there *before* the last turn.

title: Platoon movement and radioless afvs
question:
I'm About head into a scenario with radioless afvs and need clarification on a rule. Sorry can't specify rule # as I dont have rb with me.

If a radioless afv makes a successful dr to break away from it's platoon does it need to retake that tc every move that other members of it's original platoon still exist on board or is the one tc all if needs? The way I read it the afv will need to keep making the tc dr every turn.
author: bluetiger80
consensus_answer:
Hmm I seem to remember something about the tc not required if only 1 afv is left out of the platoon? Oh well, sort Of makes it hard to move them then.The 2006 erraticized rules add, in the D4.22 Gaps rule (last sentence) "If only one AFV is remaining, it is free from platoon restrictions for the remainder of its current MPh".

Just a precision : the TC only happens at the start of the AFV(s) MPh (14.23).

Good clarification, Robin.  The "only at beginning of MPh" is so ingrained in my understanding of this TC that that didn't occur to me.

S

replies.body: Yes, he needs to take a TC every MPh that he wants to move without a platoon.

I'd add that the existence of his platoon-mates doesn't matter at all.  Think of it as a TC to move independently.  If you have a two-vehicle platoon and one is destroyed, the other will be subject to this TC every turn.  This distinction can also matter on defense, since radioless vehicles must enter in platoons, but are not required to set up in platoons.

title: Confused about vehicular IFE
question:
3.5 VEHICULAR MG/IFE FIRE: The MG/IFE armament of a vehicle, unlike a SW counter (A9.2), may make only one fire attack per Player Turn unless it is the vehicle's MA with a specific Multiple ROF, in which case it and its ROF will be listed as the MA in the lower left-hand corner of the counter.

Umm, so can a MA, with ROF 3 and IFE FP in brackets, make multiple attacks or not?
author: Hipsu
consensus_answer:
A vehicular MA MG can fire in the MPh until ROF expires, and it is marked with First Fire.
  Only Infantry can Subsequent First Fire, so the vehicular MA MG cannot fire again in the MPh.
  The rule you quote specifically allows the vehicular MA to use Final Fire in the DFPh against an adjacent or same hex unit.

It's always fun to thrash out how these rules interact!

D3.5 VEHICULAR MG/IFE FIRE states, 
"Non-CC vehicular MG fire is limited to the same fire phase (A. 15) as the vehicle's other weapons or that of its PRC; if any weapon is fired from a vehicle, the remaining weapons must fire in the same phase or forfeit their non-CC fire attack opportunity for that Player Turn" 

I've always interpreted this to mean that, other than the listed exceptions for CC, Multiple Overruns and Bounding First Fire, ALL AFV weapons have to fire and complete their fire in the same phase. 

A9.3 does say "Sustained Fire cannot be used by a vehicular MG [EXC: MA, as per 8.4]" and 8.4 says "Any such units/weapons that are marked with a First Fire counter may also fire again (by flipping their First Fire marker over to the Final Fire side), but as Area Fire and only at units in an adjacent (or same) hex"

When it's all added up I believe a MG MA on an AFV can use sustained fire against an adjacent unit in the DFPh but only if all his fire from that AFV took place during that phase. But I don't believe you can fire during the enemy MPh until ROF is exhausted and then use Sustained Fire in the DFPh since D3.5 clearly prohibits firing AFV weapons in multiple phases of the same turn. 

You're incorrect.  D3.5 references A.15.  

A.15 says: Even though Defensive First Fire occurs during the MPh and Defensive Final Fire usually occurs during the DFPh, qualifying units may fire in both without violating the general rule that no unit can fire in more than one phase per Player Turn (7.1).

Therefore, if you keep ROF, you can fire again in DFPh OR if you have a qualifying MA, you can use Sustained Fire in the DFPh (within within the limits of Final Fire).

S

title: Entrenchments and initial placement
question:
If a scenario provides foxholes at setup are foxholes placed on board at setup or only once in Los of the enemy?

Just read A12.3, all sorted.
author: bluetiger80
consensus_answer:
Foxholes are also revealed *during* play when enemy units gain a LOS to them. So they, like most Fortifications, remain hidden until seen.
This creates a situation that was very hard for me to wrap my head around when I was starting with ASL. 

The Foxhole or trench sets up hidden but the units inside do not necessarily. This means that units at setup will often be sitting out in the open. They are visible but the foxhole that they are hiding in is hidden until a LOS is established. (I'm pretty sure this is how it works but please correct me if I'm wrong). 

My brain had a hard time with the notion that you could see the guys inside the hole in the ground but you couldn't see the actual hole. 

Seeing enemy units wihtout having LOS to them is like having intelligence information from scouts or air assets that there are enemies here, here and here. But they have not seen fortifications. When your troops really get there, they see all that's there to see.

title: Concealment and TH table
question:
Seking clarification on firing guns at concealed troops:

1) if firing a gun at a concealed target do you have to use area fire or is the +2 drm the only benefit?

2) do you gain acquisition against concealed targets, and if so are you free to switch between area and unit acquisition types?
author: bluetiger80
consensus_answer:
As to the final part, I am not sure, but I don't think you can use acquisition gained using Area Target Type against concealed units if you switch to Infantry or Vehicle Target Type.

I think you can:

"C6.52 BRACKETING: Acquisition DRM gained on one target/Target-Type can be transferred to another target/Target-Type when the firer announces a shot at-that-new-target/using-that-new-Target-Type, provided the target Location (or hex, if using the Area Target Type) remains the same during the transfer"

although note that 

"C6.57 A concealed target becomes acquired only if using the Area Target Type - or, when using the Vehicle or Infantry Target Type, if the acquiring shot causes the loss of that concealment."

replies.body:
As to the final part, I am not sure, but I don't think you can use acquisition gained using Area Target Type against concealed units if you switch to Infantry or Vehicle Target Type.

I think you can:

"C6.52 BRACKETING: Acquisition DRM gained on one target/Target-Type can be transferred to another target/Target-Type when the firer announces a shot at-that-new-target/using-that-new-Target-Type, provided the target Location (or hex, if using the Area Target Type) remains the same during the transfer"

although note that 

"C6.57 A concealed target becomes acquired only if using the Area Target Type - or, when using the Vehicle or Infantry Target Type, if the acquiring shot causes the loss of that concealment."

1) Don't have to use Area Target Type.  Whichever target type you use, the +2 To Hit DRM applies.

2) Can't gain acquisition if you use Infantry or Vehicle Target Type.  Can gain acquisition if you use Area Target Type.

As to the final part, I am not sure, but I don't think you can use acquisition gained using Area Target Type against concealed units if you switch to Infantry or Vehicle Target Type.
That is, you cannot bracket from Area Acq to a Infantry Acq if there are no known units in the hex.

title: NOOB using OVA
question:
Hey all,

I am trying to work out how a OVA works. Case in point, my Pz III during the movement phase OVA a Russian crew manning a 45L AT gun. The gun has already first fired was well as intensive fired so that can't respond to the attack. The crew are pinned from other fire too btw. So first up the crew take the PAATC and pass. So they cc the tank as part of reaction fire?

OK assume that's correct they roll high so no effect. Now this is where I am confused.

I work out the FP for my tank - 16FP after working out the mgs and the 4 inherent. So is the 16FP resolved on the IFT table or on the cc table? I can't find the rules that actually specifies this? I assume as the rules talk about sw destruction then it has to be the IFT table. 

Also what are the DRMs. One states the crew get the TEM effect so I would assume +2 for being emplaced but a cheat sheet I have says -1 emplaced but +2 for being in motion???

Please help!

Cheers
author: xcom101
consensus_answer:
Some other comments.

The gun could have used OVR Prevention (C5.64) after the OVR MP expenditure but before its resolution. One (only) shot allowed even after IF.

After the OVR resolution you could use CCRF (C7.21) or NCCRF (C7.22), if allowed:
- As your crew is pinned, they cannot use CCRF (must be unbroken, unpinned and neither Unarmed or in Melee, C7.21). 
- As your gun has already IF'd, they cannot fire the gun as NCCRF (C7.23). Also, as the crew are pinned they could not change the gun's CA if needed (A7.81).
- The only possible action for the crew is to FPF TPBF as NCCRF (C7.221), but of course if the AFV is BU, it will do nothing except acting as a NMC against the crew, as per FPF (A8.31).

replies.body:
Do you have the ASLRB 2nd Edition?  If so, there's a flowchart that walks you through the steps.  It sounds like it would be very helpful to you, but here are some answers to your questions:

CCRF is always after the OVR.  The Gun could have fired (incl. OVR Prevention, even if marked Intensive Fire, unique in ASL to be able to fire already marked IF).

The modifiers are also included on that chart.  That -1 is for Open Ground, the reference to emplaced just tells you that emplaced doesn't negate the OG penalty.  So it looks like you'd have a 16+1.  If it was emplaced in brush (for instance) it would be 16+2.  You never pay a Motion penalty on an OVR (Motion is part of it, after all...).  The resolution is on the IFT.

I strongly encourage you to go through each box of the chart.  It may take a couple times (it sure did for me!), but it'll get you there.  For a bit more "plain English" and some advanced insight, Carl Noguiera wrote an excellent article on OVRs in ASL Journal 8.

S

title: Berserk vs disrupted unit
question:
Hi guys,

Hope you can clarify this situation that occured while playing solitaire last weekend.

A Berserk German infantry unit charges into a woods hex containing a  disrupted and broken minor allied 437 squad.

During the RtPh, will the 437 surrender? (since it cannot rout away for being disrupted).
Can the berserker accept the surrender? If no and the 437 is eliminated, then will no quarter take effect?

The way i played it ....the 437 is eliminated but no quarter does not take effect.

Hope some of the veterans can clarify.

thanx   :)
author: Lamskiy
consensus_answer:
Hi guys,

Hope you can clarify this situation that occured while playing solitaire last weekend.

A Berserk German infantry unit charges into a woods hex containing a  disrupted and broken minor allied 437 squad.

During the RtPh, will the 437 surrender? (since it cannot rout away for being disrupted).
Can the berserker accept the surrender? If no and the 437 is eliminated, then will no quarter take effect?

The way i played it ....the 437 is eliminated but no quarter does not take effect.

Hope some of the veterans can clarify.

thanx   :)

A19.12 allows a disrupted unit to rout if the only ADJACENT enemies are "in-Melee/berserk/vehicular" (lines 11 & 12). So it would rout away, possibly taking interdiction, and the berserker would remain berserk.

S

My understanding is that since the berserker is in the hex with the broken squad, there's a CC marker and it does not rout, but would have to wait for withdrawal from cc if it were eligible to rout. As it is, it would surrender, die and invoke NQ.
Yes? No? Maybe? We love the game for its complexity, right?

No, actually.  You're not prevented from routing under a CC counter, only if you're in Melee (A10.5).  And you're not in Melee until you've been through one CCPh (as you certainly know re: withdrawal, Andy! ;))

So you rout right out of that berserker's hex.  Similar thing often happens on banzais.  Since the defenders are often broken by their FPF, they end up broken and rout away.

S

title: SW with ROF in PFPh can't fire in AFPh - rules reference?
question:
Hi All,

I believe that a SW that has maintained ROF in the PFPh can't then fire in the AFPh as per A3.5 but is there any other rule that explicitly states that a SW which has fired in the PFPh and maintained ROF can't then fire in AFPh?

Thank you....
author: sapper_D
consensus_answer:
Hi All,

I believe that a SW that has maintained ROF in the PFPh can't then fire in the AFPh as per A3.5 but is there any other rule that explicitly states that a SW which has fired in the PFPh and maintained ROF can't then fire in AFPh?

Thank you....

A3.5 Advancing Fire Phase tells you that "The ATTACKER's units which did not fire in the Prep Fire phase may fire..."

This references back to A3.2 Prep Fire Phase where you're told to mark those units that fire with a Prep Fire phase.

Basically, keeping ROF may allow you additional shots, but you can still only fire in one phase.  Keeping ROF doesn't mean you didn't fire.

S

So Spencer, if I understand you correctly, you're essentially saying that there is no rule other than A3.5 that prohibits a SW that has maintained ROF in the PFPh to fire in AFPh?

Really I'm just wondering if there is some EXC: clause somewhere that allows ROF SWs to fire again in the AFPh after firing in the PFPh...

No, that was just the first one I found.  A7.1 that Dan cited is the clearest statement in all likelihood.

S

title: Optional panzerfaust rule.
question:
My friend and I think that German infantry is just too powerful with unlimited PF's to blast away at allied tanks, so we were thinking of using the optional rule where you get a set number of PF's depending on what year the scenario you are playing takes place.
What are the Geeks thoughts on this rule? Is it better? Does it unbalance scenarios? Does it make life slightly easier for Allied tank crews?
author: blatant
consensus_answer:
PF are powerful, but in my games I don't see them used that frequently,  You have to roll to see if the unit has the PF, if you roll a 6 they are pinned, and use constitutes use of an SW.  Back blast is also a problem. 

But the biggest thing is players just don't get too close to German Infantry with tanks when the Germans have PF.  Until June 44 the PF range is only 1 hex, from June 44 to December 44 the range in only 2 hexes, and after that the range is 3 hexes.  But by then, the PF is often about all the German has to defend themselves from tanks.  Also you can use combined arms, screen your tanks with infantry to prevent the German infantry from approaching close to your tanks.

The optional rule you mentioned (C13.311) requires bookkeeping and for me it isn't worth the extra work, but your mileage may vary.

replies.body:
My friend and I think that German infantry is just too powerful with unlimited PF's to blast away at allied tanks, so we were thinking of using the optional rule where you get a set number of PF's depending on what year the scenario you are playing takes place.
What are the Geeks thoughts on this rule? Is it better? Does it unbalance scenarios? Does it make life slightly easier for Allied tank crews?

I should note that I'm no fan of optional rules, just by way of full disclosure.

But to try to give a fair answer, I would say that if you think the Germans are too powerful, I'd have to ask "in what context?"  If you're talking about in published scenarios, I have to simply disagree.  I can pretty much guarantee you that all playtesting at every major ASL publisher does not use the Optional PF rule, so scenarios are not tested with it in mind.  If you're doing DYO, well, balance is pretty much a shot in the dark there and I don't have much advice to offer you, except to note that German BPVs do go up through the course of the war to account for (inherent) PF ability.

As a bit of a mitigating point, the Germans are not the most powerful nationality in ASL (IMO, there is no such thing).  They are, however, the easiest to use well, which is reinforced by them being the most frequently appearing.  That means that your "base tactics" may have developed with Germans in mind.  Those tactics will not translate 100% to Russians or Americans (or others, for that matter).  You have to play each nationality somewhat differently.  My won-loss record tells me my Russian tactics needs work (probably because I try to play them like Germans).

So my practical suggestion is this: don't change the rules, change the way you play against the Germans.

S

PS: PFs are never unlimited...you are allowed only a certain number, based on your number of squads and the year.  Also keep in mind that the range is limited based on the timeframe.  PFs are good, but they're not omnipotent.

We think we figured out that this rule is not in fact optional (getting ready for a KGP I campaign, my first foray into ASL).  One gets a max of 1.5 PF To Hit Rolls times the number of your squads for the scenario.

There are optional rules that you can use to provide even more detail AFAIR.

Edit:  1.5 in 1944, that is.

I've used it for SASL. It's worth it to (i) have them be equivalent to the other SCWs in that they are readily available and do not require the dr and (ii) prevent a unit that normally would not have a lot of them from firing a schwack of them, which is theoretically possible. But I've also used Battlefield Integrity, so I'm obviously insane.

But the biggest thing is players just don't get too close to German Infantry with tanks when the Germans have PF.  Until June 44 the PF range is only 1 hex, from June 44 to December 44 the range in only 2 hexes, and after that the range is 3 hexes.  But by then, the PF is often about all the German has to defend themselves from tanks.  Also you can use combined arms, screen your tanks with infantry to prevent the German infantry from approaching close to your tanks.

The optional rule you mentioned (C13.311) requires bookkeeping and for me it isn't worth the extra work, but your mileage may vary.

I would only play that rule if asked for by an SSR.

What is more powerfull : a German unit which could have a PF and risks a dr that counts as if it fired one (and if a 6, pins the unit) or a German whom you are sure possesses a number of PFs and can fire them at will ?

With the optional rule, SMCs and HSs can much more easily carry and fire PFs than in the normal rule.

All in all, the presence of potential PFs just asks one to adapt his tactics to the situation (you don't fight 1945 German infantry as you fight it in 1942)... and ASL is all about adapting to a given tactical challenge.
Personally, I think that rule would make them more powerful.  They are guaranteed to have PF.  At least before  your opponent had to roll a specific number.

title: Firing through Smoke??
question:
Ok so quick question in regards to a situation,

Ordnance has laid down smoke in multiple hexes (so +3 smoke). My units advanced into the smoke for cover. The enemy opens fire on my unit in their prep fire phase using a fire group. 1 unit in the group has direct LOS to the unit in smoke so suffers a +3 penalty to IFT. The second unit has to trace fire through smoke in an adjacent hex first with +3 smoke) then into the target hex holding my unit. So is the total modifier for the fire group +6? Also the smoke rules state that it can't be any more than a +3 but only in one location. Does this apply? I assume not as it is two different locations?

So if the hindrance modifier is now +6 does that mean the FG can't then see the target and as such can't function as a fire group?
author: xcom101
consensus_answer:
Once you get up to +6 in hindrances, you can longer see the unit.  It is considered blocked.
A multi-Location FG which discovers that one or more of its units' LOS is blocked forfeits the participation of only those units whose LOS was blocked. The FG's other units with a valid LOS must still attack the same target (unless it was eliminated by a previous attack, in which case their attack is forfeit and they are marked with an appropriate fire phase counter) after resolving the blocked firer's DR (6.11), but as a smaller FG or as separate attacks. (A7.52) 

Part of the FG has so many hindrances that they no longer have LOS. You have to resolve a separate DR for the blocked guys. Then the rest of the original FG must still attack the target, but without any hindrances from the blocked guys. It also sounds like if there was more than one remaining unit you can decide whether to do separate attacks or a FG as long as they all attack.

I was surprised by this: both that the blocked guys get a separate DR and that you could then choose to break up remaining units instead of still having to go with the FG you originally committed to.

I have never seen this played correctly.  Wow.  Thanks.  I put the sticky errata in there, but, wow, just...always learning.

S

The blocked attack gets a DR, but will not affect the target.  It's for Malf etc...just as a normally, "hard" blocked LOS would be resolved.

Nothing new here. Just that Smoke is a Bitch to fire through.

He who uses Smoke most effectively will have a much easier fight ahead of him.

He..no use...no win...

title: Cellars in RB and FP rules?
question:
Hey all,

Ok another noob question, playing RB the cellar rule states:

6.4 FIRE EFFECTS: The Inherent FP of a unit/FG in a RB Cellar is halved as Area Fire if the LOF leaves their building's depiction and is not traced to an ADJACENT RB Cellar Location, and the US# of the unit(s) currently using such Inherent FP is ≥ 3. (A leader directing fire from an RB Cellar Location does not add his US# for this calculation.) Otherwise, a RB Cellar has no effect on the use of SW/Inherent-FP other than those normally caused by being fired in a building. A DC in a RB Cellar may be Thrown only into an ADJACENT Location.

Ok so I have a unit ground level in a building, in the same hex the enemy are in the cellar. So since their fire is not leaving the building depiction, I assume they don't get 1/2 FP even if there are 2 squads there with a sw in the cellar?

If I was in the same building, again at ground level but in an adjacent hex I assume the enemy in the cellar still don't suffer the 1/2 FP issue?

Also I assume in both cases, the enemy in the cellar would get 2x FP for being point blank but not TPB as I am not in the same location?

So from what I can see, a enemy unit in a cellar would only get 1/2 FP if they were firing from the cellar to say an adjacent hex next to building but only if that hex is not part of that building hex (ie open ground next to the building). Is that right?

Cheers from a noob and thanks for all your help in advance.
author: xcom101
consensus_answer:
I'm not an expert in RB...

I'd say that your conclusion is wrong. Look at example in O6.2. If you fire from C25 RB Cellar to C24h0, there is LOS, they are in the same building BUT the LOF leaves the building depiction WHILE the target is not an ADJACENT hex. So if US >= 3, inherent FP would be Area Fire.

Note that this affects only inherent FP, not SW.

In the same example, fire against B25 RB Cellar would not be affected, fire against B24h0 would be affected and there would be no LOS against B25h0.

Is it clear?

DI is a useful weapon if employed at the right times.  The main lessons are:

-Size modifiers are a huge thing on DI.  5-6-7 is a dense part of the probability curve.  It's actually pretty easy to DI a double-large King Tiger (1/3 chance if it's sitting still).  Thankfully, large targets tend to be the heavily armored ones.

-ROF matters.  You can't use acq, but you can take multiple shots (note you gain acq, you just can't apply it).  The exact math is complicated, but a ROF 3 weapon has around a 50% better chance of pulling this off than a ROF 0 weapon.  Lots of light AT Guns have high ROF, so this is in the DIer's favor as well.

title: Japanese squads with underlined morale. What happens when they exceed ELR?
question:

Full Squad breaks and exceed ELR

Step Reduced Squad breaks and exceed ELR

author: Hipsu
consensus_answer:
As already said :
- an underscored morale squad which exceeds its ELR is exchanged to two broken HS of its class (A19.13).
- an underscored morale HS which exceeds its ELR is Disrupted - but a Japanese HS does not disrupt (G1.2), so it is simply broken with no change of class.

"G1.16 DEPLOYING: A Japanese squad Deploys in the normal manner [EXC: if Reduced-Strength, it is exchanged for just one of its HS]."

So, in the case of an underscored morale, Step Reduced squad, it is exchanged with a single broken HS.

question: Just wondering if when entering a gully hex you have the option of not entering INTO the gully? title: Half Height LOS obstacle  Question
question:
Ok so a friend and I read somewhere that firing through a half-Level LOS obstacle adds +1 to all fire traced through that hex, provided that hex isn't the target. I am unsure though rereading the section. 

Can a unit fire through a half-level LOS obstacle to a unit 1 hex behind said obstacle? 
EX: a unit is a rubble hex. The hex directly in front of that hex is also rubble. Directly in front of that hex is a enemy unit in open ground. Can the unit in the rubble hex fire on the unit in open ground (assume neither has moved)?

Cheers and thanks for your help in advance.
author: xcom101
consensus_answer:
You seem to have some confusion between obstacle and Hindrance. An obstacle blocks LOS, so in your example, LOS is blocked by the rubble between the two units.

However (1): Grain, or brush is a half-level Hindrance. If it was a grain hex in between, there would be a +1 DRM for the Hindrance.

However (2): Half-level obstacles have no effect if there is an elevation difference. If the firing unit was on the first level of a building, and the hex in between was woods (full-level obstacle), LOS would be blocked. Rubble (or any other half-level obstacle or Hindrance) would have no effect in that case.

title: D7 OVERRUNS
question:
Is an OVR the only allowed way to attack a unit in the same hex during one's own MPh? Or is it allowed to enter the hex just at the COT and attack with regular Bounding Fire?
