If an enemy unit manages to enter your location during MPh:
- If MMC, you must shoot at it, be it First Fire, Subsequent First Fire or even FPF. (A8.3212)
- Remember Triple Point Blank Fire (TPBF). (A7.21)
- While the enemy unit is in your location, you cannot shoot out of that location. (A8.311)
- Put a CC counter on the location but don't resolve the CC until in CCPh. (A8.31)

:halfstar: Residual FP clarification (A8.26)
- The strength of Residual FP shifts one column to the left on the IFT for each positive DRM caused by conditions outside the target hex (hindrance, CX, etc).
- This was clarified from SK2 onward.

Defensive Fire Phase (DFPh)

:star: Clearance (B24.7)
This is another phase where you can make a Clearance attempt.
- Except you can't clear Rubble or a Minefield. Those you can only do in your MPh.

Advancing Fire Phase (AFPh)

:star: Fire spreads
Flame/Blaze
- Flames can turn into Blazes. (B25.15)
- Blazes can spread new Flames. (B25.6)

:star: In the same location with the enemy (and not in Melee)
You can shoot them, with TPBF, even if a CC marker was placed earlier in the MPh. Remember to also halve the FP because of AFPh.

:star: Opportunity Fire (A7.25)
Units that used Opportunity Fire at PFPh can now shoot with full FP.

Rout Phase (RtPh)

:star: Voluntary Break (A10.41)
You can voluntarily break your unit at the start of the RtPh so it can rout away if need be.
- Must be ADJACENT or in normal range and LOS of an unbroken enemy ground unit.

:star: Concealment (A10.533)
- "?" stacks must be ignored as if they weren't there when choosing a rout destination. This can be either helpful or catastrophic to your routing units.
- If you rout into a "?", one enemy unit is revealed using Random Selection and if the stack is not a dummy, your unit is eliminated.
- A concealed unit may reveal itself anytime during RtPh. It can be a good tactic to force the routing unit to immediately choose a different destination to rout to.

:star: Surrendering and No Quarter
- If your broken unit is ADJACENT to a Known, Good Order, armed enemy Infantry unit and unable to rout without taking interdiction or resorting to Low Crawl it must surrender to that unit. See the prisoner rules. (A20.21)
- The captor can refuse to take prisoners and eliminate it instead. However this invokes No Quarter for the rest of the game and any subsequent Router must take Interdiction or use Low Crawl just like in Starter Kits. (A20.3)

:halfstar: Direction (A10.51)
- You can of course rout up/down building levels.
- You can use shellholes/entrenchements/pillboxes to your advantage to avoid Interdiction if they are along the shortest route to your destination even if you can no longer reach that destination (it takes 1 extra MF to enter or exit a foxhole for example).
- You don't have to rout through a minefield or a hex being bombarded by off-board artillery.

:halfstar: Voluntary Rout clarifications (A10.71)
As you might remember, an unbroken leader can rout with the broken units. It's called Voluntary Rout in the full ASL. Anyway, there are some restrictions that the SK rules don't mention:
- A leader cannot rout with a broken unit if he's Pinned (or Berserk).
- A leader does not improve the broken unit's portage capacity.

Advance Phase (APh)

:halfstar: Eligible advancing destinations (A4.7)
Location Primer
You can advance either:
- From one location to another.
Or
- One hex horizontally, as counterintuitive as it may sometimes sound. 

You cannot combine the two. No moving from downstairs to an adjacent hex upstairs.

For example you can advance directly from beneath a foxhole into another foxhole in an adjacent hex. It may sound strange because if it were the MPh, you'd first have to spend 1 MF to get out, then 1 MF to move into an adjacent hex, then 1 MF to move into a foxhole. But that move is allowed in APh because foxholes are not considered separate locations. (B27.13)
A pillbox on the other hand is a separate location. So you cannot advance out of a pilbox and into an adjacent hex at the same time.

:halfstar: Difficult terrain (A4.72)
SK rules makes it clear that if a move would cost all of the unit's MFs then that unit becomes CX, or if already CX, that move cannot be made. Full rules adds another twist:
- If the cost to enter that hex is (excluding SMOKE) four MF or more, it's the same deal (makes the unit CX, or if already CX, that move cannot be made). Example: Woods on an upper level hill.
- This cannot be avoided with the help of a leader. 

:halfstar: Entering the Board (A2.5)
As mentioned in the MPh, your units can enter the board in APh, instead of MPh.

Close Combat Phase (CCPh)

No longer are you doomed to stay in Melee for possibly the rest of the game since the full ASL rules introduce mechanics for Withdrawal. Ambush or Infiltration may let you withdraw from the first CC, otherwise you can only try to withdraw from a Melee.

:halfstar: Ambush (A11.4)
- Ambush can occur not only in woods or buildings but also anywhere where either side has concealed units.
- No Ambush if the CC counter was placed before CCPh.
- Successful Ambush lets you withdraw from CC either before or after the CC resolution, your choice. (A11.41)

:halfstar: Infiltration (A11.22)
If your CC DR is 2 or your opponent's CC DR is 12, you may immediately withdraw from the CC/Melee. 

Infiltration momentarily suspends the simultaneous nature of the CC, so what happens next depends on if you’re the ATTACKER or the DEFENDER (remember, the ATTACKER rolls first even in a simultaneous CC).
- First, remember to resolve the possible Field Promotion. (A18.12)
- If the ATTACKER rolls 2 he must first choose if he wants to withdraw before the DEFENDER resolves his attack. If he does, the DEFENDER does not get a change to strike back. That DR of 2 is still resolved against the DEFENDER but even if the DEFENDER was eliminated the ATTACKER does not gain control of that CC location. 
- If the DEFENDER rolls 2, he must suffer the ATTACKER’s roll first regardless.
- If the ATTACKER rolls 12, the DEFENDER does not roll for his attack if he chooses to withdraw.
- If the DEFENDER rolls 12, the ATTACKER’s roll is still resolved even if he chooses to withdraw.

:halfstar: Withdrawal from Melee (A11.2)
You can try to withdraw from Melee (not from CC) by announcing so at the start of the CCPh.
- Broken units must attempt to withdraw from Melee. A11.16
- Every Withdrawing unit gets -2 DRM to all CC attacks against them but also +1 DRM for every friendly unit that "stays and covers" i.e. is not withdrawing.

:star: Withdrawal Mechanics (A11.21)
- You withdraw to an adjacent location in the same manner as you'd advance in APh.
- The location cannot be occupied by a Known enemy unit.
- If you withdrew into a location containing enemy "?" or HIP units and it turns out it wasn't a dummy, your units are immediately eliminated.

:star: Concealment in CC/Melee (A11.19)
- HIP units in a CC location come to board under "?".
- All concealed units in CC must temporarily reveal their Strength factor which means dummy units gets removed. This doesn't remove the "?" altogether though.
- CC FP against "?" is halved.
- You only lose your "?" if you attack in that CC or suffer a Casualty Reduction. Thus it might be wise to forfeit your attack in order to retain your "?". Remember, concealed units are not held in Melee and can move or attack (with TPBF even) in the next turn.

:halfstar: SW/Gun elimination in CC (A11.13)
SW/Gun can be destroyed if its owner dies in CC and the colored dr of that CC DR is 1. Roll a subsequent dr and if it is < black Kill Number of that CC attack, then it's eliminated.

:star: Taking Prisoner in CC (A20.22)
- You can try to capture enemy units in CC if you announce a capture attempt before rolling the dice.
- +1 DRM to CC DR unless enemy is inexperienced in which case it's -1 DRM. If the final CC DR = Kill number you get one HS of the defender's choice.

:star: Resolve non-Flame Clearance (B24.7)
If you decided to clear some obstacles, other than Flame, in your MPh or DFPh, then now is the time to resolve those and see if you succeeded.

:star: Gain Concealment (A12.12)
Just a reminder, your units can gain concealment at the end of your turn if they are out of enemy LOS. Consult the Concealment Loss/Gain Table.

What's new with Support Weapons

:star: Assembling/Disassembling SWs (A9.8)
Some SWs (and Guns) may be dismantled to make them easier to carry.
- Such a weapon may start the scenario dismantled if wanted.
- The converting happens in PFPh or DFPh provided that the weapon has not yet been fired in that phase. It counts as using the weapon, meaning that if you convert it during PFPh, that weapon cannot move in MPh or fire in AFPh.
- A German HMG/MMG can be fired as LMG in its dm state. That's because the German HMG/MMG is basically the same weapon as LMG, just with more bells and whistles attached on.

:halfstar: Recovery of SWs (or Guns) (A4.44)
Spilky's ASL Play Aids. Table 7
- If an MMC breaks and drops its SW/Gun, a SMC in that location can immediately try to pick it up.
- SMC can try to grab the SW/Gun from a broken unit in RPh or MPh. Don't even have to pay 1 MF for that.

:halfstar: SWs/Guns may set up unpossessed
Starter Kit 2 and onwards clarifies that a Weapons may not be set up unpossessed. However, there is no such rule in full ASL.

Machine Guns

:halfstar: Permanent Breakdowns (A.11)
Whenever the #B decreases, the original #B changes to #X (for example Sustained Fire or Captured Use).

:halfstar: Field of Fire (A9.21)
If a MMG or HMG is in woods/building/rubble, shoots, and has the ability to shoot again (ROF, Subsequent First Fire) it must shoot inside the same CA (Covered Arc, see Gun rules C3.2) as its previous shot for the rest of that phase. Use the Field of Fire counter.
- Unlike Gun however, the CA includes the MG's own hex.
- Pinned MG retains its CA until the end of DFPh.

:halfstar: Mandatory Fire Direction (A9.4)	
Enemy infantry over 16 hexes away are treated as concealed.

Remember Bore Sighting (C6.4), Spraying Fire (A9.5) and Fire Lanes. (A9.22)

Flame Throwers (FT)

:halfstar: FT's effect on terrain (B25.12)
- A FT may create a Flame if an Original K or KIA is rolled on the IFT. A subsequent DR is made like it was a regular Kindling attempt.

Demolition Charges (DC)
Demolition Charges

:star: DC's effect on terrain
- A DC with an Original KIA on the IFT, like any sufficient HE strike, can cause Rubble (B24.11) or Flames (B25.13).
- The Rubble creation is checked first with a subsequent dr; If that also hits the KIA then that building location, and all the levels above it, are Rubbled. If not, then a Kindling DR is made to see if a Flame is created.

:halfstar: Thrown or Set DC
In addition to placing DC, it can also be Thrown or Set.
- DC is Thrown during friendly fire phase (That means your PFPh, DFPh or AFPh) or Defensive First Fire. It's less reliable and affects both the target's and the thrower's location. (A23.6 - 23.63)
- Setting a DC in a location costs the unit all of its MFs and is Hazardous Movement. That unit can detonate it during any subsequent friendly fire phase only. That does not include Defensive First Fire! (A23.7 - 23.72)

:star: Making a Breach with a DC
DC can be used to Breach a Rowhouse Building (B23.711), or a Fortified Building. (B23.9221)

Panzerfausts (PF)

:star: In 10/43+ Germans can use Panzerfausts (C13.3)
Germans
It's an inherent SW, meaning it's available for the Germans in every scenario from 10/43 onwards (or PFks prior that by SSR but those are very rare).
- To use them, you'd first have to learn about Ordnance (SK2 stuff. They are similar to PSKs, see Part 2 for more). However, PFs are primarily used against tanks and have only limited application vs Infantry. It's perfectly OK not to use PFs in an infantry only scenario if you're not ready to learn about Ordnance just yet.

What's new with ELR

:star: Disruption (A19.12)
A unit is Disrupted if it breaks and exceeds its ELR but cannot downgrade to anything worse anymore (Conscripts are prone to disruption for example)
- Disrupted units surrender more easily, cannot self-rally, do not like to rout, won't withdraw from Melee etc. All in all they're a bunch of miserable folk.

:halfstar: Replacement (A19.13)
There is no neat single unit replacement chart like in the backs of Starter Kit manuals. Instead look at the pictures in chapter A25. If that doesn't help you can always work it out yourself using the following rules:
- The unit's class must be lower than its current class. So a 1st line unit cannot downgrade to another 1st line unit.
- At least one of the Strength factors (FP, range, morale) must decrease.
- None of the Strength factors can increase.

:halfstar: Underlined morale (A19.13)
Underlined morale no longer grants total immunity to ELR. Instead, if a unit with an underlined morale breaks and exceeds its ELR:
- If a squad, it splits into two broken HS.
- If a HS, it Disrupts.

In the event that a squad with an underlined morale rolls an original 12 AND it also exceeds its ELR: (A10.31)
- First split the squad into two HS.
- Then eliminate one HS.

Other Miscellaneous new rules, changes and clarifications

:star: Nationality distinctions (A25)
Germans
Be sure to read Chapter A25 before you start a game. Russians, for example, might get a Commissar which is always fun.
- For some reason, the German's ability to get Panzerfausts in 10/43+ is not mentioned here but in C13.3 instead.

:halfstar: Victory Conditions (A26)
- All the Control rules are much more detailed here than in the SKs.
- Unlike in the SKs, the Victory Point values are defined in the rules, not in the scenarios. (A26.2)

:halfstar: Random Selection (A.9)
In Starter Kits you might roll some dice to choose randomly which target is affected in some situation but in full ASL there's an official way called Random Selection. The basic difference to Starter Kits is that more than one target may be affected. Read all about it.

Some examples where Random Selection is used
- #KIA and K/#. (A7.3)
- FG cowers. Check which ones get Prep Fire/Final Fire marker (A7.9)
- Multiple SW Malfunction. (A9.71)

:halfstar: Morale Level Ceiling (A.18)
Some game effects (Fanatic, Human Wave, etc) may cause the morale level to rise but it can never rise above 10.
- This has nothing to do with DRMs to Morale Checks however. 

:halfstar: Stacking Limits (A5)
The limit is still 3 full squads; however it's no longer absolute:
- You cannot exceed it in setup but can during play. There will be penalties however.
- It also no longer makes a location invalid to Rout to.
- 5 SMCs equals 1 HS. (A5.5)

:halfstar: Mandatory Leadership clarification (A10.72)
Leadership DRMs, whether positive or negative cannot be ignored except when attacking.

:halfstar: Right of Inspection (A12.16)
You actually cannot check what's in a big stack of enemy units unless they are in LOS to some of your units. And of course you can never check what's under opponent's "?" counters.

:halfstar: Wounded SMC (A17)
- If SMC is wounded during movement and it has already spent over 3 MFs, it's Pinned right there.
- A MMC can carry a wounded leader at the cost of 5 PP. The leaders +2 MF bonus still works.

:halfstar: Self-rally clarification (A18.11)
DR 2 on Self-rally, in addition to Field Promotion, always rallies the MMC.

:halfstar: CX does not affect MC or PTC (A4.51)
- This was clarified from SK2 onward.

:halfstar: Half-Hex clarification (A2.3)
- If the scenario instructs you to setup only on board 1 you cannot setup on a half-hex that's butted against a half-hex on board 2.
- Same thing for Victory Conditions. If you have to control all the hexes on Board 1 this does not include the half-hexes that are butted against Board 2.

:halfstar: Official word on how to handle errors (A.2)
If you've made a rules mistake earlier, it cannot be unmade later. A good rule to remember in tournaments.

My personal opinion: I will, for the most part, ignore this rule and use my own judgement on a case-by-case basis. If it's a friendly game and my opponent forgot to make his one self-rally attempt in RPh, and he remembers it in PFPh, I'll let him do that self-rally.

Part 2

What's changed from Starter Kit 2

Foreword
I was going to say that after reading Part 2 you'll be ready to play any scenario with just Infantry and Guns. While it's true, it also turned out that those kinds of scenarios are pretty rare in full ASL. In fact amongst the scenarios in Beyond Valor and ASL Classic (the two products you're likely to start with), I only found one: "5 - In sight of the Volga". This basically means that when you get to Guns you will most likely have to learn about tanks as well. Oh well, so much for the smooth transition.

Still, this article serves its purpose in pointing out what's new with Guns vs. Infantry, regardless of any tanks that may be roaming around the scenario.

Actually, this is a great opportunity to learn one great secret about tanks. They are in many ways just moving Guns! 
Let's see the definitions for Gun and Ordnance from the index: 
Gun: for firing purposes, any weapon on a 5/8" counter currently firing as ordnance; for non-firing purposes, any non-vehicular weapon on a 5/8" counter.
Ordnance: Any weapon which must score a hit on a To Hit Table before rolling again on the IFT or To Kill Table to resolve that hit. 

See? Whenever a tank uses the To Hit process with its Main Armament (MA) then it's considered to be a Gun for that moment. So when you read these rules, just remember they can also apply to tanks.

Setting up Guns

:star: Guns in upper level building locations (B23.423, B23.93, C2.7)
A Gun cannot occupy an upper level of a building, unless the location, and all the levels below it, are fortified.
- A Mortar of 82mm or less can fire from the roof if rooftops are in play by SSR. (B23.85)

HIP and Concealment of the Gun

:halfstar: A Gun that fires is not necessarily revealed! (A12.34)
A HIP/Concealed & Emplaced Gun that fires (not including IFE) does not necessarily lose its concealment:
- Reveals only if in LOS of a Good Order enemy unit and the colored die of TH DR is 5 or 6 (or just 6 if in LOS at range of 17+ hexes)
- If HIP and does not reveal, it's still placed on board but under "?".
- If there's no Good Order enemy unit in LOS, it doesn't even lose its HIP when firing!

:halfstar: HIP & Emplaced Gun in Open Ground (A12.2, A12.34)
- Unlike in the SKs, a HIP Gun in Open Ground can be seen at any range, but it does not reveal completely. It's placed on the board under a "?". 

(In SK2, because there was no concealment, a Gun was completely revealed but only in LOS at ranges of 16 and less.)

:halfstar: You can advance into a HIP location (A12.31)
Because HIP is a form of concealment, it behaves the same way as concealment.
- In SK2, any move (MPh, APh) into a HIP location reveals the HIP and bounces the moving unit back. In full ASL this only happens in the MPh. (A12.15)
- In APh you can move into a HIP location no problem. At the start of the CCPh the HIP unit is placed on the board under "?" and thereafter follows all the normal rules of concealment (-2 for ambuch etc.). (A11.19)

What's new with firing the Gun

:halfstar: To Hit numbers are calculated manually (C3)
The biggest single "change" from SK2+ to full ASL is that you have to determine the To Hit number (TH#) for the applicable Target Type (ITT, ATT, VTT) and the FP of the Gun yourself. There's no ready-made To Hit Chart because there are way too many different Guns in the system and such charts would be too big and unwieldy. Don't worry, it's pretty easy. To calculate the Final TH# we need to know the caliber and the barrel length of the Gun, the range to the target, and possibly the special ammo type if used.

A mini tutorial about TH#s:

Grab the blue chapter divider (or IFTMQRDC) and look at the To Hit Table. For comparison's sake find the SK2 To Hit Chart as well.

First look at the Range and Target Type. By cross-indexing these we can determine the Basic TH# (C3.3). For example a Gun shooting ITT at range 15 has a Basic TH# 6 (or 5 if using red numbers). However the Basic TH# does not take into account the Gun or Ammo type so it can't be used by itself. Note that the ranges go much farther than just 24 hexes (C2.25).

Next are "Gun & Ammo Basic To Hit Number Modifications" (C4)
These are modifiers that take into account the Gun we are shooting with and transforms the Basic TH# into a Modified TH#. The first three lines are the barrel length of the Gun (* = short, L = long, LL = extra-long). Notice how short barrels give minuses and long barrels give pluses. Pluses are good. These are not DRMs, these are modifiers to the TH#. We want as high a number as possible so we can roll under it.

The next two lines are special Ammo. APDS/APCR are used against tanks. It's harder to hit with them at longer ranges than with regular AP ammo. SMOKE gives +2 (up to 12 range). You might remember that in SK2 SMOKE used to be a -2 DRM (case 7) instead. A -2 DRM or a +2 modifier to the TH# leads to the same end result.

The final two lines are about the caliber of the weapon. Smaller shells lose velocity faster so small calibers give minuses at longer ranges. Note that a 40 mm or smaller caliber gets both of the negative modifiers.

Now that the Modified TH# has been determined we can start minding the DRMs to the shot. Now the pluses are bad again. Like in SKs, they are divided into Firer- and Target-based DRMs. Pay attention to the different symbols on the left and the explanations at the bottom.

Note the case L. Then look at the SK2 To Hit Chart, ranges 1 and 2. While SMOKE defected onto the side of minuses, Case L defected away. In SK2, case L gives plus modifiers to the TH# instead of being a minus DRM.

Now. Let's pick a Gun on the SK2 chart and see if we can calculate the Modified TH# ourselves. Let's choose the German 2cm FlaK 38 AA gun.
Ranges 1 and 2: The Basic TH# is 8. None of the Gun type modifiers apply at this range so the modified TH# should be 8 too. But remember case L, the turncoat that wanted to be a TH modifier instead. +2 at range 1 and +1 at range 2 makes TH#s 10 and 9 respectively.
Range 3-6: The Basic TH# is 8. No modifiers.
Range 7-12: The Basic TH# is 7. Still no modifiers at this range.
Range 13-18: The Basic TH# is 6. Now the modifiers kick in giving +1 for long barrel and -1 for being less than 57 mm and also -1 for being less than 40 mm. 6 + 1 - 1 - 1 = 5.
Range 19-24: The Modified TH# should be 4.

If you're wondering why the 37mm Gun below has different values than the 20mm Gun when they should be the same, then bonus points for you for finding an error in the SK chart. See this file for corrected numbers.

Mini tutorial concluded.

:halfstar: How to determine the FP of the Gun (C.6)
Assuming you're firing HE against Infantry, the FP can be easily determined straight from the IFT. You may have noticed that there are millimeter numbers ranging from 20 to 200+. Yes, those are Gun caliber sizes. Just use the appropriate column.
- If using ATT, halve the FP.
- If gaining a critical hit, double the FP. See below if it exceeds 36 FP.
- In either case, it's the FP that gets halved/doubled, not the Gun's caliber!

:star: Heavy Payload (C.7)
A 200mm shell is not the biggest in the world so this rule covers the really big guns. Basically the attack gets -1 DRM for every excess 50 mm. This only applies to OBA (Off Board Artillery) and Bombs. Those are only in play through SSRs so you won't see that for a while. But this rule also covers critical hits for lesser weapons:
- For a CH, every whole multiple of 8 FP over 36 gets a -1 DRM.

HE equivalence for AP and HEAT (C8.31)
- If, for some reason, you're firing AP, APCR/APDC or HEAT against infantry, you can determine the applicable FP from table C8.31, also found in the blue chapter divider.

:star: Target's concealment (C3.53)
- Concealment gives +2 DRM to TH, but does not halve the FP of a hit.

:halfstar: Improbable Hits (C3.6)
When it's impossible to make the TH# (too much +DRMs for example), it's still possible to hit with an original TH DR of 2.
- It's not automatically a critical hit.
- Make a subsequent dr: 1-3 is a hit and 1 is a critical hit.

:halfstar: Another chance to score a Critical Hit using ITT (C3.7)
Spilky's ASL Play Aids. Table 9
In full ASL a CH using ITT is also possible when you hit with an original 2 on the TH DR, even if the +DRMs would raise the Final TH# to, or higher than, half of the Modified TH#.
- Make a subsequent dr: 1 is always a CH and so is less than or equal to half of the Modified TH#.

:halfstar: Multiple Hits (C3.8)
A Gun of 15-40mm that scores a hit while rolling doubles using VTT or ITT achieves two hits instead of one.
- Make two IFT rolls (or TK rolls if shooting tanks) and choose one.
- IFE/LATW/MG = NA.

:star: Elevation differences (C2.6)
- Any Gun may fire at a target at a different level if the range is equal to, or greater than, the elevation difference.
- Only Mortars or AA Guns can fire at a higher-level target if the range is less than the elevation difference.
- A Gun in a building cannot shoot below it in the same hex. Only an AA capable Gun can shoot above it in the same hex.

:halfstar: Rubble, Flame & Shellholes
The common theme with these is that they can happen with an Original KIA on the IFT. The IFT on the Chapter A divider is a helpful reference.
- Any HE attack of 70mm or more (including DC) has a chance of creating Rubble. If a subsequent dr is also KIA then that building location, and all the levels above it, are Rubbled. (B24.11)
- Any HE attack regardless of caliber can cause a Flame in a location. If a Rubble was not created then a subsequent Kindling DR is made to see if a Flame is created. (B25.13)
- Shellholes can only happen by OBA strike of 150 mm or more. (B2.1)

What's new to Mortars
Mortars

:halfstar: The consequences of Indirect Fire (C.1, C9.1)
Both the OBA (Off Board Artillery) and Mortars fire Indirect Fire, even though Mortars on the board use the same Direct Fire To Hit procedures as other Guns. I'm just pointing it out because the -1 DRM of Air Bursts you learned in SK2 is actually a consequence of Indirect Fire and thus applies to OBA as well. Other consequences:
- TEM of Walls and Hedges is lowered by one against Indirect Fire. (B9.34)
- Building levels give protection to lower levels. So units in a stone building at ground level get a +3 TEM for the stone building and +1 TEM for every level above them. (B23.32)

:halfstar: Spotters (C9.3)
A Spotter may be designated for a Mortar. This allows the Mortar to stay out of LOS while a spotter in an adjacent hex shouts the directions for it.
- +2 DRM is added to the TH DR so its more difficult to hit.
- ROF is lowered by 1.
- See C9.3 for full details.

:halfstar: Mortars can be dismantled also (C9.2)
- Even 76-82mm mortars (those bigger counters) can be dismantled like a SW, so no need to manhandle them around.

Miscellaneous

:halfstar: Elite OB and Special Ammo (C8.2)
If your OB is designated as either German SS or Russian Guards or if the SSR specifies that your OB is "Elite":
- Your special ammo Depletion Numbers are increased by one!
- Example, underlined by me: "Elements of Fifth Guards Army [ELR: 4] set up as follows: {SAN: 3}"
- An important note for all the tank drivers: This does not include Smoke dispensers. (C8.9)

:star: How do Panzerfausts differ from PSKs? (C13.3)
LATW
The PFs were mentioned in Part 1, but here I go into more detail. They behave almost like Bazookas/PSKs, but with a few exceptions (grab the dark gray chapter divider):
- Because it's an inherent weapon, a dr determines if PF is available or not. 1-3 = yes, 6 = pin (or worse).
- A hit against infantry only affects one target. Before making the Random Selection, you can choose the target straight away if it carries a SW/Gun. RS is still made to see if there are ties.
- TH roll of 12 is not only a miss but also causes Casualty Reduction to the shooter. 11 if Inexperienced.
- IFT (or TK) roll of 12 is a dud (even against infantry which is exceptional. Usually duds are applicable only to TK DRs against vehicles).

:halfstar: Changes to Backblast (C13.8)
- In addition to buildings, backblast also happens in these terrain locations: vehicle, rubble, pillbox, cave, sewer.
- Out of those locations, backblast can only be avoided (+2 DRM) at the ground level of rubble or a building location (or at the rooftop, or inside a factory). In all those other locations the Desperation Penalty will happen. (C13.81)
- The +2 Backblast avoidance DRM can be avoided by using Opportunity Fire. (A7.25)
- Backblast weapons cannot be fired at a target two or more levels higher in an adjacent hex, or directly above them in the same hex.

:halfstar: An official way to solve an undeclared Target Type (C.9)
- It's the first applicable Target Type listed on the To Hit Table (i.e., Vehicle, Infantry or Area in that order).

:halfstar: Stacking Limit of Guns (A5.4, A5.5)
There's no stacking limit for Guns (or SWs for that matter). However a Gun and it's crew are considered equal to a squad for stacking purposes. This limits the amount of Guns in one location to three.

What's new to Manhandling the Guns

Usually, if a Gun needs to be moved, a Vehicle of some sort is also present which can tow the Gun. I'll talk about towing in Part 3. For now, let's just focus on what's new to Manhandling.

:star: Limbering and Unlimbering (C10.2)
In SKs you only moved QSU (Quick Setup) Guns. In order to move a Gun that's not a QSU it must first be Limbered.
- Both Limbering and Unlimbering are done in a phase where the Gun could normally shoot (PFPh, AFPh, DFPh). That Gun cannot shoot in that turn, not before, nor after (Un)limbering.
- Unlimbering is TI activity, meaning you can't do anything else in that turn.
- Limbering is not TI activity, meaning if you Limber in PFPh, you can start pushing it in MPh right away. It makes more sense when you learn that pushing the Gun is TI activity (and so is hooking the Gun to a Vehicle during MPh).
- Some Guns can shoot in a Limbered state, but most Guns cannot. (C10.24)
- CA can be changed while (Un)limbering the Gun.
- A Gun can be set up either Limbered or Unlimbered (just like SWs can setup dismantled) (A2.52)

:halfstar: Pushing the Gun is a Labor task and causes TI (C10.3)
- When the Manhandling DR fails the pushing units get a Labor counter. This helps them move the Gun in the next turn.
- Regardless of your success, when the pushers are done they are put under a TI counter.

Notes/Changes/New cases for TH DRMs, case by case

SMOKE you won't find here. It's moved to the To Hit Number Modifications.

:halfstar: Case A; Fire outside CA (C5.1)
Once a Gun (other than a mortar) fires from woods/building/rubble and it has the ability to shoot again (ROF, Intensive Fire), it must shoot inside the same CA for the rest of that phase.
- This is consistent with the same restriction to MGs (Field of Fire, A9.21), so it's easy to remember.

T, ST, NT? What does a Gun use?:
- A Gun with a white circle around it (360 mount) uses T (Fast Traverse) modifiers (1/1/1).
- A Gun without the white circle uses NT (Non-Turreted) modifiers (3/1/1).
- The ST (Slow Traverse) modifiers are only applicable to tanks.

:halfstar: Case B; Fire in AFPh (C5.2)
- A Gun firing in AFPh gets +3 instead of +2 if firing from woods/building/rubble.

:star: Case C3; LATW (C5.34)
- A LATW still only gets +2 in AFPh no matter where it shoots from.
- Backblast can only be avoided at the ground level of rubble or a building.

:star: Case E; Firing within hex (C5.5)
- A Gun firing at its own hex gets +2 DRM because the target is too close to track effectively.

:star: Case J; Moving/Motion vehicular target (C6.1)
- Note that this also applies to Dashing Infantry, not just to moving vehicles.

:star: Case K; Concealed target (C6.2)
- In SKs you got this when firing at empty hexes (case 18) but this also applies against Concealed Targets.
- Remember to not halve the FP if a hit occurs!

:halfstar: Case L; Point blank range (C6.3)
- This used to be factored into the TH# in SKs, but here it is a DRM instead.

:star: Case M; Bore Sighted location (C6.4)
Part 1 only mentioned what's applicable to MGs. Guns can Bore sight as well:
- Unlike MGs, Guns get the Bore sight benefit in any phase, not just for the Defensive First Fire.
- Is not cumulative with case N (Acquired Target).

:halfstar: Case N; Acquired target (C6.5)
Acquisition Player Aid Sheet
- Note that if using ITT (or VTT) against a concealed target, that target becomes acquired only if the acquiring shot causes the loss of that concealment. ATT has no such requirement. (C6.57)

:halfstar: Case P; Target size (C6.7)
- Those -2 to +2 DRMs apply to tanks only. Guns are still sized only between -1 to +1. (C2.271)

Unless you are firing from/at a vehicle, you can safely ignore:
- Cases C, C1, C2, C4, G, I, J1, J2.
- Bypass TCA Change to/through side Target Facing.
- Bypass TCA equals side Target Facing unless.
- Stun.
- Firer in Ocean during Heavy Surf if the attack is resolved on the IFT.
- vs Motorcyclist.
- Aerial attack vs Upper-Cliff cave/its contents.
- vs Wading vehicle.
- Target in Ocean during Heavy Surf if the attack is resolved on the IFT.

:halfstar: Infiltration (A11.22)
If your CC DR is 2 or your opponent's CC DR is 12, you may immediately withdraw from the CC/Melee. 

Infiltration momentarily suspends the simultaneous nature of the CC, so what happens next depends on if you’re the ATTACKER or the DEFENDER (remember, the ATTACKER rolls first even in a simultaneous CC).
- First, remember to resolve the possible Field Promotion. (A18.22)
- If the ATTACKER rolls 2 he must first choose if he wants to withdraw before the DEFENDER resolves his attack. If he does, the DEFENDER does not get a change to strike back. That DR of 2 is still resolved against the DEFENDER but even if the DEFENDER was eliminated the ATTACKER does not gain control of that CC location. 
- If the DEFENDER rolls 2, he must suffer the ATTACKER’s roll first regardless.
- If the ATTACKER rolls 12, the DEFENDER does not roll for his attack if he chooses to withdraw.
- If the DEFENDER rolls 12, the ATTACKER’s roll is still resolved even if he chooses to withdraw.

title: MF expenditure for smoke placement and Defensive fire
question:
So my 747 US Paratrooper declares a smoke grenade attempt into an adjacent hex which expends 2 MF.

Can the defender declare D1stF vs the squad as the attempt is declared but before the smoke is placed? or is the MF expended only once the smoke is placed/attemp fails?
author: bluetiger80
consensus_answer:
The MF spent is always considered as done before you can fire against it. Of course, smoke placement could fail, but the action is done.

Just yesterday my opponent spent 2 MF to place smoke grenades at an adjacent hex, but he forgot about a SQ of mine placed on another hexgrid, with clear LOS. So his SQ placed smoke on an hex and gave me two nice MF to shoot him with clear LOS, FFNAM and FFMO. You just have to love this game.

replies.body:
The MF spent is always considered as done before you can fire against it. Of course, smoke placement could fail, but the action is done.

Just yesterday my opponent spent 2 MF to place smoke grenades at an adjacent hex, but he forgot about a SQ of mine placed on another hexgrid, with clear LOS. So his SQ placed smoke on an hex and gave me two nice MF to shoot him with clear LOS, FFNAM and FFMO. You just have to love this game.

DFF must take in account the smoke placed at the occasion of the MF expended (if the placement attempt succeeded of course).

To help you grock the rule, it works as other MF expenditures : when a unit spends 2 MF to enter a stone building, DFF upon that MF expenditure takes the building's TEM into account.

The MF is expended for attack purposes after the smoke placement is resolved.

title: Residual fire and rof
question:
So in a game we're playing an mmc fired its  inherent fp plus mmg, mmg retained rof and fired again.

We figured the first fire attack leaves no res but does the second attack leave any?
author: bluetiger80
consensus_answer:
So in a game we're playing an mmc fired its  inherent fp plus mmg, mmg retained rof and fired again.

We figured the first fire attack leaves no res but does the second attack leave any?

Let me give an example so we can be clear. An American 6-6-6 squad and 4fp MMG fire at a moving unit that spends 2MF entereing a hex in normal range of both the squad and MMG.

The MMG makes ROF. The squad leaves a residual firepower of 2 in the hex.

The MMG fires again. This time it loses ROF. It would normally place a residual firepower of 2, but that doesn't increase the already existing residual firepower of 2 so it has no additional effect.

However, it the player had elected to forgo ROF (retained) from the first shot in order to increase RF (for tactical purposes lets say) then the attack was 6+4=10FP, resolved on the 8FP, leaving a 4FP RF counter instead of 2FP.

I usually find it more useful to place 2FP residual in two Locations instead of just one. But sometimes you have a proper choke-point that needs the 4FP residual.

when the mmg loses it's ROF it would leave its residual.

you could (though usually not the best option) leave residual with both the inherent and mmg with the first attack - and forgo the ROF.

title: Mila 18 Questions before we play (Mopping Up, Massacre, Search Casualties drm)
question:
All of these questions will sound soo anal and rules-lawyery but at least I ask them before the game so nothing's riding on these yet. :)

1. One of the VCs for Germans is:

"The German win at game end by Mopping Up 27 of the 32 buildings. The Germans must perform the Mopping Up procedure to claim a building for VC purposes. ZOB re-occupation of a Mopped Up building has no effect on the Victory Conditions."

Does the building need to be claimed for that Mopping Up to count or is it enough to just "perform the Mopping Up procedure"?
So if the first Mopping Up procedure reveals hidden ZOB units in a building, those must first be dealt with and then a second Mopping Up must be made to actually claim the building for it to count for VC?

2. Let's say Germans manage to get a ZOB prisoner. Then the Guard goes Berserk and Massacres those prisoners causing No Quarter. Result: Mopping Up cannot be performed anymore. Is this right, or does the VC somehow overrule this so that the Germans still can do Mopping Ups?

And I know, that would be rare, but obscure situations happen to us all the time and this time I'm going to ask in advance. :)

3. One of the Search Casualties drms is

"-1 Per HS equivalent > one concealed DEFENDING HS"

Just to clarify: Every extra HS must also be concealed for this to count? Because I read it so that only one HS needs to be concealed and all the others need not to...
author: Hipsu
consensus_answer:
Does the building need to be claimed for that Mopping Up to count or is it enough to just "perform the Mopping Up procedure"?

You just need to mop up.

So if the first Mopping Up procedure reveals hidden ZOB units in a building, those must first be dealt with and then a second Mopping Up must be made to actually claim the building for it to count for VC?

The building is successfully mopped up the first time regardless of outcome.

2. Let's say Germans manage to get a ZOB prisoner. Then the Guard goes Berserk and Massacres those prisoners causing No Quarter. Result: Mopping Up cannot be performed anymore. Is this right, or does the VC somehow overrule this so that the Germans still can do Mopping Ups?

It is true. If the Germans invoke no quarter then there is no more mopping up and the Germans will have to go for the other victory condition. Partisans won't surrender by rout phase method so if the Germans have prisoners it is because they wanted them.

Just to clarify: Every extra HS must also be concealed for this to count? Because I read it so that only one HS needs to be concealed and all the others need not to...

I really am not sure what you are getting at here so let me just say this. You may not mop up a building that contains unconcealed unbroken enemy units.

title: Emplaced guns - Have i got this right?
question:
Hi Guyz

Was playing ASL 84 - Round One last weekend; mainly solitaire with my usual opponent (i.e., my son) playing through the first 2 turns and i continued thereon. 

We have this early war scenario with the Germans vs Poles. The Poles have got 5 guns with SSR stating that the guns must be setup in fortified buildings.

As i understand the rules for guns:
1.    Guns set up in concealed terrain are emplaced.
2.    Emplaced guns can setup HIP until an enemy unit comes into LOS.
3.    Fortified building locations are not marked until the appropriate DRMs are required or an enemy unit attempts to enter the location (which in this case is a moot point as SSR states all guns MUST set up in fortified building location).

Now we have the guns set up covering the length of the streets. A german HS moves to the end of on of the streets ..thus coming into LOS of the gun. Must the gun now be revealed? ...i gather the answer is YES! 

Can we have confirmation? thanx in advance

cheers
-Lamskiy-
author: Lamskiy
consensus_answer:
1.  Guns set up in concealment terrain are HIP, buildings are concealment terrain.  Since they have to be in buildings, being Emplaced does not matter for HIP gain as it is a form of TEM. Read C11.2

2.  HIP guns remain HIP until they lose HIP as per Concealment Loss/Gain Table.  They will be emplaced in the building but the table application is the only reason this matters because you will use the "EMPLACED GUN (and manning Infantry)" row on the table.   Most common ways are firing, changing CA, or an enemy entering the location that guns lose HIP.  Emplacement has nothing to do with HIP.  For example a Gun can HIP in bamboo, but can not be emplaced in Bamboo.

3. Yes, well and the location being searched.

Read A12.34 Hidden Guns and C11.2 Emplacement

Read A12.34 Hidden Guns and C11.2 Emplacement

One more thing: even when firing, the gun may still remain under concealment even after losing HIP depending on what you roll.  Check the rules carefully...I don't remember exactly how it works (and I always forget), but you shouldn't!

Note that an HIP emplaced Gun in Concealment terrain which fires is revealed only if the colored die of its TH is 5-6 (or 6 at 17+ hexes) -otherwise it is no more HIP, but still concealed.

BUT, if it changes its CA within LOS of an unbroken unit, it loses concealment and is thus fully revealed.

Now, a sneaky nasty element of the rule : if the only enemy units which have LOS to the HIP Gun are not in Good Order, there is no HIP or Concealment loss (A12.14).
That means a HIP Gun can pump rounds against an in Melee, Berserk or Broken unit and remain HIP (under the condition, of course, no other enemy Good Order unit).:arrrh:

Also the emplacement is not really relevant for a gun in a fortified building.It only is to allow the Gun to keep concealment if it fires and does not roll a 5-6 on its colored dr.
You are right about the TEM thing (it also applies to a Gun in a non fortified stone building).

some guns can be set up in upper floors as long as both their level and the levels below them are fortified.... but only in stone buildings - I discovered that after a number of years of practice (in ASL one is allways learning).;)
B23.93 GUNS: A Fortified Building differs from a building in that any ART/AT/INF Guns ≤ 76mm may set up in the fortified upper levels of a multi-level stone Fortified Building.

Thanx very very much. One is always learning in ASL. 

I remembered an AAR that i read concerning guns in fortifications set up in HIP but is revealed when an enemy unit comes into LOS. After reading your replies ...i rechecked that AAR and fount out that the gun concerned was NOT in concealment terrain (in fact it was a desert AAR).

Shows you will need to check the actual circumstances of what you read ....  :p

Now, if an emplaced Gun in concealement terrain is in a fortification (Trench, Pillbox) and an Good Order enemy unit has LOS to it, the fortificatin is revealed, but not the Gun - nor any other HIP unit in that fortification.

title: Broken Units in CC - How does that work?
question:
Hi,

Maybe I should post this in the SK #1 forum (that's the scenario we're playing), but I'm guessing the CC rules are the same throughout? If a CX half squad advances into a hex with two broken squads and an unbroken leader, how do the CC odds get calculated? Can the half squad attack only the two broken squads, or only one squad, or only the leader? Etc.

Thanks!

Chris
author: fatgreta
consensus_answer:
It's very, very rare that the situation will come up in the Starter Kit rules - and no, they aren't identical.

Please note that a broken unit ADJACENT to an unbroken unit must rout during the Rout Phase (just before the Advance Phase) until no longer ADJACENT. (And it can't move ADJACENT to unbroken units throughout the rout). If it can't, it's eliminated for failure to rout. 

As I recall - and you'll get a more definitive answer shortly from someone who knows the game better than me - the leader must attack alone and the two broken squads can't attack. (In the full game, where this can occur, they're forced to withdraw, IIRC). You can then attack the leader, either of the two broken squads, or any combination of them, using their unbroken strength as their effective strength for calculating the ratio, but getting a DRM (of -2, IIRC).

I'm curious as to the situation where this occurred, or if you just missed the requirement for routing.

Cheers,
Merric

title: Making the move - new rules
question:
I'm now getting used to the Starter Kit 1 rules, and itching to play some full ASL.  Yes, I know I should ideally play all the Starter Kits first:whistle:

I thought I might attempt to solo ASL S1 - Fighting Withdrawal, since it only involves infantry and machine guns.

I'm wondering what new rules I'll have to read up on.  So far I'm assuming:-

Terrain (there are some big and different buildings on Board 21).
Concealment & HIP (I'll have to wing the HIP as I'm solo'ing)
Snipers
Heat of Battle
Weather
Ammunition Shortage (SSR)
Bypass Movement

What else is there I should read up on?  Or is this a foolhardy idea?!
author: Wiltshiresaint
consensus_answer:
If you've gotten a lot of play out of Starter Kit #1 and already have the ASLRB and BV, you can start this scenario.  It will be a huge chunk to bite off, but it's doable if you are willing to devote the time to reading and re-reading the rules as you play.  Some of the bigger things to get a handle on are:

Movement is a good bit different.  There's Bypass and Dash Moves, with attendant Snap Shots against hexsides units move through.  Takes some getting used to.  

Concealment and HIP is just for starters, you'll also have to get Searching and Mopping Up under your belt.  Huge effects of concealment on things like movement, ambush and close combat, determining rout paths, etc. 

Snipers, Heat of Battle, etc., aren't that hard.  Neither is weather--yet!  Ammo shortage isn't hard to understand either (just irritating as the Soviet).  

Blazes and fires--and smoke (with wind effects) will take some getting used to in this scenario.  Really important to leverage this as the Soviet player in coming up with a defensive scheme.  This stuff is going to channelize--and you don't want to be the one channelized into the streets under the muzzles of Finnish LMGs!  

Terrain.  Oh yeah, the buildings take some real practice to learn how to use them to good effect--particularly the multi-levelled ones.  Great article in the newest ASL Journal (#9) on buildings, written by Mark Pitcavage.

It becomes a journey in discovery.And there is the wonderfull A.2 rule !

A.2 ERRORS: All results stand once play has progressed past the point of commission. In other words, if an error is discovered after play has passed that point, the game cannot be backed up to correct the error, even if such error is in violation of a rule.1 For example, assume an attack is resolved without the application of a proper DRM, and a subsequent attack is resolved, or another unit moved, or play proceeds to another phase before a player remembers he was entitled to a DRM in the previous attack, thus changing the result. His failure to apply that DRM at the time of commission has cost him his right to claim that DRM. Or perhaps a player moves a unit before remembering that he wanted other units to attempt to Rally in the RPh or fire or entrench in the PFPh. Once the Phase for execution of a particular action has passed, the player has lost any claim to that capability.

title: Orchard Road hinderances
question:
Here's the deal:

B14.6 talks about Orchard Road but I can't decipher it.

In MPh the 447 moves from Q4 to P4 crossing the road hexside. I know it can decide if it actually wants to use the road movement or not which obviously affects FFMO.

but does that decision affect 467's ability to fire along that road unhindered?

So does the 447 get +3 hinderance or not based on if it uses road movement or not?

And if 447 stands in P4, can 467 fire unhindered in PFPh too, or does B14.6 somehow only apply to movement phase?
author: Hipsu
consensus_answer:
entrance of an orchard rd through a road hex incurs -1 FFMO, unlike the rules for woods road the rules for orchard rd (B14.6) do NOT give the option for entering the hex at the non road movement rate.

Unless this has been modified by official Q&A 

If you enter through a road hexside you are exposed, if you enter through a non road hexside you are not

In terms of non moving fire the TEM is ZERO, there is no hindrance.LOS is traced from hex centre to hex centre. You dont change the LOS rules just because they are stating they are not on the road. in the example LOS from the 447 would also only incur the in hex TEM of the 467 

LOS is traced down the road and into the hex, the hex TEM is zero.

For a woods road you have the option of paying 2MP to enter the hex to avoid FFMO, but you still trace LOS down the road hex centre to  hex centre except the in hex TEM is +1. You can still be shot at except you have better cover, unless you are copping an airburst. 

If we were to apply hindrance to the orchard rd, then a unit claiming the +1 TEM for woods road would have LOS bocked to it as per the same logic This is NOT the case.

replies.body: The Line of Fire is unhindered, as the Line of Sight between firer and target never leaves the confines of the road depiction.
If the LOS passes along a road without hindrance it is not hindered.

Some days ago there was a discussion in GameSquad about the same question. It was finally settled as this:

I think that the principle is the same for all non-Open-Ground-Terrain/roads combinations:
1. If you cross a road hexside and declare you are using the road, FFMO can apply (vs fire staying within the road depiction);
2. If you move across the road, FFMO doesn't apply.

In either case (obviously in case 1) if the fire is coming from along the road depiction (ans stays within it) the other terrain does not block/hinder the attack.

In fact, I think that even in regular Open Ground/road hexes, one can still cross the road hexside and declare one is not using the road. FFMO will usually apply anyway, but one reason to do it is to avoid the special A4.132 LOS possibility.

So FFMO and hindrance are not bound. If the LOS goes along the road depiction, there is no hindrance (in any turn phase). BUT, FFMO only applies if the Infantry uses the road when crossing the road hexside.

So if you cross the road hexside without using the road, orchard hindrance is not used and there is no FFMO.

Sure, there is a rule trail:

A4.132

Infantry entering a hex via a road hexside must pay either the road entry cost or the cost of other terrain in the hex. [...] If Infantry pays the cost of other terrain in the hex, it is considered in that terrain and avoids FFMO DRM unless that other terrain is Open Ground. If any LOS Hindrance [...] is present, FFMO is negated even though the unit uses Road Movement.

So when using a road hexside you can always choose if you are on or off the road.

B14.6 says

A hex [...] is actually a tree-lined road. Entrance of such a hex through a road hexside is identical to movement along any road. Hindrance rules do not apply to such hexes if [...]; in such cases, the -1 FFMO DRM applies to Infantry using the road to move.

So it seems clear reading two basic rules that if Infantry crosses the road hexside without using the road to move, they avoid the FFMO.

That's my POV.

If one reads the Orchard-Road rule in ASLSK 2&3, it becomes evident that the road aspect of the hex is operable only during the MPh. It deals with FFMO penalties for moving units using the road for movement, if LOS is along the road symbol. The rule finishes with the following: "Otherwise, orchard-roads are identical to orchards in every respect." [emphasis added] During Prep Fire, the unit is in an "orchard" hex, not sitting in the middle of the road running through it.

Edit: Oops! I thought I was in SK world. Sorry for the reference down to SK2/3

I'm with Marti here. The specification in B14.6 that "in such cases, the -1 FFMO DRM applies to Infantry using the road to move" clearly implies that the 4-4-7 has a choice to use the road or not. If the units enters via the road and a firing unit (the 4-6-7 here) has an LOS down the road, then FFMO applies.

However, the first part of that sentence in B14.6 ("Hindrance rules do not apply to such hexes...") is completely general and not only about the MPh. So if the 4-4-7 stayed in the hex and the 4-6-7 Prep Fired on it, I don't believe the shot should be hindered. That seems unrealistic, as the 4-4-7 presumably wouldn't be hanging out in the road after movement. But that seems to be what the rules say, barring some Q&A to the contrary.

title: Berserkers and smoke
question:
Can a berserker attempt to place smoke on the way to the nearest known enemy?

I'm in a hotel and don't have my rule book with me, but if I recall correctly, the rule says the bererk unit has to take the shortest path to the enemy unit, but it that doesn't mean the berserk unit has to spend the minimum movement points to get there, just that he has to use the shortest route.
author: jcurtis55
consensus_answer:
Can a berserker attempt to place smoke on the way to the nearest known enemy?
According to the ASOP, no:

A berserk unit executes its charge in Step 3.31A, After this, you jump directly to Step 3.35D... so a berserk unit never executes Step 3.32A, which is the step that allows SMOKE grenades to be placed. Berserk units technically can't do *anything* that's listed in Step 3.32A.

Consider, for example, Infantry OVR. This too occurs in Step 3.32A, seemingly making it NA to berserk units, so the berserk rules have to specifically allow it (A15.432). But there's nothing in the berserk rules that specifically allows the use of SMOKE grenades.

replies.body: I don't see anything in the relevant rules that expressly prohibits this, but there's no way I'd let an opponent try this on me. COWTRA. The rules say the Berserker charges, so that's what he does. If he's willing to bypass woods and buildings to get to his target faster (which the rules do mention), then he's presumably not going to spend the time laying down smoke cover.

title: Clearance  attempts and movement
question:
We played the first Pegasus Bridge scenario last weekend.  The British have to both control and clear the bridge.  This was our first game where the clearance rules came into play.   We were a bit suprised clearance attempts occurred in the movement phase and not the prep fire phase.    This led to the question, can a unit both move and assist with the clearance attempt?   

We couldn't seem to find a rule that prohibited a unit that moved from participating in the clearance attempt, yet logic would say a unit moving wouldn't have as much time to dedicate to the clearance attempt.
author: jcurtis55
consensus_answer:
I just pulled out the PB1 'Ham and Bloody Jam' card - the SSR reads, 'To "clear" the bridge, the British must make a successful Clearance DR in any bridge Location as though removing a Set DC (B24.75).'

24.75 SET DC: Unpinned, Good Order Infantry which has not moved or fired (or directed fire) during that Player Turn (as evidenced by placement of a TI counter and the declaration of their removal attempt during their MPh/DFPh) in a Location containing a Set DC may remove that Set DC with a successful Clearance DR at the end of the CCPh.

So, you'll need to have a unit in place and ready to rock at least by the beginning of the last British Player Turn.  Since you roll at the end of the CCPh the German will still be able to interfere with the clearance attempt.

Good luck, and post an AAR when you're done!

JR

Thanks!    I'll see about an AAR as it was an eventful game.   The bottom line was every German unit was eliminated and the British missed clearing the bridge.    I rolled a six on my final clearance roll (I got two chances at it), but without getting another unit moved into the hex, I needed a 4.   Had the unit moving in counted, I would have cleared it.

It completely seems reasonable that you cannot both both and assist with a clearance, but the clearance rules make no mention of it.  I appreciate the rule reference, as that's been bugging me to no end, even if it did cost me the win. :)

title: Can stunned crew repair something in the next rally phase?
question:
I ask because on the stun marker it reads "no repair" but the marker is flipped in the next advance phase before the crew even has a chance to repair anything.

author: Hipsu
consensus_answer:
You're not the first first to notice this error. Ian Daglish mentions it in his article: "Heads Up! Heads Down! AFV Passengers and Crews" that was published in ASL Journal #5.

AH-printed pin counters are correct.

"A broken unit is also automatically under DM whenever a Known enemy unit becomes ADJACENT to it (even if it does not end the phase ADJACENT to it)."

author: FlashPan
consensus_answer:
Main reason I stay out of ASL (yet). It looks to me that RB is like a bible open to never-ending discussions.ASL is a complex game.
If you compare the level of questions and errata in proportion of the size of the rules, they remain within reasonable bounds.
Note, too, that many questions arise from quite marginal situations, where rules interact in an unusual way.
What is nice, is that there are published official errata and clarifications which lead the community to play along the same rule interpretations.

It might be the reason that more than some ASLers play ASL and only ASL.The main reason of being hooked to ASL, is that it offers such a variety of possibilities, that players seem to discover its multiple facets on and on.

Shhh! Under any circumstances we should not even suggest that this ancient text might need some serious rewrite...The ASL RB is not the most pedagogical ruleset - I believe that is a statement that has been accepted from the beginning.
The SL had a "step by step" rule learning system.
But each addition to the rules created a dispersion (and unsuperable contradictions) that led to the "reference" ruleset style we have now.
However, there remains some dispersion (e.g Smoke rules), which can be countered by reference cards.

The coherence of the rules remains, IMO, remarkable, compared to many less abundant rulesets.
To try for a "serious" rewriting, one should have a very experimented knowledge of the present Rulebook - or the risk of missing essential interactions and taxonomy conventions will be enormous.
And the interaction of the rules rely upon the paragraph references : the basic structure could not be modified.

One way to go - I have been tempted to do it, but haven't enough energy and time to - would be to illustrate about each point of rule with an example and to have a "shortened" description of each point of the rule (more graphical).
It would not replace the current RB, but help checking the rules more easily.
Note that the Index is really a precious resource, as it often has sumarized definitions and lists most of the rules interactions.

But ASL is a complex game. There is a price of effort to learn it (and the learning doesn't really end - even on the side of learning the rules).

Now, to be an ASLer, I believe one must have a twist of mind that allows one to appreciate that type of game.
I don't mind if it is slightly pathological : to spend hours pushing cardboard units and having fun is a special way of life. ;)

The other thing to bear in mind Rafaell is that I haven't played ASL for a long time. This is only my second game since coming back a few weeks ago, what's more I still have a lot on pre-conceptions from SL, which tend to muddy the waters a little :)

I had got back into board gaming the middle of last year as I wanted a different experience from that provided by computer wargames. To get me back into the hobby I bought Conflict of Heroes (CoH) which I have now played to death. 

CoH is a very good game and what is more the rulebook is only 30 odd pages from what I remember - maybe less. When playing CoH my initial reaction was why did I ever bother with ASL in the eighties when CoH seems to simulate most of the salient points of WW2 warfare.

But after many plays of CoH and its sequel I started yearning for something more. Something with more depth, tactical variety and a little more unpredictability. In the latter case CoH only uses one DR for an attack, which makes it very easy for a player to work out what is likely to happen. In games like ASL there are effectively two or more DR, one for effect and several DR's for any pertinent morale checks that might be needed. This makes ASL both predictable and unpredictable at the same time(!) work that one out!

What 'turned' me was when I went through Jay Richardson's pdf ASLSK tutorial here on boardgame geek with VASSAL. title: Can Banzai Units Fire In the AFPh?
question:
A7.211 allows it, I think.

Mike
consensus_answer:
It seems that low level Japanese commanders were not trained to use any tactical flexibility at all - rather they were instilled with the Samurai tradition of relentless frontal attacks. 
 

I'm not at all sure this is an accurate statement. The Japanese were well versed in military tradition and learning, and had a set of tactical solutions provided in manuals. The Japanese Army ran rings around the Chinese Army, and did well against the Soviet Army in 1939.

Japanese field tactics had some distinct differences to the US Army, the most significant being the belief in closing with the enemy to close combat (shared by the British), the primacy of offensive action (which WW1 had knocked out of the Western Allies), and the need for swiftness in assault (which the Japanese had demonstrated in the 1905 War with Russia). The Japanese also often used infiltration and outflanking. A combination of terrain and technology base generally precluded the use  of massive bombardment and massed armoured blitzkreig, but the Japanese did use these relatively small arms effectively.

Japanese field tactics worked well in China, Manchuria, Malaya, Burma, Philippines and Dutch East Indies. The problem came when the Allies started heavily equiping their troops with individual automatic weapons. In essence, the Allied solution to Japanese Banzai charges was firepower, the same solution as happened in WW1, and the Japanese had no technological solution available. The best option was the night attack, which limited the amount of time units were under fire. 

It is probably fair to say that Japanese Officers were indifferent to the casualties of an attack, and that most were taught that the best chance of victory was through close combat assault. So the Japanese tactics reflected that view, but were not chosen without consideration, and indeed later in the Pacific war, they clearly changed to much more defensive and attritional tactics to further the grinding war strategy the Japanese were relying upon to seek an offer of conditional surrender.

http://www.lonesentry.com/articles/intelligence-report/small-unit-tactics.html

title: Wall Advantage Between Infantry and Armor?
question:
Since the Russian crew has Wall Advantage in DD5 I believe that prevents the PzIV from claiming Wall Advantage in EE5. And since Wall Advantage is claimed for a whole hex, not for a hexside, the PzIV cannot claim Wall Advantage over hexside EE5/EE6. So when the Russian tank rushes up to EE6 does this mean he can claim Wall Advantage over the PzIV? I assume so.

Correct the Rushing Russian tank can claim Wall Advantage as the PzIV cannot deny Wall Advantage.

When Russian Tank F and the German tank fire at each other the Russian will be hull down and the German will have no advantage?

Correct. Firing as ordnance.

Finally, what about when Russian Tank E fires from two hexes away?

The PzIV recieves all benefits of the wall.

I would guess that the German tank still gets +2 TEM for being behind a stone wall even though he does not get the hull down benefit of Wall Advantage. 

If the Russians fire ordnance the German tank is hull down. If the Russians fire on the IFT. The German tank gets the +2 TEM.

This all seems fairly odd - the way the little crew can hold Wall Advantage over the tank that I wanted to make sure I was playing everything right. A situation much like the one I constructed here was the pivotal point in a game I played recently. 

The whole idea of having pieces lined up against a wall is a mechanic that has never really been solved. ASL makes a good attempt at simulating who is at the wall versus who is in the street, but the system leads to what you would call an unusual situation.

On the other hand I don't think a tanker would get that close to infantry on his own. He might stand back and give up the protection of the stone wall. To be on the wall the PzIV would essentially drive to within 5 feet of the infantry and stop. Takes some bravery.
consensus_answer:
I would guess that the German tank still gets +2 TEM for being behind a stone wall even though he does not get the hull down benefit of Wall Advantage.
Wall Advantage is *not* required for Hulldown Status. As per B9.36, Hulldown applies whenever Wall TEM could apply. So the PzIV is Hulldown to Russian E, but not to Russian F. (And Russian F is Hulldown to the PzIV, but Russian E is not.)

This all seems fairly odd...
Partly this is a simplification for ease-of-play purposes. This same situation, if played on the large Deluxe ASL boards (2.2" hexes), would indeed have the PzIV claiming WA over the Russian tank, because in Deluxe ASL WA is claimed individually for each hexside, rather than for an entire hex at once.

I think that regular ASL was originally intended to work this way, but it proved impractical to keep track of WA on a hexside-by-hexside basis with the small regular hexes. Thus, the requirement that you can only claim WA if you can claim it for the entire hex keeps confusion to a minimum, but it does lead to some odd situations like this.

title: Simple AFV Combat Question
question:
Now it's the Defensive Fire Phase. I fire at the tank two hexes away. Because the enemy tank moved during this turn it is still considered a "moving target" even though it spent a MP to stop. Correct?
Yes. It remains a Moving Target until the end of the Player Turn.

So do I get no apply Case L Point Blank Range?
Case L will apply because the target is stopped; the fact that the target is still a Moving Target is irrelevant here. The target would have to be non-stopped or in Motion for Case L to be NA.

C.8 says that he is a "moving target" because he entered a new hex during the current turn? But does that make him a Motion target?
Nope... "in Motion" and "Moving Target" are two different things.

Case L does not apply to a Motion/Non-Stopped target/firer. The whole "moving", "Motion", "In-Motion", "Non-stopped" business seems very non-intuitive.
Yes, indeed it is. The unfortunate terminology used can be quite confusing.

Hi,

Unfortunately I don't have the page up with your answers in them, however I do believe you are incorrect on a few issues. 

 I will add what I said to another player here since it follows from your examples a bit- it was particularly talking about PBF episodes here. 

Pup Teevo wrote:
So do I get no apply Case L Point Blank Range?

Case L will apply because the target is stopped; the fact that the target is still a Moving Target is irrelevant here. The target would have to be non-stopped or in Motion for Case L to be NA.

Wrong./

summary (if AFV): If either the firer or recipient of fire has moved (changed hex) then PBF is not possible.

 
C.8 MOVING VEHICULAR TARGET: A vehicle is considered a moving target for To Hit/Effects purposes only if during the current Player Turn it has entered a new hex, or used VBM (D2.3), or began its MPh in Motion (D2.4), or is currently in Motion. A Stopped (D2.13) vehicle is also treated as moving if during the current Player Turn it has entered a new hex, used VBM, or began its MPh in Motion. Thus a Non-Stopped vehicle is a moving, Mobile (D.7) vehicle that has not expended a Stop MP (D2.13) since its last Start MP (D2.12) expenditure.

AS one can see this will be an extremely rare event against two AFV since one will almost certainly be moving or non- stopped.

 
PBF time.   It also seems to me that tanks that go adjacent to buildings with ATG in them also do NOT get PBF since the vehicle is moving/ in motion .

I am pretty sure you missed that,

replies.body:
As a former Tank Officer in the Marine Corps, here's how to think about this:

"Moving" targets get the DRM because you don't have as much time to spot them as you do a target that stays in one place the whole phase.  It's a function of the crew looking around for potential targets (when they're not tied up with other turret tasks, like operating intercoms/radios, getting out more ammo for the machine guns, and the like).  "Moving" targets provide fleeting opportunities to engagement them, but only fleeting, compared to other targets that sit stationary and never go anywhere at all.  

"Motion" targets are harder to put the gunsight reticle on them, apply the right "lead" to get a hit.  You can have a target that moved in the phase, making it harder to see in time to put the gunsight reticle on it, but when it's stopped, it's a lot easier to put the "crosshairs" (figuratively speaking) on the target.

A target that "Moved" in the movement phase and is still in Motion is the hardest of all to hit for the above reasons.  A target that "Moved" in the movement phase--giving you only a few seconds or a minute to see it, assess it, and engage it--but Stopped is a good bit easier, but not as easy as a target that sat there and never when anywhere.

Hopefully that explains this.
...except that non-stopped targets are easier to spot because they're in motion, which attracts the eye.

You'd think that would be the case--moving targets attract the eye.  Not always.  When I was in Fort Knox at armor school doing the ten day war, we had one instance when my tank completely drove by a moving enemy tank going in the opposite direction--both vehicles were less than fifty meters apart.  Over an open hill. Both the controllers up on the turret waved to each other.  We were so busy with our radios/intercoms/turret tasks on both tanks and the loaders, TCs, and drivers were just looking in the wrong direction.  Of course, we weren't really well trained crews at that point.  But it does illustrate something.  It can happen!  

But sure, such "one off" exceptions are a lousy basis for a rule.  

As one of the original ASLRB and BV playtesters, there was only so much "reality" we were willing to tolerate.  So much got abstracted--I know that's hard for many to believe. There was discussion about the "motion attracting the eye."  But then we got into endless arguments about how much benefit to grant to moving targets that spent their entire Movement Phase in LOS of the firing unit compared to a target that was stationary.  Then some of the playtesters wanted to split hairs over that issue regarding units that spent less than their full movement allowance moving in full view of the firer  It just got too contentious and we couldn't get any sort of agreement. So what did we do?  Tried to work that philosophy from the other end--DFF DRM as additional modifiers to Case J when the target spends 3 or less MP in the firer's LOS. That was the compromise that was reached at "AH Headquarters."  So, if you've got a moving vehicle that spends 4 MPs in the LOS of the firer, the same Case J +2 DRM applies as it does if it spends all of its MPs in the LOS of the firer.  I know that riles some people, but trying to add complexity just wan't seen as worth it (say, basing DRM on "thirds" or "quarters" of total MP allowance expended in LOS of the firer).  I don't know how many similar arguments Don Greenwood got from the other playtest groups, but you see the final result.  It works well enough for most cases, although admittedly not all (especially over open, billiard table flat desert with no scrub or other undulations in the terrain, as one example).  There so much of ASL that is like that.

("Pay no attention to that man behind the curtain." -- the Wizard of Oz)

If you come up with a house rule that works better, share it.  I know ASL aficionados hate home-brewed rules (and the community discourages it), but you never know; somebody might pick up on it and incorporate it as a SSR for a scenario or in a TPP....

You have my sympathies...there's no pleasing everyone on this. Most of my playing these days is Combat Mission (instead of VASL) and Combat Commander (instead of infantry-only ASL), although the latter is mainly due to opponent availability in Saskatoon.

Combat Mission is so good at the AFV modelling compared to board games that nothing comes close. Now if only they can eventually do all the early-war west front stuff...and let's hope the whole thing doesn't disintegrate with the CMX2.

My main ASL interest is being maintained by HASLs, which ASL still handles best.

title: Are FGs allowed for Snap Shot?
question:
I'm new to ASL and still trying to get the hang of reading the rules correctly.

When something like 8.15 SNAP SHOT, refers to "Any unit", are they:

a) Specifically trying to say that declaring a Snap Shot is only available to individual units (resolved one at a time).

b) Assuming you understand that Snap Shot is a form of DFF and DFF is a type of Fire Attack and thus Snap Shot can be taken by any single unit or any valid collection of units operating as a Fire Group.

I'm leaning towards 'b' but could also see the logic that said, given the small window of opportunity for a Snap Shot, it's executed every unit for themselves rather than as one large coordinated attack.
author: hodji
consensus_answer:
Between A7.55 and B8.15, I agree that choice b) is correct.

Kris

replies.body:
I don't see anything in the rules that would limit it from being a FG, but then again, I don't see anything specifically allowing it.

If all units participating in the FG have the same eligibility on the snap shot, I think it'd be legal.

In fact, I think if you're going to have multiple units/SW fire, which are in the same hex, then you'd fall into the A7.55 Mandatory FG rules.

Between A7.55 and B8.15, I agree that choice b) is correct.

Kris

b) is the answer I would give.
There is no explicit restriction in the rules that would prohibit a FG to snap shot - however, units in the same Location firing at the same target MUST form a FG and cannot fire separately.

I am in the 'b' group. "Any unit wishing..." means to me:

Unit A can fire snap shot.
Unit B can fire snap shot.
Or they can fire at the same time (i.e. FG)

Realistically, all the squads would have their arcs pointed out to them by their squad leaders if they were in position long enough ie defensive.  However you can imagine a platoon of 3 squads moving into a wood line or building and all the leaders shouting 'watch the roads', watch the woods path' or whatever.  When one or two guy would open up on a target they would shout (maybe just before firing) 'Enemy! crossing left street!.  Then the rest would follow. Plus any gunners would have tracer which would also help but we are only talking about 2 or 3 seconds so firepower is drastically decreased as per the rules.

:bd6-1::d6-1: 

It's dangerous to apply real-life logic to ASL rules.  Remember that it's a game and in many many cases it does not simulate what would have been done, but rather what works in game terms.
I have always played using option b ...whenever the situation warrants (which is rarely).

title: Residual Firepower Question
question: A unit is attacked by 4FP in a hex filled with (infantry placed) smoke.  Am I right in thinking that, if there are no other modifiers to the IFT roll, the 2 Residual FP counter that would normally be placed in the hex is negated by the +2 smoke modifier, with the end result that no Residual FP is placed in the hex?
author: Wiltshiresaint
consensus_answer:
Do Snipers activate on Res. FP attacks?

Yes - any non-OBA IFT DR qualifies.

JR

There you go.  It's probably beneficial to one player or the other to put it down.

This goes along with the concept of Snipers in the first place.  Are you obligated to down Res. FP?  If it is not beneficial to you (that is let's say the only way it can affect a unit is to roll your sniper) are you required to place it?

Snipers are my favorite rule.  If you roll your opponent's sniper and he doesn't notice it, are you obligated to point it out?  If so, then how can he prove it?  Maybe you didn't see it either?  And he didn't see it in the first place so how would he even know?

This is when you invoke the Banozic Sniper activation method.  That is, every time your opponent rolls a DR which is capable of activating the sniper, you yell out, "Sniper!".  Then the onus is on your opponent to disprove you, which is easy to do by just pointing at the dice.  But if you do this, no sniper will ever be missed.  Same thing could be said for ROF.

I guess my point is that laying Res. FP is always more beneficial to one of the players, not necessarily the Defender.  But as the Attacker you should be cognizant of this and make sure Res. FP is placed appropriately.

Someone asked in another thread how to get better at the game.  I think one way is to jump into these tiny details and understand them as deeply as possible.  In this instance we are kind of talking about player obligation and ethics, but still...  If  you want to learn the game you need to get real geeky about it.
