Nope.  It's halved to two (because residual FP always starts as half of the enacting FP), and that's it.  Residual FP is only reduced by effects from OUTSIDE the target hex.  Why?  Because effects INSIDE the target hex can be applied when the target is hit by the residual firepower.  This way you don't have to remember where the fire came from.   So, any unit entering the target hex would be attacked with a 2FP attack with a +2 DRM for smoke.  Normally this would be so unlikely to cause damage that I might not bother placing the counter, but if the scenario is really tight and a lucky roll might cause it to sway my way, I'll take what I can get.

Equally likely to end up as a 2+1 (since units may be using NAM) - which is not a worthless attack.

Are you obligated to down Res. FP?  If it is not beneficial to you (that is let's say the only way it can affect a unit is to roll your sniper) are you required to place it?

I'm pretty sure you have to put it down whether you want to or not:

8.2 RESIDUAL FIREPOWER: When a unit is attacked by Defensive First Fire/Subsequent First Fire/FPF, the target Location in which the attack is resolved (even if in Bypass) is marked with a Residual FP counter equal to half (up to a maximum of 12 after adjustment as per 8.26; FRD) of the highest IFT FP column used for that attack.

title: Snow!
question:
I'm a newb who's making his way through the ASL Starter Kits, so don't have the full rules yet but have a question.

We have our first real snowfall here in the south of England and walking around this morning I was thinking snow in ASL would potentially make troops easier to see (if not wearing camouflage), and maybe reduce movement allowances.  

Can anyone enlighten me (in general terms) on the impact of snow in ASL?
author: Wiltshiresaint
consensus_answer:
There's Deep Snow and Extreme Winter.
Thus the following rules sections will apply:

Deep Snow: E3.73x

Extreme Winter: E3.74x

The SSR doesn't specify that the roads are plowed or anything so should I just ignore the roads for all intents and purposes or do the roads still function at all?
Roads still exist, but you have to study E3.723, E3.733, and E3.7331 carefully to understand how it all works. I'm no expert on the snow rules, but it appears to me that, for example, a squad would pay 2 MF to enter a woods hex across a hexside that had no road, and 1.5 MF to enter a woods across an unplowed road hexside. (E3.733)

Hopefully someone with more experience in using the snow rules can either confirm this example, or correct me if I'm mistaken. I'm assuming that the .5 MF additional cost for crossing an unplowed road hexside would apply unless the squad chooses to ignore the road and pay the normal 2 MF to enter the woods.

There seems to be one shellhole on the map. Does it exists in Deep snow or not?
Shellholes are not mentioned in E3.73 or in E3.722 (invoked by E3.73), so I would assume that they still exist and play normally even under these conditions.

replies.body:
I'm a newb who's making his way through the ASL Starter Kits, so don't have the full rules yet but have a question.

We have our first real snowfall here in the south of England and walking around this morning I was thinking snow in ASL would potentially make troops easier to see (if not wearing camouflage), and maybe reduce movement allowances.  

Can anyone enlighten me (in general terms) on the impact of snow in ASL?

There are no penalties for *not* wearing winter camouflage in ASL, but if your troops *do* have winter camouflage (by SSR) they get some added benefits (they can advance and assault move in open ground without losing concealment, and are harder to hit at longer ranges).  

Falling snow can generate an 'LV Hindrance' to fire which gets progressively worse with range.

Ground snow freezes ponds, marshes and streams, makes it harder to dig in, and makes it more difficult for infantry and cavalry to change elevations (except inside buildings, of course).  Vehicles no longer enjoy the 1/2 MP road rate.

Deep snow muffles the effect of HE and minefield attacks, makes movement even harder for infantry, cav, and vehicles, and vehicles can bog if they leave a road.  Also, you can no longer use smoke except inside buildings.

There are also rules for extreme winter (vehicles and weapons are less reliable, Fate occurs on rally/morale check DRs of 11 or 12) and drifting snow (drifts create hexside terrain that acts like a wall but is more difficult to cross).

All of this is covered in the crazy carnival of Chapter E, and I recommend you read the relevant bits carefully should you ever venture outside in the cold in ASL.  The above is just an outline, but this being ASL there are always exceptions and special cases.  

After you've had a taste of snow, move on to the real gem of Chapter E:  Night!

JR

title: Vehicles in DFF (again)
question:
Hi Guys,

Steadily learning vehicles the hard way, straight from the monstrous tome itself rather than through the SKs.

I am really hazy on DFF and VCA/TCA changes. I notice rule D2.401 allows a "motion attempt" at any moment during your opponent's move. The rule doesn't say why you'd want to do that (a constant failing of the ASLRB, I"m finding - good at how, terrible at why/when you'd want to use a given rule). 

Here are my questions:

1) is a successful motion attempt required to allow VCA change in DPh/DFF? That is to say, does a NT vehicle NEED to make a succesful motion attempt to change its VCA in the Dph?

2) can a vehicle freely change its TCA in DPh/DFF, or does this also require a motion attempt?

Up til now we've played that a stopped/not-in-motion turreted vehicle can change its TCA freely in the DPh and apply case A, and thus far we haven't had a NT vehicle need to do it. However, I now realise that may be wrong. Help me BGG ASL Community, you're my only hope!

- Nick
author: Boots01
consensus_answer:
I am really hazy on DFF and VCA/TCA changes. I notice rule D2.401 allows a "motion attempt" at any moment during your opponent's move. The rule doesn't say why you'd want to do that (a constant failing of the ASLRB, I"m finding - good at how, terrible at why/when you'd want to use a given rule).
Hi, Nick. A motion attempt during your opponent's MPh is usually used so it's harder for the enemy AFV to hit you since the fact you're in motion will add the Case J +2 TH DRM. The rulebook does have it's faults, but in this case I think it's pretty clear why you'd want to make a motion attempt since D2.401 is immediately followed by D2.41: "TARGET CONSEQUENCES: Any Motion vehicle is eligible for the Case J To Hit (Motion Target) DRM when fired upon, regardless of fire phase."

Here are my questions:

1) is a successful motion attempt required to allow VCA change in DPh/DFF? That is to say, does a NT vehicle NEED to make a succesful motion attempt to change its VCA in the Dph?
Not exactly. If you make a successful motion attempt (again, to make it harder to get hit) then you are free to make VCA/TCA changes, per D2.401. But you can also change your VCA during your opponent's MPh or the DFPh by firing outside your VCA. Check out D2.11: "A VCA can also be changed following a successful Motion Attempt (2.401), as a result of firing outside its CA during any fire phase (other than its own Mph; C5.1), or at the end of any fire phase in which it is still eligible to fire a turret/bow-mounted weapon (3.12 and C3.22)."

However, remember that if you change your TCA or VCA to fire on an enemy, your TH DR will face the Case A DRMs depending on what kind of AFV you have and how many hexspines your shifting your CA. If you're just turning your turret, you face either a +1 or +2 for the first hexspine (depending on whether you have a fast- or slow-traverse turret) and +1 for each additional hexspine. If your AFV is non-turreted OR has a turret but elects to change the entire VCA instead (maybe because you want your stronger armor facing the enemy) it faces the +3 VCA change DRM for the first hexspine and +1 for each additional hexspine. Check out D5.11: "All Guns use Case A to fire at targets outside their current CA when changing their CA for a shot in that phase. Turreted vehicles change only their TCA so that their target lies within that TCA. Should they elect to pivot their vehicular counter instead so as to change their VCA, the NT To Hit DRM apply to the first shot of all vehicular weapons (see also D3.51)."

2) can a vehicle freely change its TCA in DPh/DFF, or does this also require a motion attempt?
I answered this question above: If you're firing on the enemy AFV, you don't need to make a successful motion attempt to change your TCA, but you will face the Case A TH DRMs.

Up til now we've played that a stopped/not-in-motion turreted vehicle can change its TCA freely in the DPh and apply case A, and thus far we haven't had a NT vehicle need to do it. However, I now realise that may be wrong. Help me BGG ASL Community, you're my only hope!
Well, you already know about Case A! I should have read your entire post before responding. So the NT vehicle would pay the +3/+1/+1 Case A DRMs for shifting its VCA during defensive first fire.

title: OBA - Conversion of SR to FFE:1 possible with no enemy units in/adjacent to SR hex?
question:
Situation as follows:

- Radio Contact maintained.
- Battery access.
- SR on board.
- Observer has LOS to ground level of SR-hex.
- No (enemy) units in/adjacent to SR-hex.

Question:

Is it possible to convert the SR to FFE:1 in place although there are no (enemy) units in/adjacent to the SR-hex?

The OBA flowchart states:

Does Observer have a LOS to the base level of the hex? 

If there are units in or adjacent to the SR hex, are all of them unknown to the Observer?

This seems to point rather to the question, if there are known and/or unknown units. But what if there are no units at all? Would there be an extra chit draw necessary?

As a background: In the previous Advance Phase, all enemy units advanced out of the potenital blast zone. Nevertheless, I would still like to convert the SR to FFE:1 to deny the enemy re-entry and to try to rubble a building and to possibly clear wire/mines.

Thanks for your help
author: von Marwitz
consensus_answer:
C1.33 to C1.337 (SR & FFE:1/2 options) does not (on my reading) expressly deal with the situation where you can see the SR but there are no enemy units (Known or otherwise) in the blast radius.

However, C1.21 (Battery Access) says this:

"... whenever Converting any SR/FFE:C to a FFE:1 ..., Battery Access must be attempted a second (ie an extra) time if >= one non-hidden enemy ground unit is in/adjacent-to the AR (or, when Converting, to the SR/FFE:C) counter's hex but none of those units are Known to the Observer ..."

So the way I see it, if the projected blast area is empty, you can convert without an extra Battery Access draw.  It is only if there are enemy units there which are not Known that the extra draw is required.

replies.body:
NRBH, but I think that with no enemy units in the blast zone, an extra chit draw would be required.
Edit: Nevermind.  See Rindis' explanation below for why the extra chit draw is not required unless there are enemy units the FO can't see.

NRBH, but I am almost positive you can convert to FFE:1 in place without an extra chit draw.

You have LOS to the base level of the hex, which allows you to convert it. There are no unknown enemy units in or adjacent to the SR hex, so no extra chit draw is necessary.

"... whenever Converting any SR/FFE:C to a FFE:1 ..., Battery Access must be attempted a second (ie an extra) time if >= one non-hidden enemy ground unit is in/adjacent-to the AR (or, when Converting, to the SR/FFE:C) counter's hex but none of those units are Known to the Observer ..."

So the way I see it, if the projected blast area is empty, you can convert without an extra Battery Access draw.  It is only if there are enemy units there which are not Known that the extra draw is required.

That sounds right.

The presumption is that if you're putting an FFE into an area that really is empty, there is presumably a good reason for it (choke point, etc...). But if you're putting it where there are units the observer can't see, then there's potential metagaming going on (the FO is acting on knowledge you have, but he doesn't), so you are punished with the extra chit draw.

I am with Brian on this one. The whole known, not known thing only comes in if there are units there. The idea is that if YOU the player see the pieces, but the OBSERVER does not, there should be some kind of penalty for using your omnicient observer, thus the extra chit draw.

Well, it seems that all of you think it conversion from SR to FFE:1 with no units in the blast-area to be under the described circumstances is possible.

Thanks for helping me out.

Best regards
von Marwitz
Another "realism" possibility is that the unknown units could be friendlies....  But if there's nothing there-- fire away!

title: Couple o questions from a recent game.
question:
Me and a friend are currently learning to use vehicles and all the fun that brings but during our current game (Counterattack on the Vistula) we ran into a few probs.

1) Can a vehicle move past another vehicle (through the same hex), and can this be done on a forested road?

2) When an inf unit bailsout of a truck that has been eliminated does the dm MMG they are carrying need to roll for malfunction, and if so how do you represent it as having malfunctioned. (we just made a note and replaced the dm MMG with a malfunctioned MMG).

author: bluetiger80
consensus_answer:
1) Yes, at +1 MP per wreck or vehicle, doubled if on any kind of road, and doubled again for woods, sunken road, and elevated road.  (B4, B5, B13, D2.14, and D10)

2) If an AFV rider bails out, any SW possessed are lost if it breaks before/during/after bailing out. (D6.24)

If passengers survive the destruction of their transport, any SW they possess survive with them, and do not need to roll for malfunction. (D6.9)

(There are malf counters that you can put on dm SW to indicate their condition - they're usually only used if an assembled malfed weapon is dm for transport.)

D9.3 Wrecks give a +1 TEM for infantry in the same Location (with some exceptions), and
D9.4 A wreck is +1 hindrance for fire through but not into or out of a wreck hex.

title: A couple of questions about MGs, and the campaign game.
question:
Hey Guys,

Well, I'm really enjoying learning to play ASL, but alas it has stolen my time off from work.

Given I'm now entering the last days of my extended break, I was planning on trying out the shorter Valour of the Guards campaigns whilst I've got the time. I'm relatively new to the game, so I'm just asking if you've got any tips or advice about rules that are commonly missed/mistaken, or just generally?

Second, I've a couple of questions about MGs, which I hope you can help me with:

I seem to remember (along with my opponent) that MMGs and HMGs cannot fire if moved that turn, but in one of my cursory re-reads of the MG section, I can't find where it says this. It's not in the Assault Phase section either, so have we just invented this rule whole-cloth, or is it hidden somewhere in the book..?

Also, I'm having trouble deciphering the rules about the ability of HMGs to take down vehicles - and I fear I've got them very confused. Am I right in thinking that they simply cannot take down armoured vehicles, but can take down an unarmored vehicle by firing as ordinance, and then rolling under the number on the 'star' row of their IFT column?
author: savantt
consensus_answer:
I seem to remember (along with my opponent) that MMGs and HMGs cannot fire if moved that turn, but in one of my cursory re-reads of the MG section, I can't find where it says this. It's not in the Assault Phase section either, so have we just invented this rule whole-cloth, or is it hidden somewhere in the book..?Here is the rule :

A4.41 AFPh SW FIRE LIMITS: No MMG, HMG, mortar, INF/RCL SW, or 5/8" non-vehicular ordnance counter which moved [other than being Recovered (4.44)] during the MPh may fire during the ensuing AFPh [EXC: German dm MMG/HMG may fire as LMG; 9.8]. However, if such weapons remained stationary while their new owners moved into their Location, they can be fired during the ensuing AFPh with the normal penalties for fire in the AFPh—assuming they were Recovered during that MPh (4.44). A weapon fired during the AFPh cannot use Intensive Fire and is limited to one shot regardless of its ROF [EXC: if using Opportunity Fire; 7.25].

Also, I'm having trouble deciphering the rules about the ability of HMGs to take down vehicles - and I fear I've got them very confused. Am I right in thinking that they simply cannot take down armoured vehicles, but can take down an unarmored vehicle by firing as ordinance, and then rolling under the number on the 'star' row of their IFT column?
vs armored, an MG (whether LMG, MMG or HMG or vehicle MA MG) uses the TH-TK process.
vs unarmored, it uses the IFT's * line.

A9.6 VEHICULAR TARGETS: The process for resolution of MG fire vs vehicular targets is dependent on whether the vehicle Target Facing/Aspect is armored or not. If the Target Facing is armored, such fire is resolved on the AP To Kill Table after securing a hit on the To Hit Table; otherwise it is resolved on the * Vehicle line of the IFT and no To Hit DR is necessary. A non-captured MG To Hit DR always uses the black To Hit numbers regardless of nationality when firing as ordnance.
9.61 explains further the processes used.
Note that any cause of halving the MG's fire prohibits it from firing as ordnance (e.g. an LMG that has moved during the AFPh).

Hope that helped.

Ted,

Robin's post mentioned this in the example he gave, but I thought it worth pointing out more directly:  all (non vehicular*) MGs (not just HMGs) can fire To Hit / To Kill vs AFVs in normal range.

title: Prisoners and Leadership
question: Does a prisoner benefit from the guard's leadership modifier when taking a morale check?
author: drmark64
consensus_answer:
Well, I can't find any rule that addresses this question.

A10.7 specifies that a leadership modifier affects the performance of other Personnel in the leader's location without actually excluding enemy Personnel or prisoners (and prisoners are Personnel as defined in ASL).

But, my guess is that the answer to your question is "No":

Prisoners never suffer a LLTC/LLMC if a leader is broken/eliminated in their location (A20.54). My thinking is, if they are exempt from the potential penalty of the leadership modifier (LLTC/LLMC), then they should also be exempt from the benefits of the leadership modifier as well.

It's also unclear how you would even apply a leadership modifier to a prisoner. Leadership is reduced in effectiveness for Allied troops of a different nationality (A10.7), so would leadership also be reduced for prisoners, who are definitely a different nationality?

title: Is exchanging SW counted as action ?
question:
Hi all,

  If a leader receives a SW from another good order unit in the same hex, is he still legible for rallying broken units in that RPh? It's a questions against 4.431, which is very unclear to me.

  Thanks.
author: hhuu
consensus_answer:
I don't believe a Ldr is required for transfer of SWs between units, is he?
Correct. Two units in the same location may transfer a weapon between themselves without the presence of a leader. The only requirement for a transfer is that both units involved be in Good Order and unpinned. (A4.431)

If the transfer takes place in the RPh, then the "one action per unit per RPh" restriction also applies to both units. For example, a unit that attempts to recover a weapon in the RPh could not participate in a transfer in the same RPh.

Note that the Attacker may also conduct transfers at the start of the APh. (Step 7.11A of the ASOP)

If not, then is it that he's occupied recieving a SW *himself* (or transfering from himself), that counts as an action and prevents him then from rallying?
Right. If a leader gives a weapon that he's carrying to another unit, or receives a weapon from another unit, that's his one allowed action for that RPh. As long as he is not personally involved in a transfer (or any of the other listed RPh actions) he is free to rally broken units.

title: ASL Noob Has Questions?
question:
Armor Leaders and ELR are not explicitly written down, but the info is there in the rules. For ELR replacement, the rules say:

A19.13 REPLACEMENT An unbroken Personnel unit which fails an MC by and amount > its ELR is immediately Replaced by a broken Personnel unit of lesser quality but the same size.

According to A19.11:

 All crew-types, Commissars, heroes, unarmed and already broken units are never subject to Replacement due to ELR failure

Now, the definition of "personnel" in the Index is:

All SMC and MMC counters, including those mounted as Cavalry or Passengers/Riders, but excluding inherent crews since they are not in counter form.

Note the word "inherent", for in the section relating to Armor Leaders, it says:

D3.41 An Armor Leader is considered inherently present in the particular AFV his owner assigns him to...

and further more:

D3.43 An Armor leader affects only its own vehicle/crew (even a captured vehicle) and ceases to exist once the crew takes counter form. Should that particular vehicular crew reoccupy a vehicle, the Armor Leader will once again exist in that vehicle.

Now, since by definition, an Armor Leader is not personnel, then he is not subject to ELR Replacement. This is reinforced by the fact that inherent crews are explicitly excluded and the Armor Leader is part of an inherent crew according to D3.43.
consensus_answer:
What is the ELR if none is specified in a scenario?

According to the rule book:

A19.1 EXPERIENCE LEVEL RATING (ELR) ... Each scenario OB will list an ELR for that group of units as a number ranging from 0 to 5.

By the rules, if the ELR isn't listed, there isn't one - except for certain units which have ELR 5 by definition. I would assume that you would simply not use section A19 for that scenario.

Can an infantry unit advance directly under a foxhole from an adjacent hex during the advance phase? Into a shellhole? A pillbox? A cave?

Yes to foxhole and shellhole, because they are not separate locations.

No to pillbox and cave because they are separate locations. Entering them from another hex involves entering two separate locations, so cannot be done in the Advance phase.

title: Targeting Buildings for Deliberate Rubbling - harder to hit a bldg than a vehicle?
question:
I have researched this fairly welland am pretty unhappy with what I found...hopefully someone here can tell me that I got it wrong. I'm reconstructing this from memory so I apologize for being unable to cite the text verbatim.

Sometimes if the gun is big enough you just want to level the building...never mind targeting the squads inside.

1) In the discussion of target types under multiple targets (weird place for it) the rules state that a player can use the infantry target type to target a building (among other things) even when there is no personnel there...but it doesn't say if you still have to use the TEM to score a hit 

2) In the notes to I believe sction B for TEM it says something like 'stone buildings aren't harder to hit than wooden buidlings, but it's harder to place an effective shot'...OK so the concept is there in the rules if only in the notes

Why should it be easier to hit a Mark IV than the multi-story building behind it? If I just want to hit a stone building and try to rubble it to I have to use a TEM of +3 (a '5' at a range 0-6) to try to hitit or just an '8' since I'm not trying to hit a target withing the building?

This becomes even more unpalatable when one has to use the direct fire rules for an air attack...is it really easier to drop a bomb on a AFV than on a big honking building? I really have to get a '5' or less to attack a squad in a stone building with a stuka? 

What if I don't want to target the squad but just want to try and level the building? You can't really target a squad with a bomb if they're in a building...not in the 40s anyway

Area target type for this is particularly unsatisfying. 1) it doesn't help much in the to hit process 2) if you hit your chances of rubbling are greatly reduced.

Please tell me I'm missing something here. ASL is so specific in so many instances...how could it be so off the mark in such a basic question?
author: mettiksvetik
consensus_answer:
I think B24.11 covers the rubble creation process fairly well while C3.41 only adds in some confusion by implying that you can target a building. I wonder if there was ever any errata or clarification of C3.41?

Well, add to that rule 6.5 Case N; Acquired Target. It says that a Gun that fires at a Known unit or a bridge may get acquisition.

So I guess a bridge can be specifically targeted, so a building could also be targeted. C3.41 is clear in both bridges and buildings.

replies.body:
Why should it be easier to hit a Mark IV than the multi-story building behind it? If I just want to hit a stone building and try to rubble it to I have to use a TEM of +3 (a '5' at a range 0-6) to try to hitit or just an '8' since I'm not trying to hit a target withing the building?

To rubble the building, you have to hit a target within the building: You have to hit a so important structural part that the buliding is sufficenty destroyed to become rubble. Such a part may be more difficult to hit that a vechicle, despite the fact that the building itself is easy to hit.

I am checking the procedure for targeting a building. It is something I have never considered. The rules makes it pretty clear that such  a thing is possible [C3.41]. To target a building you must use the infantry target type or the area target type. So you have that correct.

This is unfortunate as the rules are silent as far as I can tell about where to proceed from there. It sounds like your interpretation is reasonable.

Apparently this has come up before. Here is a link to a thread where no real conclusion was reached.

http://forums.gamesquad.com/showthread.php?72246-Rubble-Question&highlight=targeting+bridge

You can always fire on an empty location. The usual reason to do this is to gain Acquisition on a Location that the enemy may wish to move into (say, an unoccupied Victory Location).

C6.2 is fairly clear: you must add Case K to hit HIP/Concealed targets. If there are no units in a Location, there is no Case K. If there are HIP units in the Location, they are only subject to an effects roll (with its potential for revealing them) if it hit is gained while applying Case K. If there are concealed and Known units present, Case K applies to the concealed ones. If there are non-hidden/concealed units present that are not Known to the firer, Case K applies (this usually only happens when a MTR fires on a multi-level building, and there are units in Locations not in LOS of the firer).

In the case of an empty building, it is just like any other shot, and there is no Case K. Note that if the only possible result of a die roll is Sniper Activation, the roll is not made. So an effects die roll is only made if the Gun can rubble the Location. Also note, that you cannot gain Acquisition if there is no Known enemy target. So it is also best to use ATT unless you're close enough to get range bonuses to get better than the normal 8TH (+2/3 TEM). Also note using ATT, that any type of building is just as easy to hit, the stone building is just more resistant to rubbling (TEM applies to the effect instead of the TH).

I recently did this in a game I'm playing on VASL.  I used ATT to acquire the building hex so that a unit would not be able to gain a good vantage point after skulking out of the hex during movement phase.  I got ROF and slapped down my -2acq, but didn't actually rubble the building.  

It would be REALLY hard to rubble a building with an HE charge, especially a stone one.  Like Harald said above, you'd have to hit an interior support beam, and those old European buildings had some big-ass beams!

I think B24.11 covers the rubble creation process fairly well while C3.41 only adds in some confusion by implying that you can target a building. I wonder if there was ever any errata or clarification of C3.41?

Well, add to that rule 6.5 Case N; Acquired Target. It says that a Gun that fires at a Known unit or a bridge may get acquisition.

So I guess a bridge can be specifically targeted, so a building could also be targeted. C3.41 is clear in both bridges and buildings.

I appreciate your informed responses. I would guess that many of you are tournament players and I am confident these interpretations are reliable for tournament play.

I don't play in tournaments. In fact I live on the shores of Lake Victoria thousands of miles away from the nearest tournament and only play with my son...so I'm going to go ahead and do something very verboten. I'm going to say what I think a good house rule is and see what you guys think, not in terms of what IS, but rather what SHOULD BE...because the current rules just don't pass the smell test for me concerning this particular detail. 

My proposed home rule is the to hit for a terrain feature is an unmodified infantry target type. That is to say...an 8 to hit either a stone or wooden building. 8 is still less than 10, taking into consideration the abstractions of critical structural components. The IFT die roll against the building would be full value and clean (no halving or TEM except the +1 dr for stone). The effect against any infantry in the structure would be area fire with the ordinary TEM.

The argument that you have to have a target to roll on the IFT doesn't hold water for me because using the same logic demo charges wouldn't be able to attack buidlings or bridges unless there was some token 'target' there...and that's just dumb. It's too...gamey. And ASL is supposed to be a premier tactical SIMULATION.

I also kind of wish they would bring back the old SL near miss rule (not the ordnance ASL rule)...because a 150 shell or 500kg bomb has to go somewhere. The whole idea of having a stuka divebomb a crowded mapboard area, miss it's die roll and have NO EFFECT AT ALL...that's stupid. Bombs have to land somewhere. Something like an artillery drift roll with the bomb resolved as area fire seems appropriate.

OK...flame away.:p

Maybe ASL compatible products (critical hit, heat of battle) are my answer. I've never bought any but I know some of them introduce 'grudge rules' that apply only to their particular product... is anyone aware of an ASL comp peoduct that addresses this issue?

None of the issues you brought up are in a third party grudge rule that I am aware of. The game can be quite gamey as it is a game. How hard is it to topple a structure with an HE round? It is hard to answer that accurately. If your opponent is willing to play house rules have at it. I'd be willing to play by your house rules for a free room in the guest quarters on Lake Victoria. :D

NOT ASL, but in the same family:

Squad Leader later modules allow you to target the building, and the taller it is, the easier it is to target.  The DRM that would normally apply to the To Hit DR applies instead to the To Kill DR.  KIA rubbles the building.

Obviously, they changed this for ASL, but did not really think it through...

title: Tanks in motion firing in DFF
question:
I've just upgraded to ASL from the SKs, and I never got SK #3. I'm at my wits' end trying to sort out the intricacies of the five versions of Case C during DFF.

Let's say I have a tank under a motion counter, and it's my opponent's turn. For argument's sake, let's say it doesnt' have gyostabilizers, and it has a fast traverse turret. replies.body:

Of cases C, C1 or C2, which is applicable?  It doesn't say to "apply" the case, merely use the one that is appropriate.  Case C is used all the time.  Cases C1 and C2 are only used if you are expending MP, which you are not.

So, to do the math, 

Case C4 is consulted, which uses Case C, which refers upwards to Case B and is +2 for a fast turret.  Case B is +2 +2.

So your modifiers for the shot are +4 and you must double the lower dr.

Other common firer based DRM are Case I (+1 for BU) and of course Case A if you must change your CA.

There are 4 statuses to describe the current mobile-ness of a tank.  Moving, Stopped, Non-Stopped and Motion.  They all have very specific definitions and apply at very specific phases during a turn.  Some can coexist, others can't.  One tip is that Non-Stopped and Motion basically mean the same thing.  Non-Stopped applies during the unit's MPh.  And Motion applies in all other phases.  Moving is a bit trickier.  And Stopped is there so... well, you can stop.  But you can be Stopped and Moving at the same time.  But you can never be Non-Stopped and in Motion.  It's basic physics  (hehe, that was a joke).

Find the article about this somewhere.  It is quite informative and imperative for understanding how vehicles work in ASL.  And once it clicks, it all makes sense.

Rule D2.42 points me to rule C5.35, case C4. That states that in the vehicles' MPh, I must add an applicable Case C DRM, as well as double the lowest die (as I have no gyrostabilizers).

I'm following so far.

QUESTION 1: Does rule D2.42 supercede the advice in Rule C5.35 that Case C4 only applies in the vehicle's MPh? In other words, does Case C4 apply even though it's my DPh? (For the record, I think the answer is 'yes')

There is errata that tells us to delete "in the MPh" from C5.35. That fixes the problem. So yes Case C4 does apply.

Rule C5.35 also directs you to apply Case C, C1 or C2 to the shot. Since it is my DPh, I have not expended any MP at all, so what the hell do I do? Apply Case C, for a total of +2 DRM and a turret DRM of a further +2? Apply Case C2, as I have spent no MP at all this player turn, for a DRM of +2, +2 turret DRM, +2 for Case C2?

Case C1 and C2 are specific to the MPh, so they don't apply. So you are applying Case C which is Case B(+2) and  Case C (+2 fast traverse) for a total of +4 with the lower dr x 2.

Just Case C.

No, I think you were reading the rules very closely. Much more so than most of us and that bit that the errata was fixing threw you off.

title: Moving vs expending MF
question:
1. If an ATTACKER SQ in OG does not declare AM and then expends 2 MF to deploy smoke and it gets first fired by this MF expenditure (with clear LOS), does the DEFENDER get FFNAM/FFMO modifiers?

2. Further, everywhere in the ASLRB where there is a rule about "moving", is MF expending always considered a form of "moving" or must the Infantry units really move from a Location to another to be considered "moving"?

If you know the answers, could you please indicate the specific rules? 

Thanks!

Edit: spelling.
author: esparver73
consensus_answer:
A4.2 Whenever a player moves a unit during his MPh he states alound the MF expended by that unit in entering each hex or in performing any other activity within its current hex.

So activities that spend MF are "moving" - throwing smoke, picking up a SW, going into a foxhole.

A4.61 Assault Movement, if it is to be used, must be declared prior to movement of that unit,

So, to answer your questions;

1. If you do not declare AM and the expend 2MF - you are moving (per A4.2) and not AM (per A4.61) so yes, you will receive the FFNAM modifier (and the FFMO modifier if you are in open ground).

SIDEBAR - if you are successful with your smoke - that can negate the FFMO modifier, and you will receive the smoke hindrance as well for the FF shot.

2. See A4.2. MF expending is "moving"

Hope that helps,
Dan

2: I think I might want some more particular examples of what you're talking about. But, in general, any MF expenditure is something that can be reacted to (i.e., fired upon). Placing smoke, Recovering SW, Searching, are all activities that can be fired upon. (So is Pushing a Gun, which may or may not involve movement....)

title: D 6.64
question:
In regards to this rule can a carrier/halftrack form a multi-location FG or can they only form a multi-unit single-hex FG? Based off reading the rule I think it is the latter but I wanted some clarification.

Cheers,
Josh
author: j23flo
consensus_answer:
Multi-hex is allowed (unless Passengers/Riders are also firing)  

D6.64
In all cases, the normal rules for FG (A7.5-.55) still apply.

A7.5
A FG may consist of units from more than one Location only if each participating unit occupies a Location ADJACENT to another participating unit of the same FG.

Why would passengers/riders also firing matter?

CE halftrack paasengers may FG normally. Other passengers are restricted to firing with other passengers of the same vehicle and with the vehicles non-MA (unless it is IFE capable) armament. Riders may only FG with other same-vehicle riders and the AAMG of that vehicle.

Cheers,
Josh

title: Shooting at a target inside smoke. Does residual FP shift to the left or not?
question:
I've always played that when shooting at a target inside smoke, then residual FP shifts left by the amount of DRM that smoke provides. But I just realized that Residual rules (A8.26) says that only conditions outside target location affects the residual FP. Is it really true that the smoke doesn't lower it?

Or is it handled so that when the unit enters in that residual, that smoke DRM is then added to that residual attack?
author: Hipsu
consensus_answer:
No.

Only when firing through smoke.  Any subsquent attacks by the RF are modified by the smoke dr mod. and that is where the impact comes...

Now if we are talking about firelanes, it's different.  no left-shift and no dr mod impact either.  That's one of the things that makes Firelines useful.

title: Does a squad with Underlined Morale get replaced with a Disrupted HS if it rolls boxcars and exceeds ELR?
question:
Rules say that:
- Boxcars on a morale check leads to Casualty reduction
- A squad with Underlined Morale gets replaced with two HS if it exceeds ELR (5)
- A HS with Underlined Morale is Disrupted if it exceeds ELR.

If both happens to a squad, is it first casualty reduced to 1 HS which is then disrupted?

OR

Is it first split into 2 HS and then one of them is eliminated leaving 1 non-disrupted HS?
author: Hipsu
consensus_answer:
ASLRB is pretty clear here.

A10.31 Casualty MC: If an unbroken Personnel unit rolls an Original 12 during a MC, it suffers Casualty Reduction and is broken (or eliminated if not subject to breaking)...after any unit Replacement which may also be required by ELR Failure (19.13). If a broken unit rolls an Original 12 during a MC, it is eliminated. See D5.341 for Inherent Crews.

So it breaks into 2 HS, then 1 HS is eliminated.  Thats the way I see it.

title: Half Track FG with leader, MP cost of woods and dismantling SW
question:
I have a game in an hour so I'm gonna ask these fast (and hopefully get answers fast :P)

1. Can a CE leader in Half-Track direct a multihex firegroup? (I assume no, but have a feeling I heard somewhere he could)

2. Fully Tracked tank enters Woods. I think it costs 1/2 total MP but why does the Terrain chart lists ALL (as well as note Z: half total MP)?

3. If I dismantle an SW in PFPh, can I move it right away in MPh or is it somehow considered under Prep Fire marker and thus cannot move yet?
author: Hipsu
consensus_answer:
Mantling and dismantling a SW counts as usage of the SW, so the unit will be marked with the appropriate fire marker.

So no move then? That's harsh.

To number 1...

The leader in question can only direct fire from units in the same Location, just like any other leader.  This leader could take part in a multi-Location firegroup as long as all the Locations had a leader of equal or better leadership rating.

So a leader in a half-track in OG with a squad in that hex could direct a FG of the squad plus the half-track AAMG, for example.

Can't he direct infantry in his own hex? I thought that was the one advantage of halftracks. Doesn't D6.65 say something like.. a leader cannot direct units in his hex if the HT has moved implying that he COULD direct if the HT has not moved?

D6.65 says:

The leadership modifier of any CE (or otherwise exposed to fire) leader Passenger may be used to direct the fire of other Passengers in that halftrack (including their use as a FG).

Halftrack FG rule is D6.64 which says that armored halftracks can be part of FG using other halftracks and Infantry (note "armored") and their Passengers can be part of these FG.

Carrier Passengers are limited to FG within the Carrier.

title: ASL Machinegun Firelanes Question.
question:
I don't see any examples in the 1st ED. RB where you can take the shot and also lay down a firelane - I was assuming the firelane would be placed seperately from the shot.
A Fire Lane is basically just a fancy form of Residual Firepower. Just like a normal Resid, you take a DFire shot first and the Resid or Fire Lane is what's left behind. It doesn't take any kind of separate action to make the Fire Lane. You just declare it as an option with your DFire.

I don't know how the 1st edition rules were different here, though I understand Fire Lanes were one of the sections that changed significantly. So it's hard for me to comment on exactly what you're reading or thinking. I'm sure someone else will come by with a better explanation.
consensus_answer:
can a Firelane be laid down without actually firing at a unit?Only during Night.

E1.71 FIRE LANE: At night, a Fire Lane Residual FP counter can be placed beyond the firer's NVR although the firer must still have a LOS to the moving initial target. [EXC: Once any starshell/IR has been fired, a MG can place a Fire Lane without firing at any moving target if it can place a Fire Lane Residual FP counter in a Location that is Bore Sighted by that MG; however, if it does so it must thereafter place (if otherwise able to do so) a Fire Lane to that Location in every enemy MPh (and must do so before the ATTACKER begins moving his first unit in that MPh) until the start of an enemy MPh in which it can see a Known enemy unit. The firer must make an IFT DR to check for malfunction/cowering/SAN. Once that MG's Bore Sighting advantage has been lost, it cannot thereafter use this Bore Sighted type of Fire Lane.]

title: Residual FP
question: A squad with 4 FP defensive first fires at a concealed enemy squad moving in open ground. You still place a 2 FP RFP marker in the hex right?
author: grahamj
consensus_answer:
Under what situation would this be possible?  Wouldn't a unit moving in open ground with LOS to the enemy lose their concealment anyway?

I should have worded it this way. 
The RFP is reduced because the target was concealed but why would it be reduced for a non-concealed unit that enters that same hex/location? The RFP should be determined by the firepower of the firing unit not the firepower subjected to by the concealed target (if you know what I mean)
A squad with 4 FP is putting 4 FP into the targeted hex but because the target itself is concealed, it (the concealed unit) is only subject to 2 FP although 4 FP is still present and ending up in the targeted hex resulting in 1 RFP 
Here is a poor example: I throw 4 tennis balls at someone but because that person I am throwing them at is crawling (concealed) on the ground, he only gets hit by 2 of them (RFP = 1 tennis ball). In effect there are still 4 tennis balls being thrown into that location. So anyone entering that same location that is not crawling on the ground would be subject to at least 2 tennis balls (1/2 x FP or 1/2 x 4 tennis balls) not 1 based on the first target's status.

In effect there are still 4 tennis balls being thrown into that location. So anyone entering that same location that is not crawling on the ground would be subject to at least 2 tennis balls (1/2 x FP or 1/2 x 4 tennis balls) not 1 based on the first target's status.

It's just the way I see it, RFP should be based on the originating fire's FP not the FP a target has been subjected to, but then again, to each his own.Note that, in the case of a unit firing vs a concealed target, it is using "area fire", which means that it is much more "spread out" than if it were aiming at a more precise target.
So the originating fire's FP is actually the half of the printed FP (otherwise, one should reduce the RF of a unit using PBF, to "stick" to the printed FP).
The printed FP is actually a relative element, a base of calculation.

I would say that you are making a difference between the "originating fire's FP" and the "FP a target has been subject to".
But the FP a target has been subject to is actually the FP that originated from the firer...

Note, too, that if another concealed unit enters the RF Location, it would be strange that it recieved the same amount of FP than the first (main) concealed target.

Remember too, that RF has no "memory" of its origin.

It is a game mechanic which tries to attenuate the non simultaneous movement of units.

RF is not another shot of the firing unit, but the "lead flying around" when a unit fires on a given target.
If a unit fires upon a concealed target, it sprays its fire much more...

BTW, an assault moving concealed unit loses concealment (if in non Open Ground) only if a PTC (or worse) result is rolled.

It's just the way I see it, RFP should be based on the originating fire's FP not the FP a target has been subjected to, but then again, to each his own.

As Mark said above, it doesn't matter what you think should happen. The rules are clear that the highest FP column used in the attack is the basis for residual, not the actual FP of the unit.

title: Defensive First Fire
question:
If a squad moves into a building and an enemy squad decides to defensive first fire at it, what is the correct procedure?

1.  place a First Fire counter on the squad after the first shot

2.  place a First Fire counter on the squad after the second shot since the enemy unit spent 2 MFs to enter the building and so may be fired twice.
author: grahamj
consensus_answer: After the first shot, place FF. After the second shot, flip the FF counter over to the SFF side. Note that the second shot has the further requirements and restrictions of SFF (normal range, no farther than closest enemy, half FP, etc).

replies.body: After the first shot, place FF. After the second shot, flip the FF counter over to the SFF side. Note that the second shot has the further requirements and restrictions of SFF (normal range, no farther than closest enemy, half FP, etc).
The answer is "1". But you may SFF that unit immediately because it has spent 2MF in that hex,
The answer is also "1a" - place Final Fire if it cowers after the first shot.

title: Bridges, Tank's MG armament and Hull Down questions

Couple days ago we played T2 Puma Prowls which was our first game with tanks.

My head still hurts...

Anyways.. some questions arose (suprise)

1. A bridge and a strange bypass move :)

When the Russian tank moves to the bridge it can of course continue to J1. But what if it doesn't want to. Can it move to J2? I don't remember what the movement cost is to move into a building but I mean can it move there from the bridge or must it continue moving along the road? This slight confusion comes from
"B6.1 Bridges usable by vehicles always connect directly to any adjacent road to which the bridge depiction points, and are considered extension of that road."

Does that mean the the vehicle must move to the road hex (J1 in this case) and nowhere else?

Finally the red line... bear with me..
Could the tank start bypassing the house by the right side by first going to the Vertex J1/J2/K2, change VCA there, and continue down from there? So it would never have to move to the LOS of Puma?

2. Hull Down
Is Hull Down something that happens automatically any time a tank is behind a wall, or is it something that must be claimed and must the tank be stopped or can it be moving (or in motion or whatever)?

Here a Russian tank is just cruising along the road. Is it automatically Hull Down to Puma?

Also

Are both tanks Hull Down or only the first tank there, claiming it?

3. Tanks in same hex
So this is the situation. My Puma has plenty of MP left

I'm planning to move through the Russian tank to V7 and shoot it in the rear. If I move to the same hex with enemy tank, what exactly happens? Or what are the Russian tank's options? Especially since it hasn't fired it's CMG yet? (Although I told my opponent to save his CMG until I get in his rear so he could shoot and change his VCA in the process (which he did but I still had plenty of MP to get to his rear again)).

Anyways, what if he shoots in the same hex. What modifiers does he get (in addition to buttoned up, moving target and intensive fire)?

What if his Turret was pointing to the right and I moved to his hex from left. Must he change his TCA even if I'm in his hex?

Does he retain Acquired Target in the same hex? What about when I move past him to V7?

Something else?

4. And what about that CMG....
I never found a good summary about all the modifiers that applies to tank's MGs in different situations..

The IFT only lists motion/bounding first fire as 1/2 FP but surely there are more to this...

Where's the +2 protection for the CE crew? It's not on the IFT or I'm blind.

Doesn't it matter if the opponent tank is moving? Isn't it harder to hit?

Is there PBF or TPBF ever?

Cower?

Back to question 3. What if that CMG fired when the Puma was in the same hex? What are all the modifiers?

That's it for now I think.
Tanks :)
author: Hipsu
consensus_answer:
1. A bridge and a strange bypass move 
When the Russian tank moves to the bridge it can of course continue to J1. But what if it doesn't want to. Can it move to J2?
No, you have to cross a road hexside when entering or leaving a bridge (B6.4).

2. Hull Down
Is Hull Down something that happens automatically any time a tank is behind a wall, or is it something that must be claimed and must the tank be stopped or can it be moving (or in motion or whatever)?
A vehicle behind a wall always has HD status if the +2 Wall TEM would otherwise apply (D4.21), so even a moving/Motion vehicle can have HD status when it is behind a wall.

Gaining HD status from a Height Advantage is not automatic, however (D4.22).

Here a Russian tank is just cruising along the road. Is it automatically Hull Down to Puma?
Yes.

Are both tanks Hull Down or only the first tank there, claiming it?
Wall Advantage applies, so only one of the two vehicles would have HD status.

3. Tanks in same hex
I'm planning to move through the Russian tank to V7 and shoot it in the rear. If I move to the same hex with enemy tank, what exactly happens? Or what are the Russian tank's options? Especially since it hasn't fired it's CMG yet? (Although I told my opponent to save his CMG until I get in his rear so he could shoot and change his VCA in the process (which he did but I still had plenty of MP to get to his rear again)).

Anyways, what if he shoots in the same hex. What modifiers does he get (in addition to buttoned up, moving target and intensive fire)?
Also Case E, fire within hex, +2. Note that Case L will *not* apply.

What if his Turret was pointing to the right and I moved to his hex from left. Must he change his TCA even if I'm in his hex?
Yes (C5.51).

Does he retain Acquired Target in the same hex? What about when I move past him to V7?
Yes to both, because you have not moved out of his LOS.

4. And what about that CMG....
I never found a good summary about all the modifiers that applies to tank's MGs in different situations..

The IFT only lists motion/bounding first fire as 1/2 FP but surely there are more to this...
Bounding (First) Fire: x 1/2 FP (D3.31)
Motion/Non-Stopped: x 1/2 FP (D2.42)

So, if a moving AFV fires its MGs, they fire at 1/2 FP if the AFV is Stopped; if the AFV is non-Stopped, they fire at 1/4 FP.
(1/2 x 1/2)

Where's the +2 protection for the CE crew? It's not on the IFT or I'm blind.
D5.31 (it is not on the IFT).

Doesn't it matter if the opponent tank is moving? Isn't it harder to hit?
Not when you're firing on the IFT with small arms (D2.41).

Is there PBF or TPBF ever?
Yes, as normal.

Cower?
Vehicular MGs never cower.

Back to question 3. What if that CMG fired when the Puma was in the same hex? What are all the modifiers?
FP x3 for TPBF, +2 DRM.

title: Bridge TEM question
question:
The RB states that unhindered fire against unit(s) on a Bridge that crosses only the road depiction is eligible for -1 FFMO DRM, and fire against units on a Bridge that does not cross only the road depiction is subject to a +1 TEM DRM, no?

I understand there were changes made to these rules via published errata (that were controversial in some circles), and that they were subsequently rescinded?  

Not looking for any flame wars! - just wondering if anyone can provide a short history of the rule changes, and confirm if my understanding of the rules as posted above is correct and current.
author: walternewton
consensus_answer:
The bridge TEM controversy wasn't just a simple case of MMP making a mistake... there is actually an error in the game's components.

The bridge counters show 0 TEM along the road, +1 TEM otherwise.

The Terrain Chart says -1 TEM along the road, +1 TEM otherwise.

The two components do not agree, so one of them is wrong.

When MMP was asked to rule on this, they ruled that the Terrain Chart was correct (-1 TEM), and issued errata to fix the wording of the rules in Chapter B to support this. But it seems that most players were using 0 TEM for bridges, which was supported by the original wording of the Chapter B rules... hence the uproar and controversy.

The players eventually convinced MMP that the Terrain Chart was, in fact, wrong and MMP rescinded their original errata.

So, the final result is that the bridge counters are correct as printed; the Terrain Chart is wrong (errata in Journal 8 corrects the wording of the Terrain Chart); and the Chapter B rules were correct (errata in Journal 8 "undoes" the earlier errata).

But it seems that most players were using 0 TEM for bridges, which was supported by the original wording of the Chapter B rules... hence the uproar and controversy.

So, the final result is that the bridge counters are correct as printed; the Terrain Chart is wrong (errata in Journal 8 corrects the wording of the Terrain Chart); and the Chapter B rules were correct (errata in Journal 8 "undoes" the earlier errata).

The -1 FFMO is correct.

The errata that caused the controversy was a -1 TEM for the bridge, so theoretically a squad crossing a bridge could get -3, -1 for FFMO, -1 for FFNAM and -1 for bridge TEM.  Later this rule was rescinded and only the -2 would occur, -2 for FFMO/FFNAM.

It lasted about a year, where there was a bridge TEM of -1.  

MMP also introduced some other controversial rules, something about a concealed unit retaining its concealment when it "bumped" in the jungle.  That was also reversed as cooler heads prevailed.  The ASL community usually wins with "history" over "MMP's interpretation".  Thankfully.

title: Miscellaneous rules questions
question:
We've now played 3 games of this Full ASL (moving from SKs) and I gotta say it's great. I do have some obscure rules questions though, not all related to the games we played.

1. Human Wave and stairs. 
Can you ever go backwards in hexes for example to go back 1 hex to get down the stairs so they can get to ground level and start moving forward?

Is going downstairs considered moving forward? Or do I mark the stack with Range counter if I move from level 1 to ground level? 

If so then I suppose starting HW from Level 2 is not the greatest idea. :)

2. Must a HW really move forward until all their MF are out or is there any way I can "stop" the HW at will?

Example:
We played Guards Counterattack and I did the HW as soon as possible. It was a phenomenal success, leaving only one broken russian in the streets while getting into the building and breaking 2 German half squads in their FPF.

Here's the situation at the end of Impulse 2 (leaving out stuff in upper levels and other buildings). HW started at E4,F3,G4:

Two out of my three stacks were in a hex with an enemy so they must stop there (even if the enemy is broken right?). Only 3 MF has been spent so far.
But the stack in E6.. Must it really continue on even if I don't wanna? They are so gonna get nailed by first fire from I7 and other buildings... At the time I resolved it by going to F6 and then level 1 upstairs with Range counter and stopping there having nowhere else to go but that was a rules mistake I know. Now, If I had to go forward I'd propably go to F6 (5MF), F7 (6MF) and finally F8 (8MF) ending there.

3. LOS question 1
Does LOS exist between Ground level D7 and Level 1 (or 2) E7 in this situation because the LOS crosses open ground on the hexside?

4. LOS question 2
Same kind of situation but no open ground on the hexside so LOS is blocked between levels?

5. Does Residual attack DRs activate Snipers?
My opponent fired in a building hex leaving 1 resid and I started moving my 8 morale russian squads through that hex. It immediately occurred to us that 1FP +2 TEM (or +3, I assault moved some) does not have a good change of hurting my guys but it does have a good chance of activating my Sniper (SAN 6) if I just exploited that hex and kept moving guys through it.....

6. 3KIA and Random Selection (No. 3KIA didn't happen in our games.)
Could someone explain me how the Random Selection is done in this case?
The RB says at 7.301 #KIA:
"..The number of units can exceed the number specified if Random Selection results in a tie for the last unit to be eliminated, but in no case are more units affected than are subject to that attack."

For some reason I don't get it. What does "last unit to be eliminated" mean? The lowest of the 3 highest numbers in 3KIA case?

Example: Stack of 5 units: A,B,C,D,E. I roll 5 dice.

5,4,3,2,1 
Kills kills A, B and C of course. No ties.

What about:
5,5,4,3,1
Only, A, B and C are killed right? Because the tie was the highest number and not the "last" unit?

5,4,4,3,1
A, B and C again?

Then:
5,4,3,3,1
Now this kills also D?

BUT What about...
5,5,4,4,1
Wait, I think I got it by now.. A,B,C,D dies because 4 tied C and D..
Seems like writing down these questions already helps me understand this stuff.. Oh, well. Next question:

7. Heroes, Prisoners and Exit VPs.
Can a Hero guard prisoners and gain VPs by exiting the board with them in Exit VP scenario?

We were playing Fighting Withdrawal. My opponent, the Finns, was running out of time. His leaders were killed or broken and without the Leader's movement bonus couldn't exit his squads in time. But he had 2 Heroes (6MF) which could exit the map and tons of Prisoners. His ingenious move was to transfer the prisoners to these Heroes and have them exit the map. Oh man. He failed in the end but it was an interesting idea. Is this allowed? The heroes and the prisoners would have been his only units exiting the map. :p

Hope I didn't give you a headache..

consensus_answer:
1. Human Wave and stairs. 
Can you ever go backwards in hexes for example to go back 1 hex to get down the stairs so they can get to ground level and start moving forward?

Is going downstairs considered moving forward? Or do I mark the stack with Range counter if I move from level 1 to ground level? 

If so then I suppose starting HW from Level 2 is not the greatest idea. :)
I am not sure of my answer - never saw the situation occur.
25.232 allows a HW to "move up or down in a building while moving closer to the Ground Level and/or an enemy unit in that hex".
This would seem to prohibit such a move.
But 25.2321 allows increasing range to the Hex Grain : would that allow some backwards moving ?
Moving downstairs without moving "backwards" is not increasing range vs the HW hex grain : I would not mark it with a Range counter - as I presume that the HW unit is getting closer to its target.
I would ask Perry Cocke about that one.

2. Must a HW really move forward until all their MF are out or is there any way I can "stop" the HW at will?If it has not reached an enemy unit's Location, the HW unit goes on charging...

3. LOS question 1
Does LOS exist between Ground level D7 and Level 1 (or 2) E7 in this situation because the LOS crosses open ground on the hexside?
Sure there is LOS. If they were two ADJACENT separated buildings, LOS would apply too.

4. LOS question 2
Same kind of situation but no open ground on the hexside so LOS is blocked between levels?
Same answer as for preceding question. ADJACENT building Locations have LOS.

5. Does Residual attack DRs activate Snipers?
My opponent fired in a building hex leaving 1 resid and I started moving my 8 morale russian squads through that hex. It immediately occurred to us that 1FP +2 TEM (or +3, I assault moved some) does not have a good change of hurting my guys but it does have a good chance of activating my Sniper (SAN 6) if I just exploited that hex and kept moving guys through it.....RF surely activates SAN.
The cases are given in A14.1 : "TH, MC, TC, non-OBA IFT, or Entrenching, Original DR [EXC: those made for Prisoners] equal to the enemy SAN"
RF IFT attacks belong to the "non-OBA IFT" attacks.

6. 3KIA and Random Selection

Example: Stack of 5 units: A,B,C,D,E. I roll 5 dice.

5,4,3,2,1 
Kills kills A, B and C of course. No ties.Yes

What about:
5,5,4,3,1
Only, A, B and C are killed right?Right 
5,4,4,3,1
A, B and C again?Yes

5,4,3,3,1
Now this kills also D?Yes

5,5,4,4,1
Wait, I think I got it by now.. A,B,C,D dies because 4 tied C and D.Yes
Seems like writing down these questions already helps me understand this stuff.. Oh, well.It seems.
Note that a "Yahtsee" (say 5,5,5,5,5) kills everybody.

7. Heroes, Prisoners and Exit VPs.
Can a Hero guard prisoners and gain VPs by exiting the board with them in Exit VP scenario?Prisoners count as Casualty VPs.
Now, if you have to exit a number of VPs, Prisoners do count - unless the VC clearly says that Prisonners don't count [which is the case in quite a lot of scenarios].
Heroes by themselves don't score any VP.
And they only can guard units up to 5 times their US#, that is 5 (e.g a squad and a HS).

Hope I didn't give you a headache..No. Rules questions are allways interesting to examine.

I would suggest, however, that you create a thread for each type of question : that helps other forum members see if a given question already has been adressed.
Other advantage : another ASL player will feel better if he is able to answer a specific question, when other ones are out of his own understanding.

Have a nice day !

title: Snipers
question:
I only just started palying ASL and am trying to work out how snipers actually work. 

Is it right that when your opponent roles less than or equal to your SAN you roll 1 die, and score a hit on a 1 or 2. You then roll two die and use the results to determine distance and direction from the current location of your sniper counter (say white = direction and colour = distance). 

Is this right?
author: bluetiger80
consensus_answer: Close. It's when your opponent rolls equal to (not less than) your SAN, that you roll the sniper check dr. And only for attacks, MC or TC during PFPh, MPh, DFPh, or AFPh. (No SAN checks if your opponent rolls your SAN during RPh, for instance.)

OBA attack DRs do not count as SAN DRs, but any resulting MC/TC do.

title: Bounding First Fire Question
question:
I a mprobably over-thinking this but, can a vehicle use its MG MA as BFF in a TK attempt? 
A9.61 seems to say no and I can not find an exception that says a MA MG can make a TK attempt if it suffers from a halved FP penalty (as would be the case in BFF) in either section A, C, Or D.

Thanks for your help.

Cheers,
Josh
author: j23flo
consensus_answer:
D3.53 The Case B To Hit DRM does not apply to vehicle MG; the FP of any MG firing during the AFPh is halved instead, unless it is MA attempting a To Kill DR as ordnance (A9.61). 

D3.54 vs AFV: A vehicular-mounted MG may not attempt a To Kill attack unless it is the vehicle's MA. Another MG may never substitute for the listed MA of a vehicle.

title: Surrounded in Row Houses
question:
Hi guys,

Just wondering whether i played this correctly :

A broken Russkie 4-4-7 squad is in the middle of row houses with a Finn squad each on the left and right of that 447 squad.During the RtPh, the brokie cannot rout and must surrender. Who does it surrender to? ....Russian player decide or Finn player decide?

What if ...there is only 1 Finn Squad? All rout paths looks like being covered by interdiction except for the row house to its rear. Can the brokie rout to that row house? ...I reckon it cannot as there is a black bar across that hexside ...and so must surrender.

cheers
-Lamskiy-
author: Lamskiy
consensus_answer:
If I understand your question correctly, the Russian squad is not forced to Rout as it is not ADJACENT to the Finnish units.  (assuming the Finnish units are in the same Rowhouse)

Locations [and units in them] are considered ADJACENT if any Infantry unit in one Location could conceivably - ignoring any enemy presence - advance into the other during the APh and a LOS exists between the two Locations

If there was only one Finnish squad then the Russian brokie could Rout to the next Rowhouse 

B23.71  ..Infantry in a Rowhouse may move/rout/advance/Withdraw-from-CC directly into another Rowhouse hex of the same building only at the ground or Rooftop (23.8) level; if at the ground level they must specify which side of the building they are "bypassing". Such units moving/routing on the ground level expend three MF (one to "bypass" in the hex it is leaving where it would be attacked by any OBA/Residual-FP and two to enter the building), and can be Interdicted or Defensive First Fired upon with FFMO/FFNAM DRM by any unit capable of doing so that can trace a LOS to the vertex of the hexside crossed by the moving/routing unit on that side of the building.

With the Rowhouses, I know you can move around at the vertex point, but assuming open ground in the area, that would still leave you open to interdiction (as I belive LOS would measure to the vertex point).  If no LOS to vertex, then it should be ok.  Oh, and this is assuming that they were ADJACENT to an enemy unit, as the poster on top here said.

As for the surrender, I believe is the player accepting surrender that has choice where the unarmed units go if multiple counters are eligible.

That said, I don't have manual with me here, and the last 2 times I answered these I was partially wrong, so I would wait confirmation from someone who knows more than me :)

[edited to not look quite as stupid.....]
And and by the way, if a broken squad at Ground Level in a Rowhouse hex was completely surrounded, it could Rout upstairs.

When a unit surrenders, the force taking the prisoners decides who takes them, and the now guarding unit may deploy if desired.

Routing in rowhouses is complicated. Units normally cannot go through the black bar, but can bypass the black bar by exiting the building. This opens their rout up to Interdiction, but sometimes you have to do what you have to do. Also, most rowhouses are multi-storey, so routing upstairs is an option.

Thanks for the clarifications.

The situation occured in (you probably guessed it ...Fighting Withdrawal). There was actually another Finnish unit next to the 4-4-7 but i forgot that it could rout upstairs.

All the while, i was under the impression that a brokie cannot rout using Bypass moevement ...but the quote from the rules clarified the situation with respect to Rowhouses. 

Thanks again n cheers
-Lamskiy-

title: Voluntary concealment loss
question:
May a player voluntarily remove concealment from units at any time?  
Or does concealment loss only ever occur through application of a concealment table case?  
Are there only certain times when concealment may be voluntarily removed? 
Specifically may concealment be voluntarily removed during an opponent's RtPh prior to or during a rout? 
May concealment be voluntarily removed from adjacent would-be interdictors to force surrender via the RtPh method even if the routing player declares low-crawl while the unit is concealed?
author: funnymarx
consensus_answer:
May a player voluntarily remove concealment from units at any time?  
Or does concealment loss only ever occur through application of a concealment table case?  
Are there only certain times when concealment may be voluntarily removed? 
Specifically may concealment be voluntarily removed during an opponent's RtPh prior to or during a rout? 
May concealment be voluntarily removed from adjacent would-be interdictors to force surrender via the RtPh method even if the routing player declares low-crawl while the unit is concealed?  

Why would you want to voluntarily lose concealment (aside from firing)?  It has no disadvantage.

replies.body:
May a player voluntarily remove concealment from units at any time?  
Or does concealment loss only ever occur through application of a concealment table case?  
Are there only certain times when concealment may be voluntarily removed? 
Specifically may concealment be voluntarily removed during an opponent's RtPh prior to or during a rout? 
May concealment be voluntarily removed from adjacent would-be interdictors to force surrender via the RtPh method even if the routing player declares low-crawl while the unit is concealed?  

Why would you want to voluntarily lose concealment (aside from firing)?  It has no disadvantage.

It can also be useful to deny your opponent a free LOS check when you are moving. If your unit is moving while concealed and your opponent reasonably believes that the may be line of sight to that unit, he can make a free LOS check to find out.  However, if you have first removed your concealed status, he has to declare fire in order to check the LOS. If it is close, the LOS may actually be blocked, but now his unit has fired uselessly.

Concealed units do not interdict/prevent routs, for one. Note JaggedTech's note above. Moving a concealed unit can allow free LOS checks to try to strip '?', while an unconcealed unit can only get a LOS when fired upon.

There are other, more esoteric, reasons, but those are the most common reasons to voluntarily drop '?'.

title: Rout off board for exit VC?
question: Played "Gavin Take" last night, and ran into the situation where US half-squads were able to rout off the board at the exit victory condition location.  The VC on the scenario card required exit of half-squad equivalents, but said nothing about good order or unbroken status.   I couldn't find an applicable rule in A26, so for expediency (and to help the newer player) we deemed routers as counting towards the victory condition.  Was this a legal move?
author: funnymarx
consensus_answer:
I dont think so.

A2.6 Exit: Units may leave the mapboard using normal MPh/APh capabilities from any mapboard edge hex or half-hex as if they are entering an imaginary offboard hex which is the mirror image of the one they currently occupy. Bypass can be claimed to exit a hex (such as 2X0) only if the unit has one additional MF/MP in excess of that needed for Bypass. The mapboard cannot be left during the RtPh. Units which leave the mapboard [EXC: glider contents (E8.5); paratroops (E9.41)] may not return. 

Brad

title: 2nd Ed Rulebook - what replacement pages have been published and where are they?
question:
Hi Guys,

I’ve just acquired the ASL Rulebook and a few of the available modules and I’m trying to sort out where to collect all the errata pages.

My RB is of very current vintage:  It is the second edition.

I have Armies of Oblivion, which contains quite a few replacement pages:  

I have Action Pack 4, which contains Revised rules pages B9 & B10

So… what came before that and what replacement pages were provided?

I’m focusing totally on the 2nd ed rulebook.

Thanks!

Foob
author: fubar awol
consensus_answer:
I think I have figured it out for new players:

1.  Make sure you get latest version of the rulebook: the second printing of the second edition.

2.  Get Armies of Oblivion (good luck with that... OOP and I haven't seen any copies for auction on EBAY in over a month).  It contains dozen or so errata pages.  Replace those pages.

3a.  Get AP 4 for errata pages. Replace.

3b.  Get Replacement pages: Page A-15-A16vB, Page B7-B8vB and Page D5-D8vB from the MMP website and replace.

4.  Download the sticky errata from the Texas ASLer's website (see link above).  Print on label paper and cut-and-paste it into place where it is different from your rulebook.  Some of it is already incorporated (particularly most the chart errata, which was fixed in the 2nd printing of the 2nd edition).  Get all the Errata: AP4-6, AP7 and AP8.

Now you are fully up to date.  Did I miss something?

Foob

Note:

AoO Pages are: A51 through A62 and D21 through D26

Pages from MMP website: Page A-15-A16vB, Page B7-B8vB and Page D5-D8vB (NOTE: Page A53 and A54 from MMP website are superseded by the AoO pages and should be ignored)

AP4 pages are:  B09, B10, B10A, B10B

These are all the necessary replacement pages if working from latest and greatest RB 2nd ed.

title: Gun/SW question
question:
I have a full MMC in a hex with a MMG (portaged into the hex, under unit's control) and a recovered AT gun.  Can the squad fire both the MMG *AND* the AT gun with no penalty other than the unqualified unit +2TH DRM?  Rules state that you can have as many weapons as you want, but can one actually FIRE them all?

Thanks, experts.  We can't find the answer in the rules...
author: paulus22
consensus_answer:
I guess another option would be to deploy the squad into two half-squads and be able to shoot both.  If you have a leader present, of course.

Absolutely you could deploy in the RPh wth a leader (if otherwise allowed) freely transfer the SW/Gun and that would work.

The other thing to take into consideration are the non-qualified/captured weapon use penalties. So if you're in this situation and you're not elite you have a good chance of breaking the Gun when you go to fire it..

A21.11 MALFUNCTION: A captured Gun/SW (or vehicle) has its B#/X# decreased by two due to lack of familiarity with the equipment and difficulty of resupply (see A.11). Ammunition Shortage (19.131) penalties do not apply to captured Gun/SW 

21.12 PERFORMANCE: Captured weapons must reduce any Multiple ROF capability by one. All attacks by captured ordnance must use the red To Hit Numbers and add a +2 DRM to all To Hit attempts (Case H). Captured non-ordnance weapons are penalized only by the decrease in their breakdown number and ROF. 

21.13 NON-QUALIFIED USE: An ordnance weapon which requires a crew to man it may be operated by non-qualified friendly MMC or qualified enemy MMC by applying the 21.11-.12 penalties to their use. Non-qualified enemy MMC may use these special weapons by doubling these penalties. title: Hand To Hand combat?
question: So I have been going through the valor of the guards material the last couple days, and I noticed that it references Hand to hand combat and a rule in Section J (deluxe ASL).  I recalled seeing something in my PTO rules (I have 'em, just havent figured em out yet /ducks) about HtoH combat, but nothing really seemed to apply.  I dont want to have to fork out 100 bucks for deluxe ASL, when it isnt something I really care a bunch about anyways.  Is there anywhere else these rules are avaiable?  I saw the scenarios on MMPs site, but no rules.  Are they that important anyways?
author: Colonel Ripper
consensus_answer:
The single section J page (J1 front, J2 back) should be right between H (vehicle notes) and the K chapter about training (the examples of play).  It is only one page.

Basically, when you start close combat the ATTACKER (if not ambushed) can declare Hand-to-Hand close combat after which both sides use the red Kill Numbers rather than the black for the duration of the CC/Melee.  Infantry/Cavalry is stacked together (I think thats just a reference to the deluxe practice of spreading out counters in a hex, so should't matter to VotG).  Vehicles still use the black Kill numbers NOT the red.  

There are other conditions and exceptions in the rule as well, but that's the jist of it.

I think the logic here, such as it is, pertains to gameplay rather than realism.  HIP is one of the most powerful elements of the game, and granting HIP to troops just because they're in foxholes exaggerates the value of a pretty common order of battle component.  You *can* put dummies in foxholes, by the way, as long as the dummies conform to other setup restrictions (must be in Concealment terrain).  It can be a useful ruse when you plunk the foxhole counter on top when the enemy comes in LOS - "Why would he waste a foxhole on a dummy?"  Food for thought,

Well, think it through before you dismiss it. The rule is the fortifications are not seen 'until you get an LOS to them' 

So, if you don't put them in LOS of the enemy troops, or the enemy sets up second or offboard, they do NOT know where you intend to 'draw the line' until they 'scout' the board.  

By then, they have committed their troops and their setup supports their strategy - that didn't count on you 'digging in' exactly where you did!/ 

It works - give it a try, and a chance. You'll come to like it.

title: A couple of questions
question:
Do you "cower" everytime you roll doubles, even snake eyes, when shooting?

Do you go under DM everytime you fail a MC or get Casualty reduced?
author: shakespear
consensus_answer:
Do you "cower" everytime you roll doubles, even snake eyes, when shooting?

You cower, even on snake eyes, unless an SMC (like firing a MG), berserk, Fanatic, British elite and first line, Finnish, ordnance, OBA or vehicular.

Do you go under DM everytime you fail a MC or get Casualty reduced?

You go under DM when you break, even voluntarily.

You also go under DM if you are already broken and: 

a) you're attacked by White Phosphorus

b) you're attacked with "enough FP to possibly inflict a NMC on the target" (even if the firing unit cowers). Ordnance must secure a hit to be considered an 'attack'

c) you're in a Location attacked by an effective (1 or 2 result) Sniper

d) a Known enemy unit becomes ADJACENT to you (even if the enemy unit Moves on, even if it is an enemy unit advance)

Casualty Reduction alone does not cause you to go DM. A77.302 (first edition) says "A squad is reduced to a HS with the same broken/non-broken status of the squad it was Reduced from.."
